items.title: ClinVar-GKM
items.text:
ClinVar-GKM provides a standardized, machine-readable representation of ClinVar release data using the GKM (Genomic Knowledge Model) schema set — VRS, Cat-VRS, and VA-Spec — from the GA4GH Genomic Knowledge Standards workstream. It is developed and maintained by the ClinGen driver project.

1.1.0 moved every download URL

1.1.0 (released 2026-10-22) moved every download URL to v1/1.1/ and renamed the proposition sections — see the changelog migration notes.

New here?

How to Read These Docs maps each section to what it gives you, with three reading paths: understanding the data from ClinVar's website, following how ClinVar's XML becomes this format, and building a pipeline or application on it.

New to GKM datasets? Start with the GKM Starter Kit

The GA4GH GKM Starter Kit is a practical entry point for working with GKM data. It brings together the reference libraries (vrs-python, cat-vrs-python, va-spec-python), the GKM Toolkit for loading and exploring published bundles, and user stories from projects putting GKM to work. clinvar-gkm is a GKM data producer — those tools work directly on its bundles.

items.title: Why ClinVar-GKM
items.text:
ClinVar is one of the most widely used public archives of human genetic variation and its relationship to disease. However, the native ClinVar XML format presents challenges for programmatic consumption — inconsistent structures, deeply nested records, and representations that do not align with emerging genomic data standards.

ClinVar-GKM addresses these challenges by transforming every ClinVar release into a consistent, semantically rich format built on GA4GH specifications:

  • Normalized variant identifiers — Every variant receives a computable VRS identifier, enabling unambiguous cross-system matching
  • Categorical variant representations — Variants are represented as Cat-VRS categorical variants with defining allele constraints and expressions
  • Structured classification statements — Every submitted (SCV), aggregate (VCV), and condition-level (RCV) classification is represented as a VA-Spec statement with explicit propositions, evidence, and provenance
  • Semantic consistency — Classifications, propositions, conditions, genes, and cross-references use standardized structures with typed references

items.title: What It Covers
items.text:
The pipeline processes the entirety of each ClinVar XML release — every variation, submitted classification, and aggregate record is represented. While 100% of variant, SCV, VCV, and RCV records from the corresponding ClinVar XML release are included, some data types within ClinVar are not yet part of the v1 release.

ClinVar Data Type v1 Status Variation Aggregate Classifications (VCVs) Included Variation-Condition Aggregate Classifications (RCVs) Included Germline and Somatic Submissions (SCVs) Included Variations (incl. Genes, HGVS, SPDI and VCF extensions) Included Submitters Included Aggregate & Case-level observations (example) Planned Functional data submissions (example) Planned

Items marked Planned are not currently included in the v1 release. If this data is requested by the community, it will be added as demand indicates.

Functional Data Submissions

Functional data is submitted to ClinVar as an SCV and may or may not be associated with a germline or somatic classification record. Functional data SCVs are excluded from the v1 release regardless of whether they are linked to a classification SCV. They will be included in a future release when functional data support is added.

Feedback and feature requests are welcome via the GitHub issue tracker. For release announcements and change notices, join the email list clinvar-gkm@broadinstitute.org. Stay Informed explains how to join and what the list announces: new releases, version changes, and events where ClinVar-GKM is presented.

New releases are produced within a day or two after ClinVar's XML releases and are intended to be synchronized with ClinVar's release dates.

items.title: Who It's For
items.text:
• Variant scientists seeking a clear, consistent representation of ClinVar classifications with explicit propositions, conditions, and evidence
  • Platform engineers building systems that consume ClinVar data and need a structured, well-documented format for integration
  • GA4GH implementers using ClinVar-GKM as a real-world validation of VRS, Cat-VRS, and VA-Spec schemas

items.title: Getting Started
items.text:
Prefer tables to JSON?

The latest release is also published as one set of 22 typed Parquet tables, rebuilt every week, that you can query with SQL, with no database and no data loading. Query the Data starts with a live query console in your browser and works up to joins, recipes and large-scale analysis.

items.title: Download the Latest Release
items.text:
The latest ClinVar-GKM release is available as a single compressed JSON file:

# Download the newest official monthly release
curl -O https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.1/clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz

# Decompress
gunzip clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz

items.title: What's in the File
items.text:
The release file is a single JSON object with bundle sections at the root level. Each section is a keyed collection of objects — the key is the object's unique identifier, and the value is the object itself.

{
  "sequenceReference": { "SQ.abc123": { ... } },
  "location":          { "ga4gh:SL.xyz789": { ... } },
  "allele":            { "ga4gh:VA.def456": { ... } },
  "gene":              { "ncbigene:3077": { ... } },
  "variation":         { "clinvar:10": { ... } },
  "condition":         { "clinvar.trait:9580": { ... } },
  "conditionSet":      { "clinvar.traitset:1234": { ... } },
  "therapy":           { "clinvar.therapy:{sha256}": { ... } },
  "therapyGroup":      { "clinvar.therapygroup:{sha256}": { ... } },
  "submitter":            { "clinvar.submitter:500139": { ... } },
  "propositionPathogenicity":         { "SCV001234567-PATH": { ... } },
  "propositionOncogenicity":          { "SCV002345678-ONCO": { ... } },
  "propositionSomaticClinicalImpact": { "SCV003456789-TR": { ... } },
  "propositionClinvarCustom":         { "SCV004567890-RF": { ... } },
  "scv":                  { "clinvar.submission:SCV001234567.1": { ... } },
  "vcv":               { "VCV000012582.63-G-PATH-CP": { ... } },
  "rcv":               { "RCV000012345.8-G-PATH-CP": { ... } }
}

Objects reference each other using #/ JSON pointer strings. For example, an allele references its location as "#/location/ga4gh:SL.xyz789", and an SCV statement references its proposition as "#/propositionPathogenicity/SCV001234567-PATH". Propositions are delivered in four sections grouped by meaning (propositionPathogenicity, propositionOncogenicity, propositionSomaticClinicalImpact, propositionClinvarCustom) — the pointer names the section the proposition lives in.

See Output Format for the full structure and reference patterns.

items.title: Quick Example
items.text:
To find the classification statements for a specific variant, start with the variation ID. ClinVar variation 10 (the HFE p.His63Asp variant) has the key clinvar:10 in the variation section:

{
  "variation": {
    "clinvar:10": {
      "id": "clinvar:10",
      "type": "CategoricalVariant",
      "name": "NM_000410.4(HFE):c.187C>G (p.His63Asp)",
      "members": ["#/allele/ga4gh:VA.ELQCnIBGqaTl0AEE0Az18XZ2cgIHAQIY"],
      "constraints": [ ... ],
      "extensions": [ ... ],
      "mappings": [ ... ]
    }
  }
}

The SCV statements for this variant reference it via #/variation/clinvar:10 in their propositions. To find them, look for entries in the proposition sections (propositionPathogenicity, propositionOncogenicity, propositionSomaticClinicalImpact, propositionClinvarCustom) where subject matches, then find the corresponding scv entries that reference those propositions.

items.title: Key Concepts
items.text:
Statements are the core unit of ClinVar-GKM. Each statement represents a classification — either submitted (SCV), aggregated per variation (VCV), or aggregated per condition (RCV). Statements carry:

  • A classification — the clinical significance label (e.g., Pathogenic, Likely benign)
  • A proposition — what the classification asserts (variant X causes condition Y)
  • Direction and strength — whether the evidence supports, disputes, or is neutral toward the proposition
  • Evidence lines — links to the contributing submissions or lower-level aggregations
  • Extensions — provenance metadata including submitted conditions, review status, and submission details

Propositions define the relationship being classified — a variant's causal role for a condition, its oncogenic potential, or its clinical impact. Each proposition has a type (e.g., VariantPathogenicityProposition), a predicate (e.g., isCausalFor), a subject variant, and an object condition.

Conditions represent the diseases or phenotypes that classifications are made against. Single conditions reference #/condition/clinvar.trait:{id}, while multi-condition sets reference #/conditionSet/clinvar.traitset:{id}.

items.title: Data Access
items.text: ClinVar-GKM is distributed as official monthly full bundles, weekly full bundles and weekly deltas, laid out like NCBI's ClinVar XML folder, plus one typed Parquet dataset (one file per section) for the latest release. Each bundle is a gzip-compressed JSON file. The files are freely available for download from Cloudflare R2 object storage with no authentication required and no egress fees.

items.title: Release Schedule
items.text:
• Weekly releases: for every ClinVar weekly release, a weekly full bundle in weekly/ and a delta in deltas/ (the records added or updated since the prior release, plus a manifest listing per-section adds, updates, and deletes). weekly/ keeps the current month only
  • Official monthly full bundles are published once a month, aligned to ClinVar's own monthly VCV releases — each ClinVarVCVRelease_YYYY-MM triggers our clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MM full, built from the most recent weekly release before ClinVar's monthly cut
  • At the start of each month, the previous month's deltas move to deltas/YYYY-MM/ and its weekly fulls are deleted (the last one once the new month's monthly is published); at the start of each year, the previous year's monthlies and deltas move to archive/YYYY/

The stable filenames clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz (official monthly) and weekly/clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz (weekly full) always point to the newest of each. Any past week can be rebuilt from a monthly plus the deltas after it.

items.title: Downloads
items.text:
Download the newest official monthly and the newest weekly full:

curl -O https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.1/clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz
curl -O https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.1/weekly/clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz

See How Releases Work for the release model, and Weekly Deltas for the deltas and the replay recipe.

items.title: Directory Structure
items.text:
All paths are under the current line folder, v1/1.1/:

clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz                newest official monthly full
clinvar-gkm_yyyy-mm.json.gz                  official monthly fulls (current year)

weekly/
  clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz       newest weekly full
  clinvar-gkm_yyyy-mmdd.json.gz              weekly fulls (current month only)

deltas/
  clinvar-gkm-delta_yyyy-mmdd.json.gz        weekly deltas (current month)
  clinvar-gkm-delta_yyyy-mmdd.manifest.json  per-release change manifest
  yyyy-mm/                                   earlier months of the current year

archive/yyyy/                                prior years: monthlies and deltas/yyyy-mm/

parquet/                                     one Parquet dataset, overwritten every release

items.title: Release Notes
items.text: Pipeline changes that affect the structure or content of the output are recorded in the Changelog, and each tagged release is listed on GitHub Releases. They cover changes specific to the ClinVar-GKM pipeline and do not replicate ClinVar's own release notes.

items.title: How It Works
items.text:
The pipeline runs on Google BigQuery using SQL stored procedures, with an external VRS Python processing step. The two most expensive stages — variation identity and VRS processing — run incrementally, recomputing only the variations that changed since the prior release and carrying the rest forward. From 1.1.0 the downstream GKM procedures rebuild in full every week. A per-release change log drives the weekly delta published to R2.

See the Pipeline Overview for the full workflow.

items.title: Data Use, Citation and License
items.text:
ClinVar-GKM re-represents ClinVar data, which comes from NCBI at the U.S. National Library of Medicine. ClinVar's disclaimer and data use policy applies to this data and to anyone who uses or redistributes it:

  • Not for direct clinical use. ClinVar's information "is not intended for direct diagnostic use or medical decision-making without review by a genetics professional."
  • Attribute and cite ClinVar as the data source, as ClinVar asks, and cite ClinVar-GKM (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18343663) if you used these files.
  • License. The code and the published files — the transformed bundles and Parquet sets — are dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0 Universal. CC0 covers ClinGen's contribution and adds no restriction; NCBI's and ClinVar's policies still apply to the ClinVar content.
  • No endorsement. ClinVar-GKM is not an NCBI, NLM or NIH product and is not endorsed by them.

Data Use and Citation gives the citations, what to carry with the data when you redistribute it, and the policy text behind each point.

items.title: Data Use and Citation
items.text:
ClinVar-GKM re-represents ClinVar data. ClinVar is produced by the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI), part of the U.S. National Library of Medicine (NLM). ClinVar-GKM is produced by ClinGen. ClinGen's CC0 dedication covers what ClinGen adds. The ClinVar content inside the files remains subject to NCBI's and ClinVar's own policies, which apply to everyone who uses or redistributes these files.

In short

  • Not for direct clinical use. The ClinVar disclaimer applies to this data unchanged: the information "is not intended for direct diagnostic use or medical decision-making without review by a genetics professional." See Clinical use.
  • Attribute ClinVar. ClinVar asks that anyone who distributes or copies its data provide attribution to ClinVar as a data source. Cite ClinVar, and cite ClinVar-GKM if you used these files. See How to cite.
  • CC0 covers ClinGen's contribution only. It adds no restriction, and it cannot grant rights that NCBI or ClinVar's submitters hold. See License.
  • Pass this on. If you redistribute these files or data derived from them, carry the attribution and the disclaimer with them. See Redistributing the data.

items.title: Data source
items.text:
The ClinVar content comes from the public XML releases of ClinVar, at NCBI, NLM, National Institutes of Health (NIH). The pipeline adds the GKM structure and the VRS identifiers it computes. Weekly and delta file names carry the ClinVar release date, and each version line's index.json and the Parquet manifest.json name the release each file was built from; see How Releases Work.

ClinVar is an archive of classifications made by its submitters. When submitters disagree, ClinVar's FAQ says that "ClinVar does not arbitrate and resolve these conflicts", and its disclaimer says that "NIH does not independently verify the submitted information." ClinVar-GKM changes the representation, not the classifications. It keeps each submission's submitter and dates: every SCV statement's contributions reference a record in the submitter section. ClinVar remains the authoritative source. Check a record on ClinVar before you rely on it, and see Known Issues for what the transformation does not yet carry.

items.title: Clinical use
items.text:
ClinVar's disclaimer and data use policy applies to ClinVar-GKM data as it does to ClinVar:

The information on this website is not intended for direct diagnostic use or medical decision-making without review by a genetics professional. Individuals should not change their health behavior solely on the basis of information contained on this website.

NLM's Medical Information and Advice Disclaimer urges users "to consult with a qualified physician for diagnosis and for answers to your personal questions." The same advice applies to this data.

items.title: ClinVar
items.text:
ClinVar asks for attribution in its data use policy: "If you distribute or copy data from ClinVar, we ask that you provide attribution to ClinVar as a data source in publications and websites." It asks you to cite one of the ClinVar publications. The newest is:

Landrum MJ, Chitipiralla S, Kaur K, et al. ClinVar: updates to support classifications of both germline and somatic variants. Nucleic Acids Res. 2025;53(D1):D1313–D1321. doi:10.1093/nar/gkae1090. PMID: 39578691.

The data use policy gives PMID 29165669 as an example (Landrum MJ et al., Nucleic Acids Res. 2018;46(D1):D1062–D1067).

To refer to a specific ClinVar record, follow ClinVar's FAQ: cite the SCV accession and version for a submission, and the VCV or RCV accession and version for an aggregate record. ClinVar-GKM keeps these accessions and versions in its statement ids and extensions.

items.title: ClinVar-GKM
items.text:
If you used these files, also cite ClinVar-GKM and name the release you used, for example the bundle file name or the Parquet manifest.json source_release:

Babb L, Ferriter K, O'Neill T. ClinVar-GKM. ClinGen. doi:10.5281/zenodo.18343663.

The repository's CITATION.cff has the machine-readable citation, and GitHub's Cite this repository button formats it.

items.title: License
items.text:
ClinGen dedicates the ClinVar-GKM code and the published files, the transformed bundles and Parquet sets, to the public domain under CC0 1.0 Universal. CC0 covers what ClinGen contributes: the transformation, the structure and the identifiers it computes. It adds no restriction of its own.

CC0 does not change the terms that apply to the ClinVar content inside the files:

  • NCBI's Molecular Data Usage policy says that "NCBI itself places no restrictions on the use or distribution of the data". It also says that some submitters "may claim patent, copyright, or other intellectual property rights in all or a portion of the data", and that NCBI "cannot provide comment or unrestricted permission concerning the use, copying, or distribution" of it. CC0 waives only rights that ClinGen holds, so it grants nothing in rights that a submitter may claim.
  • ClinVar's submission policy says that "Once the data are in ClinVar, they are available for unrestricted distribution."
  • CC0 itself (section 4) offers the work as-is, with no warranty, and disclaims responsibility for clearing other people's rights in it.

You are responsible for following NCBI's and ClinVar's policies, including their attribution request, when you use or redistribute this data.

items.title: Redistributing the data
items.text:
You may redistribute ClinVar-GKM files, or data derived from them, under CC0. When you do:

  • Keep the attribution. Name ClinVar as the data source, as ClinVar asks, and name ClinVar-GKM and the release.
  • Keep the disclaimer visible. Carry the clinical use disclaimer, or link to it, wherever people see the data. NCBI asks the same of services built on its servers: its Guidelines for Scripting Calls to NCBI Servers state that "NCBI's Disclaimer and Copyright notice must be evident to users of your service."
  • Keep the submitter attribution. ClinVar's introduction says that "Each submitter is explicitly acknowledged". Do not strip the submitter records or SCV contributions from data you pass on as ClinVar's classifications.
  • Don't imply endorsement. See No endorsement.

items.title: No endorsement
items.text: ClinVar-GKM is not an NCBI, NLM or NIH product and is not endorsed by them. NCBI's Website Disclaimer says that "NCBI does not endorse or recommend any commercial products, processes, or services", and NLM's logo policy restricts use of its logo. ClinVar-GKM uses no NCBI or NLM logo. Products built on this data should likewise name ClinVar as a source without suggesting that NCBI, NLM, NIH or ClinGen endorses them.

items.title: Download the Latest Release
items.text:
The latest ClinVar-GKM release is available as a compressed JSON file (with Parquet files also available for analytical use):

Monthly full or weekly full?

clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz is the newest official monthly; it reflects the last release of the previous month — e.g. the 2026-10 monthly is built from the 2026-09-28 release, the last one before ClinVar's October monthly cut. For the current week, download weekly/clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz instead — see Weekly Full Bundles.

https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.1/

Download and decompress:

# Download the newest official monthly release
curl -O https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.1/clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz

# Or the newest weekly release
curl -O https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.1/weekly/clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz

# Decompress
gunzip clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz

See Data Access for the full release schedule, archives, and file naming conventions.

items.title: How to Read These Docs
items.text: These docs serve three kinds of reader. Some want to understand the data, often starting from what they already know of ClinVar's website. Some want to know how ClinVar's XML becomes this format. Some are building a pipeline or an application on top of it. Find yours below, follow its path as far as you need, and use the tab map to jump around.

items.title: The sections at a glance
items.text:
The site has six tabs, one per reader goal:

Tab What it gives you Read it when Home What ClinVar-GKM is and its key concepts, plus this guide, Data Use and Citation (the ClinVar disclaimer, how to cite, the license) and Stay Informed (the announcement list) You are new to the project, or about to use, publish or share the data Get the Data The files: monthly and weekly full bundles, weekly deltas, Parquet, and how releases work You need the data, or need to keep a copy current Understand the Data What each part of the bundle means: variations, SCV, VCV and RCV statements, ID references and annotated examples. Also the Data Model, every class and field generated from the schemas, and Mapping & Vocabularies, which maps ClinVar's statement types, classifications and review status You want to understand the data, or need exact field definitions Use the Data Query the Data (the 22 Parquet tables, a browser query console, joins, recipes and working at scale) and two end-to-end User Stories You want to work with the data in SQL, or see it used for a real task How It's Built Each step from ClinVar's XML to the published bundle You want to know how a value was produced Reference Versioning, Changelog, Release Validation, Known Issues, FAQ, Glossary and more You need what changed, what is guaranteed, or a definition

The tabs build on each other:

  • Get the Data delivers the files.
  • Understand the Data explains what is in them and defines every field exactly.
  • Use the Data offers the same content as tables you can query.
  • How It's Built explains how each value was derived from ClinVar.
  • Reference records what changes between releases and what each release guarantees.

items.title: Path 1: I know ClinVar's website and want to understand the data
items.text:
Everything on a ClinVar variation page has a place in the bundle. This table maps the pieces of the page you know to where they live, and to the page that explains each one.

On ClinVar's website In ClinVar-GKM Explained in A variation (VCV000012582) and its details: HGVS names, location, genes A variation record (clinvar:12582), a Cat-VRS categorical variant, defined by GA4GH VRS allele and location records Variations The Germline classification and its review status A vcv statement in the germline group, with its aggregate classification VCV Statements The Somatic clinical impact and oncogenicity classifications vcv statements in the somatic clinical impact and oncogenicity groups VCV Statements, Statement Types Each row of Submitted classifications (an SCV) An scv statement, which points to its submitter, its proposition and its evidence SCV Statements A classification for one condition (an RCV) An rcv statement RCV Statements The condition (a MedGen-linked trait) A condition, or a conditionSet when there are several Output Format Review status stars The statement's review status, which also sets its rank when submissions are aggregated Review Status "Pathogenic", "Drug response", and the other classification terms A classification on a typed proposition (for example VariantPathogenicityProposition) Classifications, Propositions

Suggested order: 1. The Key Concepts on Home. 2. Output Format, for how the bundle's sections fit together. 3. The statement pages, starting with SCV Statements. 4. The annotated Examples, to see one real variation end to end.

Keep the Glossary and the FAQ at hand. To explore without writing code, the query console runs SQL in your browser.

items.title: Path 2: I want to know how ClinVar's XML becomes this format
items.text:
The Pipeline Overview walks the whole release. ClinVar's XML is first loaded into relational BigQuery tables by the upstream clinvar-ingest pipeline and prepared by clinvar-ingest-bq-tools. ClinVar-GKM's stored procedures take over from there.

Suggested order: 1. Variation Identity and VRS Processing: how each variant gets its GA4GH VRS identity. 2. Cat-VRS: how a ClinVar variation becomes a categorical variant. 3. Conditions & Traits: how submitted conditions are matched to ClinVar's traits. 4. SCV Statements, then VCV Statements with their aggregation rules, then RCV Statements. 5. Export & Distribute: bundle assembly, weekly deltas, Parquet and publication.

When a value in the data surprises you, the matching pipeline step says where it came from. Mapping & Vocabularies records the mapping rules. Release Validation lists the checks every release passes before publication. Design decisions are recorded as ADRs, for example ADR 0007 on pipeline principles.

items.title: Path 3: I am building a pipeline or an application on this data
items.text:
Suggested order: 1. How Releases Work: monthly and weekly full bundles, weekly deltas, and how to keep a copy current. Then Weekly Deltas for applying a delta to a full bundle. 2. Versioning & Releases: what is guaranteed. 1.1.0 is the general-availability release; published files are immutable, and a breaking change opens a new major line. 3. Pick an interface: - JSON bundles: the Output Format, ID References for resolving #/section/id pointers, and the Data Model for exact fields and schemas. - Parquet: Query the Data, from the 22 tables and joins to working at scale and other tools. 4. The GA4GH libraries: the GKM Starter Kit (vrs-python, cat-vrs-python, va-spec-python and the GKM Toolkit) works directly on these bundles. See GA4GH Standards. 5. Worked problems: the User Stories, and Sub-Bundle Extraction for cutting a self-contained subset.

Before you depend on a release, check the Changelog for migration notes and Known Issues. The Release Validation page lists the checks behind each release.

items.title: Getting help and news

items.title: Stay Informed
items.text: ClinVar-GKM announces releases, version changes, and events on an email list, the Google Group clinvar-gkm@broadinstitute.org. Anyone can join, and you don't need a Broad Institute or GitHub account.

items.title: What the list announces
items.text:
• New releases. When a new version is ready (for example 1.1.0), with what changed and links to the Changelog and the downloads.
  • Version changes, in advance. Before any breaking change, the list carries the proposal (a Request for Comment) and its comment window. Before a republish into a new version line, it carries a notice with the switch-over date. See Versioning & Releases.
  • Corrections and known issues that affect published data. The current list is on Known Issues.
  • Events and presentations where ClinVar-GKM is featured, such as conference talks, workshops and webinars. Past decks are on Presentations.

items.title: Join the list
items.text:
With a Google account. A Google account can use any email address; it doesn't have to be Gmail.

  1. Open the group page: groups.google.com/a/broadinstitute.org/g/clinvar-gkm.
  2. Sign in, then select Join group.
  3. Choose how you receive messages: every email, a daily digest, or web only. Then confirm.

By email, without a Google account.

  1. Send an email, with any subject and body, to clinvar-gkm+subscribe@broadinstitute.org.
  2. Reply to, or follow the link in, the confirmation message that comes back.

To leave, select Leave group on the group page, or send an email to clinvar-gkm+unsubscribe@broadinstitute.org.

items.title: Other ways to follow along
items.text:
• Release feed: each version line publishes an Atom feed, for example https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.1/feed.xml, which any feed reader can follow. It lists every published release, including each weekly update.
  • GitHub: watch the repository. Choose Custom, then Releases and Discussions, to get tagged releases and change proposals.
  • Questions and feedback: GitHub Discussions for questions and ideas, and GitHub Issues for problems with the data.

items.title: User Story: Auditing a Submitter's ClinVar Footprint
items.text:
Why this matters

A lab that submits to ClinVar accumulates a large body of classifications over years — and it is easy to lose track of which ones have aged, slipped to a weak or flagged review status, or point at conditions and therapies that no longer look right. Because ClinVar-GKM republishes every ClinVar release as typed Parquet (and a self-contained bundle), a submitter can pull their own complete footprint and run a repeatable audit on every release — turning "is anything of ours stale or wrong?" into a query that produces a fresh report each time ClinVar updates.

At a glance

  • Implementer — a ClinVar submitting lab (worked example: the Institute for Genomic Medicine (IGM) Clinical Laboratory at Nationwide Children's Hospital, submitter 196472)
  • Products — VA-Spec, Cat-VRS, VRS, GKM-Core
  • Pattern — Submitter self-audit / QC across releases
  • Tools — DuckDB or pandas over the published Parquet; the sub-bundle extract; optionally va-spec-python
  • Status — Release candidate

New to GKM datasets?

The GA4GH GKM Starter Kit is the best place to get oriented — it collects the reference libraries, the GKM Toolkit for loading and exploring bundles, and other user stories showing how projects put GKM to work.

items.title: The challenge
items.text:
An active submitter can have hundreds to thousands of SCVs in ClinVar, submitted and re-evaluated over many years. Several quality questions are hard to answer from ClinVar's web UI or flat XML:

  • Which classifications are stale? Assertions last evaluated years ago may predate current criteria and warrant re-review.
  • Which sit at a weak or flagged review status? Submissions with no assertion criteria provided, no classification provided, or a flagged submission status stand out for cleanup.
  • Which point at odd conditions? Placeholder or non-specific traits ("not provided", "not specified") — or conditions that have since been remapped — are worth a look.
  • Which reference unusual therapies? For therapeutic-response submissions, a malformed or unexpected drug or drug combination is easy to miss one record at a time.

Answering these one variant at a time doesn't scale, and ClinVar offers no turnkey "export everything we submitted as a queryable table."

items.title: What GKM enables
items.text:
ClinVar-GKM makes the whole submission set queryable and self-describing:

  • Every SCV is a typed VA-Spec Statement with an explicit classification, a quality (the review status / star level), direction and strength, submitter contributions (each with a date and activity type), and a proposition linking the variant to a condition — or, for therapeutic response, to a therapy or therapy group.
  • The whole release is typed Parquet — one file per bundle section, each with an id, typed columns for the common fields, and the full JSON object — so filtering your SCVs and joining them to conditions, therapies, and variants is ordinary SQL.
  • Releases are dated and incremental. The Parquet dataset at v1/1.1/parquet/ is rebuilt from the newest release every week, so the same audit re-runs against each release and its results can be diffed over time.

items.title: The data
items.text:
To make this concrete, the repository ships nch-igm-bundle.json.gz — the complete GKM extract of one real submitter, the IGM Clinical Laboratory at Nationwide Children's Hospital (submitter 196472): all 2,443 of their SCVs plus every variation, condition, therapy, proposition, and submitter record those statements reference, in a single self-contained 1.6 MB file. It is exactly "everything one submitter has in ClinVar," and it is the shape an audit consumes. It was regenerated from the 2026-10-18 release with the maintainer sub-bundle tool — sub-bundle.py --submitter 196472 — so it carries the 1.1.0 proposition sections and schema_version 1.1.0, and it passes strict GA4GH gkm-toolkit validation (6,432 records, 0 failing).

For the recurring, release-over-release audit, a submitter works from the published Parquet instead. A single DuckDB query flags the records that need a second look:

-- Everything submitter 196472 has in ClinVar, flagged for review.
-- (scv.parquet, the four proposition*.parquet tables and condition.parquet
--  from v1/1.1/parquet/ — rebuilt from the newest release every week.)
WITH mine AS (
  SELECT
    s.id,
    s.classification.name AS classification,
    s.quality.name        AS review_status,
    cond.name             AS condition_name,
    (SELECT max(c.date)                        -- most recent evaluation
       FROM unnest(s.contributions) AS t(c)
      WHERE c.activityType = 'evaluated')      AS last_evaluated
  FROM 'scv.parquet' s
  JOIN read_parquet('proposition*.parquet') p ON s.proposition_id = p.id
  LEFT JOIN 'condition.parquet' cond          -- CASE keeps this an equi-join (fast); an AND in ON plans a nested loop
         ON cond.id = CASE WHEN p.object_type = 'condition' THEN p.object_id END
  WHERE list_contains(
          [c.contributor FOR c IN s.contributions],
          'clinvar.submitter:196472')
)
SELECT
  id, classification, review_status, condition_name, last_evaluated,
  last_evaluated < '2022-01-01'                        AS stale,
  review_status IN ('no assertion criteria provided',
                    'no classification provided',
                    'flagged submission')               AS weak_status,
  coalesce(lower(condition_name) IN ('not provided', 'not specified'), TRUE)
                                                        AS odd_condition
FROM mine
WHERE stale OR weak_status OR odd_condition
ORDER BY last_evaluated;

The column shapes follow the bundle's JSON field names; run DESCRIBE SELECT * FROM 'scv.parquet' to confirm them for a given release. The four proposition tables share one column schema, so read_parquet('proposition*.parquet') covers every SCV; a condition-set object (object_type = conditionSet) has no condition.parquet row and is flagged for a look. The same idea extends to therapies: filter the propositions on object_type IN ('therapy', 'therapyGroup') and join object_id to the therapy / therapyGroup tables (with condition_qualifier_id for the tumor type) to spot a malformed or unexpected drug or drug combination.

Because the Parquet dataset is rebuilt from every weekly release, running the query each week and diffing against the previous run's output turns the audit into a standing report — new stale rows, newly flagged statuses, and newly odd conditions surface on their own.

items.title: The tools used
items.text:
• DuckDB / pandas — query the published Parquet locally and build the audit report; DuckDB reads the .parquet files directly with no load step.
  • The clinvar-gkm Parquet — one typed file per bundle section, refreshed every release.
  • The sub-bundle tool (maintainers) — --submitter <id> extracts one submitter's entire footprint into a single portable bundle, as with nch-igm-bundle.json.gz.
  • va-spec-python — optionally load the flagged statements as typed VA-Spec models for deeper, programmatic checks.

items.title: How to explore this
items.text:
• Get the data — Parquet Files (the one Parquet dataset, at v1/1.1/parquet/).
  • See one submitter's whole footprint — open nch-igm-bundle.json.gz (2,443 SCVs, self-contained).
  • Understand review status — Review Status (the star levels the audit flags on).
  • Extract your own — maintainers can run the sub-bundle tool by --submitter; anyone can filter the Parquet by their submitter id as shown above.
  • See more GKM use cases — the GKM Starter Kit's user stories.

items.title: User Story: Harmonizing ClinVar by VRS Identity
items.text:
Why this matters

ClinVar is the largest public collection of expert interpretations linking genetic variants to health conditions. But using it alongside other resources has meant reconciling how each one describes a variant — HGVS strings, genomic coordinates, assembly versions — even when they mean the exact same change. ClinVar-GKM republishes ClinVar in the GA4GH Genomic Knowledge Model (GKM): every variant carries a computed VRS identifier — a content-based fingerprint that is identical wherever that same change appears — and every classification is a structured VA-Spec statement with its evidence and provenance attached. So you can look up a variant's ClinVar classifications by identity, and line ClinVar up against any other VRS-aware dataset, without translating coordinates.

At a glance

  • Implementer — ClinGen / ClinVar-GKM (a transformation of NCBI ClinVar)
  • Products — VRS, Cat-VRS, VA-Spec, GKM-Core
  • Pattern — Cross-source variant harmonization
  • Tools — vrs-python, va-spec-python, and the GKM Toolkit; the published clinvar-gkm bundle
  • Status — Release candidate

New to GKM datasets?

The GA4GH GKM Starter Kit is the best place to get oriented — it collects the reference libraries, the GKM Toolkit for loading and exploring bundles, and other user stories showing how projects put GKM to work. clinvar-gkm is one such producer.

items.title: The challenge
items.text: A lab or knowledgebase that wants to annotate its variants with ClinVar's classifications has to answer "is my variant the same variant ClinVar classified?" — a surprisingly hard question when the two sides use different HGVS transcripts, 0- vs 1-based coordinates, or different genome builds. Teams end up maintaining brittle normalization code just to join two tables, and the join silently misses variants whose descriptions don't line up. And once a match is found, ClinVar's flat XML says what the classification is but not, in a machine-actionable way, who made it, how, or against which method.

items.title: What GKM enables
items.text:
clinvar-gkm removes both frictions:

  • Identity, not description. Each ClinVar variant is represented as a Cat-VRS CategoricalVariant over one or more VRS alleles. The VRS allele id (ga4gh:VA.…) is a digest of the normalized sequence change, so the same change computed from any other source produces the same id — the join is an equality check, no coordinate math.
  • Structured knowledge with provenance. Each classification is a VA-Spec Statement asserting a Proposition (variant → condition) with its strength, review status, submitter Contributions, and citations — the same shape whether it came from a single submitter (SCV), a variant-level aggregate (VCV), or a condition-level aggregate (RCV).
  • One self-describing file. Everything is delivered as a bundle of named sections that reference each other by #/section/id pointers, so a variant, its classifications, conditions, and submitters are all reachable from one download.

items.title: The data
items.text:
Take the ClinVar expert-panel call on BRCA1 c.68_69del (a pathogenic frameshift). In the bundle it is a small connected graph — the classification statement points at a proposition, which points at the variant, which resolves down to a VRS allele:

// scv/  — the expert-panel classification statement
{
  "id": "clinvar.submission:SCV004101425.2",
  "type": "Statement",
  "classification": { "name": "Pathogenic", "primaryCoding": { "code": "pathogenic", "system": "ACMG Guidelines, 2015" } },
  "quality": { "conceptType": "Quality", "name": "expert panel" },
  "proposition": "#/propositionPathogenicity/SCV004101425-PATH",
  "contributions": [ { "contributor": "#/submitter/clinvar.submitter:509268", "activityType": "evaluated", "date": "2024-06-11" } ]
}

// propositionPathogenicity/  — what it asserts
{ "type": "VariantPathogenicityProposition", "predicate": "isCausalFor",
  "subject": "#/variation/clinvar:17662", "object": "#/condition/clinvar.trait:76328" }

// variation/  → allele/  → the VRS identity you can join on
{ "id": "clinvar:17662", "type": "CategoricalVariant", "members": [ "#/allele/ga4gh:VA.EE08XW4IpzeWhJAwComKOSmsPHTcP-1R" ] }

Any dataset that computes the same ga4gh:VA.EE08XW4IpzeWhJAwComKOSmsPHTcP-1R allele — a VCF annotation pipeline, gnomAD, another knowledgebase — matches this ClinVar classification exactly, and can then read its strength, review status, submitter, and condition straight from the bundle.

items.title: The tools used
items.text:
• vrs-python — compute the VRS allele id for your own variants to join against clinvar-gkm's allele section (GKM-Core + VRS).
  • va-spec-python — construct and validate the classification Statements / Propositions as typed Python models.
  • GKM Toolkit (ga4gh.gkm) — load a published bundle, follow #/… pointers, and export a connected slice, without writing the resolution yourself.
  • The clinvar-gkm bundle — the monthly full plus weekly deltas on Cloudflare R2.

items.title: How to explore this
items.text:
• Get the data — Downloads.
  • Understand the shape — Output Format and ID References (including a small resolve() helper for pointers).
  • Pull one variant's full graph — maintainers can use the Sub-Bundle Extraction tool to slice a self-contained example like the one above.
  • See more GKM use cases — the GKM Starter Kit's user stories.

items.title: Vendored DuckDB-Wasm runtime
items.text:
These files power the in-browser live query console (docs/assets/duckdb-console.html). They are vendored (committed to the repo) rather than loaded from a CDN so the docs site is self-contained and offline-capable — there is no runtime dependency on jsdelivr.

Version: @duckdb/duckdb-wasm@1.29.0 · Bundle: eh only (WebAssembly exception handling).

File Size What it is Source duckdb-eh.wasm ~34 MB DuckDB engine compiled to WASM (eh build; includes httpfs, parquet, json) dist/duckdb-eh.wasm from the npm package, verbatim duckdb-browser-eh.worker.js ~760 KB Web Worker that drives the engine (classic worker, self-contained) dist/duckdb-browser-eh.worker.js from the npm package, verbatim duckdb-browser.bundled.js ~220 KB The browser API (AsyncDuckDB, selectBundle, …) with its apache-arrow dependency inlined built locally with esbuild (see below)

items.title: Why only the eh bundle
items.text: DuckDB-Wasm ships three bundles: mvp, eh, and coi. coi needs cross-origin isolation (COOP/COEP headers) that GitHub Pages cannot set, so it is unusable here. eh (exception handling) is supported by every modern browser, so the mvp fallback buys almost nothing for +38 MB. We vendor eh only.

items.title: Why duckdb-browser.bundled.mjs is a local build
items.text:
The package's own dist/duckdb-browser.mjs has a bare import — import * as … from "apache-arrow" — which a browser cannot resolve without an import map or a bundler. So we bundle it into one self-contained ESM:

mkdir ddw-build && cd ddw-build
npm init -y
npm i @duckdb/duckdb-wasm@1.29.0
printf 'export * from "@duckdb/duckdb-wasm";\n' > entry.mjs
npx esbuild entry.mjs --bundle --format=esm --platform=browser --minify \
  --legal-comments=none --outfile=duckdb-browser.bundled.js
# then copy duckdb-browser.bundled.js here; copy the .wasm + .worker.js verbatim from node_modules/@duckdb/duckdb-wasm/dist/

The bundle is named .js (not .mjs) on purpose: GitHub Pages has served .mjs with a non-JavaScript MIME type, which breaks the ESM import. A .js module imported with import … works and is served as text/javascript reliably.

The .wasm and .worker.js are copied verbatim from the same package version — do not re-minify them.

items.title: Upgrading
items.text: Bump the version in the commands above, rebuild all three files together (they must come from the same version), and smoke-test the console in a browser (counts, DESCRIBE, a remote query, an error) before committing. Git LFS is not an option — GitHub Pages serves the LFS pointer, not the file, so these stay as plain committed blobs.

items.title: Data Access
items.text: ClinVar-GKM is distributed as official monthly full bundles, weekly full bundles and weekly deltas, synchronized with ClinVar's XML releases and laid out like NCBI's ClinVar XML folder. Each is a gzip-compressed JSON file. One typed Parquet dataset (one file per section) is published for the latest release: it is derived from the bundle and overwritten each release. The files are freely available for download from Cloudflare R2 object storage with no authentication required and no egress fees.

items.title: Latest Release
items.text:
Monthly full or weekly full?

clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz is the newest official monthly; it reflects the last release of the previous month — e.g. the 2026-10 monthly is built from the 2026-09-28 release, the last one before ClinVar's October monthly cut. For the current week, download the newest weekly full, weekly/clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz.

Download the newest official monthly and the newest weekly full:

curl -O https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.1/clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz
curl -O https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.1/weekly/clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz

The full bundle is a single JSON object containing all bundle sections — variations, statements, propositions, conditions, and supporting reference data. A delta uses the same section structure but carries only the records added or updated since its baseline release. The Parquet dataset (one file per section) is derived from the bundle, published at v1/1.1/parquet/ and overwritten every release. See Output Format for the complete structure, Weekly Deltas for the replay model, and Parquet Files for the full Parquet list.

items.title: Release Schedule
items.text:
• Weekly releases: for every ClinVar weekly release, a weekly full bundle in weekly/ and a delta in deltas/. weekly/ keeps the current month only
  • Official monthly full bundles are published once a month at the top of the line folder, aligned to ClinVar's own monthly VCV releases — each ClinVarVCVRelease_YYYY-MM triggers our clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MM full, built from the most recent weekly release before ClinVar's monthly cut (its source_release)
  • At the start of each month, the previous month's deltas move to deltas/YYYY-MM/ and its weekly fulls are deleted (the last one once the new month's monthly is published)
  • At the start of each year, the previous year's monthlies and deltas move to archive/YYYY/
  • The Parquet dataset (parquet/) is rebuilt and overwritten from every release

The stable filenames clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz (official monthly) and weekly/clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz (weekly full) always point to the newest of each.

items.title: Directory Structure
items.text:
All paths are under the current line folder, v1/1.1/ (see Downloads for the version folders):

clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz                newest official monthly full
clinvar-gkm_yyyy-mm.json.gz                  official monthly fulls (current year)

weekly/
  clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz       newest weekly full
  clinvar-gkm_yyyy-mmdd.json.gz              weekly fulls (current month only)

deltas/
  clinvar-gkm-delta_yyyy-mmdd.json.gz        weekly delta bundles (current month; added + updated records)
  clinvar-gkm-delta_yyyy-mmdd.manifest.json  per-release change manifest
  yyyy-mm/                                   earlier months of the current year

archive/yyyy/
  clinvar-gkm_yyyy-mm.json.gz                monthly fulls from prior years
  deltas/yyyy-mm/                            deltas from prior years

parquet/
  {section}.parquet                          the one Parquet dataset (derived; overwritten every release)
  manifest.json                              build date, source release, builder, per-file sha256

Every bundle has a <file>.sha256 sidecar.

items.title: Release Notes
items.text: Pipeline changes that affect the structure or content of the output are recorded in the Changelog, and each tagged release is listed on GitHub Releases. They cover changes specific to the ClinVar-GKM pipeline and do not replicate ClinVar's own release notes.

items.title: File Format
items.text:
The primary release format is a gzip-compressed JSON file (.json.gz). Typed Parquet files (one per bundle section) are derived from the bundle for analytical use; only one dataset, for the latest release, is published. The decompressed JSON content is a single JSON object with bundle sections at the root level:

{
  "sequenceReference": { ... },
  "location": { ... },
  "allele": { ... },
  "copyNumberCount": { ... },
  "copyNumberChange": { ... },
  "gene": { ... },
  "variation": { ... },
  "condition": { ... },
  "conditionSet": { ... },
  "therapy": { ... },
  "therapyGroup": { ... },
  "submitter": { ... },
  "propositionPathogenicity": { ... },
  "propositionOncogenicity": { ... },
  "propositionSomaticClinicalImpact": { ... },
  "propositionClinvarCustom": { ... },
  "evidenceLine": { ... },
  "scv": { ... },
  "vcv": { ... },
  "rcv": { ... }
}

Each section is a keyed collection — the key is the object's unique identifier, and the value is the complete object. Objects reference each other using #/ JSON pointer strings. SCV, VCV and RCV evidence lines share the one evidenceLine section; only the Parquet keeps them in separate tables (evidenceLine, vcv_evidenceLine, rcv_evidenceLine).

See Output Format for detailed documentation of each section.

items.title: What's Next
items.text:
• Output Format — the bundle structure and reference patterns
  • Examples — annotated sample records from each section
  • Pipeline Overview — how the data is produced from ClinVar XML

items.title: Downloads
items.text:
ClinVar-GKM is distributed as monthly and weekly full bundles plus weekly deltas (JSON), with one typed Parquet dataset of the latest release, free from Cloudflare R2 — no authentication, no egress fees. The layout follows NCBI's ClinVar FTP site. New here? See How Releases Work.

1.1.0 moved every download URL

1.1.0 (released 2026-10-22) moved every download URL to v1/1.1/ and renamed the proposition sections — see the changelog migration notes.

Before you use or share the data

These files carry ClinVar data from NCBI. ClinVar's disclaimer applies: the data is not for direct diagnostic use or medical decision-making without review by a genetics professional. Attribute ClinVar as the data source, cite ClinVar-GKM, and carry the attribution and disclaimer with any copy you redistribute. The CC0 dedication covers ClinGen's transformation only. See Data Use and Citation.

items.title: Latest Release
items.text:
Monthly full or weekly full?

clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz is the newest official monthly: it reflects the last release of the previous month — e.g. the 2026-10 monthly is built from the 2026-09-28 release, the last one before ClinVar's October monthly cut. For the current week, download weekly/clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz, a full bundle of the newest release. See Weekly Full Bundles.

The interactive release table needs JavaScript. Without it, fetch the release index directly: <code>curl -s https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.1/index.json | python3 -m json.tool</code> — or grab the newest monthly and weekly fulls: <code>curl -O https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.1/clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz</code> <code>curl -O https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.1/weekly/clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz</code>

Browse history and archives: Monthly Full Bundles · Weekly Full Bundles · Weekly Deltas · Parquet Files.

items.title: Directory Structure
items.text:
Versioned layout

The root index.json is a thin version manifest that lists the release lines and points to each line's index. Each line has its own folder, v{major}/{major}.{minor}/. The current line is 1.1, served under v1/1.1/, with its release index at v1/1.1/index.json. PATCH releases (1.1.x) add to the same folder; a new MINOR starts v1/1.2/ and a new MAJOR starts v2/2.0/. A replaced line is frozen and kept indefinitely: its files stay, unchanged. The 1.0.1 generation is the frozen line v1/1.0/.

index.json                                    version manifest (each line -> its index)
v1/
  1.1/                                        current line
    index.json                                release index for the line
    feed.xml                                  Atom feed of the line's releases
    README.txt                                plain-text guide to the line
    clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz             newest official monthly full (stable URL)
    clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MM.json.gz               official monthly fulls, current year
    weekly/
      clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz    newest weekly full (stable URL)
      clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MMDD.json.gz           weekly fulls, CURRENT MONTH ONLY
    deltas/
      clinvar-gkm-delta_YYYY-MMDD.json.gz     current month's weekly deltas
      clinvar-gkm-delta_YYYY-MMDD.manifest.json
      YYYY-MM/                                earlier months of the current year
    archive/
      YYYY/
        clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MM.json.gz           monthly fulls from prior years
        deltas/YYYY-MM/                       deltas from prior years
    parquet/
      {section}.parquet                       ONE Parquet dataset, the latest (derived; overwritten every release)
      manifest.json                           build date, source release, builder, per-file sha256
  1.0/                                        frozen line: the 1.0.1 generation (bundles, delta manifests, MANIFEST.json; no Parquet)

Every bundle has a <file>.sha256 sidecar (sha256sum -c format), like NCBI's .md5 files.

items.title: When files move
items.text:
• New month. When the first release of a new month is published, the finished month's deltas move from deltas/ into deltas/YYYY-MM/, and the finished month's weekly fulls are deleted. The newest of them is kept until the new month's official monthly is published, because that monthly is normally a copy of it, and is deleted as soon as the monthly is up. A past week is rebuilt from a monthly plus deltas; see Rebuild a past week.
  • New year. When the first release of a new year is published, the finished year's monthlies move into archive/YYYY/ and its delta folders into archive/YYYY/deltas/YYYY-MM/.
  • A move never changes a file's bytes, name or checksum, only its folder. Scripts that need a dated file should look up its current path in the line's index.json.

items.title: How the layout mirrors NCBI
items.text:
The bundles are built from ClinVar's XML releases, so the layout follows NCBI's ClinVar XML folder:

NCBI ClinVar XML ClinVar-GKM v1/1.1/ xml/ — monthly releases and ClinVarVCVRelease_00-latest.xml.gz top level — official monthlies and clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz xml/weekly_release/ — the current month's weekly releases and 00-latest_weekly weekly/ — the current month's weekly fulls and clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz xml/archive/YYYY/ — monthly releases of prior years archive/YYYY/ — monthlies of prior years .md5 sidecars .sha256 sidecars — deltas/ — weekly deltas (ClinVar-GKM only) — parquet/ — one derived Parquet dataset (ClinVar-GKM only)

Each ClinVar-GKM monthly clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MM lines up with ClinVar's ClinVarVCVRelease_YYYY-MM, and each weekly full or delta with the ClinVar weekly release of the same date.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
• HTTP 403. The CDN serves only the root index.json and paths under /v1/; a path allowlist answers every other path with 403, not 404. A 403 usually means a URL from before the current layout, such as a bucket-root datasets/… path. Look up the file's current path in the line's index.json.
  • HTTP 404 under /v1/. The file is not there: a weekly full deleted at month end, a delta moved to deltas/YYYY-MM/, or a monthly moved to archive/YYYY/. See When files move.
  • HTTP 429. Requests are rate-limited. Download whole files and query them locally rather than issuing many small range requests.
