items.title: Monthly Full Bundles
items.text:
Links: Weekly Full Bundles · Weekly Deltas · Parquet Files · How Releases Work

The official monthly full bundle is a gzip-compressed JSON file containing every variation, statement, proposition, condition, and supporting reference record for a release. It lines up with ClinVar's monthly ClinVarVCVRelease_YYYY-MM: clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MM is built from the newest weekly release before ClinVar's monthly cut, and the line's index.json names that release as the monthly's source_release. For example, the 2026-10 monthly has source_release 2026-09-28.

The monthlies of the current year sit at the top of the line folder, v1/1.1/; clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz is a stable URL for the newest one. When the first release of a new year is published, the finished year's monthlies move to v1/1.1/archive/YYYY/, where they are kept. Monthlies and deltas are the durable record: every past week can be rebuilt from them (Rebuild a past week).

Prerequisites

The curl recipe needs only a shell. The Python recipe uses Python 3 and only the standard library. New to Python? Install it from python.org/downloads or your OS package manager.

Download a monthly full with curl 
# Newest official monthly full (stable URL)
curl -O https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.1/clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz

# Or a specific month of the current year, with its checksum
curl -O https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.1/clinvar-gkm_2026-10.json.gz
curl -O https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.1/clinvar-gkm_2026-10.json.gz.sha256
sha256sum -c clinvar-gkm_2026-10.json.gz.sha256      # macOS: shasum -a 256 -c

# Decompress
gunzip clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz
Download a monthly full with Python 
import urllib.request

BASE = "https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.1"

# Download the newest official monthly full bundle
urllib.request.urlretrieve(
    f"{BASE}/clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz",
    "clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz"
)

# Download a specific monthly of the current year
urllib.request.urlretrieve(
    f"{BASE}/clinvar-gkm_2026-10.json.gz",
    "clinvar-gkm_2026-10.json.gz"
)

# A prior year's monthly is under archive/YYYY/ (2026's monthlies move there when the first
# release of 2027 is published)
urllib.request.urlretrieve(
    f"{BASE}/archive/2026/clinvar-gkm_2026-07.json.gz",
    "clinvar-gkm_2026-07.json.gz"
)

Validate a downloaded bundle

Every JSON bundle conforms to the ClinVar-GKM bundle schema (JSON Schema Draft 2020-12) — the same schema covers the monthly full, weekly deltas, and sub-bundle extracts. The GKM Toolkit validates a bundle against it in one call.

items.title: Output File
items.text: ClinVar-GKM is published as gzip-compressed JSON files in the bundle format — a monthly full bundle and weekly full bundles containing all data for a release, plus a weekly delta carrying only the records changed since the prior release. For analytical workloads, one set of typed Parquet files (one per bundle section) is derived from the newest release, published under v1/1.1/parquet/ and rebuilt every release; deltas have no Parquet. See Parquet Files.

items.title: File Format
items.text:
The release file is a .json.gz file. The decompressed content is a single JSON object with named bundle sections at the root level — each section is a keyed collection of objects of the same class.

# Decompress and inspect the top-level keys
gunzip -c clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz | python3 -c "
import json, sys
data = json.load(sys.stdin)
for key in data:
    print(f'{key}: {len(data[key]):,} entries')
"

See Output Format for the full bundle structure, section inventory, and reference patterns.

items.title: Latest Release
items.text:
Monthly full or weekly full?

clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz reflects the last release of the previous month — e.g. the 2026-10 monthly is built from the 2026-09-28 release, the last one before ClinVar's October monthly cut. For the current week, use clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz — see Weekly Full Bundles.

Stable filenames that always point to the newest official monthly and the newest weekly full:

clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz               (newest official monthly)
weekly/clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz (newest weekly full)

The 00- prefix ensures these sort before dated files in directory listings, as in NCBI's ClinVarVCVRelease_00-latest.xml.gz.

items.title: Monthly Full Bundles
items.text:
Official monthly full bundles include the year and month:

clinvar-gkm_yyyy-mm.json.gz                 (current year, at the top of the line folder)
archive/yyyy/clinvar-gkm_yyyy-mm.json.gz    (prior years)

For example, clinvar-gkm_2026-10.json.gz for ClinVar's October 2026 monthly release.

items.title: Weekly Full Bundles
items.text:
Weekly full bundles include the ClinVar release year, month, and day, and are kept for the current month only:

weekly/clinvar-gkm_yyyy-mmdd.json.gz

For example, weekly/clinvar-gkm_2026-1018.json.gz for the October 18, 2026 release.

items.title: Weekly Deltas
items.text:
Each weekly delta is a bundle and a manifest named with the ClinVar release year, month, and day:

deltas/clinvar-gkm-delta_yyyy-mmdd.json.gz          (current month)
deltas/clinvar-gkm-delta_yyyy-mmdd.manifest.json
deltas/yyyy-mm/clinvar-gkm-delta_yyyy-mmdd.*        (earlier months of the current year)
archive/yyyy/deltas/yyyy-mm/clinvar-gkm-delta_*     (prior years)

For example, deltas/clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1018.json.gz for the October 18, 2026 release, which moves to deltas/2026-10/ when November's first release is published. The delta bundle carries only added and updated records; deletes and per-section change counts are recorded in the accompanying manifest. See Weekly Deltas for the delta model and replay recipe.

Every bundle has a <file>.sha256 sidecar. All paths are relative to the line folder, https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.1/.

items.title: Python
items.text:
import gzip
import json

with gzip.open('clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz', 'rt') as f:
    bundle = json.load(f)

# Look up a specific variation
variant = bundle['variation']['clinvar:10']
print(variant['name'])

# Resolve a reference
allele_ref = variant['members'][0]  # e.g., "#/allele/ga4gh:VA.abc123"
section, key = allele_ref.lstrip('#/').split('/', 1)
allele = bundle[section][key]

items.title: Command Line
items.text:
# Count entries per section
gunzip -c clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz | python3 -c "
import json, sys
data = json.load(sys.stdin)
for key in data:
    print(f'{key}: {len(data[key]):,}')
"

# Extract a single variation as pretty-printed JSON
gunzip -c clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz | python3 -c "
import json, sys
data = json.load(sys.stdin)
print(json.dumps(data['variation']['clinvar:10'], indent=2))
"

items.title: Sections Included
items.text:
Each release file contains the following bundle sections:

Section Content sequenceReference VRS reference sequences with refget accessions location VRS sequence locations with coordinates allele VRS alleles with state and expressions copyNumberCount Copy number count variants copyNumberChange Copy number change variants gene Gene MappableConcepts variation Cat-VRS categorical variants condition Trait and disease concepts conditionSet Multi-condition groupings therapy Drug therapies (content-addressed, referenced by therapeutic propositions) therapyGroup Combination (multi-drug) therapy groups submitter Submitting organizations propositionPathogenicity Pathogenicity propositions (germline; SCV, VCV, RCV) propositionOncogenicity Oncogenicity propositions (SCV, VCV, RCV) propositionSomaticClinicalImpact Somatic clinical impact propositions: Clinical Significance (SCV, VCV, RCV), and the Diagnostic, Prognostic and Therapeutic Response propositions that SCV evidence lines target propositionClinvarCustom ClinVar custom propositions: the 9 Clinvar* types plus ClinvarUndefinedProposition (SCV, VCV, RCV) evidenceLine Evidence lines (SCV, VCV, and RCV) scv Submitted classification statements vcv Variation-level aggregate statements rcv Condition-level aggregate statements

See Data Model for class descriptions and relationship diagrams.

items.title: Parquet Files
items.text:
Links: Monthly Full Bundles · Weekly Full Bundles · Weekly Deltas · How Releases Work

Want to query the files, not just download them?

This page covers where the Parquet files live and how to keep a set current. Query the Data teaches querying them: a live in-browser console, every table's columns, how the tables join, and runnable recipes.

Parquet is derived from the bundle and overwritten every release

The JSON bundles are the release record. Parquet is a convenience: every value in it can be recomputed from the bundle. One Parquet dataset is published, rebuilt every release (weekly) from the newest weekly release and overwritten in place. There are no dated, per-delta or archived Parquet sets.

The dataset lives at one stable path, v1/1.1/parquet/, one file per section, with a manifest.json beside it:

v1/1.1/parquet/
  {section}.parquet      22 files, one per bundle section
  manifest.json          build date, source release and dataset, builder, schema version, each file's size and sha256

The manifest names the release the dataset was built from, so check it before comparing results with a bundle (the index's Parquet entry carries the same source_release). For an earlier state, see Earlier releases.

items.title: Available Parquet files
items.text:
Each Parquet file contains one bundle section with typed, query-friendly columns extracted from the JSON objects. Nearly every section includes an id column (the object identifier) and a data column (the full JSON object as a string), plus additional typed columns for key fields — enabling efficient filtering and aggregation without parsing JSON. The exception: therapy and therapyGroup name the id column key and hold the JSON object in value. Before 1.1.0, condition had no data column and therapy / therapyGroup had only key and value. The column reference lists every column of every section.

Available Parquet files (22 sections):

File Description sequenceReference.parquet NCBI RefSeq sequence references location.parquet VRS SequenceLocation records allele.parquet VRS Allele records copyNumberCount.parquet VRS CopyNumberCount records copyNumberChange.parquet VRS CopyNumberChange records gene.parquet Gene records (MappableConcept with NCBI Gene / HGNC codings) variation.parquet CategoricalVariant records (Cat-VRS) condition.parquet Condition records (traits) conditionSet.parquet ConditionSet records (trait sets) therapy.parquet Therapy records (drug therapies, content-addressed) therapyGroup.parquet TherapyGroup records (combination therapies) submitter.parquet Submitter organization records propositionPathogenicity.parquet Pathogenicity propositions propositionOncogenicity.parquet Oncogenicity propositions propositionSomaticClinicalImpact.parquet Somatic clinical impact propositions (ClinicalSignificance, and the Diagnostic, Prognostic and TherapeuticResponse targets of SCI evidence lines) propositionClinvarCustom.parquet ClinVar custom propositions (the Clinvar* types) evidenceLine.parquet SCV evidence line records vcv_evidenceLine.parquet VCV evidence line records rcv_evidenceLine.parquet RCV evidence line records scv.parquet SCV statement records vcv.parquet VCV aggregate statement records rcv.parquet RCV aggregate statement records

items.title: Working with Parquet Files
items.text:
Download the Parquet files you need, then query them locally. The R2 hosting has rate limits and is designed for file downloads, not as a remote query endpoint for tools like DuckDB.

Prerequisites

The examples below use the DuckDB CLI and/or Python with pandas + pyarrow (pip install pandas pyarrow). If you don't already have these tools, install them from the linked pages first — each subsection also shows its own one-line install command.

items.title: Download
items.text:
Download individual sections or all files at once:

Download sections with curl 
# The one published Parquet dataset, overwritten every release; manifest.json names its release.
BASE="https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.1/parquet"
mkdir -p clinvar-gkm-parquet && cd clinvar-gkm-parquet
curl -O "${BASE}/manifest.json"

# Download specific sections
curl -O "${BASE}/scv.parquet"
curl -O "${BASE}/propositionPathogenicity.parquet"
curl -O "${BASE}/condition.parquet"

# Or download all 22 sections
for section in sequenceReference location allele copyNumberCount copyNumberChange \
               gene variation condition conditionSet therapy therapyGroup submitter \
               propositionPathogenicity propositionOncogenicity propositionSomaticClinicalImpact propositionClinvarCustom \
               evidenceLine vcv_evidenceLine rcv_evidenceLine \
               scv vcv rcv; do
  curl -O "${BASE}/${section}.parquet"
done

items.title: Query
items.text:
DuckDB is the fastest way to explore Parquet files — it queries them directly with no data loading step. pandas + pyarrow works well when you want DataFrames.

Query with DuckDB / pandas 
# Install DuckDB
brew install duckdb   # macOS
# or: pip install duckdb

# Query SCV statements
duckdb -c "
  SELECT id, classification.name AS classification, direction, strength.name AS strength, quality.name AS quality
  FROM 'scv.parquet'
  WHERE classification.name = 'Pathogenic'
  LIMIT 10;
"

# Count classifications across all SCVs
duckdb -c "
  SELECT classification.name AS classification, direction, COUNT(*) as n
  FROM 'scv.parquet'
  GROUP BY classification.name, direction
  ORDER BY n DESC;
"

# Join SCVs with propositions to find pathogenic variants for a specific condition
duckdb -c "
  SELECT s.id, s.classification.name AS classification, p.predicate, p.object_id
  FROM 'scv.parquet' s
  JOIN 'propositionPathogenicity.parquet' p ON s.proposition_id = p.id
  WHERE s.classification.name = 'Pathogenic'
    AND p.object_id = 'clinvar.trait:9580'
  LIMIT 10;
"

# Inspect the schema of any section
duckdb -c "DESCRIBE SELECT * FROM 'scv.parquet';"

DuckDB also works from Python:

import duckdb

df = duckdb.sql("""
    SELECT id, classification.name AS classification, direction, strength.name AS strength, quality.name AS quality
    FROM 'scv.parquet'
    WHERE classification.name = 'Pathogenic'
    LIMIT 100
""").df()

print(df)

With pandas / pyarrow:

import pandas as pd

# Load a section into a DataFrame
scv = pd.read_parquet("scv.parquet")

# Filter pathogenic SCVs — classification is a MappableConcept struct (dict), so read .name
pathogenic = scv[scv["classification"].map(lambda c: c and c.get("name")) == "Pathogenic"]
print(f"{len(pathogenic)} pathogenic SCVs")

# Access the full JSON when you need nested fields
import json
record = json.loads(pathogenic.iloc[0]["data"])
print(record["proposition"])

items.title: Column Reference
items.text:
The complete per-table reference — every column, type and description for all 22 sections — is in Query the Data → The 22 Tables. A summary:

Statement sections (scv, vcv, rcv) share a common set of typed columns:

Column Type Description id string Statement identifier type string Statement type proposition_id string FK to the matching proposition Parquet — one of propositionPathogenicity, propositionOncogenicity, propositionSomaticClinicalImpact, propositionClinvarCustom, by the proposition's type; read_parquet('proposition*.parquet') covers all four classification struct (MappableConcept) Use classification.name (or classification.primaryCoding.code) — e.g., "Pathogenic" strength struct (MappableConcept) Use strength.name — e.g., "definitive", "likely" direction string Evidence direction ("supports", "disputes", "neutral") quality struct (MappableConcept) Use quality.name — submission level, e.g., "criteria provided" has_evidence_lines list\<string> FK references to evidence line Parquet (evidenceLine for SCV, vcv_evidenceLine for VCV, rcv_evidenceLine for RCV) extensions string JSON array of extensions data string Full JSON object

SCV statements include additional columns: description, contributions, reportedIn and specifiedBy. reportedIn is a list of citation Documents, one per ClinVar citation, and specifiedBy.reportedIn is the assertion method's Document. From 1.1.0 each Document also has name, documentType and extensions; see scv.

The four proposition tables share one column schema (from 1.1.0): id, type, predicate, subject_variant_id, object_id, object_type, condition_qualifier_id, gene_context_id, gene_context_name, submitted_gene_symbols, gene_context_source, mode_of_inheritance, penetrance and data, so read_parquet('proposition*.parquet') reads them as one table. This enables JOINs across statements, variants, and conditions without parsing JSON. See Gene context for what the gene context is (one representative gene per variant, not a submitter-asserted gene), and The shared columns for each column.

Run DESCRIBE in DuckDB to see the full schema for any section.

These examples demonstrate cross-section JOINs using typed columns. Most analytical queries can be answered without parsing JSON — the proposition's gene_context_name column carries the gene symbol directly, and the condition's primaryCoding struct carries the MedGen code. (These queries join scv.parquet to propositionPathogenicity.parquet; swap in read_parquet('proposition*.parquet') to include every kind of claim, since the four tables have the same columns.)

For how the sections join — including the columns that point at more than one table, where a single-table join silently drops rows — see Joining Tables; for task-oriented queries, see Recipes.

Example cross-section queries (SQL)

All SCVs for a gene — detailed view:

-- SCVs for BRCA1: classification, review status, condition
SELECT
    s.id AS scv_id,
    s.classification.name AS classification,
    s.direction,
    s.strength.name AS strength,
    s.quality.name AS review_status,
    p.gene_context_name AS gene,
    c.name AS condition_name,
    c.primaryCoding.code AS condition_code
FROM 'scv.parquet' s
JOIN 'propositionPathogenicity.parquet' p ON s.proposition_id = p.id
LEFT JOIN 'condition.parquet' c ON p.object_id = c.id
WHERE p.gene_context_name = 'BRCA1'
ORDER BY s.classification.name;

Classification summary for a gene:

-- Count SCVs by classification and review status for BRCA2
SELECT
    p.gene_context_name AS gene,
    s.classification.name AS classification,
    s.quality.name AS review_status,
    s.direction,
    COUNT(*) AS scv_count
FROM 'scv.parquet' s
JOIN 'propositionPathogenicity.parquet' p ON s.proposition_id = p.id
WHERE p.gene_context_name = 'BRCA2'
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY scv_count DESC;

Restrict to submissions with criteria provided:

-- Only expert panel and criteria-provided SCVs for a gene
SELECT
    s.id AS scv_id,
    s.classification.name AS classification,
    s.quality.name AS review_status,
    c.name AS condition_name
FROM 'scv.parquet' s
JOIN 'propositionPathogenicity.parquet' p ON s.proposition_id = p.id
LEFT JOIN 'condition.parquet' c ON p.object_id = c.id
WHERE p.gene_context_name = 'TP53'
  AND s.quality.name IN ('criteria provided', 'reviewed by expert panel')
ORDER BY s.classification.name;

Cross-gene comparison — classification breakdown for multiple genes:

-- Compare pathogenicity classification distributions across genes
SELECT
    p.gene_context_name AS gene,
    s.classification.name AS classification,
    COUNT(*) AS n
FROM 'scv.parquet' s
JOIN 'propositionPathogenicity.parquet' p ON s.proposition_id = p.id
WHERE p.gene_context_name IN ('BRCA1', 'BRCA2', 'TP53', 'MLH1')
  AND s.quality.name = 'criteria provided'
GROUP BY gene, s.classification.name
ORDER BY gene, n DESC;

Accessing fields not in typed columns — some fields, like submitter names, HGVS expressions, and assertion methods, are only available in the data column (full JSON string). Use DuckDB's json_extract_string to access them:

-- SCVs with submitter name and assertion method (from JSON)
SELECT
    s.id AS scv_id,
    s.classification.name AS classification,
    p.gene_context_name AS gene,
    json_extract_string(s.data, '$.contributions[0].agent.name') AS submitter,
    json_extract_string(s.data, '$.specifiedBy.name') AS method
FROM 'scv.parquet' s
JOIN 'propositionPathogenicity.parquet' p ON s.proposition_id = p.id
WHERE p.gene_context_name = 'BRCA1'
  AND s.classification.name = 'Pathogenic'
  AND s.quality.name = 'reviewed by expert panel'
LIMIT 20;

When to use each access path:

Approach Best for Tradeoff Typed columns only Filtering, counting, grouping, JOINs on classification, gene, condition, review status Fast; covers most analytical questions Typed columns + json_extract_string Ad-hoc queries needing submitter names, HGVS, methods Slightly slower; syntax is verbose Parse data column in application code Bulk processing needing many nested fields Full flexibility; requires application-side JSON parsing

items.title: Earlier releases
items.text:
Only the current Parquet dataset is published; it is overwritten every release, and weekly deltas, archives and frozen lines carry no Parquet. To work with an earlier state:

  • Rebuild it from the bundles. Every official monthly stays published (in archive/YYYY/ after its year ends) with a .sha256 sidecar, and so does every delta. Rebuild the bundle for the week you need with the replay recipe, then read the sections you need.
  • Convert a bundle to Parquet with clinvar-gkm-parquet (planned). clinvar-gkm-parquet is a separate, versioned tool that builds this Parquet layout from a published bundle and writes the same manifest.json. It is in design and not yet released; until it is, earlier Parquet can't be downloaded or rebuilt in this layout.
  • The 1.0.1 generation is the frozen line v1/1.0/: its bundles and delta manifests, with no Parquet.

Parquet downloaded from an earlier release keeps its old tables and columns; see the changelog for what changed.

items.title: How Releases Work
items.text:
Links: Monthly Full Bundles · Weekly Full Bundles · Weekly Deltas · Parquet Files

ClinVar-GKM releases are hosted on Cloudflare R2 object storage. All downloads are free with no authentication required and no egress fees. The layout follows NCBI's ClinVar XML folder, with monthlies at the top, weekly/ and archive/YYYY/; see How the layout mirrors NCBI.

Distribution follows a full + delta model:

  • An official monthly full bundle — a gzip-compressed JSON file — is published once a month, lined up with ClinVar's monthly release. It contains every variation, statement, proposition, condition, and supporting reference record.
  • A weekly full bundle is published for every ClinVar weekly release, and kept for the current month only.
  • A weekly delta is published for every ClinVar weekly release. Each delta carries only the records that were added or updated since the prior release, in the same section structure as the full bundle, alongside a manifest that lists per-section adds, updates, and deletes.

The monthlies and the deltas are the durable record. A consumer that wants the state at any week takes a monthly full and replays the deltas after it; see Rebuild a past week and the manifest field reference.

The official monthly is a month-start baseline, not the current week

clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz reflects the last release of the previous month — e.g. the 2026-10 monthly is built from the 2026-09-28 release, the last one before ClinVar's October monthly cut. For the current week, use the newest weekly full, or replay the deltas onto the monthly.

items.title: Release Cadence
items.text:
A weekly release is published for every ClinVar XML release, typically within 1-2 days of it. It writes the weekly full weekly/clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MMDD.json.gz, refreshes weekly/clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz, and writes the delta deltas/clinvar-gkm-delta_YYYY-MMDD.json.gz with its manifest. All paths are under the line folder, v1/1.1/.

An official monthly full is published once a month, lined up with ClinVar's monthly VCV release. When ClinVar posts ClinVarVCVRelease_YYYY-MM.xml.gz at its XML index (early in month YYYY-MM), our clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MM full is built from the most recent weekly release before ClinVar's monthly cut datetime — so e.g. the 2026-07 monthly comes from the 2026-06-27 release. That release is published as the monthly's source_release in index.json. The upload writes clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MM.json.gz and refreshes the clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz pointer. Each delta manifest's checkpoint_full names the official monthly that precedes the delta.

Every bundle has a .sha256 checksum sidecar. From 1.1.0, a monthly or delta file is never rewritten; see the exceptions below.

items.title: Month and Year Rollover
items.text:
When What happens The first release of a new month is published The finished month's deltas move from deltas/ into deltas/YYYY-MM/. The finished month's weekly fulls are deleted, as NCBI deletes its weekly releases, except the newest: it is kept until the new month's official monthly is published (the monthly is normally a copy of it), then deleted. The first release of a new year is published The finished year's monthlies move into archive/YYYY/, and its delta folders into archive/YYYY/deltas/YYYY-MM/.

A move changes a file's folder, never its bytes, name or checksum. Deleting the weekly fulls is the one deliberate exception to "published bundles are never removed": every deleted week can be rebuilt exactly from a monthly plus deltas (Rebuild a past week).

items.title: Parquet
items.text: Parquet is derived from the bundle. One Parquet dataset is published, at v1/1.1/parquet/, rebuilt from the newest weekly release and overwritten every release. Its manifest.json gives the build date, the release and dataset it was built from, the builder, the schema version, and every file's size and sha256. No Parquet is kept per month, per delta, in archive/ or in frozen lines. Past Parquet is rebuilt from the monthly bundles with clinvar-gkm-parquet, a separate tool that is planned but not yet released. See Parquet Files.

items.title: Version Lines
items.text: Each version line has its own folder: v1/1.1/ for 1.1.x. A PATCH release (1.1.x) only adds new dated files to v1/1.1/. A new MINOR — including a content-only correction that must rewrite published bundles — starts v1/1.2/, and a new MAJOR starts v2/2.0/. The line it replaces is frozen and kept indefinitely, with its files unchanged. The 1.0.1 generation is the frozen line v1/1.0/, with bundles and delta manifests only (no Parquet). The root index.json lists every line and its status; see Versioning & Releases.

items.title: Weekly Deltas
items.text:
Links: Monthly Full Bundles · Weekly Full Bundles · Parquet Files · How Releases Work

The list groups deltas by year, newest first: the current year is open, and each earlier year is a collapsible list under Archived years.

A weekly delta is published for every ClinVar release. Each delta is a bundle, its .sha256 checksum and its manifest. The current month's deltas sit directly in v1/1.1/deltas/; earlier months of the year are in deltas/YYYY-MM/, and prior years in archive/YYYY/deltas/YYYY-MM/:

v1/1.1/deltas/
  clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1018.json.gz             added + updated records (same section structure as the full bundle)
  clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1018.json.gz.sha256
  clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1018.manifest.json       per-section adds, updates, and deletes for this release
  2026-09/
    clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-0905.json.gz           a finished month, moved here when October's first release posted
    ...

A delta's folder changes when its month or year rolls over; its file name and bytes do not. The line's index.json lists every delta with its current bundle.path and manifest path, so look paths up there rather than composing them. Deltas carry no Parquet: Parquet is derived and published only for the latest release (Parquet Files).

Download a weekly delta with curl / Python 
# A delta of the current month, its checksum and its manifest
BASE="https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.1/deltas"
curl -O "${BASE}/clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1018.json.gz"
curl -O "${BASE}/clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1018.json.gz.sha256"
curl -O "${BASE}/clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1018.manifest.json"
sha256sum -c clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1018.json.gz.sha256   # macOS: shasum -a 256 -c

import json
import urllib.request

BASE = "https://data.clinvar-gkm.org"

# The newest delta, from the line's release index
index = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(f"{BASE}/v1/1.1/index.json"))
newest = max(index["deltas"], key=lambda d: d["release"])
for path in (newest["bundle"]["path"], newest["manifest"]):
    urllib.request.urlretrieve(f"{BASE}/{path}", path.rsplit("/", 1)[-1])

items.title: Delta Bundle
items.text: The delta bundle has the same shape as the monthly full — a single JSON object with bundle sections at the root, each a keyed collection of objects. The difference is content: a delta contains only the records added or updated since its baseline release. Sections with no additions or updates are absent from the delta bundle. Deleted records are not present in the bundle — they are listed only in the manifest.

items.title: The delta manifest
items.text:
Each delta's manifest, clinvar-gkm-delta_YYYY-MMDD.manifest.json, describes exactly what changed and which monthly full the delta chain starts from:

{
  "release": "2026-10-11",
  "baseline_release": "2026-10-04",
  "compare_release": "2026-10-11",
  "pipeline_version": "1.1.0",
  "checkpoint_full": {
    "path": "v1/1.1/clinvar-gkm_2026-10.json.gz",
    "release": "2026-09-28",
    "month": "2026-10",
    "sha256": "5d41402abc4b2a76…"
  },
  "sections": {
    "allele":  { "added": 812,  "updated": 34,  "deleted": ["ga4gh:VA.oldDigest1"] },
    "scv":     { "added": 1203, "updated": 517, "deleted": ["clinvar.submission:SCV000000001.1"] },
    "vcv":     { "added": 44,   "updated": 96,  "deleted": [] }
  },
  "counts": { "A": 2063, "U": 647, "D": 2 },
  "schema_version": "1.1.0",
  "bundle": {
    "name": "clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1011.json.gz",
    "path": "v1/1.1/deltas/clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1011.json.gz",
    "size": 104857600,
    "sha256": "9e107d9d372bb682…"
  },
  "sha256": "9e107d9d372bb682…"
}
Field Description release The ClinVar release date this delta represents baseline_release The prior release this delta was diffed against — null only on the very first release compare_release The release the changes are computed to (equals release) pipeline_version The pipeline build stamp that produced the delta (git describe of the pipeline code) checkpoint_full The official monthly this delta's chain replays onto — the newest monthly whose source_release is on or before this delta's baseline_release — as {path, release, month, sha256}. release is that monthly's source_release (a YYYY-MM-DD release date, comparable with baseline_release), month is its YYYY-MM label, and sha256 is its checksum. path is where the monthly was when the delta was published; after a year rollover, find it in index.json by month. null before the first monthly full is published sections Per-section change summary — added and updated counts plus a deleted list of primary keys counts Roll-up totals across all sections — A (added), U (updated), D (deleted) schema_version The delta bundle's own schema_version bundle The delta bundle as published: {name, path, size, sha256}. path is its folder at publish time; after a month rollover, find its current path in index.json sha256 The delta bundle's sha256 (the same value as bundle.sha256 and the .sha256 sidecar)

Deletes live only in the manifest. For each section, deleted is the list of keys that must be removed; the delta bundle itself carries only the added and updated records.

items.title: Consumer Replay Model
items.text:
A monthly full plus the deltas after it rebuild the state at any weekly release. Every official monthly has a source_release in index.json: the weekly release it was built from (the 2026-10 monthly has source_release 2026-09-28). Each delta records the release it was diffed against (baseline_release) and the release it brings you to (release).

For each delta, apply the manifest's deletes first, then upsert every record present in the delta bundle, section by section.

items.title: Rebuild a past week
items.text:
Weekly full bundles are kept only for the current month (Weekly Full Bundles). To rebuild the state at any weekly release W — a past week, or the newest one:

  1. Take the newest official monthly whose source_release ≤ W.
  2. Apply, in release order, every delta whose release is later than that source_release and ≤ W.
  3. Check the chain as you go: the first delta's baseline_release equals the monthly's source_release, and each later delta's baseline_release equals the previous delta's release. A mismatch means a release is missing; stop rather than apply a partial chain.

The deltas to apply are chosen by release date, not by month. The 2026-10 monthly is built from 2026-09-28, so rebuilding 2026-10-11 takes the 2026-10 monthly and applies the 2026-10-04 and 2026-10-11 deltas, both from the monthly's own month. (An earlier version of this page skipped deltas from the monthly's month; that missed them.)

A delta's checkpoint_full names the newest monthly whose source_release is on or before the delta's baseline_release, so it is the right base for that delta and every delta after it up to the next monthly. Its release is the monthly's source_release, the release the first delta of the chain must have as its baseline_release.

Delta manifests in the frozen v1/1.0/ line

The 1.0.1 delta manifests in v1/1.0/ are kept byte-identical, so their paths still name the pre-1.1.0 v1/datasets/ and v1/deltas/ keys and every checkpoint_full says 2026-10. For that line, pick the monthly from v1/1.0/index.json (each monthly's source_release) as above, not from checkpoint_full.

Python: rebuild the full bundle at a weekly release 
import gzip
import json
import urllib.request

BASE = "https://data.clinvar-gkm.org"
W = "2026-10-11"   # the weekly release to rebuild, YYYY-MM-DD


def fetch_json(url):
    with urllib.request.urlopen(url) as r:
        return json.load(r)


def fetch_json_gz(url):
    with urllib.request.urlopen(url) as r:
        return json.loads(gzip.decompress(r.read()))


# 0. The current line's release index, via the root version manifest.
root = fetch_json(f"{BASE}/index.json")
line = next(v for v in root["versions"].values() if v["status"] == "current")
index = fetch_json(f"{BASE}/{line['index'].lstrip('/')}")

# Monthlies and deltas of the current year, plus those moved to archive/YYYY/.
monthlies = list(index["datasets"]["monthly"])
deltas = list(index["deltas"])
for year in index.get("archives", {}).values():
    monthlies += year.get("monthly", [])
    deltas += year.get("deltas", [])

# 1. The newest official monthly whose source_release <= W (skip the 00-latest copy).
base = max(
    (m for m in monthlies
     if not m.get("latest") and m.get("source_release") and m["source_release"] <= W),
    key=lambda m: m["source_release"],
)
state = fetch_json_gz(f"{BASE}/{base['path']}")

# 2. Every delta after the monthly's source_release, up to and including W, oldest first.
chain = sorted(
    (d for d in deltas if base["source_release"] < d["release"] <= W),
    key=lambda d: d["release"],
)

# 3. Replay, checking the chain: each delta must build on the release before it.
prev = base["source_release"]
for d in chain:
    manifest = fetch_json(f"{BASE}/{d['manifest']}")
    if manifest["baseline_release"] != prev:
        raise SystemExit(
            f"broken chain at {manifest['release']}: "
            f"baseline {manifest['baseline_release']}, expected {prev}"
        )
    delta = fetch_json_gz(f"{BASE}/{d['bundle']['path']}")

    # 3a. Apply deletes (manifest only), then 3b. upsert added + updated records.
    for section, info in manifest["sections"].items():
        target = state.setdefault(section, {})
        for pk in info["deleted"]:
            target.pop(pk, None)
    for section, records in delta.items():
        if isinstance(records, dict):           # skip top-level scalars such as schema_version
            state.setdefault(section, {}).update(records)

    prev = manifest["release"]

# `state` now holds the full bundle at release W (prev == W when W is a published release).

The recipe shows the logic. A monthly full is about 4.8 GB compressed and much larger as Python objects, so for real use stream the sections to disk or a database instead of holding them in memory.

items.title: Weekly Full Bundles
items.text:
Links: Monthly Full Bundles · Weekly Deltas · Parquet Files · How Releases Work

A weekly full bundle is published for every ClinVar weekly release. It has the same content and structure as a monthly full, built from that week's release, so the newest one is the current state with no replay. The weekly fulls live in v1/1.1/weekly/, the counterpart of NCBI's xml/weekly_release/:

v1/1.1/weekly/
  clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz        newest weekly full (stable URL)
  clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MMDD.json.gz               one per weekly release of the CURRENT month
  clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MMDD.json.gz.sha256

Weekly fulls are kept for the current month only

When the first release of a new month is published, the previous month's weekly fulls are deleted, as NCBI deletes its weekly releases. The newest of them stays until the new month's official monthly is published (the monthly is normally a copy of it), and is deleted as soon as the monthly is up. They are a convenience copy, not the record: the official monthly that follows is built from the month's last release, and every past week can be rebuilt exactly from a monthly plus deltas. See Rebuild a past week. Don't hard-code a dated weekly URL in a script that runs after the month ends.

Download a weekly full with curl 
# Newest weekly full (stable URL)
curl -O https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.1/weekly/clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz

# Or a specific week of the current month, with its checksum
curl -O https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.1/weekly/clinvar-gkm_2026-1018.json.gz
curl -O https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.1/weekly/clinvar-gkm_2026-1018.json.gz.sha256
sha256sum -c clinvar-gkm_2026-1018.json.gz.sha256      # macOS: shasum -a 256 -c

Monthly, weekly full, or monthly plus deltas?

  • The current state: the newest weekly full.
  • A fixed monthly snapshot that matches ClinVar's monthly release: the official monthly.
  • Keeping a local copy current without re-downloading a full bundle every week: the monthly plus the weekly deltas.

items.title: Architecture Decision Records (ADRs)
items.text: One short, dated file per significant decision — why we chose an approach, not just what the code does. ADRs are the shared, PR-reviewed record of the project's moving picture; CLAUDE.md points here rather than importing them so they don't bloat every session's context.

items.title: Conventions
items.text:
• Filename: NNNN-kebab-title.md (zero-padded, monotonically increasing).
  • Copy 0000-template.md to start.
  • Keep it short. Link to the fuller design spec in docs/superpowers/specs/ when there is one.
  • Status: Proposed → Accepted → (later) Superseded by NNNN. Don't rewrite history — supersede.
  • Land ADRs via PR review, like code.

items.title: 0001 — Incremental pipeline with carry-forward + delta publishing
items.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-08-09
  • Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-incremental-gks-downstream-and-deltas-design.md
path: 0001 — Incremental pipeline with carry-forward + delta publishing

items.title: Context
items.text: Reprocessing every ClinVar release from scratch is expensive — the two costliest stages (variation identity and VRS resolution) recompute ~4.5M variants weekly even though ~0.3% change. Consumers also wanted just the changes, not a full re-download each week.
path: 0001 — Incremental pipeline with carry-forward + delta publishing

items.title: Decision
items.text:
Make the pipeline incremental by default: recompute only the records that changed since the prior release and carry the rest forward, gated by a gkm_pipeline_version stamp (full rebuild on version-invalidating changes). The delta is a byproduct of incremental compute — gkm_change_log + gkm_delta_build produce the A/U/D manifest and delta payloads, published to R2 as weekly delta bundles + Parquet alongside the monthly full.

  • Merge primitive for the dict/identity layers: UNION-CTAS (base WHERE NOT impacted UNION ALL recomputed).
  • gkm_vrs carry-forward uses a zero-copy CLONE of the prior release + DELETE/INSERT of the changed subset (with a deep-copy fallback when BigQuery's depth-3 clone chain fills).
path: 0001 — Incremental pipeline with carry-forward + delta publishing

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
• Large slot-time win on variation identity + vrsify; the dict aggregates are roughly break-even on cost — the delta product, not slot-time, justifies making them incremental too.
  • Correctness is enforced by oracles: full-vs-incremental (per table) and delta-reconstruction must be 0,0,0 before publish. This requires deterministic output (total-order ORDER BY, single-representative picks instead of ANY_VALUE).
  • Consumers reconstruct current state = latest monthly full + replay contiguous weekly deltas.
path: 0001 — Incremental pipeline with carry-forward + delta publishing

items.title: 0002 — Monthly full bundle anchored to ClinVar's monthly index
items.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-08-24
  • Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-24-clinvar-index-monthly-trigger-design.md
path: 0002 — Monthly full bundle anchored to ClinVar's monthly index

items.title: Context
items.text: The monthly full bundle was triggered by our own weekly cadence (a schema_on calendar-month boundary), publishing the prior release as "the month's full." That drifted from ClinVar's authoritative monthly cadence and mislabeled months, because ClinVar names a monthly _YYYY-MM for the month it is released in (early that month, reflecting ~prior-month data).
path: 0002 — Monthly full bundle anchored to ClinVar's monthly index

items.title: Decision
items.text: Anchor the monthly full to ClinVar's monthly VCV index (https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pub/clinvar/xml/). Our clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MM full = the most recent GKM-capable build with release date strictly before ClinVar's _YYYY-MM Released datetime, re-exported into the YYYY-MM slot. ClinVar's monthly XML is only a trigger signal — we never ingest it. A --month-label flag decouples the published slot from the source release date.
path: 0002 — Monthly full bundle anchored to ClinVar's monthly index

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
• Our monthly labels line up 1:1 with ClinVar's; e.g. the 2026-07 full is built from our 2026-06-27 release.
  • run-release.sh Stage 5 scrapes the index (bounded to months newer than the latest published full) instead of using schema_on; the full is a re-export of existing gkm_dict_* tables, not a rebuild.
  • A one-time re-align moved existing fulls to the new scheme. Prior-month/prior-year retention is still an open design (release browser + archiving spec).

items.title: 0003 — Roadmap generated from label-authorized discussions
items.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-08-26

items.title: Context
items.text: The docs Roadmap should reflect community priorities without hand-editing a page for every idea, and without a hand-maintained list that goes stale. GitHub Discussions already provide proposals, comments, and a built-in upvote signal.

items.title: Decision
items.text:
The Roadmap table (docs/reference/roadmap.md, between <!-- ROADMAP:START/END --> markers) is auto-generated from GitHub Discussions carrying the roadmap authorized label, ordered by upvote count (desc). src/scripts/generate-roadmap.py produces it; the deploy-docs workflow runs it on discussion events + a daily schedule + release/dispatch, then builds with zensical build and publishes to GitHub Pages.

  • Governance: a community member opens an Ideas discussion; a maintainer authorizes it by adding the label (removing the label drops it). Status comes from an optional status: <x> label.
  • Voting uses the built-in Upvote button (no emoji reactions, no downvote).

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
• Adding/removing/reordering roadmap items is done on the discussions, not in the repo — the site self-updates.
  • Build-time generation only: the live site is always current; the committed roadmap.md table is a snapshot that can lag (a commit-back step could close that gap if the repo file view must match exactly).
  • Upvote changes don't fire workflow events, so ordering refreshes on the daily schedule.

items.title: 0004 — Schema versioning & release change-management
items.text:
• Status: Proposed
  • Date: 2026-10-08
  • Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-08-schema-versioning-and-release-management-design.md
  • Amended: 2026-10-21 by ADR 0008 and ADR 0009 (PR #168):
  • §1: a content-only correction that rewrites published bundles opens a new MINOR line folder (e.g. v1/1.2/); a PATCH only adds new dated files to the current line folder (ADR 0009 §5).
  • §3: a superseded line is frozen at the switch-over and kept indefinitely. There is no 6-month live window, no eol and no deprecated status; the root index.json statuses are current and frozen. "At most two lines" no longer applies (ADR 0008 (b)).
  • §5: the in-place exception closes with 1.1.0, which is GA (ADR 0008 (a)).

items.title: Context
items.text: The clinvar-gkm bundle schema is already 1.0.0 (in its $id URIs), but releases are dated, not schema-versioned, and nothing — not the index.json, the R2 path, nor the bundle — carries a machine-readable schema version. As the model evolves we need a contract that lets consumers pin a version, keeps prior releases flowing during a migration, and consults affected users before a breaking change — without forcing a full reprocessing on every change.

items.title: Decision
items.text:
Adopt semantic versioning of the bundle schema and a release change-management policy (full detail in the spec):

  1. Semver on the bundle schema — MAJOR = breaking, MINOR = additive/backward-compatible, PATCH = no change to valid instances. A content-only change (e.g. a string value's format) is not a schema version change. (amended: see header)
  2. Upstream bumps are insulated — our level reflects the actual effect on the bundle we emit, not the upstream (va-spec/cat-vrs/vrs) bump level.
  3. Breaking change ⇒ new MAJOR line. The prior line stays fully live (monthly + weekly) for a 6-month window, then freezes (archived, immutable). The window end is a fixed calendar date (successor GA + 6 months) in the manifest. At most two lines run concurrently (N, N-1). (amended: see header)
  4. R2 layout: per-major dirs /v{major}/…, each with its own index.json; a thin root manifest lists active versions, their schema, status, and EOL (amended: see header). Existing 1.x is mirrored into /v1/ now (flat originals retained for backward compatibility).
  5. Initial-stabilization window: until a maintainer-declared GA, the 1.0.x line may take corrective breaking fixes in place (announced, not RFC'd). After GA, the full MAJOR/parallel-line/RFC machinery governs every breaking change. (amended: see header)
  6. Release notes per data release + a per-major CHANGELOG, co-located with each line's files.
  7. Subscribe/consult via GitHub Discussions Announcements (releases + RFCs), a Google Group (email, for non-GitHub consumers), and an RSS/Atom feed from index.json.
  8. Breaking-Change RFC: before any post-GA MAJOR — proposal + rationale + migration impact, notify the registry, 4-week minimum comment window.
  9. Schema in lockstep: schema/clinvar-gkm/ is the source of truth. Every output change moves the schema with it in the same PR — definitions for shape changes, field descriptions for content-only changes — regenerates json/ + the bundle schema (+ docs), bumps the $id version per (1) when the shape changes, and re-validates the examples. The $id version is the authoritative version string the manifest reports.

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
• Consumers can pin a major line and keep receiving fresh data for 6 months after a breaking change; a machine-readable root manifest tells them what's current, deprecated, and when each line ends. (amended: see header)
  • The orchestrator and generate-r2-index.sh gain per-major output paths, a root manifest, a feed, and a stop-rule for frozen lines; release-notes/CHANGELOG generation is added. These are specced but not built here, and every live-R2 write stays a separately user-confirmed step.
  • Breaking changes cost ~2× pipeline/storage during a window and require a 4-week RFC post-GA — a deliberate trade for consumer stability.
  • The first breaking change under the §5 stabilization exception, the 1.1.0 proposition reorganization, is recorded in ADR 0006.
  • The prompting change (the submittedCondition CURIE de-pointer) is content-only, so it ships under the stabilization window without a version bump; this policy governs the first breaking change after GA.
  • Accepted additions: a bundle-level schema_version field (bundles self-identify) and a Home-page release indicator reading the root manifest. The email list (Google Group) was stood up on 2026-10-18 as clinvar-gkm@broadinstitute.org; it carries the same announcements as GitHub Discussions.

items.title: 0005 — R2 distribution domain, CDN caching, and fee protection
items.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-13
  • Spec (if any): —
  • Amended: 2026-10-20 by ADR 0009: the published paths changed; see Layout change (ADR 0009).
  • Amended: 2026-10-21: the Layout change (ADR 0009) notes now match the rules in src/scripts/cf-rules.sh on 1.0 (PR #182): weekly/ and README.txt bypass the cache, and weekly fulls are not cached as immutable.
path: 0005 — R2 distribution domain, CDN caching, and fee protection

items.title: Context
items.text:
Public distribution originally pointed consumers at the R2 development URL https://pub-f0ad0e0dac0345408dcc95bda20beb42.r2.dev. That endpoint is explicitly dev-only: Cloudflare rate-limits it (429s under load), throttles bandwidth, and supports no CDN caching, WAF, or rate-limiting rules. We needed a stable, production-grade hostname that consumers can hardcode long-term, with cache/abuse controls in front of the bucket.

Constraints that shaped the choice:

  • clinicalgenome.org is not usable as the host. Its authoritative DNS is on AWS Route 53, and ClinGen has no Cloudflare account. R2 custom domains must live in a Cloudflare zone. The supported ways to attach a Cloudflare-served hostname to an externally-hosted parent domain are all gated: full setup (move the whole org domain to Cloudflare — not our call), Partial/CNAME setup (Cloudflare Business plan), or Subdomain setup (Cloudflare Enterprise). None were viable.
  • A generic downloads.clinicalgenome.org / data.clinicalgenome.org would wrongly imply an org-wide ClinGen download hub; clinicalgenome.org hosts many independent data sources.
  • R2's defining property is $0 egress — so "download bandwidth" is never a cost. The only download-driven cost is Class B (read) operations, which are cheap and collapse to near-zero behind a CDN cache.
path: 0005 — R2 distribution domain, CDN caching, and fee protection

items.title: Decision
items.text:
1. Dedicated domain. Registered clinvar-gkm.org via Cloudflare Registrar (~$10/yr), which creates it as its own free Cloudflare zone — no dependency on ClinGen's Route 53 or any admin.
  2. Public host = data.clinvar-gkm.org, attached to the clinvar-gkm R2 bucket via R2 → Connect Domain (auto-creates a proxied record + TLS). data (not downloads) because consumers also range-read the Parquet in place (DuckDB/httpfs), which isn't a "download". The apex is left free for a future landing page.
  3. Scripts default to the custom host, env-overridable. All uploaders + the index generator set R2_PUBLIC_URL="${R2_PUBLIC_URL:-https://data.clinvar-gkm.org}". generate-r2-index.sh writes this as the base_url in index.json / the root manifest / feed.xml — the canonical consumer URL.
  4. Fee protection is CDN-side (Cache Rules + one rate-limit rule), plus an optional --purge path in the uploaders for the rare in-place overwrite.

The pub-…r2.dev dev URL still resolves (same bucket) and can be disabled in the dashboard once all consumers have migrated.
path: 0005 — R2 distribution domain, CDN caching, and fee protection

items.title: Consequences
items.text: Easy: a stable branded URL, free egress, near-zero op costs behind caching, full WAF/cache control. Harder / must-know for future administrators — the runbook below.
path: 0005 — R2 distribution domain, CDN caching, and fee protection

items.title: Key identifiers
items.text: Thing Value Cloudflare account (R2) 09208aa33790838db213a21f630c33e7 R2 bucket clinvar-gkm S3 endpoint (writes) https://09208aa33790838db213a21f630c33e7.r2.cloudflarestorage.com (--profile r2) Public host (reads) https://data.clinvar-gkm.org (zone clinvar-gkm.org) Dev URL (legacy) https://pub-f0ad0e0dac0345408dcc95bda20beb42.r2.dev (still works; retire later)

items.title: Reproducing the setup (if the domain/zone ever has to be rebuilt)
items.text:
1. Register / add the zone: clinvar-gkm.org via Cloudflare Registrar (or add any domain you own and point its nameservers at Cloudflare — full setup, free). Must be in the same Cloudflare account as the bucket.
  2. Connect the bucket: R2 → clinvar-gkm → Settings → Custom Domains → Connect Domain → data.clinvar-gkm.org. Cloudflare creates the proxied record + provisions TLS. Wait for Active.
  3. Verify it's proxied (Cache/WAF rules only act on proxied traffic): 
    dig +short data.clinvar-gkm.org      # → Cloudflare anycast IPs (104.x / 172.67.x), not an origin IP
curl -sI https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/index.json | grep -iE 'server|cf-cache-status'
#   → "server: cloudflare" + a "cf-cache-status:" header  ⇒ traffic is proxied, rules apply
    If a rule editor warns "may not be proxying traffic for (http.host …)", this is the check to run — R2 custom domains are proxied by design, so once Active the warning is a false positive.
path: 0005 — R2 distribution domain, CDN caching, and fee protection

items.title: Cache Rules (zone clinvar-gkm.org → Caching → Cache Rules)
items.text:
Object layout splits into write-once / immutable vs rewritten-every-release / mutable. Note "latest" appears both as a directory (/00-latest/) and inside a filename (clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz), and there are two index files plus a feed — the mutable matcher must catch all of them:

  • Immutable (dated, never overwritten): /v1/deltas/<YYYY-MMDD>/…, /v1/datasets/clinvar-gkm_<YYYY-MM>.json.gz, /v1/datasets/parquet/<YYYY-MM>/…, /v1/archives/….
  • Mutable (rewritten every release): root /index.json, /v1/index.json, /v1/feed.xml, /v1/datasets/clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz, and everything under any /00-latest/ tree (/v1/deltas/00-latest/…, /v1/datasets/parquet/00-latest/…).

These are the paths before ADR 0009; the new paths are listed under Layout change (ADR 0009).

Two rules; last matching rule wins, so keep the pointer rule below the immutable rule:

Rule 1 "R2 immutable artifacts"   (FIRST)
  When:  (http.host eq "data.clinvar-gkm.org")
  Then:  Eligible for cache; Edge TTL = Ignore cache-control, 1 month; Browser TTL = 1 day

Rule 2 "R2 mutable pointers"      (SECOND / last)
  When:  (http.host eq "data.clinvar-gkm.org") and (
           http.request.uri.path contains "00-latest"
           or http.request.uri.path contains "index.json"
           or http.request.uri.path contains "feed.xml" )
  Then:  Bypass cache

This collapses Class B cost (immutable files serve from edge, never hitting R2) while mutable pointers are always fetched fresh. The long TTL is safe only because dated artifacts are write-once — see overwrite gotcha below. Two Free-plan constraints shaped this:

  • Max cacheable object = 512 MB (Free/Pro/Business; Enterprise 5 GB). The multi-GB JSON bundles therefore never cache — they always report cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC and stream straight from R2. That is fine: egress is $0 and it's one cheap Class B op per fetch. Caching's real win is the smaller/hot files (Parquet sections, manifests, index).
  • Minimum dashboard Edge TTL = 2 hours on Free. You can't set a short TTL for the pointers that way, so Rule 2 uses Bypass cache (always fresh) instead of a 1-minute TTL. If brief pointer caching is ever wanted, stamp Cache-Control: max-age=60 on those objects at upload and set Rule 2 Edge TTL to "use cache-control header if present" (origin TTLs aren't subject to the 2 h floor).

Verify with real GET requests (curl -I/HEAD reports DYNAMIC even when a GET caches): 

u=https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/deltas/<date>/manifest.json
curl -s -o /dev/null -D - "$u" | grep -i cf-cache-status   # run twice → MISS then HIT (immutable)
curl -s -o /dev/null -D - https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/index.json | grep -i cf-cache-status  # DYNAMIC/BYPASS
path: 0005 — R2 distribution domain, CDN caching, and fee protection

items.title: Rate-limiting rule (Security → WAF → Rate limiting rules; 1 free IP-keyed rule)
items.text:
Live rule "R2 abuse backstop" (verified 2026-10-18):

When:  (http.host eq "data.clinvar-gkm.org")
Characteristics:  IP (ip.src)
Rate:  250 requests / 10 seconds
Then:  Block for 10 seconds
Order: first; Status: Active

The Free plan fixes the counting period and the block duration at 10 seconds; only the request count is adjustable. The original intent (300 requests / 1 minute, block 10 minutes) could not be expressed on Free and was first configured as 50 / 10 s. That blocked ordinary DuckDB queries after ~55 range requests, so on 2026-10-18 the threshold was raised to 250 / 10 s. A burst of 120 range requests in ~1 s now returns 206 throughout, and remote queries such as a GROUP BY over all of scv.parquet or a variant's PubMed ids (an scv × varcond-proposition join) complete in 10–35 s.

Keep it generous: DuckDB/httpfs issues many range GETs per query, cached hits still count toward the limiter, and a client that keeps retrying while blocked re-trips the rule. This is an anti-runaway backstop only — real exposure is pennies (free egress + $0.36 / million Class B, 10M/month free).
path: 0005 — R2 distribution domain, CDN caching, and fee protection

items.title: Costs (order of magnitude)
items.text: Storage $0.015/GB-mo (a few $/mo at current size); Class B $0.36/million reads with 10M/mo free; egress $0. Caching + the write-once layout keep origin reads near-zero. There is no native hard spend cap. An account-wide budget alert at $10/month is configured (Manage Account → Billing → Billable Usage → budget alert; email only, it does not pause usage). R2-specific Usage Based Billing alerts (Alerts → Overview → Add) may need a paid plan.
path: 0005 — R2 distribution domain, CDN caching, and fee protection

items.title: Path allowlist rule (Security → WAF → Custom rules)
items.text:
Added 2026-10-18, active:

Name:  PATH ALLOWLIST - block requests outside published data paths
When:  http.host eq "data.clinvar-gkm.org" and not (
         starts_with(path, "/v1/") or starts_with(path, "/archive/") or
         starts_with(path, "/.well-known/") or path in {"/" "/index.json"})
Then:  Block

Scanners probe hostnames for paths such as /wp-config.php, /.git/config and /actuator/health (about 1,600 such requests in the first four days). This rule blocks them at the edge with a 403, before they reach R2, so they cost no Class B operations. Unlike Browser Integrity Check, which is off for this zone because it rejected Python's default urllib user agent (HTTP 403, error 1010), it cannot be bypassed by faking a header. Tested on 2026-10-18: - index files, bundles, Parquet (including 206 range reads), the archive and CORS preflight are served; - scanner paths, stray documentation-site paths and the retired flat-root /datasets/… return 403.

When a new top-level path is published, add it to the rule.
path: 0005 — R2 distribution domain, CDN caching, and fee protection

items.title: Spend alert and kill switch
items.text:
R2 has no hard spend cap and the budget alert only emails, so pausing is manual. What can grow the bill: Class B reads that miss the cache (mostly range requests on files over 512 MB, which always go to R2), our own writes (Class A) and storage. Egress is $0.

If the alert fires:

  1. Stop our own writes: no run-release.sh, uploader or backfill runs.
  2. Find the cause: R2 → clinvar-gkm → Metrics (which operation type jumped); clinvar-gkm.org → Security → Events / Analytics (top IPs, ASNs, paths). If it is one client or network, block only that with a WAF custom rule on ip.src or ip.geoip.asnum.
  3. Pause all public reads with one command: 
    ./src/scripts/cdn-kill-switch.sh on       # block every request to data.clinvar-gkm.org at the edge
./src/scripts/cdn-kill-switch.sh status   # rule state + a probe of /v1/index.json (403 = blocked)
./src/scripts/cdn-kill-switch.sh off      # restore service
    It flips one WAF custom rule ("KILL SWITCH - block all public data"); cached hits are blocked too, so nothing reaches R2. Nothing in R2 changes. It needs CF_ZONE_ID and CF_WAF_TOKEN in ~/.config/clinvar-gkm/cloudflare.env; the token is scoped to zone clinvar-gkm.org with Zone → Zone WAF → Edit and Zone → Firewall Services → Edit. Run init once to pre-create the rule disabled. The dashboard equivalent is Security → WAF → Custom rules → toggle the rule.
  4. The r2.dev URL bypasses all of this. The public development URL serves the same bucket with no cache, WAF or rate limit. Disable it (R2 → clinvar-gkm → Settings → Public Development URL); nothing in the repo uses it any more.
  5. Harder stop, if needed: disconnect the custom domain (R2 → clinvar-gkm → Settings → Custom Domains). Reconnecting re-provisions TLS and takes a few minutes.
path: 0005 — R2 distribution domain, CDN caching, and fee protection

items.title: Overwrite gotcha + the --purge flag
items.text:
Within the 1-month immutable Edge TTL, Cloudflare serves cached bytes without revalidating against R2, and the cache is per-PoP. So overwriting an already-cached immutable file in place (e.g. re-publishing a release under the same date, or re-running a backfill over an existing month) serves stale, inconsistent content for up to a month. Routine releases are safe — they write new dated keys, and the only paths they overwrite (index.json, 00-latest/*) are on the 1-minute rule and self-heal.

For the rare in-place overwrite, the uploaders take --purge, which purges the CDN cache for the dated path(s) just written:

  • upload-gkm-delta-to-r2.sh … --purge → purges …/v1/deltas/<YYYY-MMDD>/
  • upload-gkm-to-r2.sh … --purge → purges the dated monthly + dated Parquet set
  • backfill-monthly-to-r2.sh … --purge → purges ${DEST} (+ dated Parquet)

--purge requires a zone-scoped Cloudflare API token with Cache Purge permission (the object-scoped r2 token cannot purge), plus the zone id:

export CF_ZONE_ID=<clinvar-gkm.org zone id>
export CF_PURGE_TOKEN=<zone-scoped token with Cache Purge>
./upload-gkm-delta-to-r2.sh 2026-07-06 delta.json.gz manifest.json --purge

Without --purge nothing changes (routine behavior). With --purge but no token, the script warns and skips (non-fatal). Overridable host via CF_PUBLIC_HOST (default data.clinvar-gkm.org). All purge methods (URL, prefix, hostname, tag, everything) are available on all plans since 2025-04. Manual equivalent: 

curl -X POST "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/${CF_ZONE_ID}/purge_cache" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${CF_PURGE_TOKEN}" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"prefixes":["data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/datasets/"]}'   # or {"purge_everything":true}
path: 0005 — R2 distribution domain, CDN caching, and fee protection

items.title: CORS
items.text: Bucket CORS is applied out-of-band (apply-r2-cors.sh with an admin token, or the dashboard; policy in src/scripts/r2-cors.json) and is returned at the bucket level, so it passes through the custom domain. The docs download browser (docs/assets/js/r2-browser.js) now fetches from data.clinvar-gkm.org; ensure the docs-site origin is allowed in r2-cors.json.
path: 0005 — R2 distribution domain, CDN caching, and fee protection

items.title: Optional future: a clinicalgenome.org entry point
items.text: If a ClinGen-branded link is ever wanted, the Route 53 admin can host an S3 static-website redirect + Route 53 alias at e.g. clinvar-gkm-data.clinicalgenome.org → https://data.clinvar-gkm.org. Purely additive; not required for anything to work.

items.title: Bucket layout note
items.text: Only the v1/ tree is live. The bucket root holds just the thin index.json manifest (ADR 0004) alongside v1/; the pre-v1/ root datasets/ and deltas/ trees plus root README.txt were deleted on 2026-10-13. All uploaders (including backfill-monthly-to-r2.sh) and the docs now reference v1/… paths.
path: 0005 — R2 distribution domain, CDN caching, and fee protection

items.title: Layout change (ADR 0009)
items.text:
ADR 0009 replaces the /v1/ layout above with per-line folders modelled on NCBI's ClinVar FTP: v1/1.1/ holds the official monthlies and clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz, weekly/ (the current month's weekly fulls and clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz), deltas/ (current month at the top, earlier months in deltas/YYYY-MM/), archive/YYYY/ and one parquet/ dataset; the 1.0.1 generation becomes the frozen line v1/1.0/. What changes here (src/scripts/cf-rules.sh holds the exact rule expressions: show compares them with the live rules, apply is a user-confirmed step):

  • Immutable rule. Unchanged; it still matches every path, so in effect it covers everything the later rules do not catch: dated monthlies, deltas, delta manifests, .sha256 sidecars outside weekly/, archive/YYYY/, and frozen line folders' bundles and MANIFEST.json. The path list above no longer applies.
  • Mutable-pointer rule. Bypasses the cache for any path containing 00-latest (which also matches clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz), ending in /index.json, /feed.xml or /README.txt, or containing /weekly/. Weekly fulls and their sidecars are deleted at month rollover, so they are not cached as immutable.
  • Latest-Parquet rule. The "Latest Parquet: cache 1 day" rule (added 2026-10-18; edge 1 day, browser 1 h) matched /v1/datasets/parquet/00-latest/, which no longer exists. It now matches any path under /v1/ containing /parquet/, which includes parquet/manifest.json. Without the change the overwritten Parquet would fall under the 1-month immutable rule.
  • Purges. Routine releases now overwrite (the Parquet dataset), move (deltas at month rollover, monthlies and deltas at year rollover) and delete (weekly fulls at month rollover; the finished month's newest once the new monthly is published) published paths. r2-rollover.sh purges every path it moved or deleted, and run-release.sh purges the parquet/ prefix after each rebuild; --purge above is no longer only for the rare in-place overwrite.
  • Path allowlist (WAF custom rule, documented on PR #173). Every published path stays under /v1/, so no new prefix is needed. /archive/ can be removed once archive/1.0.1/ has moved to v1/1.0/ and been deleted (cf-rules.sh apply --drop-archive).
  • Bucket layout note. The "Only the v1/ tree is live" note still holds; the old v1/datasets/, v1/deltas/ and dated Parquet trees and archive/1.0.1/ are deleted in the ADR 0009 cleanup.
path: 0005 — R2 distribution domain, CDN caching, and fee protection

items.title: 0006 — Ship the proposition reorganization as 1.1.0, in place under /v1/
items.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-18
  • Spec (if any): docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-18-proposition-reorganization.md (plan PR #155)
  • Amended: 2026-10-20 by ADR 0009 (R2 layout mirrors NCBI ClinVar, PR #168): Decision 2's "in place under /v1/" becomes the new line folder v1/1.1/, and the 1.0.1 generation becomes the frozen line v1/1.0/. Decisions 1, 3 and 4 stand.
  • Amended: 2026-10-21 by ADR 0008 and ADR 0009 (PR #168): the maintainer declared 1.1.0 GA. The initial-stabilization exception ends with 1.1.0; published files are immutable from 1.1.0, and a later breaking change opens v2/. A superseded line is frozen and kept indefinitely (no EOL date, no deprecation window), and a content-only correction that rewrites bundles opens a new MINOR line folder. 1.1.0 used a completion notice only (ADR 0008 (g)).
path: 0006 — Ship the proposition reorganization as 1.1.0, in place under /v1/

items.title: Context
items.text:
The next release was being prepared as 1.0.2: a schema-conformance fix to ClinvarCategoricalVariant (#142) plus corrective data and Parquet fixes, delivered through a patch-style backfill of the published releases.

On 2026-10-18 the proposition reorganization was added to the same release. The four proposition sections and Parquet tables, grouped by object shape (varcond-, varcustom-, vartumor-, vartherapy-proposition), become four grouped by meaning (propositionPathogenicity, propositionOncogenicity, propositionSomaticClinicalImpact, propositionClinvarCustom). The Parquet tables share one column schema, which renames some columns. Every statement and evidence-line pointer changes, so the patch backfill no longer fits. The release becomes one full rebuild of all 16 datasets, with every published bundle and Parquet set re-assembled and re-exported.

ADR 0004 gives three ways to label this:

  • §1: a PATCH must not change valid instances. Renaming sections and tables does, so 1.0.2 is wrong.
  • §3/§4: a breaking change after GA gets a new MAJOR line (/v2/) and the prior line stays live for 6 months, after a 4-week RFC (§8).
  • §5: until GA, the 1.x line may take breaking changes in place, announced rather than RFC'd. §5 names corrective fixes. The reorganization is a deliberate redesign, not a correction.
path: 0006 — Ship the proposition reorganization as 1.1.0, in place under /v1/

items.title: Decision
items.text:
1. Ship the proposition reorganization and the pending fixes as 1.1.0: the schema $ids (w3id.org/clingen/schema/clinvar-gkm/1.1.0/…), the bundle schema_version const and the assembler's SCHEMA_VERSION.
  2. Publish it in place under /v1/, under the §5 stabilization exception. ADR 0004 §4 keys directories by MAJOR, so a MINOR stays in /v1/. All 4 monthly fulls, 00-latest, the 15 weekly deltas and every Parquet set are rewritten, and the old var*-proposition files are removed.
  3. No new MAJOR line, no parallel line, and no 1.0.2 tag. The release is one tag, 1.1.0, on the 1.0 release branch. The branch keeps its name, since it carries the 1.x line.
  4. This ADR extends §5 to cover a deliberate structural change made before GA, not only corrective fixes. After GA, the full MAJOR, parallel-line and RFC process governs every breaking change, as ADR 0004 says.
path: 0006 — Ship the proposition reorganization as 1.1.0, in place under /v1/

items.title: Rationale
items.text:
• Not a PATCH. Under §1 a PATCH changes no valid instance. This release renames sections, Parquet tables and columns, and rewrites every pointer, so 1.0.2 would mislabel it.
  • A MINOR is the most honest label that stays in /v1/. It is not strict semver, since a MINOR should be additive. But a consumer that pins a 1.0.x $id gets a clear signal that something changed, and the R2 layout stays put.
  • A new MAJOR costs more than it protects. /v2/ would double the pipeline and storage for 6 months and add a 4-week RFC. Before GA there are few consumers, so the parallel line would protect almost no one.
  • One rebuild. Labelling the fixes and the redesign together means one rebuild and one republish, not two.
path: 0006 — Ship the proposition reorganization as 1.1.0, in place under /v1/

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
• Announcements (ADR 0004 §6, §7). These are required, in this order:
  • An advance notice with the cutover date, posted before any R2 overwrite.
  • A completion notice after the republish is verified.

Both go to GitHub Discussions Announcements, the v1/feed.xml Atom feed, the GitHub Release notes and the Changelog. The Google Group clinvar-gkm@broadinstitute.org went live on 2026-10-18 (#167). Today generate-r2-index.sh builds the feed from the R2 listing alone (one entry per file, no summary text), so the republish re-dates every entry but cannot carry the notice text. A notice entry in the feed is a generator follow-up. Both notices cover the old → new section and table mapping, the column renames, the 1.1.0 $ids and schema_version, the corrective fixes in the same release, and the fact that every published file is rewritten in place, so checksums change and earlier downloads should be refreshed. - Version strings. Every 1.0.2 string on the open 1.0 PRs (#142, #145, #153 and the rest) is relabelled 1.1.0 before they merge. Gate before tagging: grep -r 1.0.2 schema src returns nothing. - Tagging. Tagging 1.1.0 makes the new w3id $ids resolve through the existing dynamic rule (no .htaccess change). The 1.0.0 and 1.0.1 tags and their $ids stay resolvable. - Local copies. Copies downloaded before 1.1.0 keep the old sections and tables. The plan's migration notes show how to rebuild the new shape from their data column. - Precedent. The extension in Decision 4 ends at GA. Once GA is declared, a change like this needs a /v2/ line and an RFC.
path: 0006 — Ship the proposition reorganization as 1.1.0, in place under /v1/

items.title: 0007 — Pipeline principles and simplification
items.text:
• Status: Proposed
  • Date: 2026-10-18
  • Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-18-pipeline-simplification.md

items.title: Context
items.text:
ClinVar-GKM exists to give the public community reliable, high-quality ClinVar data that significantly lowers the barrier to understanding, access, use and interoperability. The pipeline has to transform ClinVar into the GA4GH GKM schema set (VRS, Cat-VRS, VA-Spec) and stay maintainable by a small team, with as few points of failure as possible.

Size today (main @ 567272c; src/ is identical on 1.0 @ 6606d3d):

Part Count Lines BigQuery procedures and functions (src/procedures/*.sql) 22 files about 9,300 Release scripts (src/scripts/, top level) 31 files about 5,000 Parquet export SQL (src/scripts/parquet-schemas/*.sql) 21 files 193 Oracle and validation scripts (oracle-*.sh, validate-*) 10 files —

The 1.1.0 work found defects that fall into four classes. None of them is a one-off; each class comes from how the pipeline is built.

  1. Duplicated logic that drifted apart.
    • The Parquet SQL re-derives every table from the BigQuery gkm_dict_* tables, so it had to copy the bundle assembler's cleanup. The copy was incomplete: typed extensions in scv and evidenceLine Parquet carried all-null placeholder elements that the bundle does not have (#143).
    • Two null-strip implementations exist: the assembler's strip_empty and BigQuery's JSON_STRIP_NULLS. Applying JSON_STRIP_NULLS to the key/value tables would have broken the VRS Range nulls in 65,964 location rows (#143).
    • The proposition type → bundle section mapping is copied in 11 places: 8 procedure sites, the NDJSON export, the delta manifest and the conformance validator (#155 §2.3). The copies already differ in detail.
  2. Mixed reference forms. Bare CURIEs and #/section/key pointers were both used for references: 7,811,379 bare values in VCV proposition object and vcv- ConceptSet concepts on 2026-10-11 (#160). The published 1.0.1 Parquet held JSON-quoted pointers in vartherapy-proposition.object_therapy ("\"#/therapy/clinvar.therapy:…\""), fixed in #143. Consumers and our own Parquet SQL strip pointers with regexes in many places.
  3. Incremental and full builds disagreed.
    • Unordered aggregates made the procedures non-deterministic: two runs of unchanged SQL gave different fingerprints for gkm_dict_variation, the VCV/RCV aggregate tables, variation_hgvs and variation_identity (#161).
    • A duplicate allele key flipped between builds, so it showed up in weekly deltas (#157).
    • The VCV/RCV carry-forward parses the accession out of the proposition id (SPLIT(key, '-')), which ties the delta model to the id format (#155 §3.B).
  4. Upstream inputs trusted without checks.
    • clinvar_ingest.entrez_gene is missing 64,854 gene ids that gene_association uses.
    • rcv_mapping lists SCVs that are absent from the VCV data, 2–3 a week. It is a faithful parse of ClinVar's RCV XML, which runs out of sync with the VCV XML. One stale SCV left four RCV propositions with no object (#158).
    • ClinVar's VCV XML carries 16 malformed HGVS expressions with no sequence-type letter (#145).
    • single_gene_variation counts gene-association rows instead of distinct genes, so 55 haplotypes and genotypes whose alleles share one gene get no gene.

Each fix so far has been local. Without a shared standard, the same classes will recur.

items.title: Decision
items.text:
These five principles are normative. Every change to the pipeline or the published data is measured against them. A change that departs from one says so in its PR, with the reason; a lasting departure needs its own ADR.

  1. ClinVar fidelity. Never alter or drop source data silently. A repair keeps the original value in an extension, and an inferred value is marked as inferred. Examples: originalClinvarExpression / invalidClinvarExpression (#145), originalClinvarCitation (#156), geneContextSource (#159), and submittedCondition kept as the submitted CURIE.
  2. One source of truth. The JSON bundle is canonical. Every other published artifact (Parquet, lookup files) must be recomputable from the published bundle. Derived columns, join keys and lookup tables are allowed. A new fact goes into the bundle first and flows out from there.
  3. Conformance on real artifacts. Validate the actual published bundles, full and delta, with the GA4GH gkm-toolkit against the strict schemas. A hand-built sample or a sub-bundle does not count: it can mask export and assembler bugs.
  4. Determinism. The same input gives byte-identical output, and incremental output equals a full rebuild. Every aggregate, pick and array order that reaches an output uses a total order.
  5. Change published data only by rebuilding. One consolidated rebuild and backfill per release, with the docs updated in lockstep. Published files are never patched in place.

items.title: Rules these principles consolidate
items.text:
These rules already exist. The principles state the intent behind them; the detailed rules stay where they are.
