Principle Existing rule Where it lives 1 ClinVar's submitted text is never altered or dropped #144 plan, decision A1; #145 2 The assembler (assemble-gkm-dicts.py + gkm_json_cleanup.py) is the single publish-layer cleanup point CLAUDE.md; scripts.md "Publish-layer cleanup & bundle conformance" 2 schema/clinvar-gkm/ is the source of truth for the schema ADR 0004 §9 3 Validate the real full and delta bundles with gkm-toolkit; sub-bundle.py output is not proof CLAUDE.md; scripts.md "Conformance validation" 3 Validate the data a procedure produces, not just that the SQL runs sql-procedures.md "Cat-VRS variant/constraint shapes" 4 Incremental procedures are byte-identical to a full rebuild; total-order ORDER BY; no ANY_VALUE for values the group key does not determine sql-procedures.md "Determinism / correctness"; ADR 0001 4 Full-vs-incremental and delta-reconstruction oracles report 0,0,0 before publishing sql-procedures.md 5 Settle every data decision, then run one consolidated rebuild and backfill; docs move with every PR maintainer rule, applied in #144 and #155 5 Never overwrite a published dated path without a CDN purge; every live R2 write is confirmed by a maintainer scripts.md "Cloudflare R2"; ADR 0005

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
The principles point the pipeline toward fewer moving parts. The simplification plan has the detail, the measurements and the decisions still needed. In summary:

  • Generate Parquet from the bundle output. Build the Parquet tables from the cleaned records the assembler writes, instead of re-deriving them from the dict tables in 21 SQL files. The copied cleanup and the placeholder class of bugs go away (principle 2).
  • One canonical definition per concept. Pointer formatting, pointer stripping, the type → section mapping and the list of tracked tables each get one shared definition (principles 2 and 4).
  • Re-evaluate the incremental machinery with cost data. Measure each procedure in full and incremental mode over several weeks before deciding where carry-forward pays for its complexity. The delta product does not depend on it: gkm_change_log already finds changes by diffing outputs (principle 4).
  • Input contract checks at the upstream boundary. Check the inputs before each run. A violation fails the run or is logged; it is never silently absorbed (principle 1).
  • One release gate command. The oracles, strict gkm-toolkit validation of the real bundles, the bundle-vs-Parquet recompute and the reference guard run as one command that blocks publish (principles 3 and 4).
  • Restraint on new published artifacts. Every new artifact needs a stated owner and gate, and derives from the bundle or the published Parquet (principles 2 and 5).

Other consequences:

  • The in-flight 1.1.0 release already applies parts of this: the canonical type → section function (#155), uniform #/ references with a bare-reference guard (#160), the determinism fixes (#161, #157) and the release gates in #155 §6.4. The simplification work starts after 1.1.0 ships.
  • Principle 5 retires the patch-style backfill used for the 1.0.0 conditionSet repair and prepared for 1.0.2 (#144). #155 had already moved 1.1.0 to a full rebuild.
  • Rebuilds cost more than patches. The #155 estimate for a full rebuild of all 16 datasets is about 3.4 TiB billed, about $21 at on-demand rates. That is small next to the cost of an unverifiable patch.
  • Reviewers gain a checklist: which principle does a change touch, and which gate proves it holds.
  • Once accepted, CLAUDE.md should point to this ADR from its project context section.

items.title: 0008 — Bundles are the public record: immutability, archives, version lines and download metrics
items.text:
• Status: Proposed
  • Date: 2026-10-18
  • Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-18-bundle-record-and-metrics.md
  • Amends: ADR 0004 §3 (no live window: a superseded line freezes at the switch-over and is kept indefinitely, with no EOL date) and §5 (the in-place exception ends with 1.1.0); ADR 0006 (on PR #146) consequences (advance notice, (g)).
  • Amended: 2026-10-20 by ADR 0009 (R2 layout mirrors NCBI ClinVar): (a) weekly fulls are an exception to immutability; (c) archives are archive/YYYY/ inside a line, and the 1.0.1 generation becomes the frozen line v1/1.0/; (e) one overwritten Parquet dataset, none in archives.
  • Decided: 2026-10-21 (maintainer): 1.1.0 is GA (a); superseded lines are frozen and kept indefinitely, status frozen, with no eol, no deprecated status and no deletion window (b); a content-only correction that rewrites bundles opens a new MINOR line (c, ADR 0009 §5). Still open: N in (f).
  • Amended: 2026-10-21 to match the code merged on 1.0 (PR #182, r2_layout.py): the finished month's newest weekly full is kept until the new month's monthly is published (a); the switch-over notice uses status: "frozen" and superseded_by as the root and line index.json publish them (b); the Parquet manifest fields (e).
path: 0008 — Bundles are the public record: immutability, archives, version lines and download metrics

items.title: Context
items.text:
Every corrective release so far has rewritten the published files under /v1/ in place: the 1.0.0 re-release, 1.0.1, and next the 1.1.0 republish (ADR 0006, on #146). Each rewrite replaced the bytes behind the same URLs. Anyone who downloaded an earlier generation now holds files that no longer exist anywhere, and nothing tells them which generation they have.

Before deciding how much machinery that problem deserves, we need to know whether anyone is downloading the data. What we know today:

  • Analytics exist only from 2026-10-14. Cloudflare GraphQL Analytics (httpRequestsAdaptiveGroups, per path, Free plan) covers data.clinvar-gkm.org from the day it started serving (ADR 0005). The zone rejects queries older than "4w3d", so it keeps about 31 days. Earlier traffic went to the r2.dev URL, which has no per-path analytics and is now disabled.

  • No complete full-bundle download so far. From 2026-10-14 to 2026-10-18, excluding our own IP:

    Path Requests Clients Served Reading v1/datasets/clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz 18 8 IP/UA pairs 1.09 GB about 0.2 of one 4.8 GB full: at most a partial download dated monthly fulls (each) 2–4 — 0 bytes HEAD requests or link checks v1/deltas/00-latest/… delta 12 — 0.03 GB about 1–2 delta downloads old flat-root /datasets/… 7 — 0 bytes stale links

  • Parquet is not yet stable. The Parquet tables are re-derived from the BigQuery dict tables by separate SQL (ADR 0007, Workstream 1), and their layout changed in 1.0.1 and changes again in 1.1.0. The JSON bundles are the canonical output (ADR 0007, principle 2).

  • The 1.0.1 bundles are being archived to archive/1.0.1/ (the v1/ paths mirrored below it), with a MANIFEST.json (sha256 per file) and a README.txt, before the 1.1.0 republish rewrites /v1/. Under ADR 0009 this generation moves to the frozen line folder v1/1.0/.
  • No subscribers yet. The email list clinvar-gkm@broadinstitute.org has no members. When this ADR was proposed the schema had not been declared GA; the maintainer declared 1.1.0 GA on 2026-10-21 (a).
path: 0008 — Bundles are the public record: immutability, archives, version lines and download metrics

items.title: Decision
path: 0008 — Bundles are the public record: immutability, archives, version lines and download metrics

items.title: (a) The JSON bundles are the public record
items.text:
The monthly full and delta JSON bundles are the published record of ClinVar-GKM. From the 1.1.0 republish on, a published bundle file is immutable: the bytes behind a published bundle path are never replaced. A correction is published into a new line folder (c), and the folder it replaces is frozen with its bytes intact. The mutable pointers are not records: index.json, the root manifest, feed.xml and every 00-latest path keep moving to the newest release.

Two amendments from ADR 0009:

  • Weekly full bundles are not records. The current month's weekly fulls under weekly/ are a convenience copy and are deleted at month rollover, as NCBI deletes its weekly releases. The finished month's newest weekly full is kept until the new month's official monthly, a server-side copy of it, is published, and is deleted then. This is a deliberate exception to immutability. The records are the official monthlies and the deltas, from which any past week can be rebuilt exactly.
  • Moves change the path, not the bytes. At month and year rollover, deltas and monthlies move into deltas/YYYY-MM/ and archive/YYYY/. Their bytes, names and sha256 stay the same.

1.1.0 is GA (maintainer decision, 2026-10-21). The ADR 0004 §5 initial-stabilization period, which ADR 0006 extended to cover the 1.1.0 reorganization, ends with 1.1.0: the in-place exception is closed, published files are immutable from 1.1.0, and every later breaking change opens a new MAJOR line (v2/) under the ADR 0004 MAJOR-line and RFC process.
path: 0008 — Bundles are the public record: immutability, archives, version lines and download metrics

items.title: (b) A breaking change opens a new line
items.text:
A breaking schema change after 1.1.0 opens a new line, v2/2.0/ (ADR 0009 §1), built in full (every monthly full and every delta in the window being republished) alongside /v1/. The old line is then frozen at the switch-over: no new releases, and its files stay downloadable and unchanged. It carries a switch-over notice:

  • in its index.json and in its entry in the root manifest's versions: "status": "frozen" and "superseded_by" naming the line that replaced it (for example "v2/2.0"), as v1/1.0 already carries "superseded_by": "v1/1.1";
  • in its MANIFEST.json and README.txt (c);
  • on the email list and in GitHub Discussions Announcements.

Decided 2026-10-21 by the maintainer: a superseded line is frozen at the switch-over and kept indefinitely. Its status is frozen; there is no eol date, no deprecated status and no deletion window. This amends ADR 0004 §3: the prior line does not stay live for a 6-month window, and the root manifest carries no EOL date. Only one line is current at a time; frozen lines accumulate.
path: 0008 — Bundles are the public record: immutability, archives, version lines and download metrics

items.title: (c) A replaced generation is kept as a frozen line folder
items.text:
Amended by ADR 0009. Each version line has its own folder, v{major}/{major}.{minor}/. A republish that replaces a line's bundles (a new MINOR or MAJOR) publishes into a new folder, and the folder it replaces is frozen in place and kept indefinitely (b): nothing is added, moved or deleted, and it is listed from the root manifest with its status. A frozen folder carries:

  • a MANIFEST.json listing every file with its size and sha256;
  • a README.txt saying what the generation is, which release replaced it and why.

The 1.0.1 generation, first copied to archive/1.0.1/ on 2026-10-18, moves to v1/1.0/. There is no root archive/<version>/ folder any more: archive/YYYY/ now means the prior-year archive inside a line (v1/1.1/archive/YYYY/, monthlies plus deltas/YYYY-MM/). A content-only correction that must rewrite bundles is published the same way, as a new MINOR line folder; a PATCH only adds new dated files (ADR 0009 §5, decided 2026-10-21).
path: 0008 — Bundles are the public record: immutability, archives, version lines and download metrics

items.title: (d) Every manifest carries sha256 per file
items.text: Every manifest that lists a bundle (the per-line index.json, each delta manifest and each frozen line's MANIFEST.json) gives its size and sha256, and every bundle has a <file>.sha256 sidecar. A user can then tell which generation a local copy belongs to by hashing it, without relying on dates or file names.
path: 0008 — Bundles are the public record: immutability, archives, version lines and download metrics

items.title: (e) Parquet is derived, not a record
items.text:
Parquet is a convenience view of a bundle, not a record:

  • The docs and the manifests label it "derived from the bundle; may be regenerated".
  • Amended by ADR 0009. One Parquet dataset is published per line, at v1/1.1/parquet/, rebuilt from the newest release and overwritten every release. parquet/manifest.json beside it gives derived: true, the build_date, the source_release and dataset, the builder and table_spec_version (the tool version), the schema_version, and each file's size and sha256. There is no Parquet in archive/YYYY/, in frozen line folders (v1/1.0/ has none) or per delta. This reverses the 2026-10-18 decision to keep one Parquet set per archived generation.
  • A versioned Parquet rebuild tool, clinvar-gkm-parquet (planned), builds the Parquet tables from a published bundle. It is versioned on its own cadence, declares which bundle schema_versions it accepts, and the pipeline pins a version of it (ADR 0007, Workstream 1), so a user can rebuild the Parquet of any monthly with the tool version that matches.
  • Caveat: the 1.0.x Parquet was produced by BigQuery SQL from the dict tables, not from the bundle, so it cannot be reproduced bit-for-bit. So is the 1.1.0 Parquet, since Workstream 1 starts after 1.1.0 ships. The tool can rebuild the content of those sets from their bundles, not their bytes.
path: 0008 — Bundles are the public record: immutability, archives, version lines and download metrics

items.title: (f) Download metrics decide how far to go
items.text:
A daily collector stores per-path request counts, bytes served and distinct-client counts for data.clinvar-gkm.org (no IP addresses). Estimated complete downloads of a bundle = bytes served ÷ its size.

Retention and the shape of a switch-over are no longer metrics questions: frozen lines and archive/YYYY/ are kept indefinitely, and a breaking change freezes the old line at the switch-over (b). The metrics decide how far to go beyond that:

  • Promote a frozen line or monthly if it shows N or more estimated complete downloads in a calendar month: consider a citable copy (for example a DOI) for it.

N is the maintainer's decision. The first review is 60 days after collection starts (plan, task 7).
path: 0008 — Bundles are the public record: immutability, archives, version lines and download metrics

items.title: (g) Announcements
items.text: An advance notice before a republish or a switch-over is required once the email list has subscribers or after GA, whichever comes first. With 1.1.0 GA, every later republish into a new line and every switch-over gets an advance notice. 1.1.0 itself used a completion notice only (changelog, GitHub Release notes, Discussions); this amends the advance-notice requirement in ADR 0006's consequences.
path: 0008 — Bundles are the public record: immutability, archives, version lines and download metrics

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
• Storage. One frozen generation of bundles is about 24 GB (19 dated bundles, 19.3 GB, plus the 00-latest copies, 4.8 GB): about $0.36 a month at R2's $0.015/GB-month. Frozen lines are kept indefinitely, so this grows by one generation per new line. Only one Parquet dataset exists under (e), so dropping the dated Parquet sets saves about 65 GB. Weekly fulls add at most about 24 GB at the end of a month (ADR 0009). A v2/2.0/ line adds a full live line beside the frozen v1/ lines.
  • Operations. Each republish that replaces a line gains steps: freeze the old line folder, write and verify its MANIFEST.json, write its README.txt. Month and year rollovers move and delete files, and each move or delete is followed by a CDN purge of the old paths (ADR 0009). The uploaders and generate-r2-index.sh publish sha256, status / superseded_by, each monthly's source_release and the frozen lines in the root manifest (built in r2_layout.py, PR #182). A daily GitHub Actions job collects the download stats (secrets CF_ANALYTICS_TOKEN, CF_ZONE_ID); a missed day can be collected again only within the 31-day retention.
  • For users. A monthly or delta file keeps the same bytes and name, though its folder changes at month and year rollover; a weekly full is gone shortly after its month, and is rebuilt from a monthly plus deltas; a superseded generation stays available indefinitely as a frozen line folder (v1/1.0/); a checksum tells them which generation they hold; a frozen line says what replaced it; and they can rebuild Parquet from any monthly with clinvar-gkm-parquet.
  • Metric limits. Cloudflare's adaptive sampling makes counts estimates. Distinct clients are counted per day by IP, so NAT undercounts and roaming clients overcount. Bytes ÷ size counts two half downloads as one. Traffic before 2026-10-14 is not measurable.
  • Harder: from 1.1.0 (GA), a mistake in a published bundle can no longer be fixed quietly. It needs a new MINOR line (content-only, ADR 0009 §5) or a new MAJOR line (breaking), with an advance notice (g).
path: 0008 — Bundles are the public record: immutability, archives, version lines and download metrics

items.title: 0009 — R2 layout mirrors NCBI ClinVar
items.text:
• Status: Proposed
  • Date: 2026-10-20
  • Amends: ADR 0004 §4 (directories per version line) and §1 (a content-only correction that rewrites bundles takes a MINOR line, §5 below), ADR 0005 (cache rules, path allowlist, layout note), ADR 0006 (on PR #146) Decision 2 (1.1.0 ships under v1/1.1/, not in place in /v1/), ADR 0008 (a), (c), (e)
  • Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-18-bundle-record-and-metrics.md
  • Decided: 2026-10-21 (maintainer): §5 is no longer open. A content-only correction that rewrites published bundles is released as a new MINOR line folder; a PATCH only adds new dated files.
  • Amended: 2026-10-21 to match the layout code merged on 1.0 (PR #182: r2_layout.py, r2-rollover.sh, cf-rules.sh, run-release.sh): the finished month's newest weekly full is kept until the new month's monthly is published (§2, §3, §4); weekly/ is not cached as immutable (Consequences); file names, the root and line index.json, checkpoint_full and the Parquet manifest fields (§1, §2).

items.title: Context
items.text:
The published bundles are built from NCBI's ClinVar XML releases. NCBI publishes them in a layout ClinVar users already know:

NCBI path What it holds pub/clinvar/xml/ the current year's monthly releases (ClinVarVCVRelease_YYYY-MM.xml.gz) and ClinVarVCVRelease_00-latest.xml.gz xml/weekly_release/ the current month's weekly full releases and 00-latest_weekly; earlier weeks are removed xml/archive/YYYY/ the monthly releases of prior years

Every file has an .md5 sidecar, and every file name carries its date.

The ClinVar-GKM layout under /v1/ grew differently: datasets/ for monthly fulls, deltas/<YYYY-MMDD>/ directories each holding a bundle and a manifest.json, dated Parquet sets under datasets/parquet/, a prior-year archives/ folder, and a superseded generation copied to a root archive/1.0.1/ (ADR 0008 (c)). Three problems came with it:

  • No weekly full. A user who wanted the current week had to download the monthly full and replay deltas.
  • No place for a new MINOR. ADR 0004 §4 keys directories by MAJOR only, so the 1.1.0 republish would have rewritten /v1/ in place (ADR 0006) and pushed the 1.0.1 generation out to archive/1.0.1/.
  • Two replay defects. Every delta manifest's checkpoint_full named the newest monthly (2026-10), not the monthly its chain starts from, and nothing published which release a monthly full was built from. The documented replay also compared months, so it skipped deltas from the checkpoint's own month.

items.title: 1. Version folders
items.text:
Each version line has its own folder, v{major}/{major}.{minor}/, starting with v1/1.1/:

  • A PATCH release (1.1.x) only adds new dated files to the current line folder. It never rewrites a published file (§5).
  • A new MINOR starts a new folder (v1/1.2/); a new MAJOR starts v2/2.0/.
  • A folder that a newer line replaces is frozen and kept indefinitely (ADR 0008 (b)): nothing is added to it, moved in it or deleted from it.
  • The 1.0.1 generation, archived on 2026-10-18 to archive/1.0.1/, moves to the frozen line v1/1.0/.

The bucket-root index.json lists the lines: manifest_version: 2, current (the current line, "v1/1.1") and versions, keyed by line name ("1.1", "1.0"). Each entry gives line, major, minor, status ("current" or "frozen"), schema, superseded_by (the line that replaced it, such as "v1/1.1", or null), index and feed. There is no eol field. Consumers pick the entry whose status is "current".

Each line has its own index.json and feed.xml. A line's index.json carries the same line, status, superseded_by and schema_version, plus current_month, latest_release, datasets.monthly[], datasets.weekly[], deltas[], archives (keyed by year) and parquet (§2).

items.title: 2. The layout of a line
items.text:
v1/1.1/
  index.json, feed.xml, README.txt
  clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MM.json.gz              official monthly full (ADR 0002), current year
  clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MM.json.gz.sha256
  clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz            newest official monthly (same bytes), + .sha256
  weekly/
    clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MMDD.json.gz          weekly FULL bundle of the current month (§3), + .sha256
    clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz   newest weekly full (same bytes), + .sha256
  deltas/
    clinvar-gkm-delta_YYYY-MMDD.json.gz    current month's deltas
    clinvar-gkm-delta_YYYY-MMDD.json.gz.sha256
    clinvar-gkm-delta_YYYY-MMDD.manifest.json
    YYYY-MM/                               earlier months of the current year
  archive/YYYY/
    clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MM.json.gz            prior years' monthly fulls, + .sha256
    deltas/YYYY-MM/                        prior years' deltas
  parquet/                                 ONE Parquet dataset, overwritten every release
    {section}.parquet
    manifest.json

A frozen line keeps the shape it was frozen with. v1/1.0/ holds the monthlies 2026-07 to 2026-10 and clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz at the top, every delta under deltas/YYYY-MM/, and MANIFEST.json, README.txt, index.json and feed.xml. It has no weekly/ and no parquet/.

  • Checksums. Every bundle (dated, 00-latest, weekly and delta) has a <file>.sha256 sidecar in sha256sum -c format (<sha256> <file name>), the counterpart of NCBI's .md5. The line's index.json repeats each bundle's sha256 and size.
  • Monthlies. The official monthly clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MM is chosen as ADR 0002 says: the newest build before ClinVar's ClinVarVCVRelease_YYYY-MM datetime. run-release.sh publishes it as a server-side copy of that release's weekly full, or re-exports it from BigQuery if the weekly full is gone. Each monthly's source_release (the release it was built from) is published in the line's index.json, next to its release (the YYYY-MM label). The 00-latest copy is an entry with latest: true and the release it equals.
  • Weekly fulls are new. A full bundle is published for every weekly release. Only the current month's are kept, plus the finished month's newest one until the new month's official monthly is published (§3).
  • Deltas keep their manifests, now named clinvar-gkm-delta_YYYY-MMDD.manifest.json beside the bundle. Each manifest gains schema_version, bundle {name, path, size, sha256}, sha256 and checkpoint_full: the newest official monthly whose source_release is on or before the delta's baseline_release, so a replay can start from it. Its shape is {path, release, month, sha256}, where release is the monthly's source_release (comparable with baseline_release) and month is its YYYY-MM label.
  • Parquet is one dataset, rebuilt and overwritten every release from the newest release. parquet/manifest.json beside it gives derived: true, build_date, source_release, dataset, builder ("BigQuery export" until the tool ships), table_spec_version, schema_version, a note, and files[] with each file's name, size and sha256. The line's index.json summarizes it under parquet. No Parquet is kept anywhere else: not per month, not per delta, not in archive/ and not in frozen line folders. Past Parquet is rebuilt from the bundles with the clinvar-gkm-parquet tool (planned; until it ships, the 1.1.0 Parquet is exported by BigQuery).
  • Cleanup. Everything on R2 outside a published line and the root index.json is deleted: the old v1/datasets/, v1/deltas/ and dated Parquet trees, and archive/1.0.1/ once it has moved to v1/1.0/.

items.title: 3. Rollover triggers
items.text:
run-release.sh runs r2-rollover.sh before a release's weekly uploads and again after its monthly step. The plan comes from r2_layout.py (plan_rollover) and is idempotent: when the line already matches the layout, nothing happens.

Trigger What moves or goes The first release dated in a new month The finished month's deltas (bundle, .sha256, manifest) move from deltas/ into deltas/YYYY-MM/. The finished month's weekly fulls and their sidecars are deleted from weekly/, except the newest, which is kept until the new month's official monthly is published: it is that monthly's ADR 0002 source candidate, and the monthly is a server-side copy of it. The rollover that runs after the monthly is published deletes it. The first release dated in a new year The finished year's monthlies and sidecars move from the line's top level into archive/YYYY/, and its deltas/YYYY-MM/ folders move into archive/YYYY/deltas/YYYY-MM/. The month rollover runs too.

A move never changes a file's bytes, name or checksum, only its folder. The 00-latest pointers stay at their paths and are rewritten every release.

items.title: 4. Weekly fulls are deleted: an exception to immutability
items.text:
ADR 0008 (a) makes a published bundle immutable. Weekly fulls are a deliberate exception: they are a convenience copy of the current month, deleted at month rollover (the newest one once the next official monthly is published), as NCBI deletes its weekly releases. Nothing is lost: the official monthly is built from the newest release before ClinVar's monthly (ADR 0002), normally the finished month's last weekly, and any past week can be rebuilt exactly from a monthly plus deltas:

  1. Take the newest official monthly whose source_release ≤ the week W.
  2. Apply, in release order, every delta whose release is later than that source_release and ≤ W.
  3. Check the chain: the first delta's baseline_release equals the monthly's source_release, and each later delta's baseline_release equals the previous delta's release.

The monthlies and the deltas are the durable record.

items.title: 5. Content-only corrections open a new MINOR line
items.text: Decided 2026-10-21 by the maintainer. A correction that must rewrite published bundles without changing the schema shape (a content-only change, which ADR 0004 §1 does not count as a schema version change) is released as a new MINOR line folder: for example, 1.2.0 is published into v1/1.2/, and v1/1.1/ is frozen and kept (ADR 0008 (b), (c)). A PATCH (1.1.x) only ever adds new dated files to the current line folder and never rewrites one. This amends ADR 0004 §1 for that case: a release that rewrites published bundles takes a MINOR number even when the schema shape is unchanged. The new line's schema $id version and every bundle's schema_version move to that MINOR (for example 1.2.0) as well (decided 2026-10-22), so a bundle's schema_version always names the line folder it was published in.

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
• Familiar for ClinVar users. The monthly, weekly/ and archive/YYYY/ folders and the 00-latest / 00-latest_weekly names match NCBI's. deltas/ has no NCBI counterpart and is our addition.
  • URLs move; bytes do not. A delta URL changes when its month rolls over, and a monthly URL changes when its year rolls over. File names and .sha256 stay the same, so a downloaded copy can still be identified. Scripts should resolve paths through the line's index.json, not hard-code them. A path written into an older delta manifest (checkpoint_full.path) can point at a monthly's pre-move location; resolve it by its release. The delta manifests in the frozen v1/1.0/ keep their 1.0.1 bytes, so their paths name the old v1/datasets/ and v1/deltas/ keys and their checkpoint_full always says 2026-10; use that line's index.json (each monthly's source_release) instead.
  • CDN purges. r2-rollover.sh purges every path it moved or deleted, or the edge would keep serving a moved small file for up to the 1-month immutable TTL (ADR 0005). run-release.sh purges the parquet/ prefix after every Parquet rebuild. The one-time 1.1.0 migration (republish-v1.sh) ends with a full purge; each of its steps is user-confirmed, with a dry run first. The rollover itself runs inside run-release.sh; --dry-run or --listing shows its plan first.
  • Cache rules. src/scripts/cf-rules.sh holds the expressions (show is read-only; apply is a user-confirmed step). Three cache rules, in this order; the last matching rule wins:
  • "R2 immutable artifacts" matches every path on data.clinvar-gkm.org: edge 1 month, browser 1 day. In effect it covers whatever rules 2 and 3 do not: dated monthlies, deltas, delta manifests and .sha256 sidecars outside weekly/, everything in archive/YYYY/, and frozen line folders' bundles and MANIFEST.json. These are write-once at their path; a rollover moves them to new keys and purges the old ones.
  • "R2 mutable pointers" bypasses the cache for any path containing 00-latest (which also matches clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz), ending in /index.json, /feed.xml or /README.txt, or containing /weekly/. Weekly fulls and their sidecars are not cached as immutable, because the rollover deletes them.
  • "Latest Parquet" matches any path under /v1/ containing /parquet/ (the dataset and its manifest.json): edge 1 day, browser 1 hour (ADR 0005), purged after every rebuild. It replaces the rule that matched /v1/datasets/parquet/00-latest/, which no longer exists.

Bundles larger than 512 MB are never cached on the Free plan (ADR 0005), so these rules matter mostly for sidecars, manifests, indexes and Parquet. - Path allowlist. Every published path stays under /v1/, so the WAF path allowlist needs no new prefix. /archive/ can be dropped from it once archive/1.0.1/ has moved (cf-rules.sh apply --drop-archive). - Storage. Weekly fulls add up to five bundles of about 4.8 GB each at the end of a month, about $0.36 a month at most. Dropping the dated Parquet sets saves about 65 GB. - Tools that read the layout (the docs download browser, the DuckDB console, generate-r2-index.sh, the uploaders, clinvar-gkm-parquet) change with it. - ADR 0008 is amended: the immutability exception for weekly fulls, archives as archive/YYYY/ inside a line, the 1.0.1 generation as v1/1.0/, and one overwritten Parquet dataset with no Parquet in archives.

items.title: Output Reference
items.text:
The ClinVar-GKM pipeline produces a single compressed JSON file per release, containing all variant representations, clinical classification statements, and supporting reference data. This section documents the output from a consumer perspective — how the file is structured, what each section contains, and how to interpret the data.

For details on how the output is built, see the Pipeline documentation.

items.title: Release Format
items.text:
Each release is available as a gzip-compressed JSON file (.json.gz) containing a root-level object with bundle sections, and optionally as a set of typed Parquet files (one per section). Each bundle section is a keyed collection — the key is the object's unique identifier, and the value is the complete object.

See Output Format Overview for a detailed guide to the bundle structure, reference patterns, and how to navigate between sections.

items.title: Sections
items.text: Section Content Key Format sequenceReference VRS sequence references SQ.{digest} location VRS sequence locations ga4gh:SL.{digest} allele VRS alleles with expressions ga4gh:VA.{digest} copyNumberCount Copy number count variants clinvar:{id} copyNumberChange Copy number change variants clinvar:{id} gene Gene MappableConcepts ncbigene:{id} variation Cat-VRS categorical variants clinvar:{variation_id} condition Trait/disease concepts clinvar.trait:{id} conditionSet Multi-condition groupings clinvar.traitset:{id} submitter Submitting organizations clinvar.submitter:{id} proposition Classification propositions {scv_id}-{CODE} / {vcv_id}-{group}-{prop}-{level} evidenceLine Evidence lines (SCV, VCV, RCV) {id}.contributing / {scv_id}.{ver} scv Submitted classifications clinvar.submission:{scv_id}.{version} vcv Variation-level aggregates {vcv_id}-{group}-{prop}-{level} rcv Condition-level aggregates {rcv_id}-{group}-{prop}-{level}

items.title: Format Conventions
items.text:
• Null stripping — null-valued fields and empty arrays/objects are omitted from the output
  • GA4GH identifiers — VRS identifiers use the ga4gh: prefix (e.g., ga4gh:VA.abc123)
  • ClinVar identifiers — ClinVar-scoped identifiers use the clinvar: prefix (e.g., clinvar:12345)
  • JSON pointer references — objects reference each other using #/{section}/{key} strings (e.g., #/allele/ga4gh:VA.abc123)

items.title: Cross-Section References
items.text:
Objects reference each other using #/ JSON pointer strings rather than embedding full objects. This keeps the file compact and avoids duplication. For example:

  • A variation references its allele as #/allele/ga4gh:VA.abc123
  • An SCV statement references its proposition as #/propositionPathogenicity/SCV001234567-PATH (propositions are delivered in four sections grouped by meaning — propositionPathogenicity, propositionOncogenicity, propositionSomaticClinicalImpact, propositionClinvarCustom)
  • A VCV evidence line references its contributing SCVs as #/scv/clinvar.submission:SCV001234567.1

See ID References for the complete reference format guide, identifier patterns, and resolution rules.

items.title: Specifications
items.text:
The output conforms to these GA4GH standards:

  • VRS 2.0 — Variation Representation Specification for allele and copy number representations
  • Cat-VRS — Categorical Variation for grouping variants at a higher categorical level
  • VA-Spec — Variant Annotation Specification for clinical variant statements

items.title: Overview
items.text:
The variation bundle section contains one record per ClinVar variation. Each record represents a ClinVar variation and its relationship to a resolved VRS genomic identity, along with expressions, cross-references, gene associations, and ClinVar metadata.

ClinVar variations are represented using the GA4GH Cat-VRS (Categorical Variation) specification. Cat-VRS defines categorical variant types that group variants at a higher level than individual VRS alleles — bridging the gap between ClinVar's variation concept and VRS's precise genomic representations.

This section is produced by the Cat-VRS procedure.

items.title: Variation Types
items.text:
ClinVar variations map to three Cat-VRS representation types:

  • CanonicalAllele — The vast majority of ClinVar variations. ClinVar identifies each variation by mapping submitted variant attributes to a GRCh38 genomic allele (falling back to GRCh37 or NCBI36 for historical data). This defining allele becomes the DefiningAlleleConstraint, and the same genomic allele generates the VRS allele referenced via #/allele/. See the Cat-VRS CanonicalAllele specification.

  • CategoricalCnvCount / CategoricalCnvChange — Copy number variants use a DefiningLocationConstraint following the same identification approach, with an additional CopyCountConstraint when an absolute copy count is provided, or a CopyChangeConstraint when only gain/loss is indicated.

  • Generalized Categorical Variant — Haplotypes, genotypes, and other complex or ambiguously defined variants that cannot yet be mapped to a specific VRS allele or location. These rely solely on the ClinVar variation ID to distinguish them. Work continues within the GA4GH GKS workstream to expand VRS and Cat-VRS coverage for these types as community need arises.

items.title: Record Structure
items.text:
Each record is a CategoricalVariant with the following top-level fields:

Field Type Description id string ClinVar-scoped identifier — clinvar:{variation_id} type string Always CategoricalVariant name string Best available HGVS expression for the variant constraints array Defining constraints linking to the resolved VRS variant. See Constraints mappings array Cross-references to external databases. See Mappings members array #/allele/ references to the defining VRS allele (empty for generalized variants) extensions array of Extension ClinVar-specific metadata and supplementary data (0..*). See Extensions

items.title: Constraints
items.text:
The constraints array defines the relationship between the variation and its resolved VRS representation. The constraint type depends on the variant class:

Variation Type Constraint Type Key Fields CanonicalAllele DefiningAlleleConstraint allele — #/allele/{id} reference to a VRS Allele CategoricalCnvChange DefiningLocationConstraint + CopyChangeConstraint location — #/location/{id} reference; copyChange — gain/loss CategoricalCnvCount DefiningLocationConstraint + CopyCountConstraint location — #/location/{id} reference; copies — integer or range Generalized None No VRS constraint — identified by ClinVar variation ID only

items.title: Allele Constraint Example
items.text:
The DefiningAlleleConstraint references a VRS Allele in the allele bundle section:

{
  "type": "DefiningAlleleConstraint",
  "allele": "#/allele/ga4gh:VA.ELQCnIBGqaTl0AEE0Az18XZ2cgIHAQIY",
  "relations": [
    { "primaryCoding": { "code": "liftover_to", "system": "ga4gh-gks-term:allele-relation" } },
    { "primaryCoding": { "code": "transcribed_to", "system": "http://www.sequenceontology.org" } }
  ]
}

items.title: Location Constraint Example
items.text:
The DefiningLocationConstraint for copy number variants references a VRS Location:

{
  "type": "DefiningLocationConstraint",
  "location": "#/location/ga4gh:SL.5-SKfXZ941W7JbZW3UmQKtijyUfd6d7z",
  "matchCharacteristic": {
    "primaryCoding": { "code": "is_within", "system": "ga4gh-gks-term:location-match" }
  },
  "relations": [
    { "primaryCoding": { "code": "liftover_to", "system": "ga4gh-gks-term:allele-relation" } }
  ]
}

items.title: Mappings
items.text:
The mappings array contains cross-references to external databases. Each mapping includes a coding (database, identifier, IRIs) and a relation:

Relation Meaning exactMatch The ClinVar self-reference — links back to the ClinVar variation page closeMatch ClinGen allele registry identifiers relatedMatch All other external databases (dbSNP, OMIM, UniProtKB, GTR, PharmGKB, etc.)

items.title: Example
items.text:
{
  "coding": {
    "system": "https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/snp/",
    "code": "1799945",
    "iris": ["https://identifiers.org/dbsnp:rs1799945"]
  },
  "relation": "relatedMatch"
}

items.title: Extensions
items.text:
Extensions carry ClinVar-specific metadata not part of the core Cat-VRS specification. Each extension follows the GA4GH Extension structure: { "name": "<name>", "value": <value> }. Extensions appear at two structural levels — on the top-level CategoricalVariant record and on nested SequenceReference objects.

See Categorical Variant Extensions (Pipeline) for details on how these extensions are built during pipeline processing.

items.title: CategoricalVariant Extensions
items.text: Extension Name Value Type Description categoricalVariationType string The Cat-VRS category assigned to this variation: CanonicalAllele, CategoricalCnvChange, CategoricalCnvCount, or Undefined. Determines which constraint types are generated. definingVrsVariationType string The VRS class assigned during variation identity processing (e.g., Allele, CopyNumberChange, CopyNumberCount, Not Available). Reflects the upstream classification used to route the variant through VRS processing. clinvarVariationType string The variation type as reported by ClinVar (e.g., Deletion, single nucleotide variant, Duplication, Indel). Present when ClinVar provides a variation type. clinvarSubclassType string The variation subclass as reported by ClinVar (e.g., SimpleAllele, Haplotype, CompoundHeterozygote). Present when ClinVar provides a subclass type. clinvarCytogeneticLocation string The cytogenetic band location of the variation (e.g., 1p36.22, 17q21.31). Present when ClinVar provides a cytogenetic location. vrsPreProcessingIssue string Issues detected during VRS pre-processing of the variation's input expressions. Present only when issues exist. May contain multiple issues separated by newlines. vrsProcessingException string Errors returned by the external VRS Python processing service. Present only when errors occurred during VRS resolution. clinvarHgvsList array of HgvsListItem Complete list of HGVS expressions from ClinVar for this variation, including nucleotide and protein expressions, molecular consequences (SO terms), and MANE transcript designations. clinvarGeneList array of GeneListItem Gene associations for this variation from ClinVar, with #/gene/ references to gene MappableConcepts, relationship types, and sources.

items.title: SequenceReference Extensions
items.text:
Extensions on SequenceReference objects nested within constraints[].allele.location.sequenceReference and members[].location.sequenceReference.

Extension Name Value Type Description assembly string The genome assembly name for this sequence reference (e.g., GRCh38, GRCh37, NCBI36).

items.title: HgvsListItem
items.text:
Each item in the clinvarHgvsList extension array represents one HGVS expression entry from ClinVar's HGVSlist element for the variation.

Field Type Description nucleotideExpression object The nucleotide HGVS expression with syntax (e.g., hgvs.c, hgvs.g) and value (the HGVS string). From 1.1.0, when ClinVar supplies an expression with no HGVS type letter, its submitted text is kept, unaltered, in this expression's extensions: invalidClinvarExpression (the submitted text) with expressionMerged: true when ClinVar also supplies a valid expression for the accession, which is the one listed; otherwise originalClinvarExpression (the submitted text) with expressionRepaired: true, on a listed expression with the type letter restored. nucleotideType string The type of nucleotide expression as reported by ClinVar (e.g., coding, genomic, genomic, top-level). maneSelect boolean true if this transcript is designated as MANE Select. Absent when not applicable. manePlus boolean true if this transcript is designated as MANE Plus Clinical. Absent when not applicable. proteinExpression object The protein HGVS expression with syntax (typically hgvs.p) and value. Present only when a protein-level expression exists for the nucleotide expression. molecularConsequence array Sequence Ontology terms describing the predicted molecular consequence. Each entry includes code (SO identifier), system, name (SO term label), and iris (identifiers.org link).

items.title: GeneListItem
items.text:
Each item in the clinvarGeneList extension array represents one gene association for the variation. Gene details (symbol, NCBI Gene ID, HGNC mapping) are on the referenced gene MappableConcept in the gene bundle section.

Field Type Description gene string #/gene/ncbigene:{id} reference to the gene MappableConcept in the gene bundle section. relationship_type string The relationship between the variation and the gene as reported by ClinVar (e.g., within single gene, genes overlapped by variant). source string The source of the gene association (e.g., submitted, calculated).

items.title: Examples
items.text:
Annotated JSONC examples of variation records are available in the repository:

  • Cat-VRS examples — CanonicalAllele records for ClinVar variations

items.title: Overview
items.text: The ClinVar-GKM bundle uses typed identifiers and #/ JSON pointer references to link objects across bundle sections. This page documents all identifier formats, reference patterns, and how to resolve them.

items.title: Identifier Namespaces
items.text:
All ClinVar-GKM identifiers use a prefix namespace to indicate the resource type:

Prefix Resource Type Format Example clinvar: Variation clinvar:{variation_id} clinvar:12582 clinvar.submission: SCV submission clinvar.submission:SCV{id}.{version} clinvar.submission:SCV001571657.2 clinvar.submitter: Submitter organization clinvar.submitter:{submitter_id} clinvar.submitter:508027 clinvar.trait: Condition / trait clinvar.trait:{trait_id} clinvar.trait:9580 clinvar.traitset: Condition set clinvar.traitset:{trait_set_id} clinvar.traitset:1234 clinvar.conditionset: Condition set minted for a VCV aggregate clinvar.conditionset:vcv-{md5} clinvar.conditionset:vcv-c620785e2025efde81bdd15c814fa83d clinvar.therapy: Therapy (drug/procedure) clinvar.therapy:{sha256} clinvar.therapy:ab221549…d1c2b clinvar.therapygroup: Therapy group (combination) clinvar.therapygroup:{sha256} clinvar.therapygroup:df1d8467…9f05c ncbigene: Gene ncbigene:{gene_id} ncbigene:3077 ga4gh: VRS identity ga4gh:{type}.{digest} ga4gh:VA.ELQCnIBGqaTl0AEE0Az18XZ2cgIHAQIY SQ. Sequence reference SQ.{digest} SQ.0iKlIQk2oZLoeOG9P1riRU6hvL5Ux8TV

VCV and RCV aggregate statement IDs use a hierarchical format without a namespace prefix — see VCV Statement IDs and RCV Statement IDs.

items.title: JSON Pointer References
items.text:
Objects reference each other using #/{section}/{key} strings. To resolve a reference:

  1. Split the string on / — the second segment is the bundle section name, the third is the key
  2. Look up the key in the named section of the bundle

items.title: Reference Patterns
items.text: Pattern Example Target Section #/sequenceReference/{key} #/sequenceReference/SQ.0iKlIQk2oZLoeOG9P1riRU6hvL5Ux8TV sequenceReference #/location/{key} #/location/ga4gh:SL.Eg_6kV6Bb4FMjm9kEolHZ_4NhU8lBEsZ location #/allele/{key} #/allele/ga4gh:VA.ELQCnIBGqaTl0AEE0Az18XZ2cgIHAQIY allele #/gene/{key} #/gene/ncbigene:3077 gene #/variation/{key} #/variation/clinvar:10 variation #/condition/{key} #/condition/clinvar.trait:9580 condition #/conditionSet/{key} #/conditionSet/clinvar.traitset:1234 conditionSet #/therapy/{key} #/therapy/clinvar.therapy:ab221549…d1c2b therapy #/therapyGroup/{key} #/therapyGroup/clinvar.therapygroup:df1d8467…9f05c therapyGroup #/submitter/{key} #/submitter/clinvar.submitter:500139 submitter #/propositionPathogenicity/{key} #/propositionPathogenicity/SCV001234567-PATH propositionPathogenicity #/propositionOncogenicity/{key} #/propositionOncogenicity/SCV002345678-ONCO propositionOncogenicity #/propositionSomaticClinicalImpact/{key} #/propositionSomaticClinicalImpact/SCV003456789-TR propositionSomaticClinicalImpact #/propositionClinvarCustom/{key} #/propositionClinvarCustom/SCV004567890-RF propositionClinvarCustom #/scv/{key} #/scv/clinvar.submission:SCV001234567.1 scv #/vcv/{key} #/vcv/VCV000012582.63-G-PATH-CP vcv #/evidenceLine/{key} #/evidenceLine/VCV000012582.63-G-PATH-CP.contributing evidenceLine #/rcv/{key} #/rcv/RCV000012345.8-G-PATH-CP rcv

items.title: Where References Appear
items.text:
Object Type Field References Location sequenceReference #/sequenceReference/ Allele location #/location/ Variation members[] #/allele/ Variation constraints[].allele #/allele/ Variation constraints[].location #/location/ Variation extensions[].clinvarGeneList[].gene #/gene/ Proposition (all types) subject #/variation/ Pathogenicity / Oncogenicity / Custom / Diagnostic / Prognostic object #/condition/ or #/conditionSet/ Therapeutic Response object #/therapy/ or #/therapyGroup/ Therapeutic Response conditionQualifier #/condition/ or #/conditionSet/ ConditionSet concepts[] #/condition/, or #/conditionSet/ for a TraitSet nested in a minted vcv- set TherapyGroup concepts[] #/therapy/ SCV Statement proposition #/proposition{Pathogenicity,Oncogenicity,SomaticClinicalImpact,ClinvarCustom}/ SCV Statement contributions[].contributor #/submitter/ VCV Statement proposition #/proposition{Pathogenicity,Oncogenicity,SomaticClinicalImpact,ClinvarCustom}/ SCV Statement hasEvidenceLines[] #/evidenceLine/ VCV Statement hasEvidenceLines[] #/evidenceLine/ RCV Statement proposition #/proposition{Pathogenicity,Oncogenicity,SomaticClinicalImpact,ClinvarCustom}/ RCV Statement hasEvidenceLines[] #/evidenceLine/ EvidenceLine hasEvidenceItems[] #/scv/, #/vcv/, or #/rcv/

Releases before 1.1.0 had two bare-id references

From 1.1.0 every field above is a #/ pointer. Before, two condition references were bare ids: a VCV proposition's object when the VCV had a single condition (clinvar.trait:2478 rather than #/condition/clinvar.trait:2478; about 7.5 million propositions), and the concepts of the condition sets minted for VCV aggregates (clinvar.conditionset:vcv-…). A bare id names the same record: look up clinvar.trait: ids in condition and clinvar.traitset: ids in conditionSet. A bundle downloaded before the 1.1.0 republish still has the old form.

The condition, conditionSet, direct_match and normalized_match values in the submittedCondition and submittedConditionSet extensions are bare CURIEs by design. They record what was submitted and how it was matched; they are not references.

items.title: Resolution Example
items.text:
import gzip
import json

# Load the bundle
with gzip.open("clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz", "rt") as f:
    bundle = json.load(f)

def resolve(bundle, ref):
    """Resolve a #/section/key reference to the target object."""
    parts = ref.lstrip("#/").split("/", 1)
    return bundle[parts[0]][parts[1]]

# Look up a variation
variant = bundle["variation"]["clinvar:10"]

# Resolve its allele member
allele = resolve(bundle, variant["members"][0])

# Resolve the allele's location
location = resolve(bundle, allele["location"])

# Resolve the location's sequence reference
seq_ref = resolve(bundle, location["sequenceReference"])

Resolving references without writing code

The GKM Toolkit (ga4gh.gkm) loads a published bundle and follows #/… pointers for you — traversing and exporting connected records without the manual resolve() above.

items.title: SCV Proposition IDs
items.text:
SCV proposition IDs combine the SCV accession with an uppercase proposition type code:

{scv_id}-{PROP_CODE}
Component Description Examples scv_id SCV accession (without version) SCV001234567 PROP_CODE Uppercase proposition type code PATH, ONCO, SCI, ASSOC, RF, DR, NP, OTH, PROTECT, AFF, CS, CDFS, UNDEF

Examples: SCV001234567-PATH, SCV004565358-PROG, SCV004565358-TR

Target (somatic evidence line) propositions use the clinical impact assertion type codes: PROG, DIAG, TR.

items.title: VCV Statement IDs
items.text:
VCV aggregate statements use a hierarchical ID format reflecting the aggregation layer:

Layer Format Example Classification {VCV}.{ver}-{group}-{PROP}-{level}[-{TIER}] VCV000012582.63-G-PATH-CP Priority {VCV}.{ver}-{group}-{PROP}-{level} VCV000012582.63-S-SCI-CP Aggregate {VCV}.{ver}-{group}-{PROP} VCV000012582.63-G-PATH

Components:

  • group — statement group: G (Germline), S (Somatic), O (Oncogenicity)
  • PROP — proposition type code (uppercase): PATH, ONCO, SCI, ASSOC, etc.
  • level — submission level: PG, EP, CP, NOCP, NOCL, FLAG
  • TIER — classification tier (somatic only, uppercase): TIER 1, TIER 2, etc.

items.title: RCV Statement IDs
items.text:
RCV aggregate statements follow the same pattern as VCV but with an RCV accession:

Layer Format Example Classification {RCV}.{ver}-{group}-{PROP}-{level}[-{TIER}] RCV000012345.10-G-PATH-CP Priority {RCV}.{ver}-{group}-{PROP}-{level} RCV000012345.10-S-SCI-CP Aggregate {RCV}.{ver}-{group}-{PROP} RCV000012345.10-G-PATH

The component abbreviations are the same as VCV.

items.title: VCV/RCV Proposition IDs
items.text:
VCV and RCV proposition IDs use the accession (without version) in the same layered format:

Layer Format Example Classification {accession}-{group}-{PROP}-{level}[-{TIER}] VCV000012582-G-PATH-CP Priority {accession}-{group}-{PROP}-{level} VCV000012582-S-SCI-CP Aggregate {accession}-{group}-{PROP} VCV000012582-G-PATH

items.title: External Cross-References
items.text:
Variation records contain mappings to external databases using standardized URL formats:

Database URL Pattern MedGen https://identifiers.org/medgen:{id} OMIM http://www.omim.org/entry/{id} HPO https://identifiers.org/{id} MONDO https://identifiers.org/mondo:{id} Orphanet http://www.orpha.net/ORDO/Orphanet_{id} dbSNP https://identifiers.org/dbsnp:rs{id} ClinGen https://reg.clinicalgenome.org/.../by_caid?caid={id} UniProtKB https://www.uniprot.org/uniprot/{id} GTR https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gtr/tests/{id} PubMed https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/{id}

Condition records contain mappings to disease/phenotype databases (OMIM, MONDO, HPO, Orphanet, MeSH) and a primaryCoding from MedGen.

items.title: Output "Bundle" Format Overview
items.text:
The ClinVar-GKM release file uses a bundle format — a single JSON object with named sections at the root level. A bundle is a dictionary-style approach to organizing a large amount of data across heterogeneous classes in a single file, where each section is a keyed collection of objects of the same class. The key is the object's unique identifier, and the value is the complete object.

This design eliminates duplication (a sequence reference shared by thousands of locations appears once), keeps individual objects compact, and enables efficient lookups by ID.

items.title: Structure
items.text:
{
  "sequenceReference": { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "location":          { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "allele":            { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "copyNumberCount":   { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "copyNumberChange":  { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "gene":              { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "variation":         { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "condition":         { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "conditionSet":      { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "therapy":           { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "therapyGroup":      { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "submitter":            { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "propositionPathogenicity":         { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "propositionOncogenicity":          { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "propositionSomaticClinicalImpact": { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "propositionClinvarCustom":         { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "evidenceLine":         { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "scv":               { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "vcv":               { "<key>": { ... }, ... },
  "rcv":               { "<key>": { ... }, ... }
}

items.title: Variation Data Sections
items.text:
These sections contain the VRS and Cat-VRS variant data:

sequenceReference — Reference sequences (chromosomes, transcripts) with refget accessions, molecule type, and assembly information. Keyed by refget accession (e.g., SQ.0iKlIQk2oZLoeOG9P1riRU6hvL5Ux8TV).

location — Sequence locations with start/end coordinates. Each location references its sequence via #/sequenceReference/{key}. Keyed by VRS location ID (e.g., ga4gh:SL.Eg_6kV6Bb4FMjm9kEolHZ_4NhU8lBEsZ).

allele — VRS alleles with state, expressions (SPDI, HGVS, gnomAD), and copy number data. Each allele references its location via #/location/{key}. Keyed by VRS allele ID (e.g., ga4gh:VA.ELQCnIBGqaTl0AEE0Az18XZ2cgIHAQIY).

copyNumberCount — VRS CopyNumberCount records for copy number variants with absolute copy counts. Each references its location via #/location/{key}. Keyed by VRS ID.

copyNumberChange — VRS CopyNumberChange records for copy number variants with relative change types (gain, loss). Each references its location via #/location/{key}. Keyed by VRS ID.

gene — Gene MappableConcepts with NCBI Gene primaryCoding and HGNC mapping. Keyed by ncbigene:{gene_id} (e.g., ncbigene:3077).

variation — ClinVar variations with their defining constraints, cross-references, HGVS expressions, and gene associations. Most variations are represented as CanonicalAlleles with a defining VRS allele (via #/allele/); copy number variants use a defining location (via #/location/); complex variants use a generalized representation. Keyed by clinvar:{variation_id} (e.g., clinvar:10).

items.title: Supporting Data Sections
items.text:
These sections contain the condition, therapy, submitter, and proposition reference data:

condition — Trait and disease concepts from ClinVar, with MedGen primary coding and cross-references to OMIM, MONDO, HPO, Orphanet, and MeSH. Keyed by clinvar.trait:{trait_id} (e.g., clinvar.trait:9580).

conditionSet — Multi-condition groupings with member condition references (concepts → #/condition/) and a membership operator (AND or OR). Keyed by clinvar.traitset:{trait_set_id} (e.g., clinvar.traitset:1234).

therapy — Individual drug therapies (Therapy MappableConcepts) referenced by therapeutic-response propositions. Content-addressed and deduplicated (therapies have no native ClinVar id). Keyed by clinvar.therapy:{sha256}.

therapyGroup — Combination (multi-drug) therapies (TherapyGroup ConceptSets) whose concepts reference member therapies via #/therapy/, with a membership operator. Content-addressed and deduplicated. Keyed by clinvar.therapygroup:{sha256}.

submitter — Submitting organizations with name and identifier. Keyed by clinvar.submitter:{submitter_id} (e.g., clinvar.submitter:500139).

propositionPathogenicity, propositionOncogenicity, propositionSomaticClinicalImpact, propositionClinvarCustom — Classification propositions defining what a statement asserts (proposition type, predicate, subject, object, qualifiers). Propositions are delivered in four sections grouped by meaning (what kind of claim the proposition makes), so a section holds one kind of claim at every level (SCV, VCV, RCV):

  • propositionPathogenicity — VariantPathogenicityProposition (germline classifications); subject → object (a #/condition/ or #/conditionSet/), with typed qualifiers on SCVs (geneContextQualifier, modeOfInheritanceQualifier, penetranceQualifier).
  • propositionOncogenicity — VariantOncogenicityProposition; subject → object (the tumor type, a #/condition/ or #/conditionSet/).
  • propositionSomaticClinicalImpact — VariantClinicalSignificanceProposition (SCV, VCV, RCV) and the VariantDiagnosticProposition, VariantPrognosticProposition and VariantTherapeuticResponseProposition that SCV evidence lines target. For Therapeutic Response, object references the therapy (#/therapy/ single, or #/therapyGroup/ combination) and the condition moves to conditionQualifier (#/condition/ or #/conditionSet/); the others point object at a condition.
  • propositionClinvarCustom — the 9 Clinvar* types (e.g. ClinvarRiskFactorProposition, ClinvarDrugResponseProposition) plus ClinvarUndefinedProposition — open subtypes of the VA-Spec SubjectVariantProposition base, each carrying its own real type name; subject → object with typed qualifiers (geneContextQualifier, modeOfInheritanceQualifier, penetranceQualifier).

Each contains the SCV, VCV, and RCV propositions of its kind. Keyed by proposition ID (e.g., SCV001234567-PATH for SCVs, VCV000012582.63-G-PATH-CP for VCVs). A #/proposition<Meaning>/{id} pointer names the exact section a proposition lives in; the section is a function of the proposition type alone.

items.title: Statement Sections
items.text:
These sections contain the classification statements:

evidenceLine — Evidence line records referenced by statements via hasEvidenceLines arrays of #/evidenceLine/ pointers. Merges SCV, VCV, and RCV evidence lines into a single section.

scv — Submitted classification statements. Each SCV carries a classification, strength, direction, proposition reference, contributions (with submitter references), evidence line references, citations, assertion method, and extensions with submitted condition provenance. Keyed by clinvar.submission:{scv_id}.{version}.

vcv — Variation-level aggregate classification statements. VCVs aggregate SCVs across a variation by classification, priority (somatic tiers), and submission level contribution. Evidence line references point to records in #/evidenceLine/. Keyed by the VCV layer ID.

rcv — Condition-level aggregate classification statements. RCVs follow the same aggregation structure as VCVs but are scoped to a specific RCV accession (variation + condition). Evidence line references point to records in #/evidenceLine/.

items.title: JSON Pointer References
items.text: Objects reference each other using #/{section}/{key} strings instead of embedding full objects inline. This keeps the file compact and enables consumers to resolve references by looking up the key in the named section.

items.title: Reference Patterns
items.text: Pattern Example Resolves To #/sequenceReference/{key} #/sequenceReference/SQ.0iKlIQk2oZLoeOG9P1riRU6hvL5Ux8TV Sequence reference object #/location/{key} #/location/ga4gh:SL.Eg_6kV6Bb4FMjm9kEolHZ_4NhU8lBEsZ Sequence location object #/allele/{key} #/allele/ga4gh:VA.ELQCnIBGqaTl0AEE0Az18XZ2cgIHAQIY VRS allele object #/gene/{key} #/gene/ncbigene:3077 Gene object #/variation/{key} #/variation/clinvar:10 Categorical variant object #/condition/{key} #/condition/clinvar.trait:9580 Condition object #/conditionSet/{key} #/conditionSet/clinvar.traitset:1234 Condition set object #/submitter/{key} #/submitter/clinvar.submitter:500139 Submitter object #/propositionPathogenicity/{key} #/propositionPathogenicity/SCV001234567-PATH Proposition object (pathogenicity) #/propositionOncogenicity/{key} #/propositionOncogenicity/SCV002345678-ONCO Proposition object (oncogenicity) #/propositionSomaticClinicalImpact/{key} #/propositionSomaticClinicalImpact/SCV003456789-TR Proposition object (somatic clinical impact) #/propositionClinvarCustom/{key} #/propositionClinvarCustom/SCV004567890-RF Proposition object (ClinVar custom) #/scv/{key} #/scv/clinvar.submission:SCV001234567.1 SCV statement object #/vcv/{key} #/vcv/VCV000012582.63-G-PATH-CP VCV statement object #/rcv/{key} #/rcv/RCV000012345.8-G-PATH-CP RCV statement object

items.title: Resolving References
items.text:
To resolve a reference string like #/allele/ga4gh:VA.abc123:

  1. Split on / — the second segment is the section name (allele), the third is the key (ga4gh:VA.abc123)
  2. Look up the key in the named section of the root object
  3. The value at that key is the resolved object

items.title: Reference Depth
items.text: References are one level deep — a resolved object may itself contain references, but those are always to other root-level sections, never nested references within references. A consumer can fully resolve any object by following at most 2-3 hops (e.g., variation → allele → location → sequenceReference).

items.title: MappableConcept Pattern
items.text:
Several fields across statements use a MappableConcept structure — a typed object with a display name, optional primary coding, and optional extensions:

{
  "conceptType": "Classification",
  "name": "Pathogenic",
  "primaryCoding": {
    "code": "pathogenic",
    "system": "ACMG Guidelines, 2015"
  },
  "extensions": [ ... ]
}

Fields that use this pattern:

  • classification — the clinical significance label (conceptType: "Classification")
  • strength — the evidence strength (conceptType: "Strength")
  • evidenceOutcome — the evidence line outcome (conceptType: "Outcome")
  • strengthOfEvidenceProvided — the evidence line strength (conceptType: "Strength")

The conceptType identifies the kind of concept. The name is the human-readable display value. The primaryCoding provides a machine-readable code and system when available. Not all instances carry primaryCoding — aggregate VCV/RCV classifications, for example, may only have conceptType and name.

items.title: Bundle Schema
items.text:
The bundle structure described above is formalized as a JSON Schema, authored to the GKM Starter Kit bundle-schema conventions:

JSON Schema: clinvar-gkm-bundle.schema.json

  • Draft 2020-12, root type: object — each root property is one of the bundle sections, and additionalProperties: false rejects unknown sections.
  • Each section is a keyed map whose keys are constrained by that section's id pattern (patternProperties) and whose values $ref the appropriate GA4GH class schema by versioned W3ID URI — VRS, Cat-VRS, VA-Spec, and GKM-Core for the shared types, and the ClinVar-GKM subtypes (ClinvarScvStatement, ClinvarCategoricalVariant, the Clinvar*Proposition family, …) for the ClinVar-specific ones.
  • No section is individually required, so the same schema validates a monthly full bundle, a weekly delta, and a sub-bundle extract — each carries only the sections it touches.

The schema constrains the bundle's shape (which sections may appear, how their keys are formed, and what each value validates against). The starter-kit's companion invariant — that every #/section/key pointer resolves within the bundle — is a producer-side guarantee, not expressible in JSON Schema alone.

items.title: Validating with the GKM Toolkit
items.text:
The GKM Toolkit (ga4gh.gkm) validates a bundle against this schema directly. It resolves the W3ID $ref URIs to the actual VRS / VA-Spec / GKM-Core class schemas and expands the bundle-local #/… pointers before validating, so each section's objects are checked against their full class definition rather than their serialized pointer strings:

import json
from ga4gh.gkm.bundles.schema_validation import (
    prepare_bundle_schema,
    validate_bundle_schema,
)

schema = json.load(open("clinvar-gkm-bundle.schema.json"))

# Validate one bundle — raises on any violation, returns None on success.
bundle = json.load(open("clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json"))
validate_bundle_schema(bundle, schema)

# Or compile the validator once and reuse it across many bundles / deltas.
validator = prepare_bundle_schema(schema)
for path in ("clinvar-gkm_2026-10.json", "clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1018.json"):
    validate_bundle_schema(json.load(open(path)), schema, validator=validator)

See the GKM Toolkit schema-validation and schema-resolution API references for exact signatures and options.

items.title: Parquet Output
items.text:
In addition to the JSON bundle, the latest release is published as typed Parquet files, one per table (22 tables: the bundle sections, with the VCV and RCV evidence lines in their own tables). They are written by BigQuery EXPORT DATA queries, not by the assembler, and use columnar storage with named, typed columns for each section's fields, making them suitable for analytical workloads, DuckDB, pandas, or Apache Spark.

See Export & Distribute for how the Parquet files are produced (derived from the bundle, latest release only). To query them — every table's columns, how the tables join, and runnable recipes — see Query the Data.

items.title: Inlining References
items.text:
The GKM Toolkit (ga4gh.gkm) converts the bundle's #/… references into inlined output at the level of detail you need. Load the bundle, then call Bundle.export():

  • export(item, deep=True) — complete: every reachable reference resolved inline, producing a standalone object (a reference that closes a cycle is kept as a pointer, since JSON cannot represent a cyclic value).
  • export(item) (deep=False) — minimal: the object's local #/… pointers are preserved as-is.
  • export() with no argument exports the whole bundle at the chosen depth.

See the GKM Toolkit's schema resolution and containers API for details.

items.title: Overview
items.text:
The rcv bundle section contains one record per condition-level aggregate classification. Each record is a Statement that aggregates individual SCV submissions for the same variant and condition into a hierarchical summary — combining classifications across submission levels to produce a single condition-specific result.

RCV statements differ from VCV statements in one important way: condition-scoped aggregation — each RCV is scoped to a specific condition (identified by trait_set_id), whereas VCV statements aggregate across all conditions for a variant.

RCV statements use #/ references for propositions, contributing SCVs, and lower-level RCV groupings. They are produced by the RCV Procedures.

items.title: Record Structure
items.text:
Each record is a Statement with the following top-level fields:

Field Type Description id string RCV layer ID — e.g., RCV001781420.1-G-PATH-CP type string Always Statement proposition string #/proposition<Meaning>/{id} reference to the aggregate proposition (the section is set by the proposition type; see ID References) classification object MappableConcept — the aggregate classification label. See Classification strength object MappableConcept — the aggregate evidence strength direction string supports, disputes, or neutral — derived from the aggregate classification quality object Concept struct with conceptType: "Quality" and name (the submission level label, e.g., criteria provided, expert panel) extensions array of Extension ClinVar-specific aggregate metadata (0..*). See Extensions hasEvidenceLines array #/evidenceLine/ references to contributing and non-contributing evidence. See Evidence Lines

The classification, strength, direction, and quality fields follow the same structure and rules as VCV Statements.

items.title: Classification
items.text:
RCV statements use the same MappableConcept classification as VCV:

{
  "conceptType": "Classification",
  "name": "Pathogenic/Likely pathogenic",
  "extensions": [
    {"name": "conflictingExplanation", "value": "Pathogenic(3); Likely pathogenic(2)"}
  ]
}

For somatic clinical impact (SCI) propositions, the classification label may include the tier, assertion type, and clinical significance.

items.title: Proposition
items.text:
RCV propositions are delivered across the four proposition bundle sections (propositionPathogenicity, propositionOncogenicity, propositionSomaticClinicalImpact, propositionClinvarCustom) by meaning. Each RCV statement references its proposition via #/proposition<Meaning>/{id}.

A resolved RCV proposition contains:

Field Type Description type string Proposition type matching the underlying SCVs (e.g., VariantPathogenicityProposition) id string Proposition ID (e.g., RCV001781420-G-PATH-CP) subject string #/variation/clinvar:{id} reference predicate string Predicate matching the underlying SCVs (e.g., isCausalFor) object string #/condition/clinvar.trait:{id} or #/conditionSet/clinvar.traitset:{id} reference — the specific condition for this RCV

The key difference from VCV propositions: the object references the specific condition for this RCV accession, sourced from the representative SCV's condition mapping. A VCV proposition with several conditions references one OR condition set minted for the aggregate (see VCV Statements).

items.title: Evidence Lines
items.text:
Evidence lines work identically to VCV. The hasEvidenceLines field contains #/evidenceLine/ JSON pointer references to evidence line records in the evidenceLine bundle section:

{
  "hasEvidenceLines": [
    "#/evidenceLine/RCV001781420.1-G-PATH-CP.contributing",
    "#/evidenceLine/RCV001781420.1-G-PATH-CP.non-contributing"
  ]
}

At the Classification layer, evidence items within the referenced records point to SCVs via #/scv/. At the Priority and Aggregate Contribution layers, evidence items reference lower-level RCV groupings via #/rcv/.

See VCV Evidence Lines for the full field reference.

items.title: Extensions
items.text:
Extensions carry aggregate metadata not part of the GA4GH VA-Spec statement model. Each extension follows the GA4GH Extension structure: { "name": "<name>", "value": <value> }. Extensions appear at two structural levels — on the top-level Statement and on the classification object.

RCV extensions follow the same patterns as VCV extensions. See RCV Extensions (Pipeline) for details on how these extensions are built during pipeline processing.

items.title: Statement Extensions
items.text: Extension Name Value Type Description clinvarReviewStatus string The aggregate review status derived from the submission level and aggregation outcome. Same value set as VCV Statement Extensions. Always present.

items.title: Classification Extensions
items.text:
Extensions on the classification MappableConcept within the Statement.

Extension Name Value Type Description conflictingExplanation string A formatted breakdown of conflicting classification counts (e.g., Pathogenic(3); Likely pathogenic(2)). Present only when the classification is conflicting.

items.title: SCI Classification Label Format
items.text:
For somatic clinical impact (SCI) propositions, the RCV aggregate classification label includes the tier, assertion type, and clinical significance:

<tier_label> - <assertion_type> - <clinical_significance> (<scv_count>)

Examples: Tier I - Strong - diagnostic - supports diagnosis (1), Tier II - Potential - prognostic - poor outcome (1)

items.title: Layer Hierarchy
items.text:
RCV statements use the same multi-layer aggregation hierarchy as VCV, with condition (trait_set_id) as an additional grouping dimension at every layer.

Layer ID Format Aggregates By Scope Classification {RCV}.{ver}-{group}-{PROP}-{level}[-{TIER}] Classification label within submission level All Priority {RCV}.{ver}-{group}-{PROP}-{level} Tier priority within submission level Somatic only Aggregate Contribution {RCV}.{ver}-{group}-{PROP} Submission level (winner-takes-all) All

Submission level ranking is PG > EP > CP > NOCP > NOCL > FLAG.

See RCV Procedures for implementation details.

items.title: Examples
items.text:
Annotated JSONC examples of RCV statement records are available in the repository:

  • RCV statement examples

items.title: Overview
items.text:
The scv bundle section contains one record per ClinVar submission (SCV). Each record is a VA-Spec Statement that captures a submitter's interpretation of a variant — including the classification, evidence, condition, variant, and method.

SCV statements use #/ references to link to propositions, submitters, and conditions in their respective bundle sections rather than embedding full objects inline.

This section is produced by the SCV Statements procedure.

items.title: Record Structure
items.text:
Each record is a VA-Spec Statement with the following top-level fields:

Field Type Description id string SCV accession with version — clinvar.submission:SCV000123456.1 type string Always Statement proposition string #/proposition<Meaning>/{id} reference to the classification proposition (the section is set by the proposition type; see ID References) classification object MappableConcept — the submitter's classification. See Classification strength object MappableConcept — the evidence strength. See Strength direction string Whether the evidence supports, disputes, or is neutral toward the proposition quality object Concept struct with conceptType: "Quality" and name (the submission level label). See Quality description string Free-text interpretation summary (when provided by the submitter) contributions array Submitter and date information with #/submitter/ references. See Contributions specifiedBy object The classification method/guideline used. Its reportedIn is the method's citation Document, built like the statement's (including documentType). See Citations reportedIn array Supporting citations — one Document per ClinVar citation: a PubMed, DOI or Bookshelf reference, or a URL-only citation such as a CIViC evidence link. A Document carries documentType when ClinVar gives a citation type. See Citations extensions array of Extension ClinVar-specific metadata (0..*). See Extensions hasEvidenceLines array Evidence lines for somatic clinical impact assertions. See Evidence Lines

items.title: Classification
items.text:
The classification field is a MappableConcept with the submitted classification:

{
  "conceptType": "Classification",
  "name": "Pathogenic",
  "primaryCoding": {
    "code": "pathogenic",
    "system": "ACMG Guidelines, 2015"
  },
  "extensions": [
    {
      "name": "description",
      "value": "for Hemochromatosis\nClassification is based on the criteria provided submission\nMay 2021 by Victorian Clinical Genetics Services"
    }
  ]
}

The primaryCoding provides the machine-readable classification code and system from the clinvar_clinsig_types lookup table. The extensions array contains a human-readable description summarizing the condition, submission level, evaluation date, and submitter.

items.title: Strength
items.text:
The strength field is a MappableConcept indicating the evidence strength:

{
  "conceptType": "Strength",
  "name": "Definitive",
  "primaryCoding": {
    "code": "definitive",
    "system": "ACMG Guidelines, 2015"
  }
}

The primaryCoding is present when the strength can be mapped to a specific code in the classification system.

items.title: Quality
items.text:
The quality field is a Concept struct indicating the submission level:

{
  "conceptType": "Quality",
  "name": "criteria provided"
}
Field Type Description conceptType string Always "Quality" name string The submission level label (e.g., criteria provided, practice guideline, expert panel)

items.title: Contributions
items.text:
The contributions array records the submitter and key dates. Each contribution references the submitter via #/submitter/:

[
  {
    "type": "Contribution",
    "contributor": "#/submitter/clinvar.submitter:500104",
    "date": "2022-12-24",
    "activityType": "submitted"
  },
  {
    "type": "Contribution",
    "contributor": "#/submitter/clinvar.submitter:500104",
    "date": "2022-12-24",
    "activityType": "created"
  },
  {
    "type": "Contribution",
    "contributor": "#/submitter/clinvar.submitter:500104",
    "date": "2021-05-06",
    "activityType": "evaluated"
  }
]

items.title: Citations
items.text:
reportedIn lists the submission's citations, and specifiedBy.reportedIn holds the citation for the assertion method. Each is a VA-Spec Document, one per ClinVar citation. A citation that ClinVar lists with several ids — ACMG 2015 has a PubMed id, a PMC id and a DOI — is a single Document:

{
  "type": "Document",
  "name": "ACMG, 2015",
  "documentType": "general",
  "pmid": "25741868",
  "doi": "10.1038/gim.2015.30",
  "urls": [
    "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25741868",
    "https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/4544753",
    "https://doi.org/10.1038/gim.2015.30"
  ]
}
  • name is ClinVar's short label for the citation and documentType is ClinVar's citation type (general, practice guideline, review, Suggested Reading or file in FileTrack), both verbatim and present only when ClinVar gives them. The same holds for the method citation in specifiedBy.reportedIn
  • urls holds every resolvable URL, ClinVar's own URL first; a citation ClinVar gives only as a URL — a CIViC evidence link, for example — is {"type": "Document", "urls": ["https://civicdb.org/links/evidence/4846"]}
  • A citation that is only free text has no pmid, doi or urls. Its text is kept verbatim in the clinvarCitationText extension. Such text is often not a reference, e.g. a list of ACMG criteria.

The pipeline never changes ClinVar's citation data silently. When an invalid id is repaired, the Document's extensions keep the original:

{
  "type": "Document",
  "documentType": "general",
  "doi": "10.1155/2023/2564200",
  "urls": ["https://doi.org/10.1155/2023/2564200"],
  "extensions": [
    { "name": "originalClinvarCitation", "value": "doi:10.1155/2023/2564200" },
    { "name": "citationRepaired", "value": true }
  ]
}

An id that cannot be used, such as a DOI recorded as https, yields no doi or URL. It appears only as { "name": "invalidClinvarCitation", "value": "https" }. Method.reportedIn holds one Document. When ClinVar lists more than one citation for an assertion method, the first stays there and the rest are Documents in the Method's additionalClinvarMethodCitations extension. The full list of citation extensions and repair rules is on the Final Statements pipeline page.

items.title: Proposition
