items.title: Mapping & Vocabularies
items.text: Formerly Statement Profiles. This section describes the fundamental aspects of how ClinVar data is organized and transformed into GKS standard statements within the ClinVar-GKM pipeline.

items.title: Overview
items.text:
ClinVar submissions (SCVs) are the baseline statements submitted to ClinVar by laboratories, expert panels, research groups, locus-specific databases (LSDBs), and other organizations. ClinVar aggregates these submissions using different rules for specific statement types to produce higher-order statements (RCVs and VCVs).

ClinVar-GKM maps each submission to a specific statement type, proposition profile, and classification with corresponding direction and strength values conforming to the GA4GH VA-Spec standard.

items.title: Sections
items.text:
• Statement Types — the 14 statement types and their categories
  • Classifications — classification values mapped to direction and strength
  • Propositions — mapping of statement types to GKS proposition types
  • Review Status — star levels, rank order, and aggregation behavior

items.title: Classifications
items.text: Each statement type has a set list of classification values to which ClinVar normalizes historic or similar classification terms used by some submitters. These classification terms are mapped to the GKS VA statement class' direction and strength.

items.title: Germline Classification
items.text:
The Germline Classification category groups 9 statement types.

# Statement Type Classification Direction Strength G.01 Pathogenicity Pathogenic supports definitive Pathogenic, low penetrance supports definitive Risk allele supports definitive Likely pathogenic supports likely Likely pathogenic, low penetrance supports likely Likely risk allele supports likely Pathogenic/Likely pathogenic supports \<null> Uncertain significance neutral \<null> Uncertain risk allele neutral \<null> conflicting data from submitters neutral \<null> Benign disputes definitive Likely benign disputes likely Benign/Likely benign disputes \<null> G.02 Drug Response drug response supports \<null> G.03 Risk Factor risk factor supports \<null> G.04 Protective protective supports \<null> G.05 Affects Affects supports \<null> G.06 Association association supports \<null> association not found disputes \<null> G.07 Confers Sensitivity confers sensitivity supports \<null> G.08 Other other supports \<null> G.09 Not Provided not provided supports \<null>

items.title: Oncogenicity Classification
items.text:
The Oncogenicity Classification category groups only 1 statement type.

# Statement Type Classification Direction Strength O.10 Oncogenicity Oncogenic supports definitive Likely oncogenic supports likely Uncertain significance neutral \<null> Benign disputes definitive Likely benign disputes likely

items.title: Somatic Clinical Impact
items.text: The Somatic Clinical Impact category groups 1 primary statement type with up to 3 evidence statement types.

items.title: Clinical Significance (Primary)
items.text: # Statement Type Classification Direction Strength S.11 Clinical Significance Tier I - Strong supports strong Tier II - Potential supports potential Tier III - Unknown neutral \<null> Tier IV - Benign/Likely benign disputes \<null>

items.title: Evidence Statement Types
items.text:
All Tier I and II Clinical Significance statements MUST have at least one of the following statement types as evidence. These sub-statement types are critical to Tier I and II clinical significance submissions in ClinVar.

# Statement Type Direction Strength S.12 Therapeutic Response supports strong or potential S.13 Diagnostic supports strong or potential S.14 Prognostic supports strong or potential

items.title: Propositions
items.text: Each statement type is mapped to a GKS proposition type. Standard GA4GH proposition types are used where they exist. For statement types not covered by the GA4GH specifications, ClinVar-GKM defines custom proposition types.

items.title: Standard GA4GH Proposition Types
items.text: Statement Type Proposition Type Pathogenicity VariantPathogenicityProposition Oncogenicity VariantOncogenicityProposition Clinical Significance VariantClinicalSignificanceProposition Therapeutic Response VariantTherapeuticResponseProposition Diagnostic VariantDiagnosticProposition Prognostic VariantPrognosticProposition

items.title: ClinVar-GKM Custom Proposition Types
items.text:
These custom propositions are defined specifically for the ClinVar-GKM dataset to handle non-standard ClinVar submission types that do not have corresponding GA4GH proposition types.

Statement Type Proposition Type Risk Factor ClinVarRiskFactorProposition Protective ClinVarProtectiveProposition Drug Response ClinVarDrugResponseProposition Other ClinVarOtherProposition Not Provided ClinVarNotProvidedProposition Affects ClinVarAffectsProposition Association ClinVarAssociationProposition Confers Sensitivity ClinVarConfersSensitivityProposition

items.title: Aggregate Propositions
items.text:
Aggregate (VCV and RCV) statements use the same proposition types and predicates as their underlying SCV submissions. For example, a VCV pathogenicity aggregate uses VariantPathogenicityProposition with isCausalFor, matching the SCVs it aggregates.

Design Consideration: Proposition Normalization

In the current v1 release, each SCV statement generates its own proposition instance keyed by {scv_id}-{PROP_CODE}. This means two SCVs asserting the exact same subject-predicate-object relationship (e.g., variant X isCausalFor condition Y) produce two separate proposition entries in the bundle, even though they represent the same logical assertion.

A future improvement may normalize propositions so that identical subject-predicate-object combinations are represented as a single shared instance — treating propositions as value objects in their own right. Since the proposition is the fundamental component for identifying which statements can be meaningfully compared, honoring that identity in the dataset would allow consumers to directly group and compare all statements that share the same proposition without field-by-field comparison.

This would require a content-addressable identifier scheme for propositions (e.g., hashing the subject + predicate + object) so that SCV statements can reference a shared proposition by its computed key.

At the aggregate VCV and RCV level, proposition sharing is less impactful — aggregate propositions build on the shared SCV propositions and further qualify them with review status, submission level, and other aggregation-specific attributes that make exact duplication less common. Evidence lines are already stored as separate records in the evidenceLine bundle section and referenced via hasEvidenceLines FK arrays, so they could similarly benefit from referencing shared propositions rather than carrying layer-specific copies.

items.title: Review Status
items.text: All ClinVar submissions contain a review status, which differentiates submissions based on their level of confidence. These review status levels (also called star levels) are used in ClinVar to group and prioritize multiple submissions for the same variant and statement type.

items.title: Individual Submission Review Status Levels
items.text: Review Status Stars practice guideline 4 reviewed by expert panel 3 criteria provided, single submitter 1 no assertion criteria provided 0 no classification provided 0 flagged submission 0

items.title: Aggregation Behavior
items.text:
If multiple submissions exist for the same variant and statement type, ClinVar aggregates them into two higher-order statements:

  • RCVs — aggregate of submissions for the same statement type, variant, and condition
  • VCVs — aggregate of submissions for the same statement type and variant (across all conditions)

RCVs and VCVs use only the highest-ranking review status levels in the aggregated result. These are considered the contributing submissions; others are non-contributing.

items.title: Rank Order
items.text:
The rank order is a quantification of the review status levels used to appropriately segregate submissions within a single statement type, variant, and condition. Rank order is not a ClinVar concept but is used during the ClinVar-GKM aggregation process.

Rank Review Status Stars Scope 4 practice guideline 4 Individual / Aggregate 3 reviewed by expert panel 3 Individual / Aggregate 2 criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts 2 Aggregate only 1 criteria provided, conflicting classifications 1 Aggregate only 1 criteria provided, single submitter 1 Individual / Aggregate 0 no assertion criteria provided 0 Individual / Aggregate -1 no classification provided 0 Individual / Aggregate -3 flagged submission 0 Individual / Aggregate

Rank 2 statuses only appear on aggregate (VCV/RCV) statements where multiple CP-level submissions exist. A single CP submission produces rank 1. The distinction between "no conflicts" and "conflicting classifications" at rank 2 reflects whether the contributing CP submissions agree on clinical significance.

items.title: Aggregate Review Status
items.text:
When individual submissions are aggregated into VCV-level statements, the resulting aggregate review status reflects both the submission level and the aggregation outcome. The aggregate review status appears as a clinvarReviewStatus extension on each VCV statement.

Submission Level Condition Aggregate Review Status PG Any practice guideline EP Any reviewed by expert panel CP Single submitter criteria provided, single submitter CP Multiple submitters, concordant criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts CP Multiple submitters, conflicting criteria provided, conflicting classifications NOCP Any no assertion criteria provided NOCL Any no classification provided FLAG Any flagged submission

CP is the only submission level where the aggregate review status changes based on the aggregation result. All other levels produce a fixed review status regardless of the number of contributing submissions.

See VCV Aggregation Rules for full details on how submission levels are aggregated.

items.title: Statement Types
items.text:
ClinVar-GKM groups ClinVar submissions into 14 unique statement types. Several of these types are no longer accepted by ClinVar but exist historically.

# Statement Type Proposition Profile Statement Category G.01 Pathogenicity Variant Pathogenicity Germline Classification G.02 Drug Response ClinVar Drug Response* Germline Classification G.03 Risk Factor ClinVar Risk Factor* Germline Classification G.04 Protective ClinVar Protective* Germline Classification G.05 Affects ClinVar Affects* Germline Classification G.06 Association ClinVar Association* Germline Classification G.07 Confers Sensitivity ClinVar Confers Sensitivity* Germline Classification G.08 Other ClinVar Other* Germline Classification G.09 Not Provided ClinVar Not Provided* Germline Classification O.10 Oncogenicity Variant Oncogenicity Oncogenic Classification S.11 Clinical Significance Clinical Significance Somatic Clinical Impact S.12 Therapeutic Response Therapeutic Response Somatic Clinical Impact S.13 Diagnostic Diagnostic Somatic Clinical Impact S.14 Prognostic Prognostic Somatic Clinical Impact

items.title: Statement Categories (VCV Groups)
items.text:
ClinVar aggregates these 14 statement types into one of 3 VCV-level categories:

  • Germline Classification — groups 9 statement types (G.01 through G.09)
  • Oncogenic Classification — groups 1 statement type (O.10)
  • Somatic Clinical Impact — groups 4 statement types (S.11 through S.14)

items.title: About Non-Standard Statements
items.text:
The non-standard statements (marked with *) are defined only in the ClinVar-GKM datasets. These are needed to handle non-standard data in ClinVar. The ClinVar-GKM dataset is a complete representation of ClinVar's XML VCV and RCV releases and must have a way to represent all of the data in ClinVar. ClinVar-GKM does NOT attempt to guess at or map submissions like Risk Factor to the Pathogenicity Risk Allele classifications since the Risk Factor classification was provided years ahead of the recent ability to classify Variant Pathogenicity submissions with established, likely or uncertain risk allele.

Additionally, some of these non-standard statements are no longer accepted as submissions to ClinVar. ClinVar has stopped accepting Risk Factor in favor of the newer Pathogenicity classification terms, as well as other, confers sensitivity, affects and association.

Not Provided statements represent submissions where the submitter provided NO classification. While this may seem counter-intuitive, ClinVar allows this under certain circumstances. Historically, ClinVar needed to allow this for Functional Impact submissions where the submitter was not explicitly classifying the variant.

items.title: About Clinical Significance & Somatic Clinical Impact
items.text:
The Clinical Significance statement is the top-level submission for all Somatic Clinical Impact Tier I, II, III & IV submissions. These submissions are different from Pathogenicity or Oncogenicity submissions in that they have a sub-statement tightly coupled with the Tier I & II classified submissions.

All Tier I & II submissions MUST have one of either Therapeutic Response, Diagnostic or Prognostic related submission data associated with them. This is defined in the AMP/ASCO guidelines. However, Tier III & IV do NOT have a combined sub-statement as they represent the Uncertain and Benign/Likely benign Somatic Clinical Impact submissions.

All Somatic Clinical Impact submissions will have a Clinical Significance statement at the top-level. Those that are Tier I & II will have the sub-statement associated through an Evidence Line.

items.title: Changelog
items.text: A running record of every schema change and data re-release on the 1.x line. See Versioning & Releases for how versions are assigned, and the GitHub Releases page for the tagged source of each.

A breaking release during the initial-stabilization period; see ADR 0006. 1.1.0 ends that period: it is generally available (GA), its published files are immutable, and a later breaking change opens v2/. It reorganizes the proposition sections and carries a set of corrections, all delivered through one full rebuild that rewrites every published file. It is published under a new line folder, v1/1.1/, in a new R2 layout that mirrors NCBI's ClinVar FTP site (ADR 0009; see New R2 layout below). Every download URL changes.

  • Breaking: propositions are grouped by meaning. The four proposition sections and Parquet tables, which were grouped by the shape of their object (varcond-proposition, varcustom-proposition, vartumor-proposition, vartherapy-proposition), are replaced by four grouped by meaning: propositionPathogenicity, propositionOncogenicity, propositionSomaticClinicalImpact and propositionClinvarCustom. Proposition ids don't change, but every statement and evidence-line pointer names the new section (#/varcond-proposition/SCV…-PATH becomes #/propositionPathogenicity/SCV…-PATH). The four Parquet tables share one column schema, so read_parquet('proposition*.parquet') reads them all. object_condition_id, object_tumor_type_id and object_therapy become object_id, and varcustom-proposition.subject_id becomes subject_variant_id. Every proposition table gains object_type (the table object_id points at: condition, conditionSet, therapy or therapyGroup) and the columns only some of the old tables had (condition_qualifier_id, mode_of_inheritance, penetrance). The section is a function of the proposition type alone; see the migration table. The bundle schema's propositionClinvarCustom section no longer lists the abstract ClinvarGermlineCustomProposition base, so each record must carry one of the concrete Clinvar* types (every published record already does). The Parquet entries below name the pre-1.1.0 tables.
  • Breaking: version. The schema $id version and the bundle schema_version move 1.0.1 → 1.1.0.
  • Corrective: everything else below. The schema changes accept every published record; the data corrections fix HGVS syntax, duplicate allele keys, RCV propositions without an object, condition pointers, condition names, citations, gene context and array order; and the Parquet changes add bare-id and typed columns and make every Parquet value match the bundle.

Do not mix 1.0.1 and 1.1.0 files

Do not apply 1.1.0 deltas to a 1.0.1 monthly. Replay v1/1.1/ deltas only onto a v1/1.1/ monthly, and the frozen v1/1.0/ deltas only onto a v1/1.0/ monthly. To be told about future releases, join the email list clinvar-gkm@broadinstitute.org; see Versioning & Releases.

Schema changes — no published record changes:

  • The four ClinvarCategoricalVariant branches are now mutually exclusive, each keyed on its constraint (DefiningAlleleConstraint, CopyCountConstraint, CopyChangeConstraint, or no constraints). Before, real variants matched more than one branch and failed the oneOf. The bundle schema now validates the variation section through ClinvarCategoricalVariant.
  • The nine ClinVar *Properties mixins (ClinvarScvStatementProperties, ClinvarAggregateStatementProperties, ClinvarCategoricalVariantProperties and six more) are now abstract. They were emitted closed (additionalProperties: false) inside allOf, so a strict validator rejected the fields their GA4GH base classes supply. Each record is still closed by its class's unevaluatedProperties: false. This works around ga4gh/gkm-metaschema#88 (#153).
  • GeneListItem now describes the published shape, {gene, relationship_type, source}, all three required: gene is a #/gene/ reference and source is calculated or submitted. It used to list entrez_gene_id, hgnc_id, symbol and iris, which no published record carries (#153).
  • ClinvarCanonicalAllele.definingContext is removed. Cat-VRS 1.1.1's closed CanonicalAllele cannot accept it, and no record carried it (#153).

Data-shape correction — 14 variants (16 HGVS expressions) had clinvarHgvsList entries with syntax hgvs.?, which VRS doesn't allow. ClinVar's submitted text had no HGVS type letter. It is now kept as an extension on the listed expression's nucleotideExpression, never altered or dropped:

  • Merged (11): ClinVar also supplies a valid expression for the same accession. That one is listed, with invalidClinvarExpression (the submitted text) and expressionMerged: true.
  • Repaired (5): no valid one exists. The expression is listed with its type letter restored, with originalClinvarExpression (the submitted text) and expressionRepaired: true.

Duplicate allele keys — when two ClinVar variations normalize to the same VRS allele, the allele section held one record per variation under the same key. A JSON reader kept whichever record came last, and Parquet had one row per record. This affected 1 allele in the 2026-09-23 to 2026-10-11 releases: ga4gh:VA.lP8drLGSbZDn4x3Dr2TPwZOvvvU6kAJl, the SERPINE1 4G/5G dup shared by variations 13572 and 4897201. It also affected 8 alleles in the June to August releases, which were ClinVar duplicate variations that ClinVar has since merged. Each allele now has exactly one record:

  • expressions is the union of the expressions from every variation that shares the allele, with no duplicates.
  • name is picked from that union by the existing rule (HGVS type, then precedence). Nothing is lost: the expressions the other variations would have used as the name are still in expressions.
  • Each variation keeps its own variation record, which points to the shared allele.

Expression order and the name are now fully deterministic. When equivalent ClinVar HGVS spellings tie for the name, the tie is broken by value. That changes the name of the few alleles with tied expressions; the number depends on the release (1 or 2 per release, 2 in 2026-10-11).

RCV propositions without an object — in the 2026-10-04 and 2026-10-11 releases, the 4 propositions of RCV000001117 (-G-PATH, -G-PATH-CP, -G-NP, -G-NP-NOCL) had no object and failed validation. This also made the 2026-10-04 delta fail. An RCV's condition comes from one of its member SCVs. ClinVar's RCV-to-SCV mapping still listed an SCV that ClinVar had removed (SCV000021267), and that SCV was picked even though it no longer had a condition. The SCV is now picked from the members that have a condition. The propositions point to #/condition/clinvar.trait:2478 again, as they did through 2026-09-28. No other RCV changes.

Condition references are all #/ pointers — two kinds of condition reference were bare ids, while every other reference in the bundle was a #/<section>/<id> pointer. Both are now pointers to the same record (counts for the 2026-10-11 release):

  • A VCV proposition's object, when the VCV has a single condition (7,474,404 of 9,156,181): clinvar.trait:2478 is now #/condition/clinvar.trait:2478, and clinvar.traitset:… is now #/conditionSet/clinvar.traitset:….
  • The concepts of the condition sets minted for VCV aggregates (clinvar.conditionset:vcv-…, 94,980 sets): members are now #/condition/… or, for a nested TraitSet, #/conditionSet/….

The ids themselves are unchanged, including every vcv- set id. A pointer-following reader (the GKM Toolkit, sub-bundle.py) now reaches these conditions. The submittedCondition and submittedConditionSet extension values stay bare CURIEs: they record what was submitted, not a reference. In Parquet, the typed id columns (object_condition_id, object_id, object_tumor_type_id, conditionSet.concepts) are unchanged bare ids; only the data columns change, to the pointer form. See ID References.

Conditions without a name — 58 condition records in the 2026-10-11 release (57 or 58 in every release since 2026-06-27) had neither name nor primaryCoding, so they failed MappableConcept validation. ClinVar gives these traits no Preferred name in the trait record, but it does name them elsewhere. Each now takes its name from ClinVar, in this order: the trait's Preferred name, then the Preferred name in the RCV's TraitSet, then the trait's Alternate name (the first alphabetically). No value is made up, and aliases is unchanged:

  • Alternate name only (51), such as clinvar.trait:9800, now named Apolipoprotein c-ii variants, molecular defect unknown. The name is also in aliases, as before.
  • Named only in the RCV (7: clinvar.trait:10547, 10548, 54780, 76440, 76481, 78166, 78167). The trait record is empty, but the RCV's TraitSet names each not provided.

When an SCV's submitted condition has no name, its classification description uses the condition's name. In 173 SCVs of the 2026-10-11 release it changes from for unspecified condition to the ClinVar name.

Citations — SCV reportedIn and specifiedBy.reportedIn now hold one Document per ClinVar citation, with no citation dropped and no ClinVar value changed silently. Counts are for the 2026-09-28 release:

  • Multi-id citations merged (5,698 citations on 5,698 SCVs): a citation with several ids, such as ACMG 2015 with a DOI, a PubMed id and a PMC id, was split into 2–3 Documents. It is now one Document with pmid, doi and every URL. Together these citations account for 10,260 fewer Documents.
  • Restored (78,142 citations on 72,603 SCVs): URL-only citations (76,379) were dropped and are now {urls: [url]}. Text-only citations (1,763) were dropped and now keep their text in a clinvarCitationText extension. The 109 text-only assertion-method citations had no reportedIn; they now get one the same way. Assertion-method citations that have both a URL and text (12,451) also gain clinvarCitationText.
  • New labels: ClinVar's citation abbrev (e.g. ACMG, 2015) is the Document name, and its citation type (e.g. general, practice guideline) is documentType, verbatim.
  • No more non-URL urls or invalid doi values. 3,874 Documents had a doi that fails the VA-Spec pattern, and 12 had a non-URL urls entry. Malformed DOIs such as doi:10.…, https://doi.org/10.… or ones with stray spaces (117) are repaired; the original is kept in originalClinvarCitation, flagged citationRepaired. A DOI-sourced PubMed or PMC id (3) moves to pmid or a PMC URL and also keeps originalClinvarCitationSource. Unusable ids, mostly 3,746 assertion-method DOIs recorded as https, are kept only in invalidClinvarCitation. A valid SICI-style DOI that the VA-Spec pattern rejects is kept in clinvarDoi, with its doi.org URL.
  • Ordering: Documents are ordered by PubMed id and then by content, so a full and an incremental build produce the same bytes.
  • Assertion methods with two citations (6 SCVs): Method.reportedIn holds one Document. ClinVar's first citation stays there. The second used to be fused into it as pmid: "29116469,29907814"; it is now a Document in the Method's own additionalClinvarMethodCitations extension (an array of Documents).

See Citations. This is a data change only; the schema already allows these Document fields and extensions. In Parquet, scv.reportedIn and scv.specifiedBy.reportedIn gain name, documentType and extensions at the end of the struct, and scv.specifiedBy gains extensions after reportedIn. The existing fields keep their names, types and positions.

Gene context — every SCV proposition geneContextQualifier gains a geneContextSource extension that says where its gene came from. The gene is still the variant's one representative gene, chosen upstream; only the name-derived genes below are new. Counts are for the 2026-09-28 release, before that change:

geneContextSource Meaning Propositions submittedSymbolMatches The submitter's symbols include the qualifier's symbol 5,781,920 submittedSymbolDiffers The submitter gave symbols, none equal to the qualifier's symbol (mostly previous symbols of the same gene, e.g. GBA for GBA1) 27,671 inferredFromVariant The submitter gave no symbols 881,325 submittedNotNormalized The variant has no single representative gene (the placeholder) 4,814
  • Symbols are compared after trimming spaces and ignoring case, so C19ORF12 matches C19orf12.
  • Schema: geneContextSource accepts only these four values. The new ClinvarGeneContextQualifier class defines them, and the bundle schema applies it to every proposition section.
  • Placeholder name: the 4,814 placeholder qualifiers are named with the submitter's symbol, verbatim, instead of the literal submitted genes were not normalized. The 5 with several symbols join them with , in submitted order. They still have no primaryCoding, and submittedGeneSymbols is unchanged.
  • submittedGeneSymbols order: the symbols are now in submitted order. Before, their order was not fixed, and the 45 lists with more than one symbol could change order from one build to the next.
  • submittedGeneSymbols trimmed: the leading space our comma split left on symbols such as " MEG3" is removed (3 propositions, 8 symbols); ClinVar's own values are unchanged.
  • Name-derived genes: gene context now comes entirely from the upstream single-gene method, including the gene's symbol and HGNC id. This adds genes named in a variant's title that ClinVar does not associate with it, such as NR_164162.1(GLRA4):n.1091C>T → GLRA4. In the 2026-10-11 release that is 25 variants (GLRA4, CCDC144NL, RNU6-81P) and 31 SCV propositions. 20 of them had the placeholder and now get the gene, with submittedSymbolMatches; the other 11 had no qualifier and now get one, with inferredFromVariant.
    • These genes are not in the bundle's gene section, which lists the genes ClinVar associates with a variant. So their Parquet gene_context_id does not join to gene.parquet.

The gene context stays on the proposition. This is a data change only: the schema already allows extensions on the qualifier. See Qualifier Extensions.

Upstream gene-context fixes — two defects in the upstream single_gene_variation table (clinvar-ingest-bq-tools) were fixed and backfilled before the rebuild, so 1.1.0 carries them. Counts are for the 2026-09-28 release:

  • Haplotypes and genotypes in one gene (bq-tools #38): when all of a haplotype's or genotype's alleles share one gene, it was rejected, so 63 SCV propositions had the placeholder or no gene context. They now get the shared gene; variation 3737 (FH Aarhus), for example, gets LDLR.
  • Gene ids missing from the gene table (bq-tools #39, fixed by #41 and #42): 37 SCV propositions lost their gene context because the variant's gene was not in the upstream gene table. Genes such as SMIM48 and LINC03103 now resolve. Genes with no HGNC id (LOC*) and NCBI-discontinued ids (such as STRTS) stay excluded by design, so not every one of the 37 regains a gene.

Both are tracked, with the other upstream defects found during 1.1.0, in #164.

Array order — several arrays had no fixed order, so two builds of the same release could list the same items in a different order. Each now has one fixed order, and every build gives the same bytes. Only the order changes; no value is added, removed or changed. Counts are for the 2026-10-11 release:

  • variation (4,686,825 of 4,687,256 records): extensions follow a fixed order by name (categoricalVariationType … clinvarHgvsList, clinvarGeneList). clinvarHgvsList entries are ordered by expression, clinvarGeneList by NCBI gene id, and mappings start with the ClinVar exactMatch. A copy-number variant lists its DefiningLocationConstraint before its copy constraint.
  • condition (12,832 of 23,392): mappings are ordered by system and code, and each coding's iris in a fixed order.
  • VCV and RCV evidenceLine (688,701 and 358,507): hasEvidenceItems lists SCVs in id order and non-contributing statements in priority order.

Values picked from several equal candidates are made deterministic the same way: the sequence reference and cross-reference IRI system of a variant, a condition's primaryCoding, membershipOperator and merged trait attributes, and the representative expression source in variation identity. On 2026-10-11 none of these picks changed a published value.

Parquet — typed columns now hold bare ids, as the other id columns already did:

  • vartherapy-proposition.object_therapy is clinvar.therapy:… or clinvar.therapygroup:…, not a JSON-quoted "#/therapy/…" pointer.
  • variation.extensions[].value_gene_array[].gene is ncbigene:…, not #/gene/ncbigene:….
  • New columns: condition.data; therapy.name and therapy.concept_type; therapyGroup.membership_operator and therapyGroup.members. condition keeps its camelCase column names, and therapy / therapyGroup keep key and value.
  • The four proposition tables gain gene_context_id (the gene-context qualifier's own ncbigene: coding; NULL for the placeholder), submitted_gene_symbols (the submitter's gene symbols, verbatim) and gene_context_source (the qualifier's geneContextSource; see Gene context above). gene_context_name is unchanged, except that a placeholder now holds the submitter's symbol. The qualifier is one representative gene per variant, chosen upstream, not a submitter-asserted gene; see Gene context.
  • location gains loc_start_min, loc_start_max, loc_end_min and loc_end_max: the bounds of each coordinate, set from the range when ClinVar gives an uncertain start or end (about 72,000 rows, mostly copy-number variants), where loc_start / loc_end are NULL. See location.
  • scv, vcv and rcv gain proposition_section: the proposition table their proposition_id is in (propositionPathogenicity, propositionOncogenicity, propositionSomaticClinicalImpact or propositionClinvarCustom), taken from the statement's pointer (#171).

References inside the JSON bundle and the data columns still use #/<section>/ pointers.

Parquet matches the bundle — every Parquet value can now be recomputed from the JSON bundle:

  • scv.extensions and evidenceLine.extensions no longer carry empty placeholder elements. Every row held all-null structs the bundle doesn't have: the unused value_* fields of each extension, with empty concepts[] and xrefs[] elements inside them (in the 2026-10-11 delta, 69,956 empty concepts[] and 58,375 empty xrefs[] elements). An unused value_* field is now NULL and the empty elements are gone. The column type is unchanged.
  • conditionSet.data is null-stripped like every other data column: a set with no conceptSetType omits the key instead of carrying "conceptSetType": null.

Validation — the rebuilt datasets and the real staged bundles were gated before publishing (reference integrity, expected difference, delta reconstruction, strict GA4GH gkm-toolkit validation, bundle ↔ Parquet). See Release Validation for the gates and the results.

Known issues — see Known Issues for the current list. In short: in the 2026-10-18 release, VRS normalization returned an error for 6 variations; 16 HGVS expressions in ClinVar's XML are malformed and were reported to ClinVar; and DOIs that VA-Spec's pattern rejects are kept in clinvarDoi. Upstream defects and their workarounds are tracked in #164.

Republish: 1.1.0 is not a patch. All 17 BigQuery datasets behind the published releases were rebuilt in full. Then the 4 monthly full bundles (2026-07 … 2026-10, and 00-latest), October's 3 weekly full bundles (2026-10-04, 2026-10-11, 2026-10-18, and 00-latest_weekly) and the 16 weekly deltas (2026-07-06 … 2026-10-18) were re-assembled and published under v1/1.1/. Every published bundle therefore carries every change above, including the new proposition sections. File contents and checksums change, so re-download anything fetched before 1.1.0. Copies downloaded earlier keep the old forms; the Query the Data pages note where they differ.

items.title: New R2 layout
items.text:
The published files move to a layout modelled on NCBI's ClinVar XML folder (xml/, xml/weekly_release/, xml/archive/YYYY/); see How the layout mirrors NCBI. The old v1/datasets/, v1/deltas/ and archive/1.0.1/ paths are removed, so update any script or bookmark:

Before 1.1.0 From 1.1.0 v1/index.json v1/1.1/index.json (the root index.json lists each line) v1/datasets/clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MM.json.gz, …_00-latest.json.gz v1/1.1/clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MM.json.gz, v1/1.1/clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz — (no weekly full) v1/1.1/weekly/clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MMDD.json.gz and weekly/clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz, current month only v1/deltas/YYYY-MMDD/clinvar-gkm-delta_YYYY-MMDD.json.gz v1/1.1/deltas/clinvar-gkm-delta_YYYY-MMDD.json.gz (current month); deltas/YYYY-MM/… (earlier months) v1/deltas/YYYY-MMDD/manifest.json …/clinvar-gkm-delta_YYYY-MMDD.manifest.json, beside its bundle v1/deltas/00-latest/ removed; the newest delta is listed in index.json, and the newest weekly full is weekly/clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz v1/archives/YYYY/ v1/1.1/archive/YYYY/ (monthlies, plus deltas/YYYY-MM/) v1/datasets/parquet/… v1/1.1/parquet/ (one dataset) archive/1.0.1/ v1/1.0/ (the frozen 1.0.1 line)
  • Weekly full bundles are new. A full bundle is published for every weekly release and kept for the current month. When a new month's first release is published, the previous month's weekly fulls are deleted (the newest once the new month's monthly is published) and its deltas move to deltas/YYYY-MM/; at a new year, the year's monthlies and deltas move to archive/YYYY/. Any past week can be rebuilt from a monthly plus deltas; see Rebuild a past week.
  • Replay fixes. Each delta manifest's checkpoint_full now names the official monthly the delta's chain replays onto, as {path, release, month, sha256} with release the monthly's source_release; before, every manifest named the newest monthly (2026-10). Manifests also carry schema_version, sha256 and bundle. Each monthly's source_release, the release it was built from, is published in index.json. The documented replay recipe compared months and skipped deltas from the monthly's own month; it now selects deltas by release date.
  • Checksums. Every bundle has a <file>.sha256 sidecar (sha256sum -c format), and the index lists each bundle's sha256. The root manifest's schema reads 1.1.0 (it said 1.0.0).

One Parquet dataset. Parquet is derived from the bundle, so it is no longer kept per release: the dated monthly sets (v1/datasets/parquet/<YYYY-MM>/) and every per-delta set (v1/deltas/<YYYY-MMDD>/parquet/) are deleted. One dataset is published at v1/1.1/parquet/, built from the newest release (2026-10-18 for 1.1.0, not the 2026-10 monthly) and overwritten every release. Its manifest.json gives the build date, the release and dataset it was built from, the builder and every file's sha256, and the index's Parquet entry (source_release) names the release too. No Parquet is kept in archive/ or in frozen lines; past Parquet is rebuilt from the monthly bundles with clinvar-gkm-parquet, which is planned and not yet released. The index's delta entries lose their parquet list.

The 1.0.1 generation. Every 1.0.1 bundle and delta manifest is kept, byte-identical, in the frozen line v1/1.0/ (monthlies at the top, deltas under deltas/YYYY-MM/), with .sha256 sidecars, a MANIFEST.json (sha256 and original key per file), a README.txt, and a new index.json and feed.xml in the line layout. It has no Parquet. Its delta manifests still name the old v1/ paths and checkpoint_full 2026-10; replay it from v1/1.0/index.json.

A schema-conformance release shipped in place during the initial-stabilization period. Every published bundle (full and delta) now validates against the schema/clinvar-gkm/ schemas with the official GA4GH gkm-toolkit — the largest published delta went from thousands of non-conforming records to zero. All data was rebuilt, oracle-gated (full-vs-incremental and delta-reconstruction, 0,0,0 across every section), and re-published to /v1/.

Data-shape corrections — bring the emitted data into conformance with the existing schema (no change to the schema shape):

  • Unmappable variants (haplotypes, genotypes, unmapped) no longer emit an empty constraints array; they validate as ClinvarNonConstrainedVariant.
  • Typed extension values (value_<type>) are collapsed to the single polymorphic value field everywhere, including nested classification.extensions.
  • Single-member condition sets are no longer emitted — a ConceptSet requires ≥2 concepts, and the lone condition is already referenced directly as #/condition/….
  • Delta bundles no longer contain empty ({}) sections.

Schema change — additive, backward-compatible:

  • flagged submission added to the clinvarReviewStatus and clinvarScvReviewStatus enumerations (FLAG tier).

Data: re-released 4 monthly fulls (2026-07 … 2026-10) and 15 weekly deltas (2026-07-06 … 2026-10-11, a newly added weekly). 00-latest advances to 2026-10-11. The schema $id version and bundle schema_version move 1.0.0 → 1.0.1; the /v1/ layout is unchanged (keyed by major version, ADR 0004).
First official release on the finalized GKM standards — VRS 2.1.1, Cat-VRS 1.1.1, VA-Spec 1.1.0, and GKM-Core 1.3.0. The 1.0.0 tag is frozen and immutable; its schema $ids remain resolvable.

items.title: FAQ
items.text: Answers to recurring questions about how ClinVar content appears in ClinVar-GKM. Each answer states where the behavior comes from in the pipeline and how to see it in the data.

items.title: Where does an SCV proposition's gene context come from?
items.text: The gene in an SCV proposition's geneContextQualifier always comes from the variant, never from the submitter. The submitter's own gene symbols are kept alongside it, in the submittedGeneSymbols extension. From 1.1.0, a geneContextSource extension says where the gene came from.

items.title: How the qualifier is built
items.text:
Step 2 of gkm_scv_statement_proc (see Propositions) builds the qualifier as follows:

  • The gene is the variant's single representative gene, taken from the upstream single_gene_variation table (built by clinvar-ingest-bq-tools). That table picks at most one gene per variant by rules applied in order, strongest evidence first: the gene named in the variant's own name (a MANE transcript, an HGVS-style name or a star allele), then ClinVar's gene associations, then the shared gene of a haplotype's or genotype's alleles. Several rules are calculated upstream rather than supplied by ClinVar. See the Single Gene Variation method for the rules, the reasons for them and their known limitations.
  • The gene sets the qualifier's name (the gene symbol), its primaryCoding (the NCBI Gene id) and its HGNC mappings. The symbol and HGNC id are the ones the upstream method used for that release, so they come with the gene, even for a gene ClinVar names in the variant title without associating it.
  • The submitter's genes are the symbols the submitter gave in their submitted variant record. They are attached to the qualifier as the submittedGeneSymbols extension, verbatim and in submitted order. They never choose the gene.
  • The source is the geneContextSource extension, on every qualifier from 1.1.0:
    • submittedSymbolMatches: the submitter's symbols include the qualifier's symbol
    • submittedSymbolDiffers: the submitter gave symbols, but none equals the qualifier's symbol
    • inferredFromVariant: the submitter gave no symbols
    • submittedNotNormalized: the placeholder (next item)

Symbols are compared after trimming spaces and ignoring case, so C19ORF12 matches C19orf12. The schema accepts only these four values. - The placeholder applies when the variant has no single representative gene but the submitter named one. From 1.1.0, the qualifier's name is the submitter's symbol, verbatim; several symbols are joined with , in submitted order. It has no primaryCoding, the submitter's symbols are in submittedGeneSymbols, and geneContextSource is submittedNotNormalized. The 1.0.1 releases name it with the literal text submitted genes were not normalized. - When neither source has a gene, the proposition has no geneContextQualifier.

VCV and RCV propositions carry no gene context qualifier.

For example, SCV000024718-PATH has a qualifier gene of GBA1 (NCBI Gene 2629), while the submitter wrote GBA, the gene's previous symbol. The symbols differ, but the gene is the same:

"geneContextQualifier": {
  "type": "MappableConcept",
  "conceptType": "gene",
  "name": "GBA1",
  "primaryCoding": {
    "code": "2629",
    "name": "GBA1",
    "system": "https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/",
    "iris": ["https://identifiers.org/ncbigene:2629", "https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/2629"]
  },
  "mappings": [
    {
      "coding": {
        "code": "4177",
        "system": "https://www.genenames.org",
        "iris": ["https://identifiers.org/hgnc:4177", "https://www.genenames.org/data/gene-symbol-report/#!/hgnc_id/4177"]
      },
      "relation": "exactMatch"
    }
  ],
  "extensions": [
    { "name": "submittedGeneSymbols", "value": ["GBA"] },
    { "name": "geneContextSource", "value": "submittedSymbolDiffers" }
  ]
}

items.title: How the two sources compare
items.text:
Across the 6.74 million SCV propositions in the 1.0.1 2026-10 monthly (built from the 2026-09-28 release and frozen under v1/1.0/), the last release before geneContextSource, with symbols compared exactly:

Case Propositions Share The submitter's gene is the qualifier gene 5,781,673 85.8% The submitter gave the qualifier gene plus others 101 <0.1% The submitter's gene differs from the qualifier gene 27,817 0.4% The gene is inferred from the variant; the submitter gave none 881,325 13.1% Placeholder: the submitter gave a gene, the variant has no single gene 4,814 0.1% No gene from either source 40,849 0.6%

The 27,817 differing cases break down as follows:

Kind of difference Propositions Example The submitted symbol is not a gene symbol in the release's gene list — mostly a previous symbol of the same gene (GBA → GBA1, MUT → MMUT, C10orf2 → TWNK, IKBKAP → ELP1) 24,545 SCV000024718-PATH The submitted gene is another gene ClinVar associates with the variant 2,541 SCV000425435-PATH: ITGA4 vs submitted CERKL The submitted gene is a gene ClinVar does not associate with the variant 731 SCV004053541-PATH: PRAMEF18 vs submitted PRAMEF22

The two sources therefore agree almost everywhere. In the 1.0.1 releases (frozen under v1/1.0/), three gaps remained:

  • Inferred genes were not marked. For 881,325 propositions the qualifier states a gene the submitter never stated, and nothing in the record distinguished an inferred gene from a submitted one. You had to compare name with submittedGeneSymbols: when the extension is absent, the gene is inferred.
  • Placeholder names were not genes. For the 4,814 placeholder propositions, the submitter's gene was only in submittedGeneSymbols. Grouping or filtering on the qualifier name treated submitted genes were not normalized as if it were a gene.
  • A differing symbol is usually a renamed gene. Matching the submitter's symbol to the qualifier's symbol by string comparison over-reports disagreement. Only the last two rows of the table above are different genes.

From 1.1.0, the first two gaps are closed and the third is labeled:

  • Inferred genes are marked geneContextSource = inferredFromVariant.
  • Placeholder names carry the submitter's symbol and are marked submittedNotNormalized. A placeholder is still not a normalized gene, so filter on primaryCoding (or the Parquet gene_context_id) when you need one. Filtering on name alone now also matches placeholders: 29 TP53 placeholders in 2026-10-18, for example.
  • submittedSymbolDiffers says only that the symbols differ, not that the genes do. With the case-insensitive comparison it covers 28,507 propositions in 2026-10-18, where an exact comparison finds 28,653. The other 146 differ only by case and are now submittedSymbolMatches.

items.title: How to see it in the data
items.text:
The qualifier is part of each SCV proposition in the bundle and in the data column of the proposition Parquet tables:

-- Extensions are picked by name: the qualifier can carry two. (`lambda e:` needs DuckDB 1.3 or later.)
SELECT id,
       data->>'$.geneContextQualifier.name'               AS qualifier_gene,
       data->>'$.geneContextQualifier.primaryCoding.code' AS ncbi_gene,
       list_filter(CAST(data->'$.geneContextQualifier.extensions' AS JSON[]),
                   lambda e: e->>'$.name' = 'submittedGeneSymbols')[1]->'$.value' AS submitted_gene_symbols,
       list_filter(CAST(data->'$.geneContextQualifier.extensions' AS JSON[]),
                   lambda e: e->>'$.name' = 'geneContextSource')[1]->>'$.value'  AS gene_context_source
FROM 'propositionPathogenicity.parquet'
WHERE id IN ('SCV001494816-PATH', 'SCV000024718-PATH', 'SCV005419060-PATH', 'SCV000039919-PATH');

With 1.1.0 data:

id                 qualifier_gene  ncbi_gene  submitted_gene_symbols  gene_context_source
SCV005419060-PATH  TTN             7273       ["TTN","TTN-AS1"]       submittedSymbolMatches
SCV001494816-PATH  KCNT1           NULL       ["KCNT1"]               submittedNotNormalized
SCV000024718-PATH  GBA1            2629       ["GBA"]                 submittedSymbolDiffers
SCV000039919-PATH  SERPINC1        462        NULL                    inferredFromVariant

In the 1.0.1 releases (frozen under v1/1.0/), SCV001494816-PATH is named submitted genes were not normalized and has no geneContextSource.

From 1.1.0, the four proposition Parquet tables also carry typed gene_context_id (the qualifier's ncbigene: id, NULL for the placeholder), submitted_gene_symbols and gene_context_source columns.

items.title: Gene context is not the variant's gene list
items.text: The qualifier holds one representative gene. A variant's full set of ClinVar gene associations — every gene it lies in, overlaps or is near, each with a relationship type — is a different relationship. It is carried on the variant as the clinvarGeneList extension (see GeneListItem). Use the gene list to find all variants touching a gene, and the gene context qualifier for the gene a classification is framed around.

items.title: GA4GH GKS Standards
items.text: ClinVar-GKM represents ClinVar data using the GKM (Genomic Knowledge Model) schema set — VRS, Cat-VRS, and VA-Spec — curated by the GA4GH Genomic Knowledge Standards (GKS) workstream and built on shared GKM-Core classes. This page links each specification, its schema repository, and its official Python implementation, and notes how each is applied in this pipeline.

items.title: Specifications
items.text: Standard What it is How ClinVar-GKM uses it Specification Schema repo Python library VRS — Variation Representation Specification Extensible spec for representing and uniquely identifying biological sequence variation Every variant receives a computable, digest-identified VRS identifier vrs.ga4gh.org ga4gh/vrs ga4gh/vrs-python Cat-VRS — Categorical Variation A terminology and data model for describing categorical variation concepts Variations are represented as Cat-VRS categorical variants with defining-allele constraints and expressions cat-vrs.ga4gh.org ga4gh/cat-vrs ga4gh/cat-vrs-python VA-Spec — Variant Annotation Specification An information model for representing variant annotations (statements, propositions, evidence) Every SCV, VCV, and RCV classification is a VA-Spec statement with explicit propositions, evidence, and provenance va-spec.ga4gh.org ga4gh/va-spec ga4gh/va-spec-python GKM-Core Common classes and schemas shared by all GKS specifications (entities, MappableConcept, extensions, etc.) Underlies the shared building blocks used across VRS, Cat-VRS, and VA-Spec output — ga4gh/gkm-core (bundled with the libraries above)

items.title: Getting started with the standards
items.text:
• GKM Starter Kit (site) — a single community-facing entry point that helps you understand and adopt the GKS/GKM standards in practice.

The three Python libraries above (vrs-python, cat-vrs-python, va-spec-python) let you parse ClinVar-GKM bundle and Parquet records directly into the standards' validated models — see the planned Starter-kit documentation page on the Roadmap for worked examples.

items.title: Glossary
items.text: Key terms, acronyms, and concepts used throughout the ClinVar-GKM documentation.

items.title: Standards and Organizations
items.text:
GA4GH (Global Alliance for Genomics and Health) : International consortium developing standards for genomic data representation and exchange.

GKS (Genomic Knowledge Standards) : The GA4GH workstream that develops standards for representing genomic knowledge. Its schema set is referred to in this project as GKM (see below).

GKM (Genomic Knowledge Model) : The set of GA4GH GKS schemas — VRS, Cat-VRS, VA-Spec, and gkm-core — that ClinVar-GKM transforms ClinVar data into. Also the project's name and output brand.

VRS (Variation Representation Specification) : GA4GH standard for normalized, computable variant identifiers. Defines how variants are represented with sequence references, locations, and states.

Cat-VRS (Categorical Variation Representation Specification) : GA4GH standard for categorical variant representations that group variants at a higher level — CanonicalAlleles, CategoricalCnvChange, CategoricalCnvCount.

VA-Spec (Variant Annotation Specification) : GA4GH standard for variant annotation statements. Defines the Statement, Proposition, and EvidenceLine structures used by SCV and VCV outputs.

ACMG (American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics) : Organization that publishes pathogenicity classification guidelines (2015, v4) used by ClinVar submitters.

AMP/ASCO/CAP : Association for Molecular Pathology / American Society of Clinical Oncology / College of American Pathologists. Published somatic clinical impact tiering guidelines (Tier I-IV).

items.title: ClinVar Concepts
items.text:
ClinVar : NCBI database of variant submissions and aggregate classifications from clinical, research, and community sources.

SCV (Submitted Clinical Variant) : Individual submission from a laboratory, research group, or other organization reporting their interpretation of a variant. Each SCV contains one classification for one variant and condition combination.

VCV (Variant-level Clinical Variant) : Aggregate classification combining all SCV submissions for the same variant across all conditions. Represents the variant-level summary.

RCV (Review-level Clinical Variant) : Aggregate classification combining all SCV submissions for the same variant AND the same condition. Used internally by ClinVar for aggregation.

Trait (ClinVar terminology) : A disease, phenotype, or finding associated with a variant submission. In GKS output, this is termed "Condition."

TraitSet : A group of traits with a membership operator. In GKS output, this is termed "ConditionSet."

Review Status : Star levels (0-4) indicating submission confidence. Determines how submissions are ranked during aggregation. See Review Status.

items.title: Submission Levels
items.text:
Submission Level : Classification of SCV authority and review rigor. Determines aggregation logic and review status derivation.

PG (Practice Guideline) : Submission level rank 4 (4 stars). Published practice guidelines from authoritative bodies.

EP (Expert Panel) : Submission level rank 3 (3 stars). Classifications reviewed and approved by expert panels.

CP (Criteria Provided) : Submission level rank 1 (1 star). Submitter provided documented criteria for their classification.

NOCP (No Assertion Criteria Provided) : Submission level rank 0 (0 stars). Classification submitted without documented criteria.

NOCL (No Classification Provided) : Submission level rank -1 (0 stars). Submission present but no classification was given.

FLAG (Flagged Submission) : Submission level rank -3 (0 stars). Submission flagged by ClinVar for quality concerns.

items.title: Data Model
items.text:
Statement (VA-Spec) : A complete assertion containing classification, proposition, evidence, contributions, and metadata. Both SCV and VCV records are Statements.

Proposition (VA-Spec) : The core claim being asserted. Contains a subject (variant), predicate (relationship), object (condition/therapy), and optional qualifiers.

EvidenceLine (VA-Spec) : Links a proposition to evidence items with direction and strength assessments. Evidence lines are stored in the evidenceLine bundle section and referenced from all statement levels via hasEvidenceLines arrays of #/evidenceLine/ JSON pointer strings.

CategoricalVariant (Cat-VRS) : Higher-level grouping that associates a ClinVar variation with its resolved VRS representation. Types: CanonicalAllele, CategoricalCnvChange, CategoricalCnvCount.

MappableConcept : A single concept with conceptType, name, and optional extension array. Used for single-label classifications and single-condition object values.

ConceptSet : A structured group of concepts with type (ConceptSet), a concepts array, conceptSetType, and membershipOperator. Used for multi-condition object values (OR operator for VCV with multiple distinct conditions; AND operator for RCV conditionSets).

Constraint (Cat-VRS) : Defining relationship between a categorical variant and its VRS representation. Types: DefiningAlleleConstraint, DefiningLocationConstraint, CopyChangeConstraint, CopyCountConstraint.

Extension : Name/value pair carrying metadata not part of core GA4GH specifications but essential for interpreting the data. Present on statements, classifications, propositions, conditions, and categorical variants.

items.title: Proposition Types
items.text:
VariantPathogenicityProposition : Proposition type for germline pathogenicity assertions. Predicate: isCausalFor. Statement type G.01.

VariantOncogenicityProposition : Proposition type for oncogenicity assertions. Predicate: isOncogenicFor. Statement type O.10.

VariantClinicalSignificanceProposition : Proposition type for somatic clinical significance (AMP/ASCO/CAP tiering). Predicate: hasClinicalSignificanceFor. Statement type S.11.

VariantTherapeuticResponseProposition : Proposition type for therapeutic response assertions. Predicate: predictsSensitivityTo. Statement type S.12.

VariantDiagnosticProposition : Proposition type for diagnostic assertions. Statement type S.13.

VariantPrognosticProposition : Proposition type for prognostic assertions. Statement type S.14.

ClinVar*Proposition : Custom proposition types for the ClinVar germline statement types that VA-Spec does not define, all in the propositionClinvarCustom bundle section: ClinvarDrugResponseProposition (DR), ClinvarRiskFactorProposition (RF), ClinvarProtectiveProposition (PROTECT), ClinvarAffectsProposition (AFF), ClinvarAssociationProposition (ASSOC), ClinvarConfersSensitivityProposition (CS), ClinvarOtherProposition (OTH), ClinvarNotProvidedProposition (NP), ClinvarConflictingDataFromSubmitterProposition (CDFS) and ClinvarUndefinedProposition (UNDEF). See Propositions.

items.title: Classification Terms
items.text:
Quality : Statement-level attribute (Statement.quality, va-spec 2026-09) indicating the submission level — a review-status/trust rating. A Concept struct with conceptType: "Quality" and name set to the submission level label (e.g., "criteria provided", "expert panel"). Present on SCV and aggregate (VCV/RCV) statements. Replaces the former confidence attribute.

Direction : Whether evidence supports or disputes a proposition. Values: supports, disputes, neutral. On aggregate statements, derived from the classification label (multi-SCV) or passed through from the contributing SCV (single-SCV).

Strength : Evidence strength level. Values: definitive, likely, strong, potential. Omitted (null) when not applicable. On aggregate statements, derived from the classification label (multi-SCV) or passed through from the contributing SCV (single-SCV).

Tier I / Tier II / Tier III / Tier IV : Somatic clinical impact classification levels. Tier I (Strong) and Tier II (Potential) require paired sub-statements. Tier III (Unknown) and Tier IV (Benign/Likely benign) do not.

Concordant : All contributing SCVs for a variant share the same classification. Produces a single aggregate label.

Conflicting : Contributing SCVs have different classifications. Produces a "Conflicting classifications of..." label with a conflictingExplanation extension.

items.title: Qualifier Types
items.text:
Gene Context Qualifier : Proposition qualifier restricting an assertion to a specific gene. Contains NCBI Gene identifier and HGNC mappings.

geneContextSource : Extension on every SCV gene context qualifier, from 1.1.0, saying where its gene came from: submittedSymbolMatches, submittedSymbolDiffers, inferredFromVariant or submittedNotNormalized. See the gene context FAQ.

Mode of Inheritance Qualifier : Proposition qualifier specifying inheritance pattern (e.g., autosomal dominant, X-linked). Maps to HPO terms.

Penetrance Qualifier : Proposition qualifier indicating penetrance level for pathogenic or risk allele classifications. Values: low, risk.

items.title: VCV Aggregation
items.text:
Aggregation : Process of combining multiple SCV submissions into higher-order VCV statements following submission-level-specific logic.

Winner-Takes-All : Aggregation strategy at the Aggregate Contribution Layer where the highest-ranked submission level's classification becomes the aggregate result. Lower-ranked levels become non-contributing.

Contributing Submission : Submission whose review status is highest-ranked within an aggregation group. Directly reflected in the aggregate classification.

Non-Contributing Submission : Submission ranked lower than the contributing submission. Preserved in the evidence structure but not reflected in the aggregate label.

Grouping Layer : First conceptual aggregation layer. Consists of Classification Grouping and Priority Grouping steps. Produces initial aggregation of SCVs into groups by submission level.

Classification Grouping (Grouping Layer) : First step of the Grouping Layer. Groups SCVs by variation + statement group + proposition type + submission level [+ tier]. Applies submission-level-specific classification and conflict detection logic.

Priority Grouping (Grouping Layer) : Second step of the Grouping Layer (somatic sci only). Aggregates tier-level groups within each submission level.

Aggregate Contribution Layer : Second and final aggregation layer. Applies winner-takes-all ranking across submission levels. Terminal layer for both germline and somatic statements.

Aggregate Review Status : Final review status of a VCV statement derived from submission level and aggregation outcome. See Aggregate Review Status.

items.title: Classification Attributes (VCV/RCV)
items.text:
classification : VCV/RCV statement-level classification attribute. Contains a single aggregate label with optional conflictingExplanation extension. The classification lives only on the statement, not on the proposition.

object : VCV/RCV proposition attribute. Contains the unique condition(s) associated with the aggregate statement. For VCV, this is a single MappableConcept or an OR ConceptSet of distinct conditions from contributing SCVs. For RCV, this is the condition sourced from gkm_scv_condition_sets — either a Condition MappableConcept or a ConditionSet ConceptSet. Extensions excluded.

items.title: Identifier Formats
items.text:
clinvar:{variation_id} : ClinVar variation identifier. References a CategoricalVariant record in the variation bundle section. Example: clinvar:12582.

clinvar.submission:SCV{id}.{version} : SCV submission identifier with version. References an SCV Statement record in the scv bundle section. Example: clinvar.submission:SCV001571657.2.

clinvar.submitter:{submitter_id} : Submitter organization identifier. References a submitter record in the submitter bundle section. Example: clinvar.submitter:508027.

clinvar.trait:{trait_id} : Condition/trait identifier. References a condition record in the condition bundle section. Example: clinvar.trait:9580.

clinvar.traitset:{trait_set_id} : Condition set identifier. References a condition set in the conditionSet bundle section. Example: clinvar.traitset:1234.

ga4gh:{type}.{digest} : VRS identity digest. References alleles or locations in the corresponding bundle sections. Example: ga4gh:VA.xXBYkzzu1AH0oyMKlbBtP2.

items.title: Output Format
items.text:
Bundle : A JSON file containing all data for a ClinVar release, organized as named sections at the root level. Each section is a keyed collection of objects of the same class, where the key is the object's unique identifier. Objects reference each other using #/ JSON pointer strings. Typed Parquet files derived from the bundle are published for the latest release only.

Bundle Section : A named top-level key in the bundle file (e.g., variation, scv, propositionPathogenicity) containing a keyed collection of objects.

JSON Pointer Reference : A #/{section}/{key} string used to reference an object in another bundle section. Example: #/allele/ga4gh:VA.abc123 resolves to the allele with that key in the allele section.

items.title: Releases and Distribution
items.text:
Official monthly full : The full bundle clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MM.json.gz, published once a month for ClinVar's ClinVarVCVRelease_YYYY-MM, built from the most recent weekly release before ClinVar's monthly cut. See How Releases Work.

Weekly full : The full bundle of one weekly release, weekly/clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MMDD.json.gz, published for every release and kept for the current month only.

Delta : The records added or updated since the prior release, clinvar-gkm-delta_YYYY-MMDD.json.gz, with a manifest listing per-section adds, updates and deletes. See Weekly Deltas.

00-latest : The stable filenames that always hold the newest file of a kind: clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz (newest official monthly) and weekly/clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz (newest weekly full).

source_release : In a line's index.json, the ClinVar weekly release a monthly full, or the Parquet set, was built from.

Version line : The folder v{major}/{major}.{minor}/ (e.g. v1/1.1/) that holds every release of one schema MINOR version, with its own index.json and feed. A line is current or frozen. See Versioning & Releases.

items.title: Technical Terms
items.text:
Null Stripping : Technique where null-valued fields and empty arrays are omitted from JSON output via JSON_STRIP_NULLS(remove_empty => TRUE).

By-Reference Format : JSON structure where related objects are referenced by ID rather than embedded inline. Reduces duplication when many statements reference the same variant.

Inline Format : JSON structure where related objects are fully embedded within the parent. Self-contained — each record has all data needed for interpretation.

JSON Pointer : Standard format (RFC 6901) for referencing nested JSON values. Used in somatic target propositions (e.g., 4/proposition/subject).

BigQuery : Google Cloud Platform data warehouse used for all ClinVar-GKM SQL procedures and table storage.

Stored Procedure : BigQuery SQL routine executing a specific pipeline step (e.g., gkm_catvar_proc, gkm_vcv_proc).

items.title: External Databases
items.text:
MedGen : Medical Genetics database providing standardized condition identifiers. Primary coding system for conditions.

OMIM (Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man) : Comprehensive database of genetic disorders. Used for condition cross-references.

MONDO (Monarch Disease Ontology) : Unified disease ontology providing standardized condition identifiers.

HPO (Human Phenotype Ontology) : Standardized phenotype terms used for conditions and mode of inheritance.

Orphanet : Database of rare diseases. Used for condition cross-references.

HGNC (HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee) : Official gene nomenclature database. Gene symbols and identifiers appear in gene context qualifiers.

dbSNP : NCBI SNP database. External cross-reference source for variants.

identifiers.org : Standardized URL namespace for biomedical identifiers used in mapping IRIs.

items.title: Known Issues
items.text: This page documents the current release status, data-coverage limitations, and transformation caveats of the ClinVar-GKM pipeline.

items.title: Release status
items.text: The current release is 1.1.0. It regroups the proposition sections by meaning and carries a set of data corrections, all delivered by one full rebuild of every published release. It is built on the finalized GKM (Genomic Knowledge Model) standards — VRS 2.1.1, Cat-VRS 1.1.1, VA-Spec 1.1.0, and GKM-Core 1.3.0 — and published under v1/1.1/; the 1.0.1 releases are kept, frozen, under v1/1.0/. See the Changelog for what 1.1.0 changed.

items.title: Data coverage
items.text:
Each release includes 100% of the Germline and Somatic submission (SCV) records from the corresponding ClinVar XML release, and their classification content is carried through without modification to what ClinVar provides. However, the pipeline does not yet extract 100% of every attribute and tertiary content:

  • Case-level and functional data — aggregate case values, grouped/individual case-level evidence, and functional-data (incl. MaveDB) submissions are not currently extracted.
  • Rarely-provided attributes — some attributes that ClinVar provides only occasionally and sparsely may also not yet be represented.

If data that exists in ClinVar is missing here and would be useful to you, it can be added to the Roadmap and prioritized by community demand — open or upvote a discussion in the Ideas category. Case-level / functional data are already tracked as roadmap items (case data, functional data).

items.title: Delta reconstruction — VRS allele records (resolved in 1.1.0)
items.text: In 1.0.1, reconstructing a release's allele section from the prior release plus its weekly delta was inexact for about a dozen VRS allele records, most at the 2026-08-29 release, where the VRS line advanced, and the rest from non-deterministic ordering in allele assembly. Resolved in 1.1.0: alleles are built once per allele id with a total order, and the delta-reconstruction oracle finds no difference (0,0,0) on every section for all 16 delta pairs, including the cross-version pair 2026-08-22 → 2026-08-29. The frozen 1.0.1 deltas under v1/1.0/ keep the old behavior.

items.title: VRS normalization errors
items.text: VRS normalization does not resolve every variation. In the 2026-10-18 release, 6 of the 43,868 variations sent for normalization returned an error. The error text is in the vrsProcessingException extension on the variation's variation record. See Categorical Variant Extensions.

items.title: Malformed HGVS expressions in ClinVar
items.text: 16 HGVS expressions on 14 variations in ClinVar's VCV XML are malformed at the source, most without an HGVS type letter (g., c.). From 1.1.0 each is kept verbatim as an extension of a listed expression, either merged onto ClinVar's valid expression for the same accession or on a repaired one; see HgvsListItem. They were reported to ClinVar on 2026-10-18 (NCBI case CAS-1713568-P1W1Q1), tracked in #163.

items.title: DOIs that VA-Spec's pattern rejects
items.text: VA-Spec's Document.doi pattern rejects some valid DOIs, such as SICI-style DOIs with parentheses (ga4gh/va-spec#461). Such a DOI is kept in the clinvarDoi extension of its Document, with its doi.org URL in urls, instead of in doi. See Citations.

items.title: RCV membership lists SCVs missing from the VCV data
items.text: ClinVar's RCV-format XML runs out of sync with its VCV XML: an RCV's SCV list sometimes names SCVs that are absent from the VCV data, 2–3 a week. This is ClinVar's data, faithfully parsed. RCV statements are built only from SCVs present in the VCV data, so an RCV's evidence can list fewer SCVs than ClinVar's RCV record.

items.title: Name-derived gene context genes are not in the gene section
items.text: An SCV proposition's gene context can be a gene named in the variant's title that ClinVar does not associate with the variant (for example NR_164162.1(GLRA4):n.1091C>T → GLRA4). The bundle's gene section lists only the genes ClinVar associates with a variant, so such a gene has no gene record, and its Parquet gene_context_id does not join to gene.parquet. In the 2026-10-11 release this is 25 variants and 31 SCV propositions. Genes with no HGNC id (LOC*) and NCBI-discontinued gene ids get no gene context, by design of the upstream method.

items.title: Bundle schema $id does not resolve
items.text: The bundle schema's $id, https://w3id.org/clingen/schema/clinvar-gkm/<version>/json/ClinvarGkmBundle, returns 404: the file is published as schema/clinvar-gkm/clinvar-gkm-bundle.schema.json, not under json/. This is true for 1.0.0 and 1.0.1 as well, whose class schema $ids do resolve. Validators that load the schemas from a local copy or registry are unaffected.

items.title: Past Parquet cannot yet be rebuilt
items.text:
Only the latest Parquet set is published. Past Parquet is meant to be rebuilt from the monthly bundles with clinvar-gkm-parquet, which has no release yet.

Additional edge cases, transformation caveats, and specific limitations will be documented here as they are identified.

items.title: Release Validation
items.text:
Every release is gated before any file is published. The gates check the BigQuery tables the bundles are exported from, the real staged bundles themselves, and the Parquet dataset derived from them. A release is published only when every gate passes. This page lists the gates and the results for 1.1.0.

The step-by-step procedure, with the exact commands and the expected output of each gate, is the 1.1.0 rebuild runbook. The changes these gates verified are listed in the 1.1.0 changelog.

items.title: Gates
items.text:
Gate What it checks Scope Proposition structure and reference integrity validate-proposition-conformance.sh: every proposition has the structure its type requires, and every statement and evidence-line pointer names the section its proposition is in — no old-section, unparsed, dangling, misrouted or bare reference Every dataset Expected difference Every row that differs from a snapshot taken before the rebuild is joined on its primary key and classified; each class of change must be attributed to a fix shipped in the release Every dataset that existed before the rebuild Delta reconstruction oracle-delta-reconstruction.sh: the baseline release minus the delta's deletes plus the delta's records equals the next release, compared on all 21 bundle tables Every consecutive pair of releases Strict GA4GH validation The official GA4GH gkm-toolkit (ga4gh.gkm 0.4.0), in strict mode, validates every record of the real staged bundle, verbatim, against the schema/ tree The first full bundle and every delta (see below) Structural check schema_version, section order, one well-formed record per line, and per-section record counts equal to the BigQuery tables Every other full bundle No null or empty values No field anywhere carries null, "", [] or {}, except the null bound of a VRS Range, which VRS uses for an open-ended coordinate Every staged bundle Bundle ↔ Parquet Per-section record counts, ids in both directions, and a sampled comparison of each row's data with the bundle record The Parquet dataset against the full bundle of the release it was built from

Why the strict scope covers every record. Each later full bundle equals the first full plus the deltas after it, which the delta-reconstruction gate proves. The 2026-06-27 full and the 16 deltas therefore together contain every distinct record of every 1.1.0 bundle, so strict validation of those 17 files validates every record that 1.1.0 publishes. The other fulls get the structural check.

items.title: 1.1.0 Results
items.text:
1.1.0 rebuilt 17 BigQuery datasets, 2026-06-27 through 2026-10-18, and staged 4 monthly full bundles, 3 weekly full bundles, 16 deltas and one Parquet dataset built from 2026-10-18.

Gate Result Proposition structure and reference integrity PASS on 17/17 datasets Expected difference PASS on 16/16 datasets: every difference attributed to a shipped fix Delta reconstruction PASS on 16/16 pairs, 0,0,0 (no missing, extra or differing rows) on all 21 tables, including the cross-version pair 2026-08-22 → 2026-08-29 Strict GA4GH validation PASS, failing: 0: the 2026-06-27 full (86,810,319 records), all 16 deltas and the 2026-10-18 weekly full (91,491,982 records), every section Structural check PASS on the other 5 full bundles (2026-08-04, 2026-08-29, 2026-09-28, 2026-10-04, 2026-10-11): schema_version 1.1.0, section order, well-formed records, and per-section counts equal to BigQuery No null or empty values PASS on all 4 monthly and 3 weekly full bundles and the 16 deltas Bundle ↔ Parquet PASS for 2026-10-18: all 20 sections have equal counts and ids (0 in the bundle only, 0 in Parquet only); 183,368 sampled records' data equal

items.title: Verification reports
items.text:
The strict GA4GH validation of the published files produces a stamped report for each file. Each report records:

  • the UTC run time;
  • the tool and schema versions;
  • the file's published URL and the sha256 of the bytes validated, checked against the published .sha256;
  • per section, the records and failures and the schema those records are validated against;
  • every check, and any warnings.

The 1.1.0 reports are attached to the 1.1.0 GitHub Release:

File Result Report weekly/clinvar-gkm_2026-1018.json.gz (the newest full bundle) PASS: 91,491,982 records in 20 sections, 0 failing Markdown · JSON deltas/clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1018.json.gz PASS: 215,170 records in 15 sections, 0 failing Markdown · JSON

Reports for the other full bundles and deltas will be added as they are produced. The report option is being contributed to the GA4GH GKM Toolkit (ga4gh/gkm-starter-kit#128).

items.title: Roadmap
items.text:
ClinVar-GKM's direction is shaped in the open. The table below is the current backlog of ideas under consideration, ordered by community upvotes. Each idea has a matching GitHub Discussion — open it and use the Upvote button (the ▲ in the bottom-left corner of the discussion's opening post) to signal you want it prioritized, and comment with your use case. Maintainers use the upvote tally to decide the order in which features and improvements are taken on.

Nothing here is a commitment or a delivery date — it's a prioritization board. Items move through Proposed → Spec'd → In progress → Shipped as they gain support and get built.
