items.title: Chunk 1: index.json generator — dates + per-delta Parquet
Task 1: Add modified dates and per-delta parquet lists to generate-r2-index.sh
items.text:
Files: - Modify: src/scripts/generate-r2-index.sh

Background: aws s3 ls <prefix> prints DATE TIME SIZE NAME for files and PRE name/ for sub-dirs. Today r2_ls_with_size keeps $3,$4 (size,name) and directory-based entries (deltas, parquet sets) carry no date. See spec §6/§7.

  • [ ] Step 1: Capture the date in r2_ls_with_size

Modify the awk in r2_ls_with_size (currently {print $3, $4}) to emit the date too:

r2_ls_with_size() {
  # Returns "DATE SIZE FILENAME" lines for .json.gz files under a prefix
  local prefix="$1"
  aws s3 ls "s3://${R2_BUCKET}/${prefix}" \
    --endpoint-url "${R2_ENDPOINT}" \
    --profile "${R2_PROFILE}" \
    2>/dev/null | awk '/\.json\.gz$/ {print $1, $3, $4}' || true
}
  • [ ] Step 2: Thread the date through build_file_array

Update the read loop and the emitted JSON object to include modified:

build_file_array() {
  local prefix="$1" latest_name="$2"
  local first=true
  local arr="["

  while IFS=' ' read -r modified size filename; do
    [[ -z "$filename" ]] && continue
    if ! $first; then arr+=","; fi
    first=false

    local is_latest="false"
    if [[ -n "$latest_name" && "$filename" == "$latest_name" ]]; then
      is_latest="true"
    fi

    arr+=$(printf '{"name":"%s","path":"%s%s","size":%s,"modified":"%s","latest":%s}' \
      "$filename" "$prefix" "$filename" "$size" "$modified" "$is_latest")
  done < <(r2_ls_with_size "$prefix")

  arr+="]"
  echo "$arr"
}
  • [ ] Step 3: Add two helper functions (after r2_ls_with_size)
# Newest immediate-file date (YYYY-MM-DD) under a prefix, or empty.
# Skips "PRE dir/" lines (they have no date in $1).
r2_newest_date_under() {
  local prefix="$1"
  aws s3 ls "s3://${R2_BUCKET}/${prefix}" \
    --endpoint-url "${R2_ENDPOINT}" \
    --profile "${R2_PROFILE}" \
    2>/dev/null \
    | awk '$1 ~ /^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$/ {print $1}' \
    | sort | tail -n1 || true
}

# JSON array of parquet section names (filename minus .parquet) under a prefix.
r2_parquet_sections_under() {
  local prefix="$1"
  local first=true
  local arr="["
  while IFS= read -r section; do
    [[ -z "$section" ]] && continue
    if ! $first; then arr+=","; fi
    first=false
    arr+=$(printf '"%s"' "$section")
  done < <(
    aws s3 ls "s3://${R2_BUCKET}/${prefix}" \
      --endpoint-url "${R2_ENDPOINT}" \
      --profile "${R2_PROFILE}" \
      2>/dev/null | awk '/\.parquet$/ {sub(/\.parquet$/, "", $NF); print $NF}' || true
  )
  arr+="]"
  echo "$arr"
}
  • [ ] Step 4: Add modified to Parquet set entries in build_parquet_array

Inside the loop, after release/is_latest are set, compute the date and add the field:

    local modified
    modified="$(r2_newest_date_under "${prefix}${dir}/")"

    arr+=$(printf '{"release":"%s","path":"%s%s/","modified":"%s","latest":%s}' \
      "$release" "$prefix" "$dir" "$modified" "$is_latest")
  • [ ] Step 5: Add modified + parquet to delta entries in build_deltas_array

Inside the loop, after path/is_latest are set:

    local modified parquet_sections
    modified="$(r2_newest_date_under "deltas/${dir}/")"
    parquet_sections="$(r2_parquet_sections_under "deltas/${dir}/parquet/")"

    arr+=$(printf '{"release":"%s","path":"%s","manifest":"%smanifest.json","modified":"%s","parquet":%s,"latest":%s}' \
      "$release" "$path" "$path" "$modified" "$parquet_sections" "$is_latest")
  • [ ] Step 6: Lint

Run: bash -n src/scripts/generate-r2-index.sh && shellcheck src/scripts/generate-r2-index.sh Expected: no syntax errors; no new shellcheck warnings beyond pre-existing.

  • [ ] Step 7: Dry-run against live R2 (read-only) and inspect the candidate index

Run: 

src/scripts/generate-r2-index.sh --dry-run
python3 -m json.tool /tmp/clinvar-gkm-index.json | \
  grep -E '"modified"|"parquet"|"name"|"release"' | head -40
Expected: monthly entries show "modified":"YYYY-MM-DD"; each delta shows "modified" and a "parquet":[...] array of section names; parquet sets show "modified". No upload occurs (--dry-run gates r2_upload). If any modified is empty, re-check the awk field positions against aws s3 ls output.

  • [ ] Step 8: Commit
git add src/scripts/generate-r2-index.sh
git commit -m "feat(r2-index): add modified dates + per-delta parquet lists to index.json"

items.title: Task 2: Create docs/assets/js/r2-browser.js and wire it in
items.text:
Files: - Create: docs/assets/js/r2-browser.js - Modify: zensical.toml (line 10, extra_javascript)

This generalizes the inline script currently in download.md into a reusable, mount-driven component. It renders five view types and shows modified dates when present. It no-ops when no .r2-browser mount exists on the page.

  • [ ] Step 1: Write docs/assets/js/r2-browser.js
/* Shared R2 release browser. Each mount element:
     <div class="r2-browser" data-r2-type="TYPE"></div>
   TYPE ∈ latest | monthly | deltas | parquet-monthly | parquet-weekly
   Fetches index.json once per page; renders each mount by its type.
   No-ops when no mount is present. CSP-safe (no external requests besides index.json). */
(function () {
  var mounts = document.querySelectorAll(".r2-browser");
  if (!mounts.length) return;

  var BASE_URL = "https://pub-f0ad0e0dac0345408dcc95bda20beb42.r2.dev";
  var INDEX_URL = BASE_URL + "/index.json";

  // Stable section order for composing Parquet URLs (full sets always carry all 22).
  var PARQUET_SECTIONS = [
    "sequenceReference", "location", "allele", "copyNumberCount", "copyNumberChange",
    "gene", "variation", "condition", "conditionSet", "therapy", "therapyGroup", "submitter",
    "varcond-proposition", "vartumor-proposition", "vartherapy-proposition", "varcustom-proposition",
    "evidenceLine", "vcv_evidenceLine", "rcv_evidenceLine", "scv", "vcv", "rcv"
  ];
  var LATEST_MONTHLY = "clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz";

  function el(tag, attrs, children) {
    var e = document.createElement(tag);
    if (attrs) Object.keys(attrs).forEach(function (k) {
      if (k === "text") e.textContent = attrs[k];
      else if (k === "html") e.innerHTML = attrs[k];
      else if (k === "className") e.className = attrs[k];
      else if (k === "style") Object.assign(e.style, attrs[k]);
      else e.setAttribute(k, attrs[k]);
    });
    if (children) children.forEach(function (c) { if (c) e.appendChild(c); });
    return e;
  }

  function formatSize(bytes) {
    if (!bytes) return "";
    if (bytes < 1024) return bytes + " B";
    if (bytes < 1048576) return (bytes / 1024).toFixed(1) + " KB";
    if (bytes < 1073741824) return (bytes / 1048576).toFixed(1) + " MB";
    return (bytes / 1073741824).toFixed(2) + " GB";
  }

  function meta(text) { return el("span", { className: "r2-size", text: text }); }
  function dateBadge(modified) {       // returns null when absent (graceful fallback)
    return modified ? el("span", { className: "r2-date", text: modified }) : null;
  }
  function fileRow(name, url, size, modified) {
    return el("div", { className: "r2-file" }, [
      el("a", { href: url, text: name }),
      size ? meta(formatSize(size)) : null,
      dateBadge(modified)
    ]);
  }
  function folder(label, open, badge) {
    var f = el("details", { className: "r2-folder" });
    if (open) f.setAttribute("open", "");
    var s = el("summary", { text: label });
    if (badge) s.appendChild(badge);
    f.appendChild(s);
    return f;
  }

  // --- view renderers -------------------------------------------------------
  function newestDated(list) {          // newest entry whose release != "latest"
    var dated = list.filter(function (x) {
      return (x.release && x.release !== "latest") ||
             (x.name && x.name !== LATEST_MONTHLY);
    });
    dated.sort(function (a, b) {
      return String(b.release || b.name).localeCompare(String(a.release || a.name));
    });
    return dated[0] || null;
  }

  function renderLatest(mount, data) {
    var monthly = (data.datasets && data.datasets.monthly) || [];
    var parquet = (data.datasets && data.datasets.parquet) || [];
    var deltas = data.deltas || [];
    var mLatest = monthly.filter(function (f) { return f.latest; })[0];
    var dLatest = deltas.filter(function (d) { return d.latest; })[0];
    var mDated = newestDated(monthly), dDated = newestDated(deltas), pDated = newestDated(parquet);

    function deltaDir(d) { return d.path.replace(/^deltas\//, "").replace(/\/$/, ""); }

    // "Get" cells: monthly = one stable bundle; delta = bundle + manifest; parquet set is a
    // directory (no single file) so link to the Parquet page. "../parquet/" is page-relative
    // from the hub (/data-access/download/ -> /data-access/parquet/); verified in the serve test.
    var monthlyGet = mLatest ? [el("a", { href: BASE_URL + "/" + mLatest.path, text: "bundle" })] : [];
    var deltaGet = dLatest ? [
      el("a", { href: BASE_URL + "/" + dLatest.path + "clinvar-gkm-delta_00-latest.json.gz", text: "bundle" }),
      el("span", { text: " · " }),
      el("a", { href: BASE_URL + "/" + dLatest.path + "manifest.json", text: "manifest" })
    ] : [];
    var parquetGet = [el("a", { href: "../parquet/", text: "browse sets →" })];

    var rows = [
      ["Monthly full", mDated ? mDated.name.replace(/^clinvar-gkm_|\.json\.gz$/g, "") : "", mDated && mDated.modified, monthlyGet],
      ["Weekly delta", dDated ? deltaDir(dDated).replace(/^(\d{4})-(\d{2})(\d{2})$/, "$1-$2-$3") : "", dDated && dDated.modified, deltaGet],
      ["Parquet (full)", pDated ? pDated.release : "", pDated && pDated.modified, parquetGet]
    ];

    var table = el("table", { className: "r2-latest" });
    table.appendChild(el("thead", {}, [el("tr", {}, ["Type", "Release", "R2 available", "Get"].map(
      function (h) { return el("th", { text: h }); }))]));
    var tbody = el("tbody");
    rows.forEach(function (r) {
      tbody.appendChild(el("tr", {}, [
        el("td", { text: r[0] }), el("td", { text: r[1] }), el("td", { text: r[2] || "" }), el("td", {}, r[3])
      ]));
    });
    table.appendChild(tbody);
    mount.appendChild(table);
  }

  function renderFileList(mount, files, archivesByYear) {
    var top = folder("datasets/", true);
    (files || []).forEach(function (f) {
      top.appendChild(fileRow(f.name, BASE_URL + "/" + f.path, f.size, f.modified));
    });
    mount.appendChild(top);
    var years = Object.keys(archivesByYear || {}).sort().reverse();
    years.forEach(function (y, i) {
      var yf = folder("archives/" + y + "/", i === 0);
      (archivesByYear[y].monthly || []).forEach(function (f) {
        yf.appendChild(fileRow(f.name, BASE_URL + "/" + f.path, f.size, f.modified));
      });
      mount.appendChild(yf);
    });
  }

  function renderDeltas(mount, deltas) {
    var top = folder("deltas/", true);
    (deltas || []).slice().sort(function (a, b) {
      if (a.release === "latest") return -1;
      if (b.release === "latest") return 1;
      return b.release.localeCompare(a.release);
    }).forEach(function (d) {
      var dir = d.path.replace(/^deltas\//, "").replace(/\/$/, "");
      var row = el("div", { className: "r2-file" }, [
        el("a", { href: BASE_URL + "/" + d.path + "clinvar-gkm-delta_" + dir + ".json.gz", text: dir }),
        el("span", { className: "r2-size" }, [el("a", { href: BASE_URL + "/" + d.manifest, text: "manifest.json" })]),
        dateBadge(d.modified)
      ]);
      top.appendChild(row);
    });
    mount.appendChild(top);
  }

  function renderParquetMonthly(mount, sets, archivesByYear) {
    function set(p, open) {
      var label = p.release === "latest" ? "00-latest" : p.release;
      var f = folder(label, open, dateBadge(p.modified));
      PARQUET_SECTIONS.forEach(function (s) {
        f.appendChild(fileRow(s + ".parquet", BASE_URL + "/" + p.path + s + ".parquet"));
      });
      return f;
    }
    (sets || []).slice().sort(function (a, b) {
      if (a.release === "latest") return -1;
      if (b.release === "latest") return 1;
      return b.release.localeCompare(a.release);
    }).forEach(function (p, i) { mount.appendChild(set(p, i === 0)); });
    var years = Object.keys(archivesByYear || {}).sort().reverse();
    years.forEach(function (y) {
      (archivesByYear[y].parquet || []).forEach(function (p) { mount.appendChild(set(p, false)); });
    });
  }

  function renderParquetWeekly(mount, deltas) {
    (deltas || []).filter(function (d) { return d.release !== "latest" && d.parquet && d.parquet.length; })
      .sort(function (a, b) { return b.release.localeCompare(a.release); })
      .forEach(function (d, i) {
        var f = folder(d.release, i === 0, dateBadge(d.modified));
        d.parquet.forEach(function (s) {
          f.appendChild(fileRow(s + ".parquet", BASE_URL + "/" + d.path + "parquet/" + s + ".parquet"));
        });
        mount.appendChild(f);
      });
  }

  function render(mount, data) {
    var t = mount.getAttribute("data-r2-type");
    var arch = data.archives || {};
    if (t === "latest") renderLatest(mount, data);
    else if (t === "monthly") renderFileList(mount, (data.datasets || {}).monthly, arch);
    else if (t === "deltas") renderDeltas(mount, data.deltas);
    else if (t === "parquet-monthly") renderParquetMonthly(mount, (data.datasets || {}).parquet, arch);
    else if (t === "parquet-weekly") renderParquetWeekly(mount, data.deltas);
  }

  function fail(msg) {
    mounts.forEach(function (m) {
      m.appendChild(el("div", { className: "r2-error", text: msg }));
    });
  }

  fetch(INDEX_URL)
    .then(function (r) { if (!r.ok) throw new Error("HTTP " + r.status); return r.json(); })
    .then(function (data) { mounts.forEach(function (m) { render(m, data); }); })
    .catch(function (err) {
      var isNetwork = (err instanceof TypeError) ||
        /failed to fetch|networkerror|load failed/i.test(err.message || "");
      fail(isNetwork
        ? "Couldn't load the release index (network/CORS). Fetch it directly: curl -s " + INDEX_URL
        : "Unable to load the release index (" + err.message + ").");
    });
})();
  • [ ] Step 2: Add the component to extra_javascript

In zensical.toml line 10, add the new file (keep any existing entry):

extra_javascript = ["assets/js/keyboard-shortcuts.js", "assets/js/r2-browser.js"]

Merge note: the search-fix PR #120 removes keyboard-shortcuts.js from this list. When both land on 1.0, reconcile to extra_javascript = ["assets/js/r2-browser.js"].

  • [ ] Step 3: Add styles to docs/stylesheets/extra.css. These supersede the per-page <style> block in the old download.md (removed in Task 9) and are shared by all child pages. The new JS uses only .r2-folder / .r2-file / .r2-size / .r2-date / .r2-latest / .r2-error; the old page's .r2-badge / .r2-group / .r2-section classes are unused and dropped. Port the old disclosure-triangle (.r2-folder > summary::before) and .r2-file a link styling into the block below if you want visual parity.

Add to docs/stylesheets/extra.css:

.r2-browser { font-family: var(--md-code-font-family); font-size: 0.82rem; line-height: 1.6; }
.r2-folder > summary { cursor: pointer; font-weight: 600; padding: 0.15rem 0; }
.r2-file { padding: 0.1rem 0 0.1rem 0.4rem; }
.r2-size, .r2-date { color: var(--md-default-fg-color--light); font-size: 0.75rem; margin-left: 0.5rem; }
.r2-latest { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; }
.r2-latest th, .r2-latest td { text-align: left; padding: 0.3rem 0.6rem; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--md-default-fg-color--lightest); }
.r2-error { padding: 0.8rem; border-left: 3px solid var(--md-accent-fg-color); margin: 1rem 0; }
  • [ ] Step 4: Build

Run: zensical build --strict Expected: "No issues found" (JS + CSS referenced; no page mounts yet, so the script no-ops).

  • [ ] Step 5: Commit
git add docs/assets/js/r2-browser.js zensical.toml docs/stylesheets/extra.css
git commit -m "feat(docs): shared r2-browser.js with per-type mounts + date rendering"

items.title: submittedCondition/Set CURIE De-pointer — Implementation Plan
items.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (if subagents available) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: In the submittedCondition / submittedConditionSet SCV extensions, change the four string fields condition, conditionSet, normalized_match, direct_match from JSON pointers (#/condition/clinvar.trait:NNN) to bare CURIEs (clinvar.trait:NNN) — a content-only change (no field/type/shape change, no schema version bump) — while keeping proposition.object and all downstream condition linkage byte-identical.

Architecture: Strip the #/… prefix at the producer (gkm-scv-condition-proc.sql), then re-wrap the CURIE back into a pointer at the three downstream sites that consume these fields as proposition.object / condition references (gkm-scv-statement-proc.sql ×2, gkm-rcv-statement-proc.sql ×1). Update the schema-source field descriptions in lockstep, regenerate json/ + bundle + docs, then oracle-gate a full rebuild and re-extract the examples.

Tech Stack: BigQuery dynamic SQL stored procedures (bash 3.2 orchestration), ga4gh.gkm metaschema (make / y2md), Zensical docs, extract-example.py.

Scope note: This plan is Part A only (the de-pointer). The versioning-policy infrastructure (root manifest, /v1/ mirror, bundle-level schema_version field, RSS/Atom feed, Home-page indicator, release-notes generation — per ADR 0004) is separate follow-on work, not built here. schema_version could ride this same rebuild if desired (see Task 7 note), but is not required for the de-pointer.

Oracle invariant (gate): every BQ-touching change must be byte-identical full-vs-incremental and delta-reconstructable. oracle-scv-condition.sh, oracle-scv-statement.sh, oracle-rcv-statement.sh, and oracle-delta-reconstruction.sh must all report 0,0,0 before anything publishes. Nothing in this plan touches live R2.

items.title: Parquet Developer Track Implementation Plan
items.text:
Status: implemented (2026-10-15), PR #139. The checkboxes below are ticked; where the build departed from a step, the difference is recorded here rather than by leaving the box open.

Renamed during review: "section" became "table" throughout the track. Each bundle section is exactly one Parquet table.

Planned As built One Section at a Time · first-queries.md Anatomy of a Table · table-anatomy.md The 22 Sections · section-map.md The 22 Tables · tables.md Joining Sections · joining.md Joining Tables · joining.md parquet-section-map.html parquet-table-map.html

Added beyond the plan: a live DuckDB-Wasm console on Start Here (vendored runtime); a third diagram, parquet-vcv-levels.html (reading a variant's statements); a complete per-table column reference on The 22 Tables; diagram table boxes linked to that reference; a pinned header with a scroll-tracking mini list of the diagrams in each frame; the "Materialize the joins you repeat" section on Working at Scale; R in Beyond DuckDB.

Departures from the steps as written:

  • Remote querying (Conventions): SET threads=1 + http_retries no longer gets a big-table scan through. The CDN returns HTTP 429 after ~55 requests in ~10 s, even single-threaded. The pages teach "explore remotely (footer, LIMIT, small tables), download to analyze", and drop the throttle as a workaround.
  • Task 4, step 5: the classification.name leaf is well under 1 MB on disk, not ~140 MB. The page uses the measured figure, and also teaches grouping by the normalized classification.primaryCoding.code (44 submitted spellings → 34 code–guideline pairs).
  • Task 8, step 2 (row-group targeting): the published files are not sorted by any lookup key, so a filter can't skip row groups. The page explains that, and points to materialized, sorted tables as the way to get row-group pruning.
  • Task 11: besides the pointer, data-access/parquet.md got two corrections: not every table has id/data, and two listed varcustom columns don't exist.
  • Also found: the repo .gitignore's bare parquet/ rule hid docs/parquet/; !docs/parquet/ added.

For agentic workers: REQUIRED: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (if subagents available) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking. Use the repo's write-docs skill for every page created or edited here.

Goal: Add a Parquet-focused developer track that teaches someone to go from "never opened a Parquet file" to "joining across 22 sections confidently" — a learning path, not a file list. Each page opens with something runnable before any prose about the model.

Problem being solved: The JSON/bundle consumer has three whole nav tabs — Data Guide (output format, per-statement-type pages, ID references, examples), Data Model (33 class pages), Pipeline (how it is built). The Parquet consumer has one page, data-access/parquet.md, which sits under Downloads and is organised around distribution mechanics. It does five jobs at once (release browsers, the 22-file table, prerequisites, query examples, delta reconstruction) and never states the relational model: which columns are keys, which joins are polymorphic, which ones silently drop rows. Today a Parquet consumer has to reverse-engineer that. Three of the five join seams cannot be guessed from column names.

The asymmetry in one line: JSON consumers are taught a pointer model (#/condition/clinvar.trait:17556); Parquet consumers need a relational model (tables, keys, prefix-dispatched foreign keys). They are different mental models, so a Parquet reader cannot simply be redirected to the Data Guide.

Architecture: A new top-level nav tab Query the Data, sibling to Data Guide, with seven pages ordered by difficulty. data-access/parquet.md stays exactly where it is and keeps all its anchors — it becomes the distribution page (release browsers, file table, stable URLs, deltas) and gains a pointer into the new track. Two new self-contained HTML diagrams live in docs/assets/diagrams/ and are embedded with <iframe>, following the bundle-section-map.html precedent.

Tech Stack: Zensical (Material theme, zensical build --strict), Markdown with pymdownx.details collapsible call-outs and admonition, hand-authored inline-SVG diagrams in standalone HTML (no JS libraries, CSP-safe), DuckDB CLI as the teaching tool.

Branch: docs/parquet-developer-track off main. Verifies with zensical build --strict and zensical serve.

Conventions:

  • No SQL ships unrun. Every query in these pages must be executed against a real downloaded monthly set and its output pasted from the actual run. Counts are release-dependent, so each page states its release date once and uses figures from that release only.
  • Zensical --strict builds and validates every .md regardless of nav, and these pages cross-link each other — so a build passes only once all seven exist. Create them all, then build and commit together (the same ordering constraint the Downloads redesign hit; see its plan, Chunk 3).
  • Preserve existing heading text in data-access/parquet.md — Parquet Files, Download, Query, Column Reference, Applying Deltas (keeping a Parquet set current) — at least ten inbound links and two prior planning docs reference them.
  • Terminology per .claude/rules/docs.md: GKM = the schema set, GKS = the workstream; say bundle, not dictionary; Variant/Variation in headers.
  • Remote querying is taught — within a boundary. data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1 serves HTTP range requests with CORS open, so DuckDB (httpfs autoloads) queries https://.../00-latest/<section>.parquet directly. Use it as the default for light work (Start Here, single-table, targeted / LIMIT reads); it is zero-friction and ~0.5 s. For heavy work (joins, full scans on big sections) download once and query local files — a parallel full-column scan over a big file bursts range requests and trips Cloudflare's rate limiter (HTTP 429). Teach that boundary and the SET threads=1 + http_retries throttle as the reason, not a footnote. Never teach pointing a query at the old pub-*.r2.dev host.

items.title: Chunk 0: Source material — what is already verified
items.text:
No task here; this is the input inventory so implementers do not re-derive it.

A full structural audit of the 14 Oct 2026 release was completed: 22 tables, 90,209,827 rows, 26 foreign-key edges, 166,889,379 references, all resolving. The findings that the track must teach:

Fact Why a reader needs it Four polymorphic FKs dispatch on id prefix object_condition_id, proposition_id, variation.members[], evidence_items[]. Joining one branch silently drops the rest. variation.members[] reads as a broken FK (98 %) until split by VRS prefix VA.→allele, CN.→copyNumberCount, CX.→copyNumberChange, each 100 %. proposition_id is 1:1, not 1:N Unique within each statement table and across all three combined. A proposition is a side-table of its statement. gene_context_name joins gene.name, which is not unique And is NULL on ~76 % of rows. Two reliable gene-id edges exist instead. SCVs are always leaves in evidence-line branching Measured: zero SCV ids ever appear as the parent of an evidence edge. Aggregate tiers are forests, depth ≤ 2, and no edge crosses an accession Which is why the SCV↔aggregate mapping needs no recursion. object_therapy is stored JSON-quoted Matches therapy.key 0 % raw, 100 % unwrapped. The data column is most of the file scv.data alone is ~15 GB uncompressed of a ~20 GB table. Column pruning is the whole performance story.

An existing interactive version of these diagrams is at https://claude.ai/artifact/TGKVvDkbH7FhE3xvYnu89v — use it as the content source for the two new diagram files, not as a drop-in asset (it carries its own palette; see Task 2).

items.title: Task 3: Create docs/parquet/index.md — "Start Here"
items.text:
Files: Create docs/parquet/index.md

Audience: someone who has never opened a Parquet file and may not write code. This page must produce a real answer from real ClinVar data in about five minutes, with no joins and no genomics knowledge.

  • [x] Step 1: One small file, chosen deliberately

Use condition.parquet — ~2 MB, 23,162 rows, and its name column holds plain disease names. It is the only section that is simultaneously tiny, human-readable, and free of VRS identifiers. Do not open with scv or variation.

  • [x] Step 2: Three queries, in this order
-- 1. How many conditions are there?
SELECT count(*) FROM 'condition.parquet';

-- 2. What do they look like?
SELECT id, name FROM 'condition.parquet' LIMIT 10;

-- 3. Find one you care about
SELECT id, name FROM 'condition.parquet' WHERE name ILIKE '%marfan%';
  • [x] Step 3: A no-install option — VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING

Offer the DuckDB Web Shell (https://shell.duckdb.org) with the downloaded file dragged in, so a reader needs no terminal at all. This is unverified. Before writing it as instructions, confirm by hand that a local condition.parquet can be dropped into the shell and queried. If it cannot, cut the step — do not ship a guess. Do not instead point the shell at the R2 URL; R2 is not a query endpoint.

  • [x] Step 4: An escape hatch to a spreadsheet

Many non-technical readers want the answer in Excel or Sheets, which cannot open Parquet. One line:

duckdb -c "COPY (SELECT id, name FROM 'condition.parquet') TO 'conditions.csv' (HEADER)"
  • [x] Step 5: Close with a map, not a lecture — one paragraph on what the other 21 files are, linking to the section map, and a "where to next" list pointing at the remaining pages by the question each answers.

Verification: zensical build --strict; run all three queries plus the CSV export against a fresh download.

items.title: Task 4: Create docs/parquet/first-queries.md — "One Section at a Time"
items.text:
Files: Create docs/parquet/first-queries.md

Still single-table — no joins. Teach the shape of a GKM Parquet section.

  • [x] Step 1: DESCRIBE SELECT * FROM '<file>' as the primary way to read a schema; show it on condition.parquet (flat) and on scv.parquet (nested STRUCTs).
  • [x] Step 2: The two columns every section has — id and data — and that data is the full JSON object as a string. Introduce json_extract / ->> for reaching into it.
  • [x] Step 3: Reading a STRUCT column with dotted access (classification.name), which is the single most common first stumble: classification is a MappableConcept, not a string.
  • [x] Step 4: The one hard warning, early — never SELECT * on a large section and never load one whole into pandas. Give the arithmetic: scv.parquet is ~3 GB on disk and ~20 GB uncompressed, of which the data column alone is ~15 GB. Name the symptom (machine swaps or the process is killed) and the fix (name your columns).
  • [x] Step 5: A worked single-table analysis — classification counts on scv.parquet reading only the classification.name leaf. Note that this leaf costs ~140 MB where the whole table costs ~20 GB, and that the values are not case-normalised (44 distinct, including pathogenic alongside Pathogenic).

Verification: zensical build --strict; every query run; confirm the quoted leaf-vs-table sizes against parquet_metadata on the current release.

items.text:

  • [x] Step 4: State which sections are leaves (condition, therapy, submitter, sequenceReference) so readers know where a traversal ends.

Verification: zensical build --strict; the iframe renders in both themes; every id shape confirmed present in the current release.

items.title: Task 6: Create docs/parquet/joining.md — "Joining Sections"
items.text:
Files: Create docs/parquet/joining.md

The core technical page. Embed parquet-join-seams.html, then one section per seam: the diagram strip, the runnable join, and the trap.

  • [x] Step 1: Seam A — Variant → Proposition. Four tables spell the subject column differently (subject_variant_id vs subject_id); UNION ALL them once into a prop CTE and reuse it.
  • [x] Step 2: Seam B — Proposition → Condition / ConditionSet. Branch on prefix: clinvar.trait: → condition, and both clinvar.traitset: and clinvar.conditionset: → conditionSet. LEFT JOIN both and keep a resolved_via flag so losses are visible rather than silent.
  • [x] Step 3: Expanding a set to member names — the trap worth its own callout. conditionSet.concepts[] holds ids, so array_to_string(concepts, …) prints clinvar.trait:2965, not a disease name. unnest and re-join to condition. Two further points: membershipOperator (AND/OR) changes what the set asserts and must travel as its own column, because array_to_string requires a constant separator; and a minted set can nest a clinvar.traitset: member, so expansion is one level deeper than it looks.
  • [x] Step 4: Seam C — Proposition → Statements. Label it 1:1 explicitly and show the three-table UNION ALL, noting each tier's shares sum to its exact row count.
  • [x] Step 5: Seam D — the aggregate group. Root cites children, children cite SCVs, SCVs are leaves.
  • [x] Step 6: Seam E — the efficient SCV ↔ aggregate mapping. The accession in the citing statement's own id names the group, so one pass over has_evidence_lines ⋈ evidence_items yields every pair with no recursion. Keep statement_id as well as the accession — it is what distinguishes -CP from -NOCP from -EP.
  • [x] Step 7: A "joins that lie" summary box — the four prefix-dispatched columns, gene_context_name on a non-unique natural key, and object_therapy needing trim(…, '"') plus prefix stripping.

Verification: zensical build --strict; every join run with its real output pasted; each "trap" demonstrated by showing the wrong result next to the right one.

Task-indexed, not table-indexed. Each recipe: the question in plain language, the query, the real output, and one line on cost. Seed set — confirm against the roadmap and GitHub Discussions before fixing the list:

  • [x] Step 2: All variants asserted for one condition, with classification counts.
  • [x] Step 3: One submitter's whole footprint — cross-link user-story-audit.md, which already tells this story for the bundle.
  • [x] Step 4: Conflicting classifications for a variant across submitters (uses Seam E).
  • [x] Step 5: Variants in a genomic window (location.loc_start / loc_end + sequence_reference_id).
  • [x] Step 6: Gene-level rollup — using the reliable gene-id edge, not gene_context_name.
  • [x] Step 7: Export a filtered slice to CSV/Parquet for another tool.

Verification: zensical build --strict; every recipe run end to end; each one's wall-clock and peak memory noted so a reader knows what to expect.

items.title: Task 8: Create docs/parquet/performance.md — "Working at Scale"
items.text:
Files: Create docs/parquet/performance.md

  • [x] Step 1: Column pruning as the one idea that matters, with the scv.parquet per-column byte table from parquet_metadata showing data dominating.
  • [x] Step 2: Row-group targeting — read one row group rather than a whole column when you need a single record.
  • [x] Step 3: DuckDB settings that matter on a laptop: threads, memory_limit, preserve_insertion_order=false, and what the spill-to-disk error looks like when a GROUP BY on high-cardinality strings exhausts temp space.
  • [x] Step 4: Reserved words that bite in real queries — rows, target, role, type, order, end all fail as bare column aliases. This is a frequent, confusing first error.
  • [x] Step 5: duckbox escapes control characters, so an embedded newline prints as \n. The data is fine; use .mode line, or emit one row per member. Worth stating because the natural fix (a newline-joined label) looks broken in the CLI.
  • [x] Step 6: Persisting a .duckdb database with materialised join tables when you will query repeatedly.

Verification: zensical build --strict; reproduce each error message quoted.

items.title: Task 9: Create docs/parquet/other-tools.md — "Beyond DuckDB"

One short, runnable section per tool, each doing the same small task so they are comparable.

items.title: Decisions this plan takes, and what it declines
items.text:
A new tab, not a subsection of Downloads. Downloads was deliberately reshaped six days ago (2026-10-08-downloads-approachable-redesign.md) into a distribution hub with four scoped child pages. A seven-page learning track nested inside it would fight that design and bury the beginner entry point three levels deep. The parallel to draw is Data Guide, which is exactly this for JSON consumers.

data-access/parquet.md is not dismantled. It is new, it is linked from ten places, and its job — browsers, file table, stable URLs, deltas — is genuinely distribution. The new track links to it for "how do I get the files" and never duplicates the file table.

Deltas stay on the distribution page. Keeping a set current is a release-mechanics problem, not a query problem, and the existing content is good. The track cross-links it.

Not proposed here: moving the orphaned data-access/index.md, data-access/output-files.md, getting-started.md and output-reference/index.md into the nav. They are reachable only by direct link today. That is a real finding from this survey but it is a separate concern, and CLAUDE.md says touch only what the request covers — worth raising as its own issue.

items.title: Open questions — resolved at review (2026-10-14)
items.text:
1. Nav label → "Query the Data". Chosen over "Parquet" to describe the reader's intent rather than the file format, and to cover future non-Parquet query paths. The tab label is Query the Data; the page directory stays docs/parquet/ (URLs unchanged) and the content remains Parquet-specific. Task 10's TOML group key is "Query the Data".
  2. The no-install beginner path is real. The DuckDB Web Shell (https://shell.duckdb.org) loads a local file by drag-and-drop or the Import button / .pick command; the file registers in browser-local memory and the filename-without-extension becomes a view (condition.parquet → FROM condition). Because the CDN sets access-control-allow-origin: * (verified), the browser shell can also query the https:// URL directly — no download, no drag. Task 3 Step 3 ships; the exact in-shell wording is pinned when Task 3 is written.
  3. Recipe list stays as inferred. The 11 roadmap authorized GitHub Discussions are feature ideas (temporal analytics, submitter tooling, weekly Parquet, functional-data capture) — none is a query recipe. Task 7's seven recipes stand as the working set, refined at review rather than blocking on a Discussions source.
  4. Release-figure drift → release-date banner per page (option a). Each page states "figures reflect the YYYY-MM-DD release" once; hard counts are kept minimal because the structure (polymorphic FKs, prefix dispatch, 1:1 proposition) is release-independent. Monthly refresh is accepted manual toil. Build-time generation from a committed metrics JSON (option c) is a possible follow-up, not done here.

items.title: Added at review: remote querying is now taught (reverses convention #5)
items.text:
The custom domain data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1 (PR #138, CDN) serves HTTP range requests (accept-ranges: bytes) with CORS open (access-control-allow-origin: *), and DuckDB autoloads httpfs for https:// paths. Verified against the 14 Oct release:

Operation (remote) Result count(*), DESCRIBE, schema footer-only, ~0.5 s even on 3 GB scv.parquet Small sections; targeted / LIMIT reads on big files fast (~0.5 s) Full-column scan / GROUP BY on a big file, default threads HTTP 429 — burst of parallel range requests (scv = 55 row groups, varcond = 223) trips Cloudflare's limiter Same scan with SET threads=1 + retry/backoff completes (~18.5 s for the scv classification rollup)

Resolution — hybrid presentation. Remote (FROM 'https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/datasets/parquet/00-latest/<section>.parquet') is the default for light work — Start Here, single-table, targeted lookups — where it is zero-friction and genuinely fast. Heavy work — the joins on Joining Sections, the big scans in Recipes — downloads once and queries local files. The range-request model, the 429 boundary, and the SET threads=1 + http_retries throttle are taught explicitly (in The 22 Sections / Working at Scale) as the reason for the split, not hidden. Base URL path: v1/datasets/parquet/00-latest/ (stable "latest"); dated pins at v1/datasets/parquet/<YYYY-MM>/.

items.title: Added at review: a live in-browser query console
items.text:
Because the CDN sets access-control-allow-origin: *, a DuckDB-Wasm console embedded in the docs runs a reader's SQL against data.clinvar-gkm.org directly — no install, no download. It is built and lives at docs/assets/duckdb-console.html (theme-aware, same palette as the diagrams), embedded by <iframe> as the centerpiece of Start Here (Task 3): a reader queries real ClinVar data in their first 30 seconds. Guardrails: SET threads=1, a client-side one-query-per-10 s cooldown (greyed Run button + countdown), and example queries chosen to be light/reliable (the heavy full-scan lesson stays in prose). Errors are humanized (plain-language headline + what-to-do hint + collapsible raw details).

Runtime is vendored, not CDN-loaded (review decision). The eh bundle lives in docs/assets/vendor/duckdb/ (~35 MB: duckdb-eh.wasm + the eh worker verbatim, plus an esbuild-bundled duckdb-browser.bundled.js with apache-arrow inlined — the package ESM has an unresolvable bare import "apache-arrow"). Plain committed files (Git LFS can't be used — GitHub Pages serves the LFS pointer, not the file). The bundle is named .js not .mjs (GitHub Pages has served .mjs with a MIME type that breaks ESM imports). Provenance + the reproducible rebuild command are in that directory's README.md.

Cost (verified against the 14 Oct release): this is cheap by design — R2 egress is $0; the only query-driven cost is Class B reads ($0.36 / million, 10 M/month free), fenced by the console cooldown and the WAF rate-limit rule in ADR 0005. Big sections (>512 MB) never cache (BYPASS); 00-latest is set to bypass cache while dated paths cache (MISS→HIT) — a possible follow-up is to default the console to the newest dated release so small-section reads serve from the edge. No native hard spend cap exists, so a usage alert is the safety net (Cloudflare has no dedicated R2-ops alert type on the Free plan — a Custom Alert is the route).

items.title: Added at review: per-table column reference + linkable diagram boxes
items.text:
• Complete per-table column reference. Today's docs only partially cover Parquet columns — the distribution page's "Column Reference" does statements + propositions; the Data Model class pages describe the schema classes, not the flattened Parquet columns. Fold a complete reference into One Section at a Time / The 22 Sections: for each of the 22 tables, definition + every column + type + description. Generate name+type from DESCRIBE on the real release, carry over the descriptions that already exist, and give each table a stable anchor (e.g. #variation) so diagrams can link to it.
  • Linkable diagram table-boxes (sequenced AFTER the reference exists). Each SVG box that names a Parquet table/section (variation, allele, condition, conditionSet, scv, …) becomes <a href="../../parquet/<page>/#<table>" target="_top"> wrapping its rect+text, navigating to that table's reference section — the bundle-section-map.html linkable-box precedent (target="_top" to escape the iframe). Applies to all three diagrams; re-run svgcheck + the viewBox-bounds check after.

items.title: Parquet Follow-ups Plan
items.text:
Relabelled 1.0.2 → 1.1.0 (2026-10-18). The release now also carries the proposition reorganization (plan PR #155) and is a full rebuild and in-place republish under /v1/; see ADR 0006. Version strings below were updated; the patch-style backfill steps described here are superseded by the full rebuild in #155.

For agentic workers: each work item below is sized to one PR (or one decision). Items marked Plan first need their own design plan before code. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking. Run /catchup before starting an item; several depend on PRs that may have merged since this was written.

Goal: Resolve the issues found while building the Query the Data track (#139) and fixing #132. These were found by querying the 2026-10 Parquet release end to end. None blocks current users, but several make correct queries harder than they should be, and three are conformance defects in published data.

Source: Every finding below was measured against the 2026-10 monthly Parquet release, the 2026-10-11 delta bundle, or the clinvar_2026_10_11_v2_6_0 BigQuery dataset, unless marked unverified.

items.title: Workstream A — Conformance and correctness (do first)
A1 · Fix hgvs.? syntax in variant HGVS lists
items.text:
Status: code done on branch fix/hgvs-invalid-expressions (off 1.0, commit 189f3d9, not yet pushed). The release steps and the backfill (option 2) below are still to do.

Problem. 14 variants (16 expressions) in the 2026-10 release carry clinvarHgvsList entries with nucleotideExpression.syntax = "hgvs.?". VRS Expression.syntax doesn't allow it, so these variants fail schema validation. They passed the 2026-10-11 delta check only because none was in that delta.

The variants are clinvar: 360, 3379, 3572, 4134, 9291, 9874, 10113, 10626, 11219, 635132, 829537, 1319991, 2503493 and 2505466.

Cause. In src/procedures/gkm-catvar-proc.sql, the hgvs_items step that builds the HGVS list falls back to a literal ?:

format('hgvs.%s', IFNULL(REGEXP_EXTRACT(exp.nucleotide, r':([gmcnrp])\\.'), '?'))

The 16 expressions come from clinvar-ingest's variation_hgvs table: ClinVar's submitted text, with no HGVS type letter where one belongs (e.g. NC_000017.10:9481617_9489649del). For 11 of them, the same upstream row also holds a valid ClinVar expression for the same accession; for 5 it doesn't. No protein expressions are affected.

Decided (2026-10-17). ClinVar's text is never altered or dropped (project policy). An invalid expression is no longer listed on its own; it becomes an extension of the listed expression:

Case Listed expression Extensions on it Merged (11): ClinVar also supplies a valid expression ClinVar's valid expression invalidClinvarExpression: submitted text · expressionMerged: true Repaired (5): no valid one our repair (type letter restored) originalClinvarExpression: submitted text · expressionRepaired: true

The repair rules strip stray leading dots, turn g( into g.(, move (g.123 to g.(123, or insert the letter for the accession's HGVS type. ClinVar's own valid copy is always preferred over a repair: repairing the 11 would have produced two wrong values.

  • [x] Change gkm-catvar-proc.sql (hgvs_exprs / hgvs_invalid_dups / hgvs_items). The extension struct is {name, value_string, value_boolean}; the assembler collapses it to {name, value}.
  • [x] Document the four extensions in the HgvsListItem description (source YAML, regenerated JSON and class page). VRS Expression already allows extensions, so there is no shape change.
  • [x] Verify on clinvar_2026_10_11_v2_6_0 (read-only):
  • HGVS-list entries go from 43,162,744 to 43,162,733 (the 11 merged)
  • 0 invalid syntax; 11 merged and 5 repaired
  • the cleaned items validate as HgvsListItem in default and strict mode
  • [ ] Push and open a draft PR against 1.0.
  • [ ] Release steps (BigQuery, gated per .claude/rules/sql-procedures.md):
  • [ ] Deploy the procedure.
  • [ ] Run the variant step in full (non-incremental) mode for the first release after the fix, or add the 14 ids to catvar_changed_ids. Incremental mode recomputes only changed variants (vfilter_ext), so unchanged ones would keep hgvs.? forever.
  • [ ] Full-vs-incremental oracle and delta-reconstruction oracle at 0,0,0. If the one-time full run is skipped, the oracle shows exactly these 14 variants as mismatches.
  • [ ] Backfill past releases: option 2, decided 2026-10-17. Patch only the variation section of already-published releases, following the conditionSet backfill precedent (see the reference_vcv_conditionset_synthetic memory). Every live write needs explicit confirmation first.
  • [ ] Per dataset behind a published release: recompute the 14 variants' gkm_dict_variation rows with the fixed logic. Change no other rows.
  • [ ] Monthly fulls (2026-07 … 2026-10, plus 00-latest): rewrite those entries in the bundle's variation section (streaming edit; no other bytes change), and re-export variation.parquet.
  • [ ] Weekly deltas: patch only the deltas whose variation section (bundle and Parquet) contains any of the 14 ids. Deltas without them are untouched.
  • [ ] Republish the changed files under /v1/ and the flat-root mirror; purge the CDN for every overwritten dated path (ADR 0005); regenerate index.json sizes.
  • [ ] Verify:
    • delta reconstruction is still exact (a monthly full + its deltas equals the next full)
    • every patched full validates against the bundle schema
    • checksums change only for the patched files
  • [ ] Note it in the changelog and release notes (ADR 0004 stabilization window: corrective fix in place).
  • [ ] File an issue on clinvar-ingest about the malformed variation_hgvs.expr entries.

Base: 1.0 · Size: S (SQL, done) + rebuild + backfill (M) · Depends on: nothing.

items.title: A3 · Fold the ClinvarScvStatement description drift into the next schema change
items.text:
Problem. Regenerating clinvar-statement-source.yaml changes one description in json/ClinvarScvStatement ("clinvar.traitset:123" in quotes vs. bare). The committed JSON and the source disagree, so every regeneration shows a spurious diff.

  • [ ] Pick one form, put it in the source YAML, regenerate, and commit. Ride along with the next schema PR (B1 or C2); not worth its own release.

Base: with B1/C2 · Size: XS.

items.title: B1 · Strict-mode validation fails every record — Plan first
items.text:
Problem. With validate-schema-conformance.py --no-relax, every statement and variant record fails with Additional properties are not allowed or Unevaluated properties are not allowed, even on ordinary fields like classification and id. Default mode passes.

On the 2026-10-11 delta, strict mode fails variation 15,758, varcustom-proposition 40, scv 11,647, vcv 18,797 and rcv 24,926 records. That's identical before and after #142, so it is a generator issue, not a data issue.

Likely cause. The generated schemas compose classes with allOf and also set additionalProperties: false inside individual allOf branches (or unevaluatedProperties: false alongside refs that don't count as evaluated). That rejects properties another branch defines. The fix belongs in gkm-metaschema (source_proc.py), not in hand-edits to json/.

  • [ ] Write a plan in gkm-metaschema covering:
  • where additionalProperties: false is emitted
  • whether only the outermost class should close the object, using unevaluatedProperties: false
  • the test case: a minimal allOf of two classes
  • [ ] In the same change, make output deterministic: sort_keys=True at source_proc.py:482. This is the deferred fix that stops the random $defs reordering.
  • [ ] Regenerate schema/clinvar-gkm/; strict mode should then pass the 2026-10-11 delta.

Repo: gkm-metaschema, then a regen PR here · Size: M · Depends on: nothing.

items.title: B2 · Bundle schema: validate variation with the fixed oneOf
items.text:
Problem. clinvar-gkm-bundle.schema.json validates each variation entry with anyOf over five variant schemas. Before #142 that hid the oneOf defect; after #142 the anyOf is redundant.

  • [ ] Replace the anyOf with a single $ref to ClinvarCategoricalVariant, which now discriminates correctly.
  • [ ] Verify: the 2026-10-11 delta passes, and a deliberately malformed variant (allele constraint with no allele) now fails.

Base: 1.0 · Size: XS · Depends on: #142 · Version: fold into the same release as #142 if it hasn't been tagged yet; otherwise this is a PATCH.

items.title: Workstream C — Data products and export (additive)
C1 · Variant-sorted statement × proposition Parquet — Plan first
items.text:
Problem. - No variant column on statements: scv.parquet has no variant column, and no published table is sorted by a lookup key. A one-variant question reads every row group. - Remote queries rate-limited: over HTTPS that trips the CDN rate limit (HTTP 429), so per-variant queries can't run in the live console. Working at Scale currently teaches building this join locally.

Measured prototype: scv_by_variant is SCV plus its proposition's subject, object and qualifiers plus PubMed ids, sorted by variant_id. It came to 107 MB, and a single-variant lookup read 1 of 55 row groups.

  • [ ] Plan the design:
  • which tables: SCV only, or also VCV and RCV
  • columns, naming, and sort keys (variant; object?)
  • row-group size
  • delta handling: rebuild it whole each release, or apply deltas
  • where it sits in the R2 layout and index.json
  • whether it carries schema_version
  • [ ] Build it from the typed Parquet in export-gkm-dicts.sh (or as an EXPORT DATA query).
  • [ ] Docs: a Recipes section, a console example (one-variant PubMed lookup), and the Working at Scale materialize section pointing to the published file.

Size: M · Depends on: #143 (so it inherits bare ids).

items.title: C2 · Typed columns for therapy and therapyGroup
items.text:
Problem. Both tables are key/value only. Names and group members exist only inside the JSON value, so every therapy query needs JSON parsing.

  • [ ] Add columns without removing key/value:
  • therapy: name, concept_type
  • therapyGroup: membership_operator and members (bare clinvar.therapy: ids)
  • [ ] Verify against the 38 therapies and 10 groups.

Base: 1.0 · Size: XS · Depends on: #143.

items.title: C3 · Uncertain-range locations
items.text:
Problem. About 72,000 location rows have NULL loc_start or loc_end because the coordinate is a VRS Range; the range exists only in data. Window queries silently skip them.

  • [ ] Add loc_start_min/max and loc_end_min/max (keep loc_start/loc_end for definite coordinates).

Base: 1.0 · Size: XS · Priority: low.

items.title: C4 · Decisions (no code until decided)
items.text:
• [ ] gene_context_name on aggregates. It is filled in only on SCV propositions (gkm-scv-statement-proc.sql builds geneContextQualifier per SCV); it is NULL on every VCV and RCV proposition. Either populate it for aggregates, or keep it SCV-only. Keeping it SCV-only is already documented as a trap on Joining Tables.
  • [ ] condition column names. condition.parquet keeps camelCase (conceptType, primaryCoding) while every other table is snake_case. Renaming breaks consumers, so defer to the next MAJOR line (ADR 0004) and record it there.

items.title: D1 · Reconcile the CDN rate limit with ADR 0005
items.text:
Problem. ADR 0005 documents 300 requests / 1 minute per IP, block 10 minutes. Observed on 2026-10-15: single-threaded DuckDB scans got HTTP 429 after about 55 requests in about 10 seconds, and blocks lifted within about 90 seconds. Cloudflare's Free plan allows only a 10-second counting period, so the live rule likely differs from the ADR.

  • [ ] Read the live rule (Security → WAF → Rate limiting rules) and record the real period, threshold and mitigation time.
  • [ ] Decide whether it is right for the live console and the documented remote-query boundary, then update ADR 0005 to match. Working at Scale and the console's error hints don't quote numbers, so they need no change.

Owner: maintainer with Cloudflare access · Size: XS (ADR edit).

items.title: D2 · R2 spend alert
items.text:
• [ ] Set up a Cloudflare Custom Alert on R2 Class B operations and storage. There is no dedicated R2 alert type on the Free plan and no hard spend cap, so this is the only safety net. Record the threshold in ADR 0005.

Owner: maintainer with Cloudflare access · Size: XS (no PR).

items.title: D3 · Console: live release list, cacheable default
items.text:
Problem. - Hardcoded release list: docs/assets/duckdb-console.html lists its releases in the HTML (00-latest, 2026-10 … 2026-07), so it goes stale every month. - Uncached default: it defaults to 00-latest, which bypasses the CDN cache, so every console read hits R2.

  • [ ] Populate the Release dropdown from https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/index.json (CORS is open), keeping the hardcoded list as a fallback.
  • [ ] Default to the newest dated release (cacheable) and label it as the latest.
  • [ ] Verify in headless Chromium: the list loads, the default is dated, and a query runs.

Base: main · Size: S · Depends on: nothing.

items.title: E1 · Link and anchor check in the deploy workflow
items.text:
Problem. zensical build --strict doesn't check #anchor fragments or links inside raw HTML (iframes, diagram boxes, the console). Every check of those in the Query the Data work was done by a one-off script.

  • [ ] Add src/scripts/check-site-links.py (built-site internal href/src and #fragment checker) and run it after the build in deploy-docs.yml. It should fail the deploy on a broken link.

Base: main · Size: S.

items.title: E2 · Point docs at the live domain
items.text:
• [ ] The site now serves from dataexchange.clinicalgenome.org/clinvar-gkm/; github.io 301-redirects. Update site_url in zensical.toml and the README link so canonical URLs, the sitemap and search use the live domain.

Base: main · Size: XS · Check first: that the custom domain is permanent.

items.title: E3 · Backlog (separate plans when picked up)
items.text:
• Query with AI: built and tested, then tabled; local branch docs/ai-query-guide (commit 82b5f3f). Needs a design review before revival; see the commit message.
  • Data Model "Profiles" naming: rename to something like "Mapping & Vocabularies", and fix "Propositions" appearing twice in that nav.
  • Orphaned pages: data-access/index.md, data-access/output-files.md, getting-started.md and output-reference/index.md are reachable only by direct link.
  • Release-figure drift: every count in the track is from the 2026-10 release. Generating figures at build time from a committed metrics file would end the manual banner updates.
  • Starter-kit page and docs links that follow the release branch: existing backlog items.

items.title: Suggested order
items.text:
Data-changing work follows the consolidated release sequence above; this order covers everything else.

  1. A1 (hgvs.?, code done; release steps + option 2 backfill) and B2 (bundle oneOf), on 1.0, alongside #142. Same release, if possible.
  2. A2 part 1 (form-agnostic queries) now, on main, before #143's first export.
  3. D1 and D2 (Cloudflare checks); quick and unblock nothing else, but close the operational gaps.
  4. E1 (link checker), so the remaining docs work is protected.
  5. D3 (console release list) and C2 (therapy columns): small, independent.
  6. B1 (strict mode, gkm-metaschema) and C1 (variant-sorted Parquet): the two items that need a plan first.
  7. C3, C4 decisions, E2, E3 as capacity allows.

items.title: Strict-Mode Schema Validation (B1) Plan
items.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (if subagents available) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Make validate-schema-conformance.py --no-relax pass on real published data, so strict validation can gate releases. Separate the generator/schema defects from genuine data defects. Only the data defects change published data, so only they bear on the consolidated rebuild and backfill.

Parent plan: B1 in 2026-10-16-parquet-followups.md. That plan assumed the fix belongs in gkm-metaschema. The investigation below shows a clinvar-gkm source fix is enough, needs no generator release, and was verified end to end.

Answer to the backfill question: the strict-mode failures are schema defects, not data defects, and fixing them changes no published data. Checking real data turned up one genuine data defect: malformed citation Documents on up to 3,872 SCVs in the 2026-10 full (Task 5). It fails default (relaxed) validation too, so it was never a strict-only problem. It went unnoticed because only deltas were validated, and none of the affected SCVs are in the 2026-10-11 delta. Fixing it changes published scv records, so it has to be decided before the rebuild.

items.title: Findings
items.text: All numbers come from the schema state of fix/hgvs-invalid-expressions (#142's 1.0.2 schemas plus the A1 HgvsListItem change), validated per section against clinvar-gkm-bundle.schema.json properties[section], with the registry from load_registry.

items.title: Baseline: strict mode on the 2026-10-11 delta
items.text: Section Records Strict failures Reported error variation 15,758 15,758 Unevaluated properties are not allowed ('constraints', 'extensions', 'id', …) varcustom-proposition 40 40 anyOf (no branch valid) scv 11,647 11,647 Additional properties are not allowed ('classification', 'contributions', 'id', 'type', …) vcv 18,797 18,797 Additional properties are not allowed ('classification', 'direction', 'id', …) rcv 24,926 24,926 same as vcv the other 10 sections 102,033 0

items.title: Root cause 1: closed *Properties mixins inside allOf (all five sections)
items.text:
Each ClinVar profile is composed as allOf: [<upstream base>, <ClinVar mixin>], with unevaluatedProperties: false on the outer class. The outer closure is correct. The problem is the mixin.

"ClinvarScvStatement": {
  "allOf": [
    { "$ref": "/ga4gh/schema/va-spec/1.1.0/json/Statement" },
    { "$ref": "#/$defs/ClinvarScvStatementProperties" }
  ],
  "unevaluatedProperties": false
},
"ClinvarScvStatementProperties": {
  "properties": { "proposition": …, "hasEvidenceLines": …, "extensions": … },
  "additionalProperties": false
}

additionalProperties only sees its own schema's properties. So the mixin rejects every property that the base Statement supplies: id, type, classification, and the rest. Every SCV/VCV/RCV statement fails on that branch. The variant and custom-proposition profiles fail the same way.

There are nine such mixins, all protectedClassOf $defs:

Mixin Schema ClinvarScvStatementProperties ClinvarScvStatement ClinvarAggregateStatementProperties ClinvarAggregateStatement (used by VCV and RCV) ClinvarGermlineCustomPropositionProperties ClinvarGermlineCustomProposition ClinvarSomaticEvidenceLineProperties ClinvarSomaticEvidenceLine ClinvarCategoricalVariantProperties, ClinvarCanonicalAlleleProperties, ClinvarAlleleProperties, ClinvarSequenceLocationProperties, ClinvarSequenceReferenceProperties ClinvarCategoricalVariant

Why the generator emits false: the source YAML declares additionalProperties: true on 8 of the 9 mixins (ClinvarGermlineCustomPropositionProperties declares nothing). But gkm-metaschema source_proc.py (lines ~906–913) overwrites it unconditionally: every non-abstract class in a strict source gets additionalProperties: false, or unevaluatedProperties: false if it is composed. The authored true is silently discarded. The same code leaves abstract classes open on purpose. Its comment notes that even additionalProperties: true would be wrong on a mixin, because it marks every property as evaluated and so disables the outer unevaluatedProperties: false.

Minimal reproduction (pure JSON Schema 2020-12, no project schemas):

base  = {"$id": "urn:Base",  "type": "object", "additionalProperties": False,
         "properties": {"id": {"type": "string"}, "type": {"type": "string"}, "extensions": {"type": "array"}}}
mixin = {"$id": "urn:Mixin", "type": "object", "additionalProperties": False,      # <- the defect
         "properties": {"extensions": {"type": "array", "maxItems": 3}}}
profile = {"allOf": [{"$ref": "urn:Base"}, {"$ref": "urn:Mixin"}], "unevaluatedProperties": False}
# {"id": "x", "type": "Statement", "extensions": []}
#   -> "Additional properties are not allowed ('id', 'type' were unexpected)"
# Drop the mixin's additionalProperties: valid, and {"bogus": 1} is still rejected by the outer
# unevaluatedProperties.

items.title: Root cause 2: GeneListItem describes an older record shape (variation only)
items.text:
With root cause 1 fixed, the statement and proposition sections pass, but 15,756 of 15,758 variants still fail. The reported error is misleading: ClinvarCategoricalVariant is a oneOf with unevaluatedProperties: false. When every branch fails, no property counts as evaluated, so the outer error lists every field. Testing one branch at a time narrows it to the clinvarGeneList extension.

Shape Data, every gene-list item {"gene": "#/gene/ncbigene:242", "relationship_type": …, "source": …} GeneListItem schema entrez_gene_id, hgnc_id, symbol, relationship_type, source, iris, plus additionalProperties: false. There is no gene.

The data is the intended form. Gene details moved to the gene section, and the docs already describe the #/gene/ pointer (output-reference/cat-vrs.md, id-references.md). The schema was never updated, and relaxed mode hid that by stripping additionalProperties. Across the 2026-10 monthly full, all 7,346,154 gene-list items have gene, relationship_type and source. None is missing one, and none has a gene that isn't a #/gene/ncbigene: pointer. This is a schema defect, not a data defect.

items.title: Latent limitation: a closed upstream parent can't be extended
items.text: If a mixin adds a property its upstream base doesn't declare, the closed base rejects it. Only one case exists: ClinvarCanonicalAlleleProperties.definingContext. cat-vrs CanonicalAllele (unevaluatedProperties: false) over CategoricalVariant (additionalProperties: false) has no definingContext. No record uses it (0 of 4,647,675 variants in 2026-10, and no procedure emits it), so it causes no failures today. It would fail strict validation the first time it was populated.

items.title: Prototype: corrected composition on real data
items.text:
Neither gkm-metaschema nor any committed schema was changed. Two prototypes were run:

  • Programmatic transform: strip the closure from every allOf-branch target, and point composed references at open copies of the upstream bases.
  • Source fix (the recommendation): in a scratch copy of the four *-source.yaml files, mark the nine mixins abstract: true, remove their additionalProperties: true, and update GeneListItem. Then regenerate with the installed generator (make -C schema/clinvar-gkm) and validate with the unmodified validate-schema-conformance.py registry in strict mode (relax=False).

The two prototypes gave identical results. Opening only the mixins is enough: no upstream base has to be opened, because no record uses a property its base lacks (see the latent limitation above).

Data Records Strict, as published Root cause 1 fixed + GeneListItem fixed Relaxed (today's default) 2026-10-11 delta, all 15 sections 174,201 71,168 15,756 (variation only) 0 0 2026-10 monthly-full sample (Parquet data column) 35,464 not run not run 4 4 (the same 4)

The monthly-full sample came from the 2026-10 Parquet data columns: about 5,000 random rows per large table plus stratified rows, covering every VCV/RCV id-suffix class (G/S, PATH/SCI/ONCO/…, CP/NOCP/EP/PG/FLAG/Tn) and every SCV proposition type × guideline system × has-evidence-lines combination.

Table Sampled scv 5,920 vcv 7,062 rcv 7,134 variation 5,600 varcond-proposition 2,634 varcustom-proposition 2,546 evidence lines (all of evidenceLine plus samples of vcv_/rcv_evidenceLine) 4,568

Negative checks under the source fix still behave as expected. A bogus top-level property is rejected in scv, vcv, rcv, variation, varcustom-proposition and evidenceLine. A bogus key inside an SCV extension is rejected. A gene-list item with a stale symbol, or with no gene, is rejected.

The regenerated JSON differs from the committed JSON by exactly 9 × (additionalProperties: false removed, abstract: true added) plus the GeneListItem change. y2md class pages are unchanged.

items.title: Remaining failures: classification
items.text:
Failure Count Class SCV specifiedBy.reportedIn.doi not a DOI 3 in the sample; 3,808 SCVs in the 2026-10 full Real data defect (Task 5) SCV reportedIn[].doi not a DOI 62 SCVs in the full Real data defect (Task 5) SCV reportedIn[].urls[] not a URL (PMID:18563784) 1 in the sample; 2 SCVs in the full Real data defect (Task 5) definingContext rejected by a closed upstream parent 0 records Known upstream limitation, latent (Task 3) Misleading top-level unevaluatedProperties error when a oneOf/allOf branch fails reporting only Validator usability (Task 4)

Bad DOI values in the full, from SELECT … FROM scv.parquet:

Field Values specifiedBy.reportedIn.doi https ×3,746, doi.org/10.1002/humu.23630 ×52, then doi:10.…, https://doi.org/10.…, DOI: 10.…, a bare PMID (25741868), a PMC id (PMC8832287) reportedIn[].doi doi:10.…, doi.org/10.…, https, doi/10.…, http://dx.doi.org/10.…, org/10.…, doi, values with a trailing .

The va-spec Document requires doi to match ^10.(\d+)(\.\d+)*/[\w\-\.]+ and urls[] to match ^(https?|s?ftp)://. The "https" DOI also produces the meaningless URL https://doi.org/https.

Origin: gkm-scv-statement-proc.sql Step 7b (temp_scv_citations, which feeds reportedIn) and Step 7c (temp_scv_method, which feeds specifiedBy.reportedIn) copy ClinVar's citation cid.id into doi verbatim. Their ELSE branch also puts cid.curie (7b) or source:id (7c) into urls, even when the value isn't a URL.

items.title: Recommendation: where the fix goes
items.text:
Option Verdict A. clinvar-gkm source YAML: mark the 9 mixins abstract: true and drop their additionalProperties: true; fix GeneListItem Recommended. Verified end to end with the installed generator. It uses the generator's own documented rule (abstract classes are left open, concrete ones closed), so no metaschema release is needed. It also matches how va-spec composes its own profiles. B. gkm-metaschema generator: honor or reject an authored class-level additionalProperties, and leave protectedClassOf mixins open Worth doing upstream, but not blocking. File an issue: the silent overwrite of an authored true is a trap for every profile author. C. clinvar-gkm post-processing step after make Rejected. It is a second, hidden schema source, and the published JSON would still differ from what the YAML says. D. Validator-only (today's relax) Rejected as the fix. The published schemas are what consumers and the GA4GH gkm-toolkit validate against, so they must be correct as published.

Deterministic output (deferred): json.dump(..., sort_keys=False) at source_proc.py:482 lets $defs come out in set order. The scratch regeneration reordered $defs in three files (ClinvarAggregateStatement, ClinvarCategoricalVariant, ClinvarScvStatement) with no change in content. Switching to sort_keys=True belongs in gkm-metaschema and stays deferred. It would also reorder properties in every emitted file, so it should land as its own one-time-churn regeneration. Until then, follow the existing rule in scripts.md: revert files whose JSON is semantically unchanged, and keep only the real diff.

items.title: Task 1: Open the nine *Properties mixins (schema only)
items.text:
Files: schema/clinvar-gkm/clinvar-{statement,variant,proposition,evidence}-source.yaml, regenerated schema/clinvar-gkm/json/*. Base: 1.0. If 1.0.2 isn't tagged yet, fold this into the same release as #142 (as with B2/A3); otherwise it's a PATCH.

  • [ ] In each of the nine mixins listed under root cause 1, add abstract: true and delete the class-level additionalProperties: true where present. Keep the property-level additionalProperties on nested objects, such as ExtensionSubmittedCondition.value and SubmittedConditionMapping.
  • [ ] Run make -C schema/clinvar-gkm. Revert files that only reorder, by checking semantic equality with json.load(a) == json.load(b).
  • [ ] Confirm the semantic diff is exactly 9 × (additionalProperties: false → absent, abstract: true added).
  • [ ] Do the version bump per scripts.md if this isn't riding in 1.0.2.

items.title: Task 2: Make GeneListItem match the published shape (schema only)
items.text:
• [ ] In clinvar-variant-source.yaml, replace entrez_gene_id, hgnc_id, symbol and iris with gene: {$refCurie: gkm.core:iriReference}, described as the #/gene/ pointer. Keep relationship_type (enum) and source. Add required: [gene, relationship_type, source]; all 7,346,154 items in 2026-10 have all three. Rewrite the class description to match.
  • [ ] Regenerate. Check that the regenerated GeneListItem class page and output-reference/cat-vrs.md ### GeneListItem agree. That docs change goes in the paired main docs PR.

items.title: Task 3: Decide on ClinvarCanonicalAlleleProperties.definingContext
items.text: • [ ] Decision: drop definingContext from the profile (recommended: it can never pass strict validation under cat-vrs 1.1.1's closed CanonicalAllele, and nothing emits it), or keep it and raise an upstream cat-vrs issue. Either way this changes no data.

items.title: Task 4: Make strict validation usable and the default
items.text:
File: src/scripts/validate-schema-conformance.py.

  • [ ] Flip the default to strict, with a --relax opt-in kept for debugging. Rewrite the relax_additional_properties docstring: the old explanation ("the metaschema stamps it at every level") is superseded by root cause 1.
  • [ ] When reporting a failure, drop unevaluatedProperties errors whenever the record also has any other error. When a branch fails, those errors only echo it and list every field; this is what made the variation failures unreadable.
  • [ ] Optional: add a --bundle mode that validates each section of a bundle file against clinvar-gkm-bundle.schema.json properties[section]. Today that loop lives only in ad-hoc scratch scripts.

items.title: Task 5: Fix malformed SCV citation Documents (data, changes published scv)
items.text:
File: src/procedures/gkm-scv-statement-proc.sql, Steps 7b and 7c.

  • [ ] Investigate (read-only BigQuery): find the raw ClinVar citation source/id/url behind the "https" DOIs (3,746 rows) and the PMID: URLs. Establish whether the bad value is in the ClinVar XML or comes from upstream clinvar-ingest parsing. If it is upstream, open an issue there as well.
  • [ ] DOI: set doi to REGEXP_EXTRACT(cid.id, r'(10\.\d+(?:\.\d+)*/[^\s]+?)\.?$'). That strips the https://doi.org/, doi.org/, dx.doi.org/, doi: and DOI: (with its trailing space) prefixes and a trailing period. It is NULL when no DOI is present (https, doi, a PMID or PMC id). Build the https://doi.org/%s URL only from the normalized DOI.
  • [ ] URLs: emit a urls entry only when it matches ^(https?|s?ftp)://. Route PubMed-style sources (PMID, and others that turn up in the investigation) to pmid and a PubMed URL, rather than through the ELSE curie branch.
  • [ ] Empty documents: if a citation Document ends up with no pmid, doi or urls, drop it. In 7c, set specifiedBy.reportedIn to NULL.
  • [ ] Determinism: keep both steps byte-identical between full and incremental runs. They are computed globally and LEFT-JOINed into gkm_dict_scv, so the carry-forward invariant isn't at risk.
  • [ ] Data impact: gkm_dict_scv is a per-SCV carry-forward output. An incremental run only recomputes changed SCVs, so the fix reaches the up-to-3,872 unchanged SCVs only if the SCV step runs in full mode once in the forward rebuild (the same pattern as A1's variant step). Expect the full-vs-incremental oracle to pass only after that full run, and the first delta afterwards to carry those SCVs as changes.

items.title: Task 6: Upstream gkm-metaschema issue (no code in this repo)
items.text:
• [ ] File an issue covering three things:
  • the class-level additionalProperties overwrite at source_proc.py ~906–913: honor or reject an authored value, and consider leaving protectedClassOf mixins open by default
  • the minimal allOf reproduction above, as a test case
  • sort_keys=True at line 482, still deferred

items.title: Verification
items.text:
• [ ] Strict, delta: strict mode on the real 2026-10-11 delta, all 15 sections, gives 0 failures, as the prototype did. Use the real published bundle, not a sub-bundle, and set schema_version to the schema const.
  • [ ] Strict, monthly full: strict mode on the 2026-10 monthly-full sample (≥ 20,000 records, stratified as above) gives 0 failures once Task 5 data is in. Before Task 5, it should show exactly the Document failures.
  • [ ] Full-coverage scan: a full-coverage scan of the Document fields over the whole monthly full (DuckDB regex on scv.parquet specifiedBy/reportedIn, as above) gives 0 bad doi and 0 bad urls[] after the rebuild.
  • [ ] gkm-toolkit: validate_bundle_schema on the real published full and delta reports 0 failures, as CLAUDE.md requires.
  • [ ] Negative tests: each of these must still fail.
  • a bogus top-level property on an scv, vcv, rcv, variation, varcustom-proposition or evidenceLine record
  • a bogus key inside an SCV extension
  • a gene-list item with symbol, or with no gene
  • B2's malformed allele constraint
  • [ ] Task 5 oracles: the full-vs-incremental and delta-reconstruction oracles report 0,0,0 after the one full-mode SCV run.
  • [ ] Docs: zensical build --clean --strict is clean for the paired docs PR.

items.title: Effect on the consolidated release
items.text:
Change JSON bundle Parquet Backfill past releases? B1 Tasks 1–3: mixins, GeneListItem, definingContext none (schema only) none no B1 Task 4: validator none none no B1 Task 5: SCV citation Documents up to 3,872 scv records in the 2026-10 full (earlier fulls not yet counted; deltas only where those SCVs changed) scv typed specifiedBy/reportedIn columns + data Decide before the rebuild (below)

Task 5 needs a backfill decision before the forward rebuild, following the parent plan's rule.

  • Forward: requires the SCV step in full mode once. The first post-fix delta then carries the corrected SCVs, so reconstruction stays consistent without touching past releases.
  • Past fulls: they are non-conformant today, even under relaxed validation. Two options:
  • (a) Leave them and document it.
  • (b) Patch the affected scv records in the same JSON backfill pass that A1 already does on every monthly full. Recommended: the files are rewritten anyway, and the extra work is a few thousand records per full.
  • Parquet: re-exporting scv for every monthly set costs a lot more (about 3 GB per month). Leaving the past scv Parquet as it is would be reasonable; the JSON bundles are the conformance artifact.

items.title: Statement Lookup Files (C1) — Design Plan
items.text:
Status: design only (2026-10-17, extended 2026-10-18). Nothing here is wired into the release pipeline. This plan answers the C1 "Plan first" item in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-16-parquet-followups.md (branch docs/parquet-followups-plan, PR #144). On 2026-10-18 it grew from one file into a family of lookup files that share one set of statement columns, each sorted by a different key. All export SQL below is a prototype, quoted here so nobody mistakes it for a live parquet-schemas/ file. Decisions marked (maintainer) are collected in §11.

Goal. Publish pre-joined Parquet files, sorted by the key a question starts from:

  • a variant
  • a condition or therapy (including through the sets that contain it)
  • a gene
  • a PubMed id

Each such question then reads one or two row groups instead of scanning scv.parquet (3.1 GB) and a proposition table. That makes the questions runnable over HTTPS, including in the browser console, which gets HTTP 429 after about 55 requests in 10 s.

Ground rule for the whole family: a column or a file never implies a relationship the source data doesn't make. Three consequences:

  • A concept reached through a condition set is labelled as such, never presented as the proposition's own object.
  • ClinVar's variant-to-gene list is never presented as a statement's gene.
  • A method citation is never presented as evidence.

Measurement sources:

  • Files: every one was built from the 2026-10 monthly Parquet set (~/Development/sandbox/clinvar-gkm-parquet) with DuckDB 1.5.4. All share the same settings: ZSTD, default 122,880-row groups, no bloom filters, a total-order sort.
  • Request counts: DuckDB's httpfs reading from a local HTTP server that supports range requests and logs each one. Every query ran in a fresh process with SET threads = 1, to match the single-threaded console. Counts include the footer fetch.
  • BigQuery (read-only): every prototype was dry-run on clinvar_2026_10_11_v2_6_0. Each was also run as a SELECT with row-count breakdowns on that dataset and on clinvar_2026_09_28_v2_6_0. The latter is the source of the 2026-10 monthly set.
  • Equivalence: on 2026_09_28, every breakdown of every file matches the local build exactly. No EXPORT DATA, CREATE or DELETE was run.
