items.title: The core statement columns
items.text:
Four files carry these 17 columns unchanged: statement-by-variant, statement-by-object, statement-by-gene-context, and statement-by-citation (which drops pmids). Users learn them once.

Column Type From Notes variant_id string proposition subject clinvar:<variation id> source_table string — scv, vcv or rcv: the table statement_id lives in statement_id string statement id Joins to id in that table proposition_type string proposition type predicate string proposition predicate object_id string proposition object, as stated A condition, condition set, tumor type, therapy or therapy group id condition_qualifier_id string conditionQualifier Therapeutic-response propositions only gene_context_name string geneContextQualifier.name Variant-derived, not submitter-asserted (§4). SCV only mode_of_inheritance string modeOfInheritanceQualifier.name SCV only penetrance string penetranceQualifier.name SCV only classification_name string classification.name strength_name string strength.name quality_name string quality.name Submission level (SCV) or aggregate level (VCV/RCV) direction string direction submitter_id string first contributions[] with activityType = 'submitted' SCV only. Joins to submitter.parquet date_last_evaluated date first contributions[] with activityType = 'evaluated' SCV only pmids list\<string> reportedIn[].pmid SCV only. Empty for VCV/RCV

The struct columns are flattened with a _name suffix, so they can't be mistaken for the structs in scv.parquet.

Not carried: data, description, specifiedBy and extensions. A lookup joins back on statement_id for those.

proposition_id dropped (maintainer): it was 91 MB of 292 MB. Every field a lookup needs from the proposition is already inlined, and the id stays reachable through the statement table.

items.title: 1. statement-by-variant
items.text:
Purpose: everything ClinVar says about one variant (submissions, VCV layers, RCVs) in one footer fetch plus one row group.

Column Notes The 17 core columns Sort: variant_id, source_table, statement_id

Which tiers. SCV, VCV and RCV, in one file:

  • All three join to a proposition 100 % of the time: 0 unjoined of 28,045,103 rows on 2026-10-11.
  • SCV alone would be 75 MB.
  • A source_table = 'scv' filter costs nothing extra, provided bloom filters are off.

Pruning. I sampled 2,000 random variants, plus clinvar:10 and the busiest variant (clinvar:17004, 189 statements). Every lookup touched exactly 1 of 226 row groups.

variant_id sorts as text (clinvar:10 < clinvar:100 < clinvar:11). That is fine for = and IN; numeric ranges don't prune.

Row-group size, with bloom filters on (so the files are slightly bigger than the final layout):

Rows per group Row groups File Footer Requests: SELECT * for one variant 122,880 226 201 MB 0.52 MB 11 61,440 451 205 MB 1.03 MB 17 30,720 901 212 MB 2.03 MB 28

Why bloom filters must be off:

  • DuckDB writes them by default. The published scv.parquet has them on 3,523 of its 3,960 column chunks.
  • When a filter's min/max can't rule a row group out, DuckDB probes that column's bloom filter, which costs one request per row group. It does this even when the sort-key filter has already excluded the group.
Query on statement-by-variant Bloom on Bloom off variant_id = 'clinvar:10' 11 10 … AND source_table = 'scv' 238 16 … AND classification_name = 'Pathogenic' 238 16

items.title: 2. statement-by-object
items.text:
Purpose: every statement about a condition or therapy, whether the proposition names the concept itself or names a set that contains it. Every row says which of those is the case.

One row per (statement, concept):

role The concept is… via_set_id membership_operator via_nested_set_id object the proposition's own object: a single condition, tumor type or therapy NULL NULL NULL set_member a leaf member of the condition set or therapy group the proposition names that set its AND/OR the inner clinvar.traitset when the member came through one nested inside a minted clinvar.conditionset, else NULL condition_qualifier a therapeutic-response proposition's conditionQualifier NULL NULL NULL

Direct rows and set rows are never merged. A query for "statements about Marfan syndrome" filters role = 'object'; "statements whose condition set includes Marfan" filters role = 'set_member'. The nested set's own operator is in concept-set-membership (§3). Only minted sets nest, and only one level, so no deeper expansion is needed. Sets themselves are not rows: they have no single meaning to look up by, and a lookup by set id is the job of §3.

Therapies come only through evidence lines. No statement's own proposition is therapeutic. In 2026-10, 13 therapeutic-response propositions are the targets of somatic SCVs' evidence lines (1,568 evidence lines, which also target 1,555 diagnostic and prognostic propositions). The file includes each targeted proposition's concepts and marks those rows via_evidence_line = TRUE:

  • Their proposition columns (proposition_type, predicate, object_id, qualifiers) are the targeted proposition's.
  • Their statement columns (classification_name, …) are the SCV's own, and the SCV's classification is about its own proposition.
  • So those rows also carry the evidence line's own evidence_outcome_name (Level A/B 1,022, Level C/D 570) and evidence_direction. Read those, not classification_name, for the therapy.

Columns:

Column Type Notes concept_id string Sort key 1. clinvar.trait: or clinvar.therapy: id. NULL only on concept_type = 'none' rows concept_type string condition, therapy, or none for a proposition with no object role string object, set_member or condition_qualifier via_set_id string The set/group the proposition names (NULL unless set_member) membership_operator string That set's AND/OR (NULL unless set_member) via_nested_set_id string Inner clinvar.traitset, when flattened through one The 17 core columns object_id is the proposition's object as stated, so it equals via_set_id on set rows via_evidence_line boolean TRUE when the concept came from a proposition an SCV's evidence line targets evidence_outcome_name string Evidence line evidenceOutcome.name (NULL unless via_evidence_line)* evidence_direction string Evidence line directionOfEvidenceProvided (same)*

* In the BigQuery prototype, not in the local measurement build. These columns are non-null on 1,592 rows only, so the size is unaffected.

NULL objects. Four propositions have a NULL object. An earlier prototype typed them as sets, so their statements silently fell out of the file. They are kept as role = 'object' rows with concept_id NULL and concept_type = 'none', sorted last, so every statement in the file is accounted for.

Sort: concept_id NULLS LAST, variant_id, source_table, statement_id, via_evidence_line, role, via_set_id NULLS FIRST, via_nested_set_id NULLS FIRST. The key is unique: 32,555,778 distinct of 32,555,778.

Rows (2026-10):

role / concept_type Rows object / condition 24,750,175 (+ 1,555 via evidence line) set_member / condition 7,019,358 direct + 784,653 through a nested traitset object / therapy 6 (all via evidence line) set_member / therapy 18 (all via evidence line) condition_qualifier / condition 13 (all via evidence line)

Marfan syndrome (clinvar.trait:2645), one lookup, 9 requests:

role SCV VCV RCV object 4,365 3,119 7,273 set_member 5,892 (15 traitsets) 9,287 direct (227 minted sets) + 6,304 nested (234) 11,760 (15 traitsets)

Heavy concepts. clinvar.trait:17556 (not provided) and clinvar.trait:16789 (not specified) each have about 7–8 M rows. A count(*) of one takes 70 requests, over the rate limit. These are catch-alls; leave them download-only (decision 8).

items.title: 3. concept-set-membership
items.text:
Purpose: "which sets contain X" and "what is in set Y", without parsing conditionSet.concepts or therapyGroup.value. It is the small companion that explains the set_member rows of §2.

One row per (set, member). Rows come from every published condition set (the >1-member filter applies) and every therapy group:

  • Direct members. A nested clinvar.traitset inside a minted set appears as a row with member_type = 'set'.
  • Flattened leaves of each nested set, with via_nested_set_id.
Column Type Notes member_concept_id string Sort key 1. Bare id member_type string condition, therapy or set (a nested traitset) member_name string From condition.parquet / therapy.parquet. NULL for nested sets, which have no name, and for 30 conditions with no name in the source set_id string The containing set set_type string conditionSet or therapyGroup concept_set_type string Disease, Finding, TraitChoice, DrugResponse for ClinVar traitsets. NULL for minted sets and therapy groups membership_operator string The containing set's AND/OR via_nested_set_id string Set when the row is a leaf flattened through a nested traitset

Sort: member_concept_id, set_id, via_nested_set_id NULLS FIRST. One duplicate pair is dropped with DISTINCT: a therapy group lists the same therapy twice.

Rows (2026-10):

Kind Rows conditionSet → condition, direct 281,065 conditionSet → condition, through a nested set 90,113 conditionSet → nested set 30,032 therapyGroup → therapy 55 Total 401,265 (6.4 MB, 4 row groups)

Lookups:

  • Which sets contain clinvar.trait:2645: 5 requests. It is in 8 Disease and 7 TraitChoice traitsets (AND), 214 minted sets directly and 290 through a nested traitset (OR).
  • Members of a given set: 9 requests. That is the whole 6.4 MB file, which is fine at this size.

items.title: 4. Genes: two different relationships, two files, never merged
items.text:
The data holds two gene relationships. They mean different things, and no file may present one as the other.

(a) ClinVar's variant-to-gene list, the variation's clinvarGeneList extension: - Shape: many genes per variant. - Columns: each entry carries a relationship_type (within single gene, within multiple genes by overlap, genes overlapped by variant, near gene, upstream/downstream, asserted, but not computed) and a source (submitted or calculated). - Meaning: it describes the variant, not any statement. - Scale: 7,346,154 pairs over 4,637,755 variants and 92,972 genes. 866 variants list more than 500 genes each, contributing 911,238 pairs (mostly genes overlapped by variant, the large CNVs).

(b) The proposition's gene-context qualifier, geneContextQualifier (gene_context_name in the typed Parquet). It is variant-derived and single-valued, not submitter-asserted. Provenance:

  1. Built in gkm-scv-statement-proc.sql, Step 2 (temp_gene_context_qualifiers). It joins each SCV's variation_id to the upstream single_gene_variation table, then to gene. That sets name = gene symbol, primaryCoding.code = the NCBI Gene id, and an HGNC exactMatch mapping.
  2. single_gene_variation comes from clinvar-ingest-bq-tools, scripts/dataset-preparation/04-single-gene-variation-proc.sql. It picks one representative gene per variation, taking the first step of this cascade that applies:
  3. a MANE Select transcript at the start of the variation name
  4. a resolvable gene symbol in an HGVS-style name (NM_…(GENE):c.…)
  5. a star-allele name (CYP2C19*10)
  6. a single gene association of any kind
  7. a single submitted association that is neither genes overlapped by variant nor asserted, but not computed
  8. a single within single gene association
  9. a haplotype/genotype whose child variations all share one gene

Steps 1–3 and 7 record source = 'cvc calculated' when no gene-association row backs the chosen gene. That marks a gene inferred by this heuristic, not one ClinVar reported. The source and relationship_type are not carried into the qualifier, so the Parquet can't tell which step chose the gene. 3. The same gene on every SCV of a variant. Because the qualifier hangs off variation_id, every SCV of a variant gets the same gene. 4. The submitter's own genes appear only as the qualifier's submittedGeneSymbols extension, a per-SCV list parsed from clinical_assertion_variation. 5. The placeholder. When the variation has no single gene but the submitter named genes, name is the literal submitted genes were not normalized, with no coding.

In 2026-10: - 6,694,162 SCVs carry a qualifier: 19,190 gene ids, plus the placeholder on 4,814 SCVs. - 5,812,837 of them also carry submittedGeneSymbols. - In 27,817 the submitted symbols don't include the chosen gene's symbol. - VCV/RCV propositions carry no qualifier today (C4).

The two must stay separate. Sending (a) through statements would label 41.8 M statement rows with genes no statement asserted, and would bury the single-gene choice among overlap genes. Sending (b) through the gene list would lose its "one representative gene" meaning.

items.title: 4.1 variant-gene
items.text:
Purpose: a thin crosswalk of (a). It saves every consumer from unnesting variation.extensions[].value_gene_array[] from a 4 GB file.

Column Type Notes gene_id string Sort key 1. ncbigene: id gene_symbol string From gene.parquet name (a join on the id, not a symbol mapping) variant_id string Sort key 2 relationship_type string As in the gene list relationship_source string submitted or calculated

Sort: gene_id, variant_id, relationship_type, relationship_source (unique). The file is 24.2 MB, 60 row groups. All CNV fan-out is kept; filter on relationship_type to drop it.

Lookups: - BRCA1 (ncbigene:672, 16,089 variants): 5 requests. - TTN (ncbigene:7273, 40,949 variants): 7 requests. - By symbol (gene_symbol = 'BRCA1', not the sort key): 60 requests. Resolve the symbol to an id in the small gene.parquet first.

items.title: 4.2 statement-by-gene-context
items.text:
Purpose: statements by (b), keyed on the qualifier's own NCBI Gene id. That id is geneContextQualifier.primaryCoding.code, already in the data, so no symbol is mapped to an id. Names are carried verbatim, including the placeholder.

Column Type Notes gene_context_id string Sort key 1. ncbigene: + primaryCoding.code. NULL for the placeholder gene_context_name string Verbatim, including submitted genes were not normalized submitted_gene_symbols list\<string> The submittedGeneSymbols extension, verbatim and in the bundle's order The core columns, except gene_context_name

Sort: gene_context_id NULLS LAST, variant_id, source_table, statement_id. The placeholder rows sort last, and a gene_context_name = 'submitted genes were not normalized' filter finds them.

Size: 6,694,162 rows (SCV only today), 73.9 MB, 55 row groups.

Query Requests SCVs for ncbigene:672 (BRCA1), by classification 4 SCVs for ncbigene:4625 (MYH7) 4 SCVs for ncbigene:7273 (TTN) 6 BRCA1 PubMed ids (from pmids) 5 By name gene_context_name = 'BRCA1' (not the sort key) 56 Symbol → id in gene.parquet as a scalar subquery, then by id 7

Typed-Parquet gap: parquet-schemas/var*-proposition.sql exports only gene_context_name. This file is built from the proposition JSON in BigQuery, so it doesn't need them. Adding gene_context_id and submitted_gene_symbols to the four proposition exports is a separate, additive choice (decision 7).

items.title: 4.3 On hold: a fat statement-by-variant-gene file
items.text:
A file of (a) × statements, sorted by gene, answers "every statement on a variant in gene X" in one lookup. It is not recommended for now: it attaches gene-list genes to statements, which is exactly the relationship the source doesn't make, unless every row carries relationship_type/relationship_source and the docs keep saying "variants in/overlapping gene X". The numbers for that decision:

Rows Size (ZSTD) Row groups All gene-list relationships 41,777,105 250.6 MB 340 Without genes overlapped by variant 30,791,138 210.7 MB 251 Rows from the 866 variants with >500 genes 4,575,394 — — Query: VCV classifications for variants in the gene Two-step: variant-gene → statement-by-variant Fat file BRCA1 (16,089 variants) 686 requests, 20.5 MB; touches 196 of 226 row groups 9 requests, 1.2 MB TTN (40,949 variants) 688 requests, 20.9 MB; 188 of 226 row groups 15 requests, 1.3 MB BRCA1, ids already in hand (local list) 681 requests — BRCA1 PubMed ids — 11 requests

The two-step path is correct but not remote-viable: a gene's variant ids are scattered across almost every row group of a variant-sorted file. It works fine on a downloaded statement-by-variant (189 MB).

items.title: 5. statement-by-citation
items.text:
Purpose: every statement that cites a given publication or URL: a PubMed id, a DOI or a URL.

Keyed on a typed citation_id (decided). The key is pmid:<n>, doi:<doi> or url:<url>, verbatim after the prefix, so every kind of citation prunes the same way. It is derived from the bundle's citation Documents, which after the citation fix (fix/scv-citations) are one Document per ClinVar citation, with pmid, doi, urls, name, documentType and verbatim-keeping extensions.

One row per (citation id, SCV, role). VCV and RCV carry no citations.

  • A multi-id Document yields one row per id. ACMG 2015 is one Document with a PMID, a DOI and a PMC URL. It gives three rows: pmid:25741868, doi:10.1038/gim.2015.30 and url:https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/4544753.
  • Ids, not every URL. pmid gives a pmid: row and doi a doi: row. Each entry of urls gives a url: row, except the resolver URL the pipeline derives from the Document's own pmid or doi (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/<pmid>, https://doi.org/<doi>), which would only repeat that id. PMC and Bookshelf ids exist in the bundle only as URLs, so they are url: rows. A SICI-style DOI that VA-Spec's pattern rejects has no doi; it is reachable through its url:https://doi.org/… row.
  • Text-only Documents are excluded. They have no pmid, doi or urls, only the verbatim clinvarCitationText extension, so they have no citation_id. The same goes for a Document that carries only invalidClinvarCitation.
  • Role comes from the bundle. evidence is reportedIn[] and method is specifiedBy.reportedIn. A reportedIn[] Document flagged clinvarAssertionMethodCitation is a second assertion-method citation that Method.reportedIn could not hold, so it is a method row. A method citation is never presented as evidence.
Column Type Notes citation_id string Sort key 1. pmid:…, doi:… or url:… citation_type string pmid, doi or url (the prefix) citation_role string evidence or method pmid string The Document's pmid, on every row of that Document, so a DOI or URL row still shows its PubMed id The core columns, except pmids Includes variant_id and object_id

Sort: citation_id, citation_role, source_table, statement_id. DISTINCT drops a key that one SCV lists twice in the same role.

Rows, estimated on clinvar_2026_09_28_v2_6_0 with the citation fix applied (BigQuery, read-only):

Role pmid: doi: url: Total Distinct keys evidence 1,546,184 8,189 86,522 1,640,895 159,641 method 3,340,801 1,790 2,947,149 6,289,740 1,222 All 7,930,635 160,318

That is about 62 % more rows than the PMID-only file measured below (4,886,981). Nearly all of the growth is 2.95 M method url: rows, most of them a few submitter-uploaded FileTrack PDFs. They are cheap because they compress to a few keys. Size and request counts were not re-measured; re-measure before publishing (task 6).

PMID-only file as measured (2026-10, before the citation fix): 1,546,181 evidence and 3,340,800 method rows, 4,886,981 in all (47.7 MB, 40 row groups). method rows are mostly a few guideline papers: PMID 25741868 (ACMG/AMP 2015) alone has 1,194,391.

Query (PMID-only build) Requests Statements citing PMID 20301691 7 PMID 25741868, by role (1.2 M rows) 23 BRCA1 PubMed ids by joining statement-by-gene-context → this file on statement_id 55, at the limit BRCA1 PubMed ids from statement-by-gene-context.pmids directly 5

With the typed key, a PMID lookup filters citation_id = 'pmid:20301691'. The prefix keeps all pmid: keys in one contiguous range, so pruning matches the PMID-only file.

PubMed ids for a gene: statement-by-gene-context already has pmids, so it is the gene → PMID path (5 requests). The join is the wrong path remotely, because this file is not sorted by statement_id.

items.title: 6. How the files are built
items.text:
1. SQL. Each file is one parquet-schemas/<file>.sql.
  2. The four statement files share the CTE fragment _statement-core.sql, spliced in at {STATEMENT_CORE}.
  3. statement-by-object and concept-set-membership share _concept-sets.sql, spliced in at {CONCEPT_SETS}.
  4. This needs a small change to extract_parquet_typed: substitute the fragments, and skip files whose name starts with _.
  5. The --delta table rewrite must never touch these files (§7).
  6. Sort in the merge. release-gkm.sh step 3 replaces the plain merge COPY for each file with:
SET preserve_insertion_order = false;
COPY (SELECT * FROM read_parquet('<shards>/<file>-*.parquet') ORDER BY <sort key from the table above>)
TO '<dir>/<file>.parquet'
(FORMAT parquet, COMPRESSION zstd, ROW_GROUP_SIZE 122880, WRITE_BLOOM_FILTER false,
 KV_METADATA {clinvar_gkm_release: '<YYYY-MM>', clinvar_gkm_schema_version: '<x.y.z>',
              sort_order: '<sort key>'});

The biggest sort (statement-by-object, 32.6 M rows) fits in the 4–8 GB the merge already uses. The full local family build peaked at 8 GB. 3. Gate in the merge. Fail the release if any of these fails: - Row counts against the source tables: - statement-by-variant = scv + vcv + rcv - statement-by-gene-context = SCVs with a qualifier - concept-set-membership > 0 - 0 NULL sort keys, except gene_context_id on placeholder rows and concept_id on concept_type = 'none' rows (the NULL-object propositions). - 0 bloom filters. - A probe key falls in exactly 1 row group. 4. Cost per monthly set. The dry runs on 2026-10-11 processed (upper bound):

File GB processed statement-by-variant 11.19 statement-by-object 11.21 statement-by-gene-context 11.19 statement-by-citation 8.63 variant-gene 1.28 concept-set-membership 0.02

That is ~43.5 GB, about $0.27 per set. Exporting the core once and deriving the other files locally would save ~$0.20 a month, but it would break the one-SQL-per-file convention and couple the files to the merge step. Not worth it.

Drift risk, and the bundle-derivability rule. Every Parquet value must be recomputable from the JSON bundle (user rule, 2026-10-18). Each file here derives only from bundle content: ids are stripped from #/ pointers, citation keys come from the citation Documents (§5), and the statement and proposition fields are inlined. Building from the dict tables in BigQuery can still drift from what the bundle publishes, because the assembler filters and cleanup (single-member conditionSet drop, strip_empty, extension collapse) must be mirrored by hand. Building the files from the published Parquet, or checking them against it, would prevent that drift. At minimum, task 6 compares each file with the same set's section files.

Why not build them locally from the section Parquet: - It ties the files to typed-table quirks: the pre-#143 quoted object_therapy, and gene_context_id, which the section Parquet doesn't have. - It only works where a full Parquet set exists on disk.

items.title: 7. Deltas
items.text:
None of these files ships in a weekly delta. Each is rebuilt whole for each monthly set.

  • The delta rewrite can't produce them. extract_parquet_typed --delta rewrites .gkm_dict_ → .delta_gkm_dict_. Every file here joins two or more dict tables: statements to propositions; sets to conditions; variations to genes. Joining delta to delta drops every row whose other side didn't change.
  • Also, the comment in extract_parquet_typed saying each schema file reads exactly ONE table is already wrong (the proposition and therapy files read 3–4). Reword it.
  • Applying a delta would undo the sort, and the sort is the whole point. A consumer replaying deltas rebuilds locally instead, with the Working at Scale recipe (about 1 minute per file).
  • They aren't bundle sections. The manifest, the reconstruction oracle and the replay examples iterate over sections. A full derived file in deltas/<date>/parquet/ would be listed as changed rows.

Weekly full copies are decision 4.

items.title: 8. R2 layout, index.json and scripts
items.text:
All six files sit in the monthly set directory: v1/datasets/parquet/YYYY-MM/<file>.parquet, copied to 00-latest/. Year-end archiving (archive_parquet_yearly) moves every file in that directory. An upload with R2_PREFIX='' publishes the flat-root copy the same way.

Script / file Change parquet-schemas/ Six new SQL files + two _ fragments export-gkm-dicts.sh Export lines guarded by if ! $DELTA; fragment splicing; fix the ONE-table comment release-gkm.sh Sorted merge + gate per file (§6) upload-gkm-to-r2.sh None. upload_parquet uploads every *.parquet and copies each to 00-latest/. The dated paths are new, so nothing needs purging generate-r2-index.sh Additive: each datasets.parquet[] entry gets a "parquet": [...] file list (reuse r2_parquet_sections_under, as delta entries do), so readers can tell which sets have the lookup files docs/assets/js/r2-browser.js Render that list, falling back to the fixed 22. Group the lookup files under a "Lookup files (derived)" sub-heading Delta scripts, build-delta-manifest.py, oracles None

items.title: 9. Past releases and the backfill
items.text:
Recommendation: give all six files to the four monthly sets (2026-07, -08, -09, -10). The 15 weeklies need nothing. The console's release picker and the docs file browser both list all four months, so a missing file would 404 there.

This doesn't need to wait for the consolidated backfill or block it: - The files are new, at paths never cached. - They are in no manifest and feed no oracle. - No published file changes.

So they can go out with that backfill if they're ready, or as a separate additive step later.

Cost per monthly set:

Step Cost EXPORT DATA ×6 from the month's source dataset (2026-10 ← clinvar_2026_09_28_v2_6_0, per ADR 0002) ~43.5 GB processed, ~$0.27 Download shards + sort/merge ~5 min, ≤ 8 GB RAM Upload ~578 MB, plus server-side copies for 00-latest (latest set only) CDN purge None (new paths)

For four sets: about $1.10 of BigQuery, about 20 minutes, about 2.3 GB of uploads, then one index.json regeneration. Nothing is overwritten and there is no oracle or reconstruction re-run.

Ordering: build after C4 is decided, because populating aggregate gene context would change the VCV/RCV rows of statement-by-gene-context and statement-by-variant. And if past months should carry the citation fix, build after it too.

items.title: 10. Docs changes (in the implementation PR, on main)
items.text:
Docs ship with the first set that has the files; examples are run against the published files first.

  • [ ] The 22 Tables → new section "Lookup files (derived)":
  • each file's column table from this plan, and its sort key
  • that the files are rebuilt monthly, are not in deltas, and have no id column
  • the two gene relationships (§4), with the provenance of the gene-context qualifier
  • [ ] Recipes: one-lookup recipes for each key:
  • a variant's PubMed ids and VCV layers
  • a condition's statements, direct versus through sets, and its P/LP calls by submitter
  • a therapy's statements, explaining via_evidence_line
  • a gene, with both relationships side by side
  • the statements citing a PMID
  • which sets contain a condition
  • [ ] Console: examples for a variant, a condition, a gene context and a PMID; point the 429 hint at the lookup files.
  • [ ] Working at Scale:
  • "Materialize the joins you repeat" opens by pointing to the published files
  • the local recipe stays for custom columns
  • "Local or remote" gains rows for the lookup files
  • the bloom-filter finding goes into "Share it as a sorted Parquet file"
  • [ ] Joining Tables: a note that gene_context_name is variant-derived, not submitter-asserted. The provenance text from §4 belongs in the Data Guide as well.
  • [ ] Downloads → Parquet Files: list the lookup files as derived and monthly-only.
  • [ ] ADR "Derived Parquet lookup files":
  • not sections
  • rebuilt per monthly set, never in deltas
  • sorted, no bloom filters, key/value metadata
  • the no-implied-relationship rule

items.title: 11. Decisions needed from the maintainer
items.text:
1. Which files to publish. Recommended: the six in the table (≈ 578 MB a month). The fat statement-by-variant-gene is on hold (decision 5).
  2. Statement tiers: SCV + VCV + RCV in every statement file (recommended), or SCV only? VCV/RCV rows reach conditions mostly through minted sets, which role/via_set_id keeps visible.
  3. Drop proposition_id from the core? Recommended: −91 MB on statement-by-variant alone.
  4. Weekly freshness: monthly only (recommended for now), or also full weekly copies at v1/deltas/<YYYY-MMDD>/lookup/? That would cost about $0.27, ~578 MB a week (~30 GB/year of R2), plus delta-script, index and console work.
  5. Fat statement-by-variant-gene (for the user). 250.6 MB with all relationships, or 210.7 MB without genes overlapped by variant. 9–15 requests per gene, against ~690 for the two-step path. If published, every row must carry relationship_type/relationship_source, and the name and docs must say "variants in gene X", never "statements about gene X".
  6. Non-PMID citations — RESOLVED (2026-10-18). The key is a typed citation_id (pmid: / doi: / url:). A multi-id Document yields one row per id, and text-only Documents have no citation_id and are excluded (§5). method rows are kept, with citation_role.
  7. Typed export: add gene_context_id and submitted_gene_symbols to var*-proposition.sql? This is additive and makes the qualifier usable without the lookup file. Recommended, with C2/C3.
  8. Catch-all concepts (not provided, not specified: ~7–8 M rows each in statement-by-object): keep them and document them as download-only (recommended), or leave them out of the file? Leaving them out would make the file a subset of the data.
  9. Sort every published section by id in the merge step? Separate from C1, but it would make statement_id → scv.parquet (data, description) cheap remotely.
  10. Key/value metadata on these files only (recommended), or on all published files?
  11. Backfill timing: with the consolidated backfill if ready, otherwise a separate additive publish (§9).

items.title: Prototype SQL
items.text:
Proposed paths are under src/scripts/parquet-schemas/. {DATASET} is substituted by extract_parquet_typed, and {STATEMENT_CORE} / {CONCEPT_SETS} by the splice step in §6. Each file below was dry-run in its spliced form on clinvar_2026_10_11_v2_6_0. None needs collapse_ext_values, since none has a data column.

Fix found while validating: through 1.0.1, gkm_dict_condition_set stored traitset members as #/condition/… pointers and minted-set members bare, and the published bundle carried the same mix. From 1.1.0 (#160, fix/uniform-condition-pointers) every member is a #/condition/… or #/conditionSet/… pointer, as is every VCV proposition object. Stripping with REGEXP_REPLACE(…, r'^#/[^/]+/', '') gives the same bare ids from either form, so it is a supported derivation from the bundle. conditionSet.sql strips them; _concept-sets.sql must too.

items.title: _statement-core.sql (fragment)
items.text:
-- Shared CTEs for the statement lookup files (spliced in where a file says {STATEMENT_CORE}).
-- prop: every proposition, aligned to one shape; bare ids (no '#/section/' pointers).
prop AS (
  SELECT
    key AS proposition_id,
    JSON_VALUE(value, '$.type') AS proposition_type,
    JSON_VALUE(value, '$.predicate') AS predicate,
    REGEXP_REPLACE(JSON_VALUE(value, '$.subject'), r'^#/[^/]+/', '') AS variant_id,
    REGEXP_REPLACE(JSON_VALUE(value, '$.object'), r'^#/[^/]+/', '') AS object_id,
    REGEXP_REPLACE(JSON_VALUE(value, '$.conditionQualifier'), r'^#/[^/]+/', '') AS condition_qualifier_id,
    JSON_VALUE(value, '$.geneContextQualifier.name') AS gene_context_name,
    IF(JSON_VALUE(value, '$.geneContextQualifier.primaryCoding.code') IS NULL, NULL,
       CONCAT('ncbigene:', JSON_VALUE(value, '$.geneContextQualifier.primaryCoding.code'))) AS gene_context_id,
    -- the bundle's array order, as in #143's var*-proposition.sql
    ARRAY(
      SELECT JSON_VALUE(sym)
      FROM UNNEST(JSON_QUERY_ARRAY(value, '$.geneContextQualifier.extensions')) AS ext,
           UNNEST(JSON_QUERY_ARRAY(ext, '$.value_string')) AS sym WITH OFFSET so
      WHERE JSON_VALUE(ext, '$.name') = 'submittedGeneSymbols'
      ORDER BY so
    ) AS submitted_gene_symbols,
    JSON_VALUE(value, '$.modeOfInheritanceQualifier.name') AS mode_of_inheritance,
    JSON_VALUE(value, '$.penetranceQualifier.name') AS penetrance
  FROM (
    SELECT key, value FROM `{DATASET}.gkm_dict_proposition`
    UNION ALL SELECT key, value FROM `{DATASET}.gkm_dict_vcv_proposition`
    UNION ALL SELECT key, value FROM `{DATASET}.gkm_dict_rcv_proposition`
  )
),
-- stmt: statement-level columns, plus two SCV-only helpers (citation_keys, evidence_line_ids).
-- citation_keys: one entry per typed id of each citation Document (§5). A reportedIn Document flagged
-- clinvarAssertionMethodCitation is a method citation. Text-only Documents yield no key.
stmt AS (
  SELECT
    'scv' AS source_table, s.id AS statement_id,
    REGEXP_REPLACE(s.proposition, r'^#/[^/]+/', '') AS proposition_id,
    s.classification.name AS classification_name, s.strength.name AS strength_name,
    s.quality.name AS quality_name, s.direction,
    (SELECT REGEXP_REPLACE(c.contributor, r'^#/[^/]+/', '') FROM UNNEST(s.contributions) AS c
       WHERE c.activityType = 'submitted' LIMIT 1) AS submitter_id,
    (SELECT c.date FROM UNNEST(s.contributions) AS c
       WHERE c.activityType = 'evaluated' LIMIT 1) AS date_last_evaluated,
    ARRAY(SELECT r.pmid FROM UNNEST(s.reportedIn) AS r WITH OFFSET AS o
          WHERE r.pmid IS NOT NULL ORDER BY o) AS pmids,
    ARRAY(
      SELECT AS STRUCT k.citation_id, k.citation_type, x.citation_role, x.d.pmid
      FROM (
        SELECT IF(EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(d.extensions) AS e
                         WHERE e.name = 'clinvarAssertionMethodCitation'), 'method', 'evidence') AS citation_role, d
        FROM UNNEST(s.reportedIn) AS d
        UNION ALL
        SELECT 'method', s.specifiedBy.reportedIn
        FROM UNNEST([1]) WHERE s.specifiedBy.reportedIn IS NOT NULL
      ) AS x,
      UNNEST(ARRAY_CONCAT(
        IF(x.d.pmid IS NULL, [], [STRUCT(CONCAT('pmid:', x.d.pmid) AS citation_id, 'pmid' AS citation_type)]),
        IF(x.d.doi IS NULL, [], [STRUCT(CONCAT('doi:', x.d.doi), 'doi')]),
        ARRAY(SELECT AS STRUCT CONCAT('url:', u), 'url' FROM UNNEST(x.d.urls) AS u
              WHERE u != CONCAT('https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/', IFNULL(x.d.pmid, ''))
                AND u != CONCAT('https://doi.org/', IFNULL(x.d.doi, '')))
      )) AS k
    ) AS citation_keys,
    ARRAY(SELECT REGEXP_REPLACE(el, r'^#/[^/]+/', '') FROM UNNEST(s.hasEvidenceLines) AS el) AS evidence_line_ids
  FROM `{DATASET}.gkm_dict_scv` AS s
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    'vcv', v.id, REGEXP_REPLACE(v.proposition, r'^#/[^/]+/', ''),
    v.classification.name, v.strength.name, v.quality.name, v.direction,
    CAST(NULL AS STRING), CAST(NULL AS DATE), CAST([] AS ARRAY<STRING>),
    CAST([] AS ARRAY<STRUCT<citation_id STRING, citation_type STRING, citation_role STRING, pmid STRING>>),
    CAST([] AS ARRAY<STRING>)
  FROM `{DATASET}.gkm_dict_vcv` AS v
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    'rcv', r.id, REGEXP_REPLACE(r.proposition, r'^#/[^/]+/', ''),
    r.classification.name, r.strength.name, r.quality.name, r.direction,
    CAST(NULL AS STRING), CAST(NULL AS DATE), CAST([] AS ARRAY<STRING>),
    CAST([] AS ARRAY<STRUCT<citation_id STRING, citation_type STRING, citation_role STRING, pmid STRING>>),
    CAST([] AS ARRAY<STRING>)
  FROM `{DATASET}.gkm_dict_rcv` AS r
),
-- core: the 17 published core columns, then helper columns no file publishes as-is.
core AS (
  SELECT
    p.variant_id, st.source_table, st.statement_id, p.proposition_type, p.predicate, p.object_id,
    p.condition_qualifier_id, p.gene_context_name, p.mode_of_inheritance, p.penetrance,
    st.classification_name, st.strength_name, st.quality_name, st.direction,
    st.submitter_id, st.date_last_evaluated, st.pmids,
    p.gene_context_id, p.submitted_gene_symbols, st.citation_keys, st.evidence_line_ids
  FROM stmt AS st
  JOIN prop AS p ON p.proposition_id = st.proposition_id
)

items.title: _concept-sets.sql (fragment)
items.text:
-- Shared CTEs for concept sets (spliced in where a file says {CONCEPT_SETS}).
-- sets: condition sets (the published >1-member filter) and therapy groups, members as bare ids
-- (members are '#/condition/…' / '#/conditionSet/…' pointers from 1.1.0; minted-set members were bare before).
sets AS (
  SELECT id AS set_id, 'conditionSet' AS set_type, conceptSetType AS concept_set_type,
         membershipOperator AS membership_operator,
         ARRAY(SELECT REGEXP_REPLACE(c, r'^#/[^/]+/', '') FROM UNNEST(concepts) AS c) AS concepts
  FROM `{DATASET}.gkm_dict_condition_set`
  WHERE ARRAY_LENGTH(concepts) > 1
  UNION ALL
  SELECT key, 'therapyGroup', CAST(NULL AS STRING), JSON_VALUE(value, '$.membershipOperator'),
         ARRAY(SELECT REGEXP_REPLACE(JSON_VALUE(c), r'^#/[^/]+/', '')
               FROM UNNEST(JSON_QUERY_ARRAY(value, '$.concepts')) AS c)
  FROM `{DATASET}.gkm_dict_therapygroup`
),
-- membership: direct members, plus the leaves of a nested set flattened one level
-- (only minted clinvar.conditionset sets nest clinvar.traitset sets).
membership AS (
  SELECT s.set_id, s.set_type, s.concept_set_type, s.membership_operator,
         m AS member_concept_id, CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS via_nested_set_id
  FROM sets AS s, UNNEST(s.concepts) AS m
  UNION ALL
  SELECT o.set_id, o.set_type, o.concept_set_type, o.membership_operator,
         im AS member_concept_id, n.set_id AS via_nested_set_id
  FROM sets AS o
  CROSS JOIN UNNEST(o.concepts) AS m
  JOIN sets AS n ON n.set_id = m
  CROSS JOIN UNNEST(n.concepts) AS im
)

items.title: statement-by-variant.sql
items.text:
-- statement-by-variant: one row per SCV/VCV/RCV statement. Merge-step sort:
-- variant_id, source_table, statement_id.
WITH {STATEMENT_CORE}
SELECT * EXCEPT (gene_context_id, submitted_gene_symbols, citation_keys, evidence_line_ids)
FROM core

items.title: statement-by-object.sql
items.text:
-- statement-by-object: one row per (statement, concept). A concept is the proposition's object when that
-- is a single condition or therapy (role = object); each leaf member of the set/group it names
-- (role = set_member, via_set_id + membership_operator, via_nested_set_id when reached through a nested
-- traitset); and a therapeutic proposition's conditionQualifier (role = condition_qualifier). Propositions
-- an SCV's evidence lines target are included with via_evidence_line = TRUE (the only route to therapies);
-- those rows also carry the evidence line's own outcome and direction, since the statement's
-- classification is about the statement's proposition, not the targeted one.
-- A proposition with a NULL object gives one role = object row with concept_id NULL, concept_type 'none'.
-- Merge-step sort: concept_id NULLS LAST, variant_id, source_table, statement_id, via_evidence_line, role,
-- via_set_id NULLS FIRST, via_nested_set_id NULLS FIRST.
WITH {STATEMENT_CORE}, {CONCEPT_SETS},
stmt_prop AS (
  SELECT c.* EXCEPT (gene_context_id, submitted_gene_symbols, citation_keys, evidence_line_ids),
         FALSE AS via_evidence_line,
         CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS evidence_outcome_name, CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS evidence_direction
  FROM core AS c
  UNION ALL
  SELECT p.variant_id, c.source_table, c.statement_id, p.proposition_type, p.predicate, p.object_id,
         p.condition_qualifier_id, p.gene_context_name, p.mode_of_inheritance, p.penetrance,
         c.classification_name, c.strength_name, c.quality_name, c.direction,
         c.submitter_id, c.date_last_evaluated, c.pmids, TRUE AS via_evidence_line,
         el.evidenceOutcome.name AS evidence_outcome_name, el.directionOfEvidenceProvided AS evidence_direction
  FROM core AS c
  CROSS JOIN UNNEST(c.evidence_line_ids) AS el_id
  JOIN `{DATASET}.gkm_dict_evidence_line` AS el ON el.id = el_id
  JOIN prop AS p ON p.proposition_id = REGEXP_REPLACE(el.targetProposition, r'^#/[^/]+/', '')
),
typed AS (
  SELECT sp.*,
         CASE WHEN sp.object_id IS NULL THEN 'none'   -- 4 propositions have no object; keep their rows
              WHEN STARTS_WITH(sp.object_id, 'clinvar.trait:') THEN 'condition'
              WHEN STARTS_WITH(sp.object_id, 'clinvar.therapy:') THEN 'therapy'
              ELSE 'set' END AS object_kind
  FROM stmt_prop AS sp
)
SELECT t.object_id AS concept_id, t.object_kind AS concept_type, 'object' AS role,
       CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS via_set_id, CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS membership_operator,
       CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS via_nested_set_id, t.* EXCEPT (object_kind)
FROM typed AS t
WHERE t.object_kind <> 'set'
UNION ALL
SELECT m.member_concept_id,
       IF(STARTS_WITH(m.member_concept_id, 'clinvar.therapy:'), 'therapy', 'condition'),
       'set_member', t.object_id, m.membership_operator, m.via_nested_set_id, t.* EXCEPT (object_kind)
FROM typed AS t
JOIN membership AS m ON m.set_id = t.object_id
WHERE t.object_kind = 'set'
  AND (STARTS_WITH(m.member_concept_id, 'clinvar.trait:') OR STARTS_WITH(m.member_concept_id, 'clinvar.therapy:'))
UNION ALL
SELECT t.condition_qualifier_id, 'condition', 'condition_qualifier',
       CAST(NULL AS STRING), CAST(NULL AS STRING), CAST(NULL AS STRING), t.* EXCEPT (object_kind)
FROM typed AS t
WHERE t.condition_qualifier_id IS NOT NULL

items.title: concept-set-membership.sql
items.text:
-- concept-set-membership: one row per (set, member) for every condition set and therapy group, with
-- nested-set leaves flattened (via_nested_set_id). Merge-step sort:
-- member_concept_id, set_id, via_nested_set_id NULLS FIRST.
WITH {CONCEPT_SETS},
names AS (
  SELECT id, name FROM `{DATASET}.gkm_dict_condition`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT key, JSON_VALUE(value, '$.name') FROM `{DATASET}.gkm_dict_therapy`
)
SELECT DISTINCT
  m.member_concept_id,
  CASE WHEN STARTS_WITH(m.member_concept_id, 'clinvar.trait:') THEN 'condition'
       WHEN STARTS_WITH(m.member_concept_id, 'clinvar.therapy:') THEN 'therapy'
       ELSE 'set' END AS member_type,
  nm.name AS member_name,
  m.set_id, m.set_type, m.concept_set_type, m.membership_operator, m.via_nested_set_id
FROM membership AS m
LEFT JOIN names AS nm ON nm.id = m.member_concept_id

items.title: variant-gene.sql
items.text:
-- variant-gene: ClinVar's variant-to-gene list (the variation's clinvarGeneList extension), one row per
-- (gene, variant, relationship). Describes the variant, not any statement. Merge-step sort:
-- gene_id, variant_id, relationship_type, relationship_source.
SELECT
  REGEXP_REPLACE(g.gene, r'^#/[^/]+/', '') AS gene_id,
  JSON_VALUE(gn.value, '$.name') AS gene_symbol,
  v.id AS variant_id,
  g.relationship_type,
  g.source AS relationship_source
FROM `{DATASET}.gkm_dict_variation` AS v
CROSS JOIN UNNEST(v.extensions) AS e
CROSS JOIN UNNEST(e.value_gene_array) AS g
LEFT JOIN `{DATASET}.gkm_dict_gene` AS gn ON gn.key = REGEXP_REPLACE(g.gene, r'^#/[^/]+/', '')
WHERE e.name = 'clinvarGeneList'

items.title: statement-by-gene-context.sql
items.text:
-- statement-by-gene-context: statements whose proposition carries a geneContextQualifier (SCV only today).
-- gene_context_id is the qualifier's own primaryCoding.code (NULL for the 'submitted genes were not
-- normalized' placeholder). Merge-step sort: gene_context_id NULLS LAST, variant_id, source_table, statement_id.
WITH {STATEMENT_CORE}
SELECT gene_context_id, gene_context_name, submitted_gene_symbols,
       * EXCEPT (gene_context_id, gene_context_name, submitted_gene_symbols, citation_keys, evidence_line_ids)
FROM core
WHERE gene_context_name IS NOT NULL

items.title: statement-by-citation.sql
items.text:
-- statement-by-citation: one row per (typed citation id, SCV statement, role). citation_id is pmid:/doi:/url:
-- (§5); a multi-id Document gives one row per id; text-only Documents have no key and are absent.
-- DISTINCT drops a key one SCV lists twice in the same role.
-- Merge-step sort: citation_id, citation_role, source_table, statement_id.
WITH {STATEMENT_CORE}
SELECT DISTINCT
  k.citation_id, k.citation_type, k.citation_role, k.pmid,
  c.* EXCEPT (pmids, gene_context_id, submitted_gene_symbols, citation_keys, evidence_line_ids)
FROM core AS c, UNNEST(c.citation_keys) AS k
WHERE c.source_table = 'scv'

items.title: Implementation tasks (after the decisions)
items.text:
Base: 1.0 for the scripts and SQL, with a paired main docs PR. Size: L as a family. The files can ship one at a time; statement-by-variant goes first.

  • [ ] 1. Add the SQL files and fragments above, adjusted for the decisions.
  • [ ] 2. export-gkm-dicts.sh:
  • fragment splicing
  • full-mode-only exports
  • fix the ONE-table comment
  • [ ] 3. release-gkm.sh step 3: sorted merge + gate per file (§6), with --month-label passed into KV_METADATA. Validate with bash -n and shellcheck.
  • [ ] 4. generate-r2-index.sh: the parquet file list on month-set entries. r2-browser.js: render it.
  • [ ] 5. Dry-run the release. Then do a real export to a scratch GCS prefix and gate it.
  • [ ] 6. Compare aggregates against the section files of the same set: the same breakdowns as the Measurements tables.
  • [ ] 7. Console check, with no R2 writes:
  • serve the files locally with CORS and range support
  • point a local docs build's console at them
  • confirm each example stays under ~20 requests in DuckDB-Wasm 1.29.0
  • [ ] 8. Publish with the next monthly set. Backfill 2026-07 … 2026-10 per §9, with each live write confirmed.
  • [ ] 9. Docs per §10, merged in the same window as step 8.

Channel Advance notice (SKIPPED) Completion notice GitHub Discussions, Announcements full text below full text below GitHub Release 1.1.0 notes — full text below, plus the changelog entry Changelog — the 1.1.0 entry (on #146) v1/feed.xml see the note below the republish re-dates every entry Google Group clinvar-gkm@broadinstitute.org (stood up 2026-10-18) full text below full text below

Post: before any R2 overwrite, at least <N> days before the cutover.

Title: ClinVar-GKM 1.1.0 on <CUTOVER DATE>: proposition sections reorganized, every published file rewritten

Body:

On <CUTOVER DATE> we will publish ClinVar-GKM 1.1.0. It is a breaking release. It replaces every published file under /v1/ in place: the 4 monthly full bundles, 00-latest, the 15 weekly deltas and every Parquet set. We are still before GA, so under our versioning policy (ADR 0004 §5) this ships in place, with no parallel 1.0.x line. ADR 0006 records why.

items.title: What changes
items.text:
Propositions are grouped by meaning, not by the shape of their object. Four new bundle sections and Parquet tables replace the old four. Proposition ids don't change; only the section does.

Proposition type (id code) Old section / table New section / table VariantPathogenicityProposition (PATH) varcond-proposition propositionPathogenicity VariantClinicalSignificanceProposition (SCI) varcond-proposition propositionSomaticClinicalImpact VariantDiagnosticProposition (DIAG) varcond-proposition propositionSomaticClinicalImpact VariantPrognosticProposition (PROG) varcond-proposition propositionSomaticClinicalImpact VariantTherapeuticResponseProposition (TR) vartherapy-proposition propositionSomaticClinicalImpact VariantOncogenicityProposition (ONCO) vartumor-proposition propositionOncogenicity the 9 Clinvar* types and ClinvarUndefinedProposition (NP, DR, OTH, RF, ASSOC, AFF, CDFS, PROTECT, CS, UNDEF) varcustom-proposition propositionClinvarCustom

Every statement and evidence-line pointer changes to name the new section: #/varcond-proposition/SCV001234567-PATH becomes #/propositionPathogenicity/SCV001234567-PATH. Code that resolves pointers generically (#/<section>/<id>) needs no change.

The four proposition Parquet tables share one column schema, so read_parquet('proposition*.parquet') reads them all with no renaming. Every table has every column, and a column that doesn't apply is NULL:

Old table.column New column varcond-proposition.object_condition_id object_id vartumor-proposition.object_tumor_type_id object_id vartherapy-proposition.object_therapy object_id varcustom-proposition.subject_id subject_variant_id varcustom-proposition.object_id object_id vartherapy-proposition.condition_qualifier_id condition_qualifier_id (now on every table) — object_type (new: condition, conditionSet, therapy or therapyGroup) mode_of_inheritance, penetrance (varcond, varcustom only) on every table

Versions: the schema $ids move to https://w3id.org/clingen/schema/clinvar-gkm/1.1.0/…, and every bundle declares "schema_version": "1.1.0".

Every published file is rewritten in place. The 4 monthly fulls (2026-07 … 2026-10), 00-latest, the 15 deltas (2026-07-06 … 2026-10-11) and every Parquet set are rebuilt and re-uploaded, and the old var*-proposition.parquet files are deleted. Contents and checksums change. After the cutover R2 serves only the new layout.

items.title: Fixes in the same release
items.text:
These ride the same rebuild, so every published file gets them too:

  • Variant schema: the four ClinvarCategoricalVariant branches are mutually exclusive, and the bundle validates variation through it. No valid record is rejected.
  • HGVS: 14 variants (16 expressions) no longer carry the invalid syntax hgvs.?. ClinVar's text is kept as an extension.
  • Duplicate allele keys: each allele has exactly one allele record.
  • RCV propositions without an object: the 4 propositions of RCV000001117 have their condition again.
  • Condition references: VCV proposition objects and the members of vcv- condition sets are #/ pointers, like every other reference.
  • Citations: one Document per ClinVar citation. URL-only and text-only citations are restored, and DOIs are repaired, with the originals kept as extensions.
  • Gene context: a geneContextSource extension on every SCV gene-context qualifier; placeholder qualifiers are named with the submitter's symbol.
  • Parquet: bare ids in the typed id columns; new typed columns on condition, therapy and therapyGroup; gene_context_id, submitted_gene_symbols and gene_context_source on the proposition tables; range bounds on location. Every Parquet value can be recomputed from the bundle.

The Changelog has the details and counts once 1.1.0 is out.

items.title: How to prepare
items.text:
• To keep the old layout, download the files you need before <CUTOVER DATE>. There is no 1.0.x line after the cutover. Your copies keep working, and the 1.0.1 schemas stay resolvable at their $ids.
  • To tell the layouts apart, read the bundle's schema_version (1.0.1 before, 1.1.0 after) or look for a propositionPathogenicity key or file.
  • Bundle code: read the proposition sections by prefix (every section whose name starts with proposition). To migrate stored pointers, swap the section name using the table above, keyed by the target record's type.
  • Parquet code: replace per-table reads and UNION ALLs with read_parquet('proposition*.parquet'), and rename the columns as above. Earlier local copies can be read in the new shape: each old row's data column holds the full record, so the new columns can be derived from it. The Query the Data pages show how.
  • Validation: validate against the 1.1.0 schemas (https://w3id.org/clingen/schema/clinvar-gkm/1.1.0/json/ClinvarGkmBundle).
  • Mirrors and caches: pause any job that mirrors /v1/ between <CUTOVER DATE> and the completion notice, then re-sync everything. Don't merge files fetched before and after the cutover.
  • Weekly releases: no new weekly release is published between <FREEZE DATE> and the cutover. Weekly releases resume on the 1.1.0 layout.

Questions or concerns: reply here before <CUTOVER DATE>.

items.title: 1. Daily download-stats collection
items.text:
Delivered with this plan:

  • src/scripts/collect-download-stats.sh queries Cloudflare GraphQL httpRequestsAdaptiveGroups for one UTC day (default yesterday, --date YYYY-MM-DD) on host data.clinvar-gkm.org. It writes date,path,status,requests,bytes,distinct_clients to a CSV. Client IPs are used only in memory to count distinct clients; they are never stored. --bq also loads the rows into clingen-dev:clinvar_ingest.gkm_download_stats (created if missing; a re-run replaces that day's rows). CF_EXCLUDE_IPS leaves out maintainer IPs.
  • src/scripts/summarize-download-stats.py estimates complete downloads per bundle as 2xx bytes served ÷ the object's size, with separate tables for monthly fulls and deltas and a summary of every other file.
  • .github/workflows/download-stats.yml runs daily at 03:23 UTC (and on workflow_dispatch with an optional date) and appends the day to stats/YYYY-MM.csv on the orphan branch ops/download-stats. deploy-docs.yml only runs on pushes to main, so these commits never deploy the site.

Steps after merge:

  • [ ] Add the repository secrets CF_ANALYTICS_TOKEN and CF_ZONE_ID (and optionally CF_EXCLUDE_IPS).
  • [ ] Backfill from 2026-10-14, the first day the custom domain served. Cloudflare keeps about 31 days, so 2026-10-14 must be collected by about 2026-11-13: gh workflow run download-stats.yml -f date=2026-10-14, then 15, 16, 17 and 18. Start each run after the previous one finishes (gh run watch): the workflow's concurrency group keeps only one pending run and cancels an older pending one.
  • [ ] Check the first scheduled run created ops/download-stats with stats/2026-10.csv.

items.title: 3. Layout, manifest and index changes (on 1.0, at the 1.1.0 republish)
items.text:
The publishing scripts are changed on feat/r2-ncbi-layout (base 1.0) to write the ADR 0009 layout under v1/1.1/. What they must produce, for the docs and the gates:

Why sidecars, not object metadata: the uploaders copy every object of 2 GB or more (every monthly full and its 00-latest pointer) with aws s3 cp --copy-props none, because R2 lacks GetObjectTagging. That copy drops user metadata, so a checksum stored as metadata would be lost. A <file>.sha256 sidecar (sha256sum -c format) survives every copy and every move.

  • [ ] Monthlies at the line's top level: clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MM.json.gz + .sha256, and clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz + .sha256. The year rollover moves a year's monthlies and sidecars to archive/YYYY/.
  • [ ] Weekly fulls in weekly/: clinvar-gkm_YYYY-MMDD.json.gz + .sha256 for every release, and clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz + .sha256. The month rollover deletes the finished month's.
  • [ ] Deltas in deltas/: clinvar-gkm-delta_YYYY-MMDD.json.gz, its .sha256 and its manifest. The month rollover moves the finished month to deltas/YYYY-MM/; the year rollover moves those folders to archive/YYYY/deltas/YYYY-MM/.
  • [ ] Delta manifest. checkpoint_full names the official monthly that precedes the delta (today every manifest names 2026-10, the newest monthly, so a replay can't find its base). Add bundle = {"path", "size", "sha256"}. build-delta-manifest.py stays BigQuery-only; the uploader patches the file fields.
  • [ ] Parquet in parquet/: one dataset, overwritten every release, with a manifest file giving the build date, the source release and the tool version (source.json is replaced). No Parquet anywhere else.
  • [ ] generate-r2-index.sh writes v1/1.1/index.json:
    • every monthly entry gets sha256 (from its sidecar; null when there is none) and source_release, the release the monthly was built from (ADR 0002);
    • every delta entry gets "bundle": {"path", "size", "sha256"} and the path of its manifest, in whichever folder the delta now sits;
    • the weekly fulls, the archive/YYYY/ contents and the Parquet dataset are listed;
    • the Parquet entry gets "derived": true, and the index a top-level "parquet_note": "Derived from the bundle; may be regenerated (ADR 0008).";
    • top level: "schema_version", "status", "superseded_by", "eol", from LINE_STATUS / SUPERSEDED_BY / LINE_EOL env vars (defaults current, null, null).
  • [ ] Root manifest. Replace the hard-coded "schema": "1.0.0" with SCHEMA_VERSION read from assemble-gkm-dicts.py (overridable by env). List each line folder (v1/1.1/ current, v1/1.0/ frozen with superseded_by and eol). It replaces the "archives" pointer to archive/1.0.1/ planned earlier.
  • [ ] r2-readme.txt. Describe the layout, the rollovers, the .sha256 sidecars and the Parquet note.
  • [ ] CDN (ADR 0005): point the "Latest Parquet" cache rule at the parquet/ folder; purge old paths after every move and delete and the Parquet folder after every release; drop /archive/ from the path allowlist after the 1.0.1 move.
  • [ ] Cleanup: delete the old v1/datasets/, v1/deltas/ and dated Parquet trees (confirmed step, dry run first, then purge).
  • [ ] Gate: generate-r2-index.sh --dry-run output validates with jq; every monthly entry has a 64-hex sha256 and a source_release; every delta's checkpoint_full names the newest monthly whose source_release is earlier than the delta's release.

items.title: 5. Parquet rebuild tool (clinvar-gkm-parquet)
items.text:
ADR 0008 (e) needs a tool a user can run on a published bundle. It is clinvar-gkm-parquet, a separate repo with its own version cadence (design plan on its PR #1). Each tool version declares the bundle schema_versions it accepts and the Parquet table spec it produces. Workstream 1 of the simplification plan then pins the tool so the pipeline and users build Parquet the same way.

Steps:

  • [ ] Build the tool against the 1.1.0 BigQuery-exported Parquet as its oracle (EXCEPT ALL in both directions = 0 rows per table, with the same schema).
  • [ ] The tool writes the Parquet manifest file (build date, source release, tool version) that the published v1/1.1/parquet/ dataset carries.
  • [ ] The tool reads inputs in the ADR 0009 layout: monthlies at the line's top level, weekly/, deltas/ with its YYYY-MM/ folders, and archive/YYYY/. To rebuild a past week it uses the replay rule in task 4, using checkpoint_full and each monthly's source_release.
  • [ ] ClinVar-GKM pins a tool version and the release builds parquet/ with it.
  • [ ] Docs: a "Rebuild Parquet from a bundle" page linked from the Parquet page.
  • [ ] Decision: which bundles the tool accepts. Parquet published before the tool (1.0.x, and 1.1.0, whose Parquet is built by BigQuery SQL) cannot be reproduced bit-for-bit. Options: the tool accepts only 1.1.0 bundles and later; or it also reads the 1.0.x section layout (var*-proposition) in v1/1.0/ and rebuilds it in the 1.1.0 table shape.
