items.title: Pipeline Simplification Plan
items.text:
Status: proposed (2026-10-18), for team review. Governed by ADR 0007. Work starts after the 1.1.0 release ships. Written against main @ 567272c and 1.0 @ 6606d3d (identical src/), with the PR stack as of 2026-10-18.

For agentic workers: REQUIRED: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development or superpowers:executing-plans. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax. Each workstream is one or more reviewable PRs. Run /catchup before starting one. Every live BigQuery rebuild and every R2 write is a separately user-confirmed step.

Goal: Fewer moving parts and fewer places for the same fact to drift, with no change to published output unless a change is intended and announced. The pipeline keeps transforming ClinVar into GKM; it does so with one definition per concept, one source for every artifact and one gate before publish.

Rule for every workstream: a simplification that is not meant to change output must prove that it does not. The full-vs-incremental oracles and oracle-delta-reconstruction.sh report 0,0,0, and the bundle and Parquet built before and after are byte-identical, or differ only in a listed, intended way.

Sources: sizes and line references were measured on the tree above. Counts and costs are quoted from the PRs that measured them; each is cited where it is used. Effort figures are rough working-day estimates for one person and are there to rank the work, not to schedule it.

items.title: 1. Already delivered or in progress in 1.1.0
items.text:
The 1.1.0 release (ADR 0006, in #146) already applies parts of ADR 0007. This plan builds on it and does not redo it.

Item Principle PR State Canonical proposition type → section function clinvar_ingest.gkm_proposition_section, replacing 11 copies of the CASE; fails loudly on an unmapped type 2 plan #155 §2.3, PR 1 planned for 1.1.0 Uniform #/ references: 7,474,404 VCV proposition objects and 336,975 vcv- set members re-wrapped 2 #160 draft Bare-reference guard: validate-proposition-conformance.sh exits non-zero on any bare value in 23 reference fields 3 #160 draft Total order on every aggregate and pick that reaches an output 4 #161 draft One gkm_dict_allele row per allele id (duplicate key that flipped between builds) 4 #157 draft Release gates: reference integrity, expected-diff against snapshots, both oracles, gkm-toolkit on every bundle, bundle ↔ Parquet 3, 4 plan #155 §6.4 planned for 1.1.0 Parquet extensions placeholder cleanup and a bundle_cleanup UDF that matches the assembler 2 #143 draft One consolidated full rebuild of all 16 datasets instead of patching published files 5 plan #155 §6 planned for 1.1.0

items.title: 2. Workstreams at a glance
items.text:
In order of value. Each has a decision that must be made before its implementation starts.

# Workstream Principle Rough effort Decision needed 1 Parquet built from the bundle output 2 5–8 days source of the build, where it runs, condition.parquet columns 2 One canonical definition per concept 2, 4 3–5 days SQL UDFs vs generated fragments; where the Python section list comes from 3 Re-evaluate incremental vs full per procedure 4 1–2 days + 4–6 weeks of data; then 2–5 days per procedure group which procedures stay incremental 4 Input contract checks 1 2–4 days fail vs log per check; where issues are logged 5 One release gate command 3, 4 4–6 days which checks run weekly vs only on procedure changes 6 Artifact restraint 2, 5 1–2 days, plus porting #151 registry format; lookup files from Parquet only

Workstreams 2 and 4 are independent of the others. Workstream 5 runs the checks that 1, 2 and 4 add, so it lands in stages. Workstream 3 needs data collected over several weekly releases, so its measurement should start first even though its decision comes later.

items.title: 3. Workstream 1: Parquet built from the bundle output
Problem
items.text:
Today release-gkm.sh runs four steps:

  1. export-gkm-dicts.sh exports every gkm_dict_* table twice: as NDJSON for the bundle, and as Parquet. 21 tables go through EXPORT DATA with a parquet-schemas/*.sql file each; condition goes through a raw bq extract, so its columns are the untyped camelCase table columns.
  2. assemble-gkm-dicts.py downloads the NDJSON one section at a time and runs each record through strip_empty and collapse_ext_values (gkm_json_cleanup.py). It streams the cleaned records straight into the bundle; they are not written anywhere else.
  3. The Parquet shards are downloaded and merged with DuckDB.
  4. Upload.

The Parquet SQL therefore re-derives each table from the dict tables, in parallel to the bundle. The same cleanup is implemented three times:

Implementation Where Python strip_empty + collapse_ext_values gkm_json_cleanup.py (the bundle) BigQuery JS UDF collapse_ext_values export-gkm-dicts.sh COLLAPSE_UDF (NDJSON proposition and extension exports, and the Parquet SQL) BigQuery JSON_STRIP_NULLS(remove_empty => TRUE) 7 struct-table data columns (scv, vcv, rcv, variation, the three evidence-line tables) and export_ndjson_ext_collapse

items.title: 143 adds a fourth, the bundle_cleanup UDF, to make the Parquet match. It found the placeholder elements in
items.text: scv and evidenceLine extensions, and that JSON_STRIP_NULLS on the key/value tables would have broken the VRS Range nulls in 65,964 location rows. Any new cleanup rule has to be added in every copy, or Parquet and the bundle disagree again.

items.title: Approach
items.text:
Build the Parquet from the records the assembler has already cleaned.

  • Recommended (A): the assembler also writes each section's cleaned records as NDJSON (one {"id": <key>, "record": <cleaned record>} per line, the same bytes it writes into the bundle). A new step replaces steps 1-Parquet and 3: DuckDB reads those files and writes the 22 tables. Each table is one DuckDB SELECT that derives its typed columns from record and sets data to the record verbatim. The 21 BigQuery parquet-schemas/*.sql files become DuckDB SQL files of the same shape. DuckDB is already a release dependency: step 3 uses it to merge the shards.
  • (B): DuckDB reads the assembled bundle. A monthly full bundle is a single JSON object of about 4.8 GB, so this needs a streaming splitter first (the stream_keys.py pattern in §7). That rebuilds the NDJSON of (A) with an extra pass.
  • (C): load the cleaned NDJSON back into BigQuery and keep EXPORT DATA. This keeps the Parquet build in BigQuery if local resources are the constraint, at the cost of a load step.

Deltas use the same path with the delta NDJSON. The NDJSON export from BigQuery stays as it is.

  • [ ] Add the per-section cleaned-NDJSON output to assemble-gkm-dicts.py (behind a flag first).
  • [ ] Port the 21 parquet-schemas/*.sql files to DuckDB over the cleaned NDJSON, with explicit column types. Carry over #143's typed columns and #155's shared proposition schema.
  • [ ] Replace step 3 of release-gkm.sh and release-gkm-delta.sh with the DuckDB build; drop the Parquet half of export-gkm-dicts.sh, COLLAPSE_UDF from the Parquet path and the bundle_cleanup UDF.
  • [ ] Update .claude/rules/scripts.md "Publish-layer cleanup" (the "mirror the same collapse in the typed-Parquet data columns" rule goes away) and the Parquet docs.

items.title: How to measure success
items.text:
• On every artifact of the published 1.1.0 set (4 monthly fulls and 15 deltas), the new Parquet has the same schema (column names, types and order) as the published Parquet, and DuckDB EXCEPT ALL in both directions returns 0 rows for every table. The only allowed differences are listed in advance: the latent JSON_STRIP_NULLS difference in §9.3, if any record has it.
  • The bundle ↔ Parquet gate (§7) passes: per table, the id set equals the bundle section's, and data equals the bundle record.
  • grep finds no JSON_STRIP_NULLS or collapse_ext_values in the Parquet path.

items.title: Risks
items.text:
• Type drift. DuckDB infers JSON types differently from BigQuery (INT64, nested STRUCT field order, JSON vs VARCHAR). Declare every column type; the schema comparison above catches the rest.
  • Local resources. A monthly full is 4.8 GB and its Parquet set about 12 GB, against about 15 GB free on the build machine (#155 §6.6). The build may need a VM or the Cloud Run job.
  • File layout. Row-group size, sort order and compression change the number of HTTP requests a remote query makes (#151 measures lookups in requests). Pin the writer settings and compare request counts for the console's example queries.
  • Release time. Assembly takes about 1.5–2.5 h per full today (#155 §6.6). Measure the new step on one full before switching.

items.title: Decision needed
items.text:
• Source: (A) cleaned NDJSON from the assembler (recommended), (B) the bundle, or (C) BigQuery reload.
  • Where it runs: the build machine, a VM, or the Cloud Run job.
  • condition.parquet: keep the current untyped camelCase columns (no consumer change), or give it typed snake_case columns like the other 21 tables (a breaking column change under ADR 0004).

items.title: 4. Workstream 2: One canonical definition per concept
Problem
items.text:
The same concept is spelled out in many places. Measured on the tree above:

Concept Copies today Where Pointer construction ('#/<section>/' ‖ id) 73 lines with a '#/ literal in 5 procedures gkm-scv-statement-proc.sql 23, gkm-rcv-statement-proc.sql 20, gkm-vcv-statement-proc.sql 19, gkm-catvar-proc.sql 10, gkm-scv-condition-proc.sql 1. Most common targets: evidenceLine 11, conditionSet 11, condition 10, variation 8, a computed section 8 Pointer stripping (REGEXP_REPLACE(…, r'^#/[^/]+/', '')) 30 lines 26 in 16 of the 21 parquet-schemas/*.sql files; gkm-scv-condition-proc.sql; validate-proposition-conformance.sh (2); extract-example.py Proposition type → section 12 CASE sites + 4 WHERE filters procedures: gkm-vcv-statement-proc.sql :223, :296, :374; gkm-rcv-statement-proc.sql :270, :343, :421; gkm-scv-statement-proc.sql :521, :1070. Scripts: export-gkm-dicts.sh PROP_GROUP_CASE, build-delta-manifest.py GROUP_SECTION_CASE, validate-proposition-conformance.sh :72, :92. Parquet: the four var*-proposition.sql filters Bundle section list 4 hand-kept lists assemble-gkm-dicts.py SECTIONS, build-delta-manifest.py table → section map, sub-bundle.py, the bundle schema Tracked output tables 2 arrays with a "Keep in sync" comment gkm-change-log-proc.sql tracked, gkm-delta-proc.sql tables Accession from a proposition id SPLIT(key, '-')[OFFSET(0)] gkm-vcv-statement-proc.sql :708, :710; gkm-rcv-statement-proc.sql :702, :704

The copies already differ. build-delta-manifest.py still reads COALESCE($.customPropositionType, $.type), while the export CASE reads only $.type. The Parquet WHERE filters drop an unmapped type silently while the NDJSON export raises (#155 §2.3).

items.title: Approach
items.text:
• Pointers: two persistent SQL UDFs in clinvar_ingest, versioned under src/procedures/: gkm_ref(section, id) returns #/<section>/<id> and raises on a NULL or empty part; gkm_ref_id(ref) returns the bare id and raises on a value that is not a pointer. Use SQL UDFs, not JavaScript, so BigQuery inlines them.
  • Type → section: #155's gkm_proposition_section (1.1.0). This workstream only checks that no copy came back.
  • Section list and tracked tables: one checked-in definition that every consumer reads. For SQL, a function that returns the tracked-table array; for Python, one module that the assembler, the delta manifest, sub-bundle.py and extract-example.py import. A test checks the module against the bundle schema's section properties.
  • Accession from an id: replace the SPLIT with an explicit accession column, or a join through the statement. This depends on Workstream 3: if the VCV/RCV statement procedures stop carrying forward, the parse goes away with the carry-forward.

  • Pointer stripping in Parquet: goes away with Workstream 1 if the Parquet SQL moves to DuckDB; otherwise the Parquet SQL calls gkm_ref_id.

  • [ ] Add gkm_ref / gkm_ref_id and a tracked-tables function; deploy them before the procedures.

  • [ ] Replace each site in the table above. One PR per procedure keeps the oracle runs small.
  • [ ] Add a CI grep guard: no '#/ literal and no ^#/ regex outside the shared definitions.

items.title: How to measure success
items.text:
• The full-vs-incremental oracles and oracle-delta-reconstruction.sh report 0,0,0.
  • Dict-table fingerprints (BIT_XOR(FARM_FINGERPRINT(TO_JSON_STRING(row))), the #161 method) and the assembled 10-11 bundle are byte-identical before and after.
  • The CI guard passes, and a seeded '#/ literal makes it fail.

items.title: Risks
items.text:
• The UDFs live in clinvar_ingest, which the upstream project also uses. Use the gkm_ prefix.
  • Every procedure change moves the pipeline gate_key, so the first run after deploy is a full rebuild of the current dataset (about 0.21 TiB, #155 §6.3). No backfill is needed, because output does not change.
  • A raising UDF fails a weekly run on bad data that used to pass silently. That is intended (principle 1), but the first runs need watching.

items.title: Decision needed
items.text:
• Persistent SQL UDFs (recommended) or SQL fragments generated into the procedure files at build time.
  • Python section list: a hand-kept module checked against the bundle schema (recommended), or generated from the bundle schema.

items.title: 5. Workstream 3: Re-evaluate incremental vs full per procedure
Problem
items.text:
ADR 0001 made the pipeline incremental by default. It records that the large slot-time win is in variation identity and vrsify, that the dict aggregates are roughly break-even on cost, and that the delta product justified making them incremental too.

The incremental machinery is a large share of the pipeline:

Part Size Upstream table diffs (dataset-diff*.sql) 4 files, 414 lines Changed-set procedures (gkm-scv-changed, gkm-rcvvcv-changed, variation-vrs-changed) 3 files, 722 lines Full/incremental branches inside the procedures (impacted filters, UNION-CTAS merges, the gkm_vrs CLONE with its depth-3 fallback) 8 procedures Version gate (gkm-pipeline-version-proc.sql, gate_key in run-release.sh) 1 procedure + script logic Proposition id parsing in the VCV/RCV carry-forward 4 sites (§4) Full-vs-incremental oracles (oracle-catvar.sh, oracle-scv-condition.sh, oracle-scv-statement.sh, oracle-rcv.sh, oracle-rcv-statement.sh, oracle-vcv.sh, oracle-vcv-statement.sh, gkm-oracle-compare-proc.sql) 8 files; they exist because there are two modes

Two of the four defect classes in ADR 0007 came from here: non-determinism showed up as incremental ≠ full, and the delta model depends on the proposition id format.

The deltas do not depend on the carry-forward. gkm_change_log finds Added/Updated/Deleted records by diffing each published gkm_dict_* table against the prior release, and gkm_delta_build materializes the A/U rows. That already is "computing deltas by diffing outputs". A procedure that always rebuilds in full still produces correct deltas, as long as its output is deterministic. gkm-change-log-proc.sql, gkm-delta-proc.sql, build-delta-manifest.py and oracle-delta-reconstruction.sh stay in either mode.

What a full rebuild costs. From #155 §6.3 (the #132 rebuild of the 16 datasets on 2026-10-11, from INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS): about 0.21 TiB billed, 11–12 min wall clock and 14 slot-hours per dataset for the downstream gkm_* stage; about 3.4 TiB for all 16, about $21 at on-demand $6.25/TiB. That is about $1.30 per weekly release. This covers the downstream procedures only; variation identity and vrsify (with its external VRS resolution) are not in it. The cost of the incremental runs per procedure has not been measured.

items.title: Approach
items.text:
Measure first; decide per procedure afterwards.

  • [ ] For 4–6 consecutive weekly releases, record per procedure, in both modes: bytes billed, slot-ms and wall clock from INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS (child jobs of each CALL, grouped by procedure). The full-mode runs that the full-vs-incremental oracles already do provide the full side; where an oracle does not cover a procedure, build it in full into a scratch dataset.
  • [ ] Record vrsify separately: VRS resolution time and request volume, full vs incremental.
  • [ ] Record the maintenance side for the same period: lines in incremental-only paths per procedure, and the defects and oracle exceptions caused by incremental mode (for example #157 and the 1.0.1 allele exceptions).
  • [ ] Write the results and a recommendation into an ADR that amends or supersedes ADR 0001.
  • [ ] For each procedure moved to full-only: remove its incremental branch, its changed-set inputs if nothing else reads them, and its full-vs-incremental oracle.

items.title: How to measure success
items.text:
• The decision is recorded with the numbers behind it.
  • For each procedure moved to full-only, its output equals the incremental output on the measured weeks (byte-identical tables), and oracle-delta-reconstruction.sh reports 0,0,0 on the published deltas.

items.title: Risks
items.text:
• Shadow cost. A full downstream build is about $1.30 per dataset, so 6 weeks of shadow builds cost about $8 at on-demand rates. Variation identity and vrsify in full mode cost much more and may not be worth shadowing every week.
  • Hidden order dependence. gkm_change_log compares rows with canonicalize_json when the raw bytes differ, so array-order drift does not show up as a change. Once outputs are deterministic (#161), that tolerance hides regressions instead of noise. Consider comparing raw bytes only and treating any order-only U as a defect.
  • Weekly wall clock. Full mode adds minutes per release for the downstream stage, not hours.

items.title: Decision needed
items.text:
• Which procedures stay incremental. The likely shape is incremental for variation identity and vrsify, full for the downstream dict procedures, but that must come from the measurement.
  • Whether gkm_change_log keeps its order-insensitive comparison.

items.title: Problem
items.text:
The pipeline trusts its upstream inputs. In 1.1.0 four input problems reached the output or nearly did:

Input problem Measured Effect Handling in ClinVar-GKM clinvar_ingest.entrez_gene is missing gene ids used by gene_association 64,854 ids, 230,303 variations (10-11) 37 SCV propositions lose gene context (09-28) none; upstream refresh requested rcv_mapping lists SCVs absent from the VCV data 2–3 a week; 2 in 10-11 4 RCV propositions with no object from 10-04 (#158) #158 joins first and picks with a total order Malformed HGVS in ClinVar's VCV XML (no sequence-type letter) 16 expressions, 14 variations (10-11) hgvs.? syntax failed schema validation #145 keeps the original in an extension single_gene_variation counts gene rows, not distinct genes 55 haplotypes/genotypes (09-28) 63 SCV propositions without gene context none; upstream fix requested

The rcv_mapping difference is not a bug: it is a faithful parse of ClinVar's RCV XML, which runs out of sync with the VCV XML. Consumers must join rcv_mapping SCVs to the VCV-side data.

Upstream issues (tracked together in clingen-data-model/clinvar-gkm#164):

  • clingen-data-model/clinvar-ingest-bq-tools#38: single_gene_variation counts gene rows instead of distinct genes (COUNT vs COUNT DISTINCT)
  • clingen-data-model/clinvar-ingest-bq-tools#39: clinvar_ingest.entrez_gene is stale; 64,854 gene ids are missing
  • clingen-data-model/clinvar-gkm#163: report to ClinVar (by email) of the 16 malformed HGVS expressions in the VCV XML

items.title: Approach
items.text:
One read-only procedure, gkm_input_contract(on_date), that run-release.sh calls before the gkm_* stage. Each check has a fixed action: fail stops the run; log records the rows and continues.

Check Action Expected today Every SCV in rcv_mapping exists in clinical_assertion, or is logged log 2–3 a week Every gene id the run uses is in clinvar_ingest.entrez_gene log 64,854 gene_association ids missing (10-11) until the refresh Every HGVS expression has a sequence-type letter log; fail if a form appears that #145's repair rules do not handle 16 No duplicate natural keys in the consumed input tables fail 0 No duplicate keys in any gkm_dict_* / delta_gkm_dict_* output (after the run; the #157 scan) fail 0 after #157

Logged rows go to clinvar_ingest.validation_issues_log, the existing table in clinvar-ingest-bq-tools, so upstream and ClinVar-GKM issues are in one place. A count that jumps well above its usual level should fail rather than log; the thresholds come from the first weeks of data.

  • [ ] Confirm the validation_issues_log schema and write access with the clinvar-ingest-bq-tools owners.
  • [ ] Write gkm_input_contract and call it from run-release.sh before stage 4.
  • [ ] Run it read-only on all 16 published-release datasets and record the baseline counts.

items.title: How to measure success
items.text:
• On the 16 datasets, the checks reproduce the counts above.
  • A seeded violation per check (negative control) fails or logs as specified.
  • Output does not change: the checks are read-only, so the oracles stay 0,0,0.

items.title: Risks
items.text:
• A check that fails too eagerly blocks a weekly release on an upstream change that the pipeline handles. Start with log, promote to fail per check once the baseline is known.
  • validation_issues_log belongs to another project. Writing to it needs that team's agreement.

items.title: Decision needed
items.text:
• Fail or log, per check (the table above is the proposal).
  • Log to clinvar_ingest.validation_issues_log (recommended) or to a ClinVar-GKM table.

items.title: Problem
items.text: The gates exist, but as separate scripts that a maintainer runs by hand in the right order; #155 §6.4 lists them for 1.1.0. Some of the most useful checks from the 1.1.0 work are not in the repo at all: agents wrote them into a session scratchpad. A gate that has to be remembered gets skipped.

items.title: Approach
items.text:
src/scripts/release-gate.sh <date> [--delta] --bundle <path> --parquet-dir <dir> runs every check in order, cheapest first, writes a pass/fail report with counts to the staging directory, and exits non-zero on any failure. release-gkm.sh and release-gkm-delta.sh call it between assembly and upload, using the staging stop (--no-upload) that #155 PR 4 adds, so a failure blocks publish.

  1. References: validate-proposition-conformance.sh (bare-reference guard from #160, reference integrity from #155 PR 1; both exit non-zero).
  2. Duplicate keys over every gkm_dict_* / delta_gkm_dict_* table.
  3. Full-vs-incremental oracles: the seven oracle-*.sh scripts, 0,0,0 (scope set by Workstream 3).
  4. oracle-delta-reconstruction.sh, 0,0,0.
  5. gkm-toolkit validate_bundle_schema with the strict registry on the staged real bundles, full and delta (validate-schema-conformance.py, extended).
  6. Bundle ↔ Parquet recompute: per table, the id set and data equal the bundle section.
  7. Monthly only: the published full plus its deltas reconstructs the next full.

Scratch tools to promote. These were written during the 1.1.0 work and are not in the repo. Each needs its hard-coded worktree paths replaced by arguments, bash -n / shellcheck (bash 3.2), and a test or negative control.

Tool (scratchpad) What it does Promote as determinism/genchain.py, genscript.py, gen_vi.py Turn a procedure's EXECUTE IMMEDIATE step bodies into a read-only CTE chain or temp-table script, so a procedure can be run against real data without writing tables src/scripts/tools/proc-chain.py (dry-run harness; used by #157, #160, #161) determinism/build_cond.sh, build_vrcv.sh Two no-cache runs of a procedure chain compared by BIT_XOR(FARM_FINGERPRINT(TO_JSON_STRING(row))) oracle-determinism.sh allele-dedup/scope.sh Duplicate-key scan of every gkm_dict_* / delta_gkm_dict_* table across the 16 datasets gate check 2 allele-dedup/gen_allele_check.py Extracts one procedure step verbatim as a read-only SELECT fold into proc-chain.py allele-dedup/toolkit_check.py, mini_bundle.py, validate_new.py gkm-toolkit validation with relaxed and strict registries, with a negative control fold into validate-schema-conformance.py (gate check 5) parquet-audit/bin/stream_keys.py, stream_small.py Stream a multi-GB bundle line by line: per-section key lists, a sub-bundle of the small sections src/scripts/tools/bundle-stream.py parquet-audit/bin/cmp_delta.py, cmp_full_small.py, scv_ext.py Compare Parquet rows and data with the bundle records gate check 6 verify/bin/verify.py, run_schema.sh, stream_pick.py; verify/run.sh Run a parquet-schemas/*.sql file against a dataset and compare old/new output with the bundle interim only; obsolete after Workstream 1 backfill102/verify_patch.sh Expected-diff of rebuilt tables against snapshots (#155 §6.4) oracle-expected-diff.sh

parquet-audit/bin/probe.py, probe2.py and cmp_sim.py are one-off probes and are not worth keeping.

  • [ ] Promote the tools above (one PR each for the harness, the determinism check and the bundle tools).
  • [ ] Write release-gate.sh and wire it into both release scripts before the upload step.
  • [ ] Record each check's run time and bytes billed on one weekly release and one monthly full.

items.title: How to measure success
items.text:
• The gate passes on the published 1.1.0 set (4 fulls and 15 deltas).
  • Each check has a negative control that makes the gate fail.
  • No release script can reach the upload step without a passing gate report for the same artifacts.

items.title: Risks
items.text:
• Cost and time. #155 estimates the oracles and gates for the 16-dataset rebuild at about 2 TiB, about $12, over several hours. A weekly run is smaller, but has not been measured; the full-vs-incremental oracles are the expensive part.
  • Gate fatigue. A gate that fails on known, accepted exceptions (such as the allele cross-version shift, §9.4) gets bypassed. Exceptions must be listed in the gate with an expiry, not skipped by hand.

items.title: Decision needed
items.text:
• Whether the full-vs-incremental oracles run on every weekly release, or only when the gate_key moves (a procedure changed). This depends on Workstream 3.
  • Whether the gate report is published with the release notes.

items.title: Problem
items.text:
Every published artifact needs building, gating, documenting and keeping. Today R2 holds, per ADR 0004:

  • per monthly set: one bundle and 22 Parquet tables (21 typed, plus the raw condition extract);
  • per weekly delta: a delta bundle, delta Parquet and the A/U/D manifest; currently 4 monthly fulls and 15 deltas (#155 §6.4);
  • aliases (00-latest), the /v1/ layout plus the flat-root mirror kept for backward compatibility, the root manifest, index.json and feed.xml.

Planned: a family of six sorted lookup files, with a seventh on hold (#151). #155 replaces the four proposition tables with four new ones, so the table count stays at 22.

items.title: Approach
items.text:
• Lookup files are a thin layer over the published Parquet. They are built only from the published Parquet set, with DuckDB, never from the BigQuery dict tables. Then they are recomputable from the bundle by construction (principle 2). The #151 prototypes are BigQuery SQL against the dict tables and would need porting.
  • Every published artifact has an entry in a checked-in registry: path pattern, owner, what it derives from, its gate, its docs page, whether it ships in deltas, and its retention. A new artifact is added to the registry in the same PR that creates it.
  • The release gate (Workstream 5) fails on any path in index.json that is not in the registry.

  • Review the existing set for retirement candidates, starting with the flat-root mirror (ADR 0004 §4) and, if Workstream 1 types it, the raw condition extract.

  • [ ] Write the registry for today's artifacts.

  • [ ] Add the registry check to release-gate.sh.
  • [ ] Port the #151 prototypes to DuckDB over the published Parquet before that work is built.

items.title: How to measure success
items.text:
• Every path in index.json matches a registry entry, and the gate enforces it.
  • Lookup files rebuilt from the published Parquet equal the #151 prototype output on the 2026-10 set.

items.title: Risks
items.text:
• A registry nobody updates becomes another copy that drifts. The gate check is what keeps it honest.
  • Building lookup files outside BigQuery needs the same local resources as Workstream 1.

items.title: Decision needed
items.text:
• Registry format and location (a YAML file next to the release scripts, or a docs page).
  • Lookup files built from the published Parquet only (recommended), which means porting #151 first.
  • Whether and when to retire the flat-root mirror; this is a consumer-facing change under ADR 0004.

items.title: 9. Small known follow-ups found during 1.1.0
items.text: Each is small and independent of the workstreams. None changes published data today except §9.4.

items.title: 9.1 variation_identity.mappings keyed by the xref id
items.text: variation-identity-proc.sql builds mappings in the xm_ctes CTE x with x.id as variation_id (:114, full mode), and the incremental merge repeats it (:1054). variation_xref has a variation_id column, but the CTE uses the xref id in its place, so mappings is grouped by xref id and joined to whichever variation has that id, or to none. No downstream procedure reads it: gkm-catvar-proc.sql builds its own temp_catvar_mappings. Fix the key, or drop the column.

items.title: 9.2 SCV mode-of-inheritance join could duplicate keys
items.text: gkm-scv-statement-proc.sql Step 3 builds temp_moi_qualifiers with one row per SCV per ModeOfInheritance attribute (about :441–:474) and LEFT JOINs it by scv_id (about :540 and :686). An SCV with two such attributes would emit two rows with the same proposition key. There are 0 such SCVs today. Pick one attribute with a total order, or fail loudly; the duplicate-key gate (§7, check 2) would catch it either way.

items.title: 9.3 JSON_STRIP_NULLS in the struct-table Parquet data columns
items.text: scv.sql, vcv.sql, rcv.sql, variation.sql, evidenceLine.sql, vcv_evidenceLine.sql and rcv_evidenceLine.sql build data with JSON_STRIP_NULLS(…, remove_empty => TRUE). Unlike the assembler's strip_empty, it drops {} list elements, so a [{}] that the bundle keeps would become [] or be dropped in Parquet. It is latent: the producing procedures emit NULL, not [{}] (sql-procedures.md). Workstream 1 removes it; until then, #143's bundle_cleanup UDF could replace it.

items.title: 9.4 Allele cross-version SPDI shift
items.text: Documented in docs/reference/known-issues.md: when the VRS line advanced at 2026-08-29, some allele and SPDI digests shifted. Keys are unchanged and every #/allele/ reference resolves, but delta reconstruction of those alleles across 08-22 → 08-29 is not exact; it is an accepted exception to the delta-reconstruction oracle. Decide whether to keep it as a documented exception (listed in the gate, §7) or to recompute the affected alleles in a future rebuild.

items.title: 10. Not proposed
items.text:
• Content-shared propositions. Deferred in #155 §3.B: about 4.7% size saving, against breaking the VCV/RCV carry-forward and every consumer that reads the level from the id.
  • Rewriting the procedures in another language or engine. The defects in ADR 0007 come from duplication and missing checks, not from BigQuery SQL.

items.title: Proposition Reorganization by Meaning — Implementation Plan
items.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development or superpowers:executing-plans. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax. Each PR in §8 is one reviewable unit. Run /catchup before starting a PR; this plan was written against main @ 567272c and 1.0 @ 6606d3d with the PR stack as of 2026-10-18. Every live BigQuery rebuild and every R2 write is a separately user-confirmed step.

Goal: Reorganize ClinVar-GKM propositions by meaning instead of object shape, in both the JSON bundle and the typed Parquet, in the current 1.x line, as part of the one consolidated rebuild and backfill (see the master plan 2026-10-16-parquet-followups.md, "Consolidated data release").

Decided (user, 2026-10-18):

  1. Four meaning-based groups replace varcond-proposition, varcustom-proposition, vartumor-proposition and vartherapy-proposition (§2).
  2. All proposition Parquet tables share one column schema, so read_parquet('proposition*.parquet') unions them with no renaming. Every column is derivable from the bundle (§4).
  3. It ships now under ADR 0004 §5 (in-place change during stabilization, announced), inside the single consolidated rebuild + backfill. Docs move with every PR.

Architecture (recommended): Keep the three per-level dict tables (gkm_dict_proposition, gkm_dict_rcv_proposition, gkm_dict_vcv_proposition) exactly as they are. Only two things change in BigQuery: the section name inside every statement and evidence-line pointer (#/<section>/<id>), and one canonical type→section function that every producer and the export share. The split into sections stays at the delivery layer (export + assemble), as Phase 2 did. Proposition ids, proposition records, the change log, the delta build and both oracles are untouched by the reorganization itself.

Consequence: every SCV, VCV and RCV statement and every SCV evidence line changes (its pointer), so the patch-style backfill prepared for 1.0.2 (scratchpad/backfill102/) no longer fits. The release becomes a full rebuild of all 16 datasets + full re-export + re-assembly of every published bundle and Parquet set, modeled on 1.0.1 (§6).

Source: Counts were measured read-only on clinvar_2026_09_28_v2_6_0 (source of the 2026-10 monthly) and clinvar_2026_10_11_v2_6_0, and type coverage across all 16 published-release datasets. Parquet sizes are from a prototype that rebuilt the four new tables from the published 2026-10 Parquet data column (the bundle record) with DuckDB, calibrated against the published files (§5).

items.title: 2. The groups
path: Proposition Reorganization by Meaning — Implementation Plan

items.title: 2.1 Coverage check
items.text:
Every proposition type in all 16 datasets behind published releases (clinvar_2026_06_27_v2_5_0 … clinvar_2026_10_11_v2_6_0, SCV + RCV + VCV dicts, 91 GB scanned) falls into exactly one group. 15 types occur:

Type Levels seen New section VariantPathogenicityProposition SCV, RCV, VCV propositionPathogenicity ClinvarNotProvidedProposition, ClinvarDrugResponseProposition, ClinvarOtherProposition, ClinvarRiskFactorProposition, ClinvarAssociationProposition, ClinvarAffectsProposition, ClinvarConflictingDataFromSubmitterProposition, ClinvarProtectiveProposition, ClinvarConfersSensitivityProposition SCV, RCV, VCV propositionClinvarCustom VariantClinicalSignificanceProposition SCV, RCV, VCV propositionSomaticClinicalImpact VariantDiagnosticProposition, VariantPrognosticProposition, VariantTherapeuticResponseProposition SCV only (evidence-line targets) propositionSomaticClinicalImpact VariantOncogenicityProposition SCV, RCV, VCV propositionOncogenicity

Stragglers:

  • ClinvarUndefinedProposition: 0 rows in all 16 datasets, but reachable. The SCV proc falls back to it when a classification has no type (gkm-scv-statement-proc.sql Step 1, the STRUCT('ClinvarUndefinedProposition' …) arm), and the RCV/VCV dict builds use IFNULL(cpt.gks_type, 'ClinvarUndefinedProposition'). The lookup table clinvar_ingest.clinvar_proposition_types also has an undef row. → propositionClinvarCustom (it is a Clinvar* custom type and is already in the custom section's schema anyOf).
  • ClinvarGermlineCustomProposition: 0 rows. It is the abstract base the custom types compose, never a type value. It gets no section. It should also leave the custom section's anyOf in the bundle schema (today it is listed there, which lets a custom-shaped record with a wrong type pass); coordinate with #153, which reworks those mixins.
  • VCV/RCV: there are no VCV/RCV-only types. Diagnostic, Prognostic and TherapeuticResponse never occur above SCV; VCV/RCV somatic aggregates use VariantClinicalSignificanceProposition, which lands in the same group as the SCI SCVs they aggregate.

Latent gap (fix in this release): the RCV/VCV statement pointer sites compute the group from cpt.gks_type without the IFNULL. A NULL type would hit the ELSE ERROR, so it fails loudly today. The new canonical function (§2.3) takes the same resolved type the dict row carries, so a future Undefined row gets a consistent pointer.

items.title: 2.2 Names
items.text:
Existing bundle sections are lowerCamelCase nouns (sequenceReference, copyNumberChange, conditionSet, therapyGroup, evidenceLine). The four *-proposition keys are the only kebab-case sections, so the reorg also removes an inconsistency.

Option Example For Against proposition<Meaning> (proposed) propositionPathogenicity lowerCamelCase like every other section; sorts together in listings and the R2 browser; proposition*.parquet is one glob; a pointer test is startsWith('#/proposition') reads noun-first <meaning>Proposition pathogenicityProposition mirrors the va-spec class names scatters alphabetically; the glob becomes *Proposition.parquet

Recommendation: keep the proposed names: propositionPathogenicity, propositionClinvarCustom, propositionSomaticClinicalImpact, propositionOncogenicity. The Parquet file names equal the section names (as every other section's do), so read_parquet('proposition*.parquet') matches exactly these four and nothing else.

Section order in the bundle (assembler SECTIONS, in place of the four current entries): propositionPathogenicity, propositionOncogenicity, propositionSomaticClinicalImpact, propositionClinvarCustom.

items.title: 2.3 One canonical mapping
items.text:
Today the type→group CASE is copied verbatim into 11 places (8 proc sites, the NDJSON export, the delta manifest, the conformance validator) and the Parquet SQL uses four separate WHERE filters. Copies can drift, and the WHERE filters silently drop an unmapped type from Parquet while the NDJSON export raises (Parquet-vs- bundle audit, finding 1).

Recommendation: one persistent SQL UDF, versioned in this repo and deployed with the procs:

-- src/procedures/gkm-proposition-section-func.sql
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION `clinvar_ingest.gkm_proposition_section`(prop_type STRING) AS (
  CASE
    WHEN prop_type = 'VariantPathogenicityProposition' THEN 'propositionPathogenicity'
    WHEN prop_type = 'VariantOncogenicityProposition' THEN 'propositionOncogenicity'
    WHEN prop_type IN ('VariantClinicalSignificanceProposition', 'VariantDiagnosticProposition',
                       'VariantPrognosticProposition', 'VariantTherapeuticResponseProposition')
      THEN 'propositionSomaticClinicalImpact'
    WHEN prop_type IN ('ClinvarNotProvidedProposition', 'ClinvarDrugResponseProposition',
                       'ClinvarOtherProposition', 'ClinvarRiskFactorProposition',
                       'ClinvarAssociationProposition', 'ClinvarAffectsProposition',
                       'ClinvarConflictingDataFromSubmitterProposition', 'ClinvarProtectiveProposition',
                       'ClinvarConfersSensitivityProposition', 'ClinvarUndefinedProposition')
      THEN 'propositionClinvarCustom'
    ELSE ERROR(FORMAT('unmapped proposition type for section mapping: %t', prop_type))
  END
);
  • The custom list is explicit (not LIKE 'Clinvar%'), so a new upstream type fails the build instead of landing in a section whose schema rejects it.
  • Every consumer calls it: the 8 pointer sites, the NDJSON export, the Parquet template's WHERE, the delta manifest and the validator. In the Parquet export the WHERE evaluates the function on every row, so an unmapped type raises and fails the export: the same fail-loud behavior as NDJSON.
  • It lives under src/procedures/, so it is part of run-release.sh's gate_key (git log -1 -- src/procedures src/scripts src/vrsify).
  • Belt and braces: the export also asserts that the four sections' row counts sum to the three dicts' total.

items.title: 3.A Gene-context qualifier: keep it on the proposition (revised)
items.text:
Not planned: moving submittedGeneSymbols to the SCV statement, or dropping the placeholder qualifiers. The user's direction (2026-10-18): propositions must capture the geneContextQualifier, because the submitter's stated gene is the strongest evidence of the gene context of the claim.

  • submittedGeneSymbols stays an extension on the qualifier.
  • The Parquet submitted_gene_symbols, gene_context_id and gene_context_name stay on the proposition tables (PR #143 adds them; the shared schema in §4 carries them on all four tables).
  • The placeholder qualifiers stay.

Measured facts (2026-09-28, 6,736,579 SCV propositions; the six cases sum to the total):

Case SCV propositions Submitter's gene equals the qualifier gene 5,781,673 Submitter gave this gene plus others 101 Submitter's gene differs from the qualifier gene (top cases are old or renamed symbols for the same gene: GBA→GBA1, MUT→MMUT, C10orf2→TWNK, CENPJ→CPAP) 27,817 Gene inferred from the variant (single_gene_variation); submitter gave none 881,325 Placeholder: submitter gave a gene, the variant has no single gene (name = "submitted genes were not normalized") 4,814 No qualifier 40,849

Candidate improvements (the user's to decide):

  • (a) a provenance extension on the qualifier: the gene came from the submitter, was inferred, or differs;
  • (b) the placeholder's name set to the submitted symbol verbatim, plus a not-normalized flag, instead of the literal "submitted genes were not normalized";
  • (c) submitter-first selection of the qualifier gene.

VCV/RCV propositions carry no geneContextQualifier today (C4 keeps it SCV-only); the shared Parquet columns are NULL on those rows.

Does the reorganization affect this? No. The qualifier lives inside the proposition record; the reorg changes only which section the record sits in and the pointer prefix. The record and its id are unchanged.

Timing constraint: (a), (b) and (c) all change SCV proposition records. Under the single-rebuild rule they must be decided before the rebuild in §6, or deferred to a later release that ships forward-only (new releases only, no backfill). Deciding one of them after the backfill would force a second backfill. (a) and (b) are additive or value-only; (c) changes which gene 27,817 propositions name, a semantic change that would need its own announcement.

Resolved (2026-10-18): (a) + (b) in this release, (c) deferred. Implemented in #159 (1.0, SCV proc Step 2), so they ride the single rebuild:

  • (a) every geneContextQualifier carries a geneContextSource extension: submittedSymbolMatches, submittedSymbolDiffers, inferredFromVariant or submittedNotNormalized. Symbols are compared trimmed and case-insensitively, which moves 146 case-only differences (C19ORF12 vs C19orf12) from "differs" to "matches". On 2026-09-28 the counts are 5,781,920 / 27,671 / 881,325 / 4,814, plus 40,849 propositions with no qualifier.
  • (b) the placeholder's name is the submitter's symbol. The 5 multi-symbol placeholders join the symbols with ", " in submitted order. There is still no primaryCoding, and submittedGeneSymbols stays. The submittedNotNormalized value is the not-normalized flag.
  • The shared Parquet schema gains gene_context_source (§4.1); #143 adds it to the four current tables.

items.title: 3.B Content-shared propositions: defer
items.text:
Measured (memory project_proposition_content_dedup, 2026-08-16; and 2026-10-18 notes): VCV and RCV propositions are about 50% exact-content duplicates; SCV dedup tops out at 10–13%. Today no proposition is shared at any level (SCV/VCV/RCV are all 1:1 with statements).

Confirmed in the procs: the incremental VCV/RCV carry-forward recovers the parent accession from the proposition key:

  • gkm-vcv-statement-proc.sql:35 (contract) and :708, :710 — SPLIT(b.key, '-')[OFFSET(0)] decides which baseline rows to carry forward (accession not impacted) and drops rows of removed VCVs;
  • gkm-rcv-statement-proc.sql:38 and :702, :704 — the same for RCVs.

SCV propositions are recomputed globally every release (gkm-scv-statement-proc.sql header, Step 7e), so they do not depend on this parse; the per-SCV outputs parse clinvar.submission: ids instead.

Consequence of content-addressed ids:

  • the VCV/RCV carry-forward breaks: a shared key names no accession, so the merge needs a statement→proposition join and reference counting;
  • delta tombstones need garbage collection: a shared proposition can be deleted only when no statement uses it;
  • the change log sees every proposition key change once (a full churn delta);
  • build-delta-manifest.py assumes "each key encodes its type code"; sub-bundle.py routes propositions by key prefix (SCV/VCV/RCV); the bundle schema's patternProperties is ^(SCV|VCV|RCV).+;
  • consumers that read the level from the id prefix break.

The size win is small: about 2.9 GB uncompressed, 4.7% of the statement+proposition core, less gzipped. Recommendation: defer, as decided on 2026-09-29. The reorganization keeps ids unchanged, so it neither helps nor blocks a later dedup.
path: Proposition Reorganization by Meaning — Implementation Plan

items.title: 3.C Version label
items.text:
ADR 0004 §1: renaming sections is breaking (a MAJOR change). §5 allows breaking fixes in place in the 1.x line until GA, announced rather than RFC'd. #142, #145 and #153 already bump the schema strings to 1.0.2.

Option What it means For Against 1.0.2 in place keep the strings #142 already set no extra bump; matches the "1.0.x line" wording a PATCH must not change valid instances (ADR §1); this renames sections and Parquet tables. §5 speaks of corrective fixes; the reorg is a deliberate redesign 1.1.0 in place under /v1/ bump $ids, schema_version and the bundle schema to 1.1.0 the most honest label available without leaving /v1/ (§4 keys directories by MAJOR); consumers pinning a 1.0.x $id get a clear signal still not strict semver (MINOR should be additive); every 1.0.2 string in #142/#145/#153 must be re-bumped 2.0.0 under /v2/ the post-GA machinery: parallel 1.x line for 6 months, RFC strictly correct contradicts the decision to ship in place now; doubles pipeline and storage for 6 months

Recommendation: 1.1.0, in place under /v1/.

Decided (user, 2026-10-18): 1.1.0, in place under /v1/. Done so far:

  • ADR 0006 (docs/decisions/0006-ship-1.1.0-in-place-under-v1.md) and the 1.1.0 changelog are on #146.
  • The advance and completion notices are drafted in 2026-10-18-1.1.0-announcements.md (not posted).

The original analysis follows.

  • No 1.0.2 tag is cut; the consolidated release is one tag, 1.1.0, on the 1.0 release branch (the branch name stays; it carries the 1.x line).
  • Amend #142's version commit to 1.1.0 before it merges, so #145/#153 inherit it.
  • Record that §5 also covered a deliberate structural change before GA: a short ADR 0006 "Propositions sectioned by meaning" (supersedes the Phase 2 grouping spec) with a one-line note in ADR 0004's consequences.

What must be announced (ADR 0004 §6, §7):

  • Where: a GitHub Discussions Announcements post, the /v1/feed.xml Atom entry (generate-r2-index.sh writes it), release notes, and the CHANGELOG entry (docs/reference/changelog.md). The Google Group is on hold.
  • When: an advance notice with the cutover date before the R2 overwrite, then a completion notice.
  • What:
  • the old → new section and table mapping (§7);
  • the pointer change in every statement and evidence line;
  • the Parquet column renames;
  • schema_version / $id 1.1.0;
  • every published release (4 monthly fulls, 00-latest, 15 deltas, every Parquet set) rewritten in place, so checksums change and earlier downloads should be refreshed;
  • the other data changes riding the same rebuild (A1 HGVS, citations, allele duplicate key, #143, C3, and D).

items.title: 3.D New: normalize VCV object and vcv- set members (found while measuring)
items.text:
Decided (user, 2026-10-18): (i). It is its own PR, #160 (branch fix/uniform-condition-pointers, base 1.0), not part of PR 1–4. The re-wrap is done at emission in gkm-vcv-statement-proc.sql (the three obj_ref builds and the synthetic vcv- set concepts), not in gkm-vcv-proc.sql's condition_ref: the vcv- id digest stays over the bare CURIEs, so no vcv- id changes, and the gkm_vcv_*_agg tables are untouched. On 2026-10-11 it rewrites 7,474,404 VCV propositions and all 94,980 vcv- sets; 0 bare references and 0 dangling pointers remain; the Parquet typed id columns are unchanged. The text below is the original analysis.

The bundle mixes reference forms for the same kind of target:

Where Form Count (2026-10-11) SCV and RCV proposition object #/condition/… or #/conditionSet/… pointer all rows VCV proposition object, single condition bare CURIE clinvar.trait:… / clinvar.traitset:… 7,474,404 of 9,156,181 VCV proposition object, several conditions #/conditionSet/clinvar.conditionset:vcv-… pointer 1,681,777 traitset ConceptSet members #/condition/ pointers 5,345 sets (audit) pipeline vcv- ConceptSet members bare ids 83,538 sets (audit) therapyGroup members #/therapy/ pointers all

Cause: the 1.0.0 submittedCondition de-pointer turned the extension's condition/conditionSet into bare CURIEs. The SCV and RCV consumers re-wrap them into pointers; gkm-vcv-proc.sql (vcv_conditions, condition_ref) does not, so VCV propositions and the synthetic vcv- sets carry them bare. Both validate (a string is a valid iriReference), but the bundle schema's description promises #/<section>/<id> cross- references, and a consumer resolving pointers misses 7.5 M VCV objects.

Options:

  • (i) Normalize now (recommended): in gkm-vcv-proc.sql wrap condition_ref as #/condition/ + clinvar.trait: / #/conditionSet/ + clinvar.traitset: (the same re-wrap the SCV/RCV procs use), and build the vcv- set concepts as #/condition/ pointers. Every VCV row is rewritten in this rebuild anyway, so the marginal cost is the review and the oracle. The Parquet object_id is bare either way; object_type becomes pointer-derived.
  • (ii) Leave as is: the shared Parquet derives object_type from the CURIE prefix as a fallback (§4.2). Document the mixed forms on Joining Tables.

Also found: 4 RCV propositions have no object (all on RCV000001117, since 2026-10-04; 2 Pathogenicity, 2 NotProvided). va-spec requires object, so these fail validation in the published 2026-10-04 delta; the 1.0.1 toolkit gate covered only the 2026-10-11 delta and a full. Trace the cause in the RCV proc (likely an RCV whose condition no longer resolves) before the rebuild, and run the toolkit gate on every published bundle (§6.4).

items.title: 4.1 Columns
items.text:
All four tables have exactly these columns, in this order; non-applicable columns are NULL. Each column cites the bundle path it derives from (user rule: Parquet holds only bundle-derivable values).

Column Type Bundle source Notes id VARCHAR section key (= $.id) unchanged ids type VARCHAR $.type predicate VARCHAR $.predicate subject_variant_id VARCHAR $.subject, pointer stripped was subject_id on varcustom object_id VARCHAR $.object, pointer stripped was object_condition_id / object_tumor_type_id / object_therapy object_type VARCHAR $.object pointer section (CURIE prefix as fallback) condition, conditionSet, therapy, therapyGroup condition_qualifier_id VARCHAR $.conditionQualifier, stripped TherapeuticResponse only gene_context_id VARCHAR 'ncbigene:' ‖ $.geneContextQualifier.primaryCoding.code from #143; NULL on placeholders gene_context_name VARCHAR $.geneContextQualifier.name submitted_gene_symbols VARCHAR[] the submittedGeneSymbols extension on the qualifier from #143 gene_context_source VARCHAR the geneContextSource extension on the qualifier, picked by name from #143 / #159 (decision A) mode_of_inheritance VARCHAR $.modeOfInheritanceQualifier.name germline SCV only penetrance VARCHAR $.penetranceQualifier.name germline SCV only data VARCHAR the whole record, collapse_ext_values applied last, as in every table

There is no tumor-type section. Oncogenicity objects are condition / conditionSet records, so object_type has four values. (vartumor-proposition.object_tumor_type_id was already a condition id.)

items.title: 4.2 The template
items.text:
One schema file replaces the four (parquet-schemas/proposition.sql, with a {SECTION} placeholder that extract_parquet_typed substitutes). The data expression is unchanged from today, so neither strip path moves (audit note 3: BigQuery JSON_STRIP_NULLS drops empty array elements at dict-build time; the assembler's Python strip_empty keeps them; the reorg touches neither).

-- One shared column schema for every proposition section ({SECTION}). Unions the SCV/RCV/VCV dicts.
-- The WHERE calls the canonical section function, which raises on an unmapped type (fail loud).
SELECT
  key AS id,
  JSON_VALUE(value, '$.type') AS type,
  JSON_VALUE(value, '$.predicate') AS predicate,
  REGEXP_REPLACE(JSON_VALUE(value, '$.subject'), r'^#/[^/]+/', '') AS subject_variant_id,
  REGEXP_REPLACE(JSON_VALUE(value, '$.object'), r'^#/[^/]+/', '') AS object_id,
  CASE
    WHEN JSON_VALUE(value, '$.object') IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN STARTS_WITH(JSON_VALUE(value, '$.object'), '#/')
      THEN REGEXP_EXTRACT(JSON_VALUE(value, '$.object'), r'^#/([^/]+)/')
    WHEN STARTS_WITH(JSON_VALUE(value, '$.object'), 'clinvar.trait:') THEN 'condition'
    WHEN STARTS_WITH(JSON_VALUE(value, '$.object'), 'clinvar.traitset:') THEN 'conditionSet'
    ELSE ERROR(FORMAT('unrecognized proposition object: %t', JSON_VALUE(value, '$.object')))
  END AS object_type,
  REGEXP_REPLACE(JSON_VALUE(value, '$.conditionQualifier'), r'^#/[^/]+/', '') AS condition_qualifier_id,
  IF(JSON_VALUE(value, '$.geneContextQualifier.primaryCoding.code') IS NULL, NULL,
     CONCAT('ncbigene:', JSON_VALUE(value, '$.geneContextQualifier.primaryCoding.code'))) AS gene_context_id,
  JSON_VALUE(value, '$.geneContextQualifier.name') AS gene_context_name,
  ARRAY(
    SELECT JSON_VALUE(sym)
    FROM UNNEST(JSON_QUERY_ARRAY(value, '$.geneContextQualifier.extensions')) AS ext,
         UNNEST(JSON_QUERY_ARRAY(ext, '$.value_string')) AS sym WITH OFFSET so
    WHERE JSON_VALUE(ext, '$.name') = 'submittedGeneSymbols'
    ORDER BY so
  ) AS submitted_gene_symbols,
  (
    SELECT JSON_VALUE(ext, '$.value_enum')
    FROM UNNEST(JSON_QUERY_ARRAY(value, '$.geneContextQualifier.extensions')) AS ext
    WHERE JSON_VALUE(ext, '$.name') = 'geneContextSource'
  ) AS gene_context_source,
  JSON_VALUE(value, '$.modeOfInheritanceQualifier.name') AS mode_of_inheritance,
  JSON_VALUE(value, '$.penetranceQualifier.name') AS penetrance,
  collapse_ext_values(TO_JSON_STRING(value)) AS data
FROM (
  SELECT key, value FROM `{DATASET}.gkm_dict_proposition`
  UNION ALL SELECT key, value FROM `{DATASET}.gkm_dict_rcv_proposition`
  UNION ALL SELECT key, value FROM `{DATASET}.gkm_dict_vcv_proposition`
)
WHERE `clinvar_ingest.gkm_proposition_section`(JSON_VALUE(value, '$.type')) = '{SECTION}'
  • 3.D (i) is decided (#160): drop the two CURIE fallback arms so a non-pointer object fails the export.
  • The delta export's .gkm_dict_ → .delta_gkm_dict_ rewrite (export-gkm-dicts.sh:112-118) works unchanged: the template references the three dicts, each with a delta_ counterpart (the invariant comment as corrected by #143 c4cabeb).
  • submitted_gene_symbols is an empty array, not NULL, where there is none (same as #143). Pick one and document it; NULL is easier to test and matches "non-applicable columns are NULL".
  • Row order is unchanged: the Parquet is not sorted, so row-group pruning is as today. Sorted lookups are C1's job (PR #151).

items.title: 6.1 Why a full rebuild
items.text:
The pointer strings live in the stored statement and evidence-line dicts (gkm_dict_scv, gkm_dict_vcv, gkm_dict_rcv, gkm_dict_evidence_line) of every dataset. Every statement changes, so every published bundle and every statement and proposition Parquet file changes. The 1.0.2 patch scripts swapped 14 variation lines per full; they cannot rewrite every statement.

A pointer-only SQL rewrite of the four dict tables in 16 datasets would be cheaper, but A1 (catvar), the citation fix (SCV statement proc), the allele duplicate-key fix and 3.D (VCV proc) need the procs to run anyway. One proc-level rebuild is simpler to reason about and to oracle-gate. Recommendation: full rebuild, the proven #132 / 1.0.1 path.
path: Proposition Reorganization by Meaning — Implementation Plan

items.title: 6.2 Order relative to merging the 1.0 PRs
items.text:
1. Settle every data decision: C (label), 3.A (a)/(b)/(c) or defer, 3.D, E, and any other decision in the master plan that changes data (§9).
  2. Merge into 1.0, in this order (each rebased on the previous; see §9 for conflicts):
  6. fix/allele-duplicate-key (one duplicate allele key in 10-04 / 10-11) — ideally with total-order tie-breakers on the allele ARRAY_AGGs (the 1.0.1 non-determinism follow-up), or the rebuild repeats the 1.0.1 allele oracle exceptions

items.title: 7.2 Querying old and new releases together (DuckDB)
items.text:
Every published release is re-written, so R2 serves only the new layout. Local copies downloaded earlier keep the old one. Because both layouts keep the full record in data, the new shape can be rebuilt from either:

-- New layout (1.1.0 and later): one glob, one schema.
SELECT * FROM read_parquet('proposition*.parquet');

-- Old layout (local copies from before 1.1.0): rebuild the new shape and section from `data`.
CREATE OR REPLACE MACRO bare(p) AS regexp_replace(p, '^#/[^/]+/', '');
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW proposition_old AS
SELECT
  j->>'$.id' AS id, j->>'$.type' AS type, j->>'$.predicate' AS predicate,
  bare(j->>'$.subject') AS subject_variant_id,
  bare(j->>'$.object') AS object_id,
  CASE WHEN j->>'$.object' LIKE '#/%' THEN regexp_extract(j->>'$.object', '^#/([^/]+)/', 1)
       WHEN j->>'$.object' LIKE 'clinvar.trait:%' THEN 'condition'
       WHEN j->>'$.object' LIKE 'clinvar.traitset:%' THEN 'conditionSet' END AS object_type,
  bare(j->>'$.conditionQualifier') AS condition_qualifier_id,
  CASE WHEN j->>'$.geneContextQualifier.primaryCoding.code' IS NOT NULL
       THEN 'ncbigene:' || (j->>'$.geneContextQualifier.primaryCoding.code') END AS gene_context_id,
  j->>'$.geneContextQualifier.name' AS gene_context_name,
  CAST(list_filter(CAST(j->'$.geneContextQualifier.extensions' AS JSON[]),
                   lambda e: e->>'$.name' = 'submittedGeneSymbols')[1]->'$.value' AS VARCHAR[]) AS submitted_gene_symbols,
  list_filter(CAST(j->'$.geneContextQualifier.extensions' AS JSON[]),
              lambda e: e->>'$.name' = 'geneContextSource')[1]->>'$.value' AS gene_context_source,
  j->>'$.modeOfInheritanceQualifier.name' AS mode_of_inheritance,
  j->>'$.penetranceQualifier.name' AS penetrance,
  data,
  CASE WHEN j->>'$.type' = 'VariantPathogenicityProposition' THEN 'propositionPathogenicity'
       WHEN j->>'$.type' = 'VariantOncogenicityProposition' THEN 'propositionOncogenicity'
       WHEN j->>'$.type' LIKE 'Clinvar%' THEN 'propositionClinvarCustom'
       ELSE 'propositionSomaticClinicalImpact' END AS section
FROM (
  SELECT data, data::JSON AS j
  FROM read_parquet(['varcond-proposition.parquet', 'varcustom-proposition.parquet',
                     'vartumor-proposition.parquet', 'vartherapy-proposition.parquet'], union_by_name = true)
);

(Extensions are picked by name: from decision A the qualifier can carry two, so extensions[0] is no longer safe. lambda e: needs DuckDB 1.3 or later. gene_context_source is NULL in releases before #159.) The same expressions reproduce the new tables exactly: they are the §5.2 prototype.

items.title: 10. Risks and open questions
items.text:
Risks

  1. Stale sections on R2. Dated Parquet directories are never wiped, and the index lists sections from the R2 listing. Without PR 4's wipe plus the explicit delete, every release would list eight proposition tables (four dead). Gate: index section lists equal the expected 22.
  2. Allele non-determinism. Independent full rebuilds pick different duplicate-key alleles (1.0.1 follow-up), which reappears as allele oracle failures and spurious allele changes in republished releases unless the tie-breakers land first.
  3. A second rebuild. Any data decision left open (3.A (c), 3.D, E, C1-driven bundle additions) that is taken after the backfill forces another full backfill. Settle them first, or explicitly defer them as forward-only.
  4. Weekly releases in the window. A weekly run from 1.0 after the merges and before the backfill would publish the new layout on top of unpatched history. Pause the weekly runs.
  5. Disk and stalls. About 15 GB free against a 4.8 GB full plus about 12 GB Parquet per monthly set; bq poll hangs seen in 1.0.1. Run one full at a time with a watchdog.
  6. Consumer breakage. Every section, table and three column names change, and every published file is rewritten. The advance announcement and §7 are the mitigation; the stabilization window is the justification.
  7. Schema-invalid records already published. The 4 object-less RCV propositions in the 2026-10-04 delta (§3.D). The all-bundles toolkit gate catches this class; fix the cause before the rebuild.
  8. Version label churn. C = 1.1.0, and three open PRs carried 1.0.2 (now relabelled); a missed string makes $ids or schema_version disagree. Gate: grep -r 1.0.2 schema src = 0 before tagging.

Open questions

  1. ~~C: 1.1.0 (recommended) or 1.0.2?~~ Decided: 1.1.0 (§3.C).
  2. ~~3.A: decide (a)/(b)/(c) before the rebuild, or defer them as forward-only?~~ Resolved: (a) + (b) in this release (#159), (c) deferred.
  3. ~~3.D: normalize VCV objects and vcv- set members now (recommended)?~~ Resolved: (i), PR #160 (fix/uniform-condition-pointers).
  4. E: add proposition_section to the statement Parquet?
  5. submitted_gene_symbols: empty array (as #143) or NULL when absent?
  6. Should the shared schema also carry a derived statement_level (scv/vcv/rcv, from the id prefix)? propositionPathogenicity mixes 27 M rows from three levels; today the level is read from id.
  7. CDN purge: purge everything on the zone, or purge by URL? Either needs CF_PURGE_TOKEN / CF_ZONE_ID.
  8. R2 backup retention for v1/_backup/pre-1.1.0/: how long?

items.title: ClinVar-GKM 1.1.0 rebuild and republish: runbook
items.text:
Status: prepared 2026-10-20, not executed. Every step that deploys, writes to BigQuery, GCS, R2 or Cloudflare, tags or merges is a separate step that the user confirms before it runs. Never touch live R2 without that confirmation. Never print the Cloudflare tokens.

Scope. Rebuild all 17 datasets with the 1.0 release branch (origin/1.0 @ 66e4af7), gate them, and publish them as 1.1.0 (ADR 0006, on PR #146) in the NCBI-style R2 layout (decided 2026-10-20, scripts in PR #182, ADR 0009 on #168): the current line v1/1.1/ gets 4 official monthlies (+ 00-latest), 3 weekly fulls for October (10-04, 10-11, 10-18, + 00-latest_weekly), 16 weekly deltas (October's at deltas/, July–September in deltas/YYYY-MM/) and one Parquet set at parquet/ built from 2026-10-18; the 1.0.1 generation moves from archive/1.0.1/ to the frozen line v1/1.0/; everything else in the bucket is deleted. This runbook replaces §6.3–§6.5 of the proposition reorganization plan where they differ:

Plan §6 assumed Now 16 datasets, 15 deltas 17 datasets (adds clinvar_2026_10_18_v2_6_0), 16 deltas (adds 2026-1018) 5 Parquet sets (4 monthly + latest) 1 latest Parquet set, built from 2026-10-18; the 440 dated Parquet objects (51.8 GB) are deleted Back up all of v1/ (60–89 GB) 1.0.1 bundles are already archived at archive/1.0.1/ (MANIFEST.json); they move to the frozen line v1/1.0/ (no separate backup) Republish /v1/ in place New layout per line (#182): v1/1.1/ (current) and v1/1.0/ (frozen); the old v1/datasets/, v1/deltas/, v1/index.json, v1/feed.xml, v1/README.txt and archive/1.0.1/ are deleted after verify passes Fulls are monthly only A weekly full every release (weekly/, current month only); the official monthly is a copy of its source release's weekly full Advance notice before any R2 write No advance notice (no subscribers yet); completion notice only Re-stamp gkm_pipeline_version on 10-11 Re-stamp the newest dataset, 10-18

The four fulls are unchanged (ADR 0002; re-checked against the ClinVar index on 2026-10-20, §0.13): 2026-07 ← 06-27, 2026-08 ← 08-04, 2026-09 ← 08-29, 2026-10 ← 09-28. ClinVar has not published ClinVarVCVRelease_2026-11 yet.

Weekly run-release.sh runs stay paused until Step 7. The upstream ingest scheduler keeps running, which is fine.

items.title: Gaps found, with proposed fixes
items.text: # Gap Impact Proposed fix (runbook default in bold) G1 run-release.sh has no stop-before-publish option. --dry-run gates only stage 5's R2 writes (it still writes GCS staging and the BigQuery stamp), and --start-step 4 would continue into stage 5 Cannot use it for 10-18 without publishing Do not use run-release.sh. Step 3.2 replays stage 4 by hand: the stamp call, then vrs-to-bq-table.sh. Follow-up: add --no-publish (stop after stage 4) G2 republish-v1.sh DELTAS stopped at 2026-10-11 stage all / upload all would skip the 16th delta Fixed: #181 is merged into #182, which rewrites republish-v1.sh as the migration driver (16 deltas, 3 weekly fulls, LATEST_SOURCE 10-18). Merge #182 into 1.0 before Step 1 (G8) G3 oracle-delta-reconstruction.sh takes one version, so the cross-version pair 08-22 (v2_5_0) → 08-29 (v2_6_0) cannot run One of the 16 pairs is ungated Optional CVER for the compare dataset. Runbook uses a sed shim (§4.4), tested with bash -n G4 No repo tool runs the gkm-toolkit over a full bundle: json.load of a 4.8 GB gzipped full does not fit in 16 GB RAM, and strict validation of variation is slow (measured 23 records/s per core) Plan §6.4 requires all 4 fulls and all deltas Appendix A toolkit-validate-bundle.py: streams the real bundle, validates every record verbatim through validate_bundle_schema, bounded memory, multiprocess. Tested on the live 2026-1011 delta. ~7 h per full on this laptop (4.7 M variation records dominate); ~1–1.5 h on a 64-vCPU VM. Decision D1 G5 No repo tool for the bundle ↔ Parquet gate, and the latest Parquet is built from 10-18, which has no published full Gate cannot run as written Appendix B bundle-parquet-check.py (count, both-direction id sets, sampled data equality, streaming), compared against a reference 10-18 full staged for the check only, never published (§4.7). Tested against the live CDN Parquet G6 No tool for "full + its deltas == next full" on the staged bundles (plan §6.4) Gate cannot run as written The BigQuery delta-reconstruction oracle (§4.4) proves the same property on the tables the bundles are exported from, and the export is deterministic per record. Accept that as the gate (D7), or write a streaming reconstruct-and-compare tool first G7 14 GiB free. release-gkm-parquet.sh downloads every shard before merging, so the Parquet stage peaks at ~26 GB (13 GB shards + 13 GB merged). Four staged fulls are 19.2 GB Parquet cannot be staged locally; fulls only one at a time Free at least 40 GB before Step 4.6 (largest candidates: ~/Downloads 22 GB, ~/Library/Caches 12 GB), and park each validated full in gs://clinvar-gkm/staging/1.1.0/ so only one is local at a time. Follow-up: merge and delete shards one section at a time G8 gate_key = last commit touching src/procedures, src/scripts or src/vrsify of the checkout. Any script fix merged into 1.0 after the stamps (G1–G3 included) changes it Next weekly would rebuild full, and the 10-18 oracles would compare mismatched gates Merge every src/ fix into 1.0 before Step 1. Re-stamp 10-18 from the final 1.0 tip in Step 7 if anything under src/ changed G9 The incremental wrappers fall back to a full build when the baseline and current gate_key differ, so a full-vs-incremental oracle passes trivially False PASS Moot for 1.1.0: Step 3 builds every dataset FULL and no full-vs-incremental oracle is run (option A). check_incr.sh (Appendix D) stays as a reference tool G18 The fallback is silent: the log prints …_incremental either way. The job history shows 07-15, 07-27, 08-29 and 09-13 fell back to full in the 2026-10-01 chain, and so did the normal 10-04 weekly. 07-15 has no diff_* drivers today The weekly incremental path is unproven Option A: 1.1.0 is rebuilt FULL, and weekly runs use --full-procs (#182) until ADR 0007 workstream 3 decides (Step 7). check_incr.sh (Appendix D) detects a fallback from the job history G10 upload-gkm-delta-to-r2.sh set each delta's checkpoint_full to the newest monthly in R2, so every 1.0.1 manifest says 2026-10 Wrong replay start Fixed in #182: checkpoint_full = the newest monthly whose source_release ≤ the delta's baseline_release, and the uploader refuses a baseline that is not the previous delta's release. Checked in §5.5 and §6. The frozen v1/1.0/ manifests keep their 1.0.1 bytes (README documents the right mapping) G15 run-release.sh r2_latest_published_month listed the bucket-root datasets/ (deleted 2026-10-13), so the monthly trigger never fired A weekly run would never publish a monthly Fixed in #182 (lists the line, incl. archive/YYYY/) G16 Cleanup (§5.11) deletes every path the docs and the R2 browser used to read (v1/datasets/, v1/deltas/, v1/index.json) Broken docs links and console until the docs move Docs #146/#168 merged and deployed before §5.11 (they read the new shapes) G17 archive/1.0.1/README.txt (public) says nothing there will ever be changed or deleted; the plan moves it to v1/1.0/ Contradicts a published promise User decision (2026-10-20) to move it; v1/1.0/README.txt states the move and the freeze G11 The bundle schema $id https://w3id.org/clingen/schema/clinvar-gkm/<v>/json/ClinvarGkmBundle resolves to 404: the file is schema/clinvar-gkm/clinvar-gkm-bundle.schema.json. Same for 1.0.1 Pre-existing; validators use a local registry Follow-up issue (emit json/ClinvarGkmBundle or change the $id); not a blocker G12 The provenance stamp (audit_stamp) of each dataset feeds every delta manifest's pipeline_version; today they read e.g. 1.0-rc3-2-g773a43a Stale provenance in republished manifests Step 3 re-stamps each dataset just before its rebuild, as run-release.sh does (D2) G13 Upstream ingest will create the next weekly dataset (~2026-10-25), and ClinVar's 2026-11 monthly lands ~2026-11-04 An 18th dataset, or a fifth full, enters scope Finish Step 5 before the 2026-11 monthly; a 10-25 dataset is built after cutover by the normal weekly run G14 No bulk re-extract command for examples/ Manual Loop in §4.9

items.title: Decisions needed before Step 1
items.text:
• D1 — gkm-toolkit on the four fulls. (A, recommended) run Appendix A on a GCE VM (n2-highcpu-64, ~1–1.5 h per full, ~$10–15 total) reading the staged fulls from gs://clinvar-gkm/staging/1.1.0/; (B) run it on this laptop (~7 h per full, ~30 h total, in the background); (C) validate the 2026-07 full plus all 16 deltas and rely on the delta-reconstruction oracle for the rest. All 16 deltas are validated on the laptop in every option.
  • D2 — Provenance. Re-stamp each dataset before its rebuild (default). Optionally tag 1.1.0-rc1 on the 1.0 tip first, so the stamps and manifests read 1.1.0-rc1 instead of 1.0.1-65-g66e4af7.
  • D3 — 1.0.1 delta-oracle exceptions. The allele cross-version SPDI gap (08-22 → 08-29) and the 09-13 → 09-23 non-determinism were accepted for 1.0.1. The total-order fix (e0fe8e9) and the allele de-duplication should clear the second; re-accept or fix any residue explicitly.
  • D4 — checkpoint_full (G10): resolved by #182 (correct per delta).
  • D5 — Snapshot retention. Default: snapshots expire on their own after 30 days (SNAP_EXPIRES).
  • D6 — Examples source. Default: re-extract from the rebuilt 2026-10-04 (as d0fbe2a did), so file names keep their accession versions; 10-18 would rename several.
  • D7 — Bundle-level reconstruction (G6): accept the BigQuery oracle (default) or build the tool first.
  • D8 — Disk (G7): free ≥ 40 GB on this laptop (default) or stage on a VM.

items.title: 0.1 Release worktree and environment
items.text:
• [ ] Create a clean, detached worktree of origin/1.0 and the environment file every later step sources.
REPO=$HOME/Development/gks/clinvar-gks
git -C "$REPO" fetch origin --tags
git -C "$REPO" worktree add --detach "$HOME/Development/gks/clinvar-gks.worktrees/release-1.1.0" origin/1.0
WT=$HOME/Development/gks/clinvar-gks.worktrees/release-1.1.0
git -C "$WT" submodule update --init submodules/va-spec
RB=$HOME/clinvar-gkm-1.1.0
mkdir -p "$RB/logs" "$RB/tools" "$RB/stage"
cat > "$RB/env.sh" <<EOF
export CLOUDSDK_CORE_PROJECT=clingen-dev PROJECT_ID=clingen-dev
export REPO=$REPO WT=$WT RB=$RB
export STAGE_DIR=$RB/stage
export LATEST_SOURCE="2026-10-18 v2_6_0"
export GCS_STAGE=gs://clinvar-gkm/staging/1.1.0
export SNAP_EXPIRES="2026-11-20 00:00:00 UTC"
# date:version for all 17 datasets, oldest first (rebuild order)
export ALL="2026-06-27:v2_5_0 2026-07-06:v2_5_0 2026-07-15:v2_5_0 2026-07-20:v2_5_0 2026-07-27:v2_5_0 2026-08-04:v2_5_0 2026-08-08:v2_5_0 2026-08-16:v2_5_0 2026-08-22:v2_5_0 2026-08-29:v2_6_0 2026-09-05:v2_6_0 2026-09-13:v2_6_0 2026-09-23:v2_6_0 2026-09-28:v2_6_0 2026-10-04:v2_6_0 2026-10-11:v2_6_0 2026-10-18:v2_6_0"
export EXISTING="\${ALL% 2026-10-18:v2_6_0}"
ds() { local d="\${1%%:*}" v="\${1##*:}"; echo "clinvar_\${d//-/_}_\${v}"; }
EOF
source "$RB/env.sh"
git -C "$WT" log --oneline -1; git -C "$WT" status --porcelain; git -C "$WT" describe --tags --always --dirty

Expect: HEAD is the 1.0 tip (66e4af7 today, later if gap fixes land); status --porcelain prints nothing; describe has no -dirty. Stop if the worktree is dirty or HEAD is not origin/1.0.

items.title: 0.2 Auth
items.text:
• [ ] gcloud auth list; bq ls --max_results=1 >/dev/null && echo bq-ok; gsutil ls gs://clinvar-gkm/2026-10-18/dev/

Expect: the active account is yours; bq-ok; three objects (vi.jsonl.gz, vi-normalized-no-liftover.jsonl.gz, …pre-retry.jsonl.gz). Stop if any command fails.

items.title: 0.3 Datasets and tables
items.text:
• [ ] Inventory the 17 datasets.
source "$RB/env.sh"
q=""; for s in $ALL; do D=$(ds $s); q="$q${q:+ UNION ALL }SELECT '$D' ds, COUNTIF(STARTS_WITH(table_name,'gkm_dict_') AND NOT ENDS_WITH(table_name,'__pre110')) dict, COUNTIF(STARTS_WITH(table_name,'delta_gkm_') AND NOT ENDS_WITH(table_name,'__pre110')) delta, COUNTIF(STARTS_WITH(table_name,'diff_')) diff, COUNTIF(table_name IN ('gkm_change_log','gkm_pipeline_version','gkm_vrs','single_gene_variation','variation_vrs_changed')) core, COUNTIF(ENDS_WITH(table_name,'__pre110')) snaps FROM \`$D.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES\`"; done
bq query --use_legacy_sql=false --format=pretty --max_rows=100 "$q ORDER BY ds"

Expect: 17 rows; existing 16: dict=21 delta=22 snaps=0, core ≥ 4; 10-18: dict=0 delta=0 diff=14, core=2 (single_gene_variation, variation_vrs_changed). 06-27 and 07-15 show diff=0 (also true before the 1.0.1 rebuild, which succeeded; full builds do not need them). Stop if a dataset is missing or an existing one lacks a dict table.

items.title: 0.4 single_gene_variation carries symbol / hgnc_id (#178 fails loudly without them)
items.text:
• [ ] Check both columns in all 17.
source "$RB/env.sh"
q=""; for s in $ALL; do D=$(ds $s); q="$q${q:+ UNION ALL }SELECT '$D' ds, COUNT(*) n, COUNTIF(symbol IS NOT NULL) n_symbol, COUNTIF(hgnc_id IS NOT NULL) n_hgnc FROM \`$D.single_gene_variation\`"; done
bq query --use_legacy_sql=false --format=pretty --max_rows=100 "$q ORDER BY ds"

Expect: 17 rows, n_symbol = n_hgnc = n (4.49 M – 4.65 M). Stop if the query errors (a missing column) or any count is 0.

items.title: 0.5 10-18 VRS output and changed set
items.text:
• [ ] Confirm the VRS file matches the changed set.
gsutil cat gs://clinvar-gkm/2026-10-18/dev/vi-normalized-no-liftover.jsonl.gz | gunzip -c | wc -l
bq query --use_legacy_sql=false --format=csv "SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM clinvar_2026_10_18_v2_6_0.variation_vrs_changed) changed, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM clinvar_2026_10_18_v2_6_0.variation_vrs_removed) removed, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM clinvar_2026_10_11_v2_6_0.gkm_vrs) vrs_1011"

Expect: 43868; changed=43868 removed=5 vrs_1011=4687256. Stop if the line count differs from changed: vrs-to-bq-table.sh would then do a full replace of gkm_vrs with only the changed subset.

items.title: 0.6 Cloud Run job
items.text:
• [ ] gcloud run jobs describe vrs-to-vi-location-transformer --region us-east1 --project clingen-dev --format='value(metadata.name,status.conditions[0].status)'

Expect: vrs-to-vi-location-transformer True. Stop if not found.

items.title: 0.7 R2 (list only)
items.text:
• [ ] List the bucket, v1/ and the archive.
bash -c 'r2() { aws --endpoint-url https://09208aa33790838db213a21f630c33e7.r2.cloudflarestorage.com --profile r2 "$@"; }
r2 s3 ls s3://clinvar-gkm/
r2 s3 ls s3://clinvar-gkm/v1/ --recursive | awk "{n++; s+=\$3} END {printf \"v1: %d objects, %.1f GB\n\", n, s/1e9}"
r2 s3 ls s3://clinvar-gkm/archive/1.0.1/ --recursive | awk "{n++; s+=\$3} END {printf \"archive: %d objects, %.1f GB\n\", n, s/1e9}"'

Expect: PRE archive/, PRE v1/, index.json; v1: 502 objects, 89.1 GB; archive: 42 objects, 24.3 GB. Stop if access is denied.

items.title: 0.8 Cloudflare tokens (verify only, never printed)
items.text:
• [ ] Verify each token with /user/tokens/verify; the token goes to curl on stdin, never on the command line.
bash <<'EOF'
F="$HOME/.config/clinvar-gkm/cloudflare.env"
( set +x; . "$F"
  for v in CF_PURGE_TOKEN CF_WAF_TOKEN CF_CACHE_TOKEN CF_ANALYTICS_TOKEN; do
    tok="${!v:-}"; [[ -n "$tok" ]] || { echo "$v: NOT SET"; continue; }
    printf 'url = "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/user/tokens/verify"\nheader = "Authorization: Bearer %s"\n' "$tok" \
      | curl -sS --max-time 20 -K - \
      | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(sys.argv[1]+":", (d.get("result") or {}).get("status") or d.get("errors"))' "$v"
  done
  [[ -n "${CF_ZONE_ID:-}" ]] && echo "CF_ZONE_ID: set" || echo "CF_ZONE_ID: NOT SET" )
EOF

Expect: four active lines and CF_ZONE_ID: set. Stop if CF_PURGE_TOKEN is not active (Step 5.8 needs it).

items.title: 0.9 Disk
items.text:
• [ ] df -h "$HOME" | tail -1

Expect: at least 40 GB available before §4.6 (decision D8). Today: 14 GiB. Steps 1–4.5 need no local disk.

items.title: 0.10 Scripts parse
items.text:
• [ ] cd "$WT" && for f in src/scripts/*.sh src/vrsify/vrsify.sh; do bash -n "$f" || echo "FAIL $f"; done; python3 -m py_compile src/scripts/*.py && echo py-ok

items.title: 0.11 Procs dry-run
items.text:
• [ ] Dry-run the 10 files Step 1 deploys (a dry run creates nothing).

for f in gkm-proposition-section-func gkm-catvar-proc gkm-scv-condition-proc gkm-scv-statement-proc gkm-rcv-proc gkm-rcv-statement-proc gkm-vcv-proc gkm-vcv-statement-proc gkm-change-log-proc variation-identity-proc; do

items.title: 0.12 Tools and venv
items.text:
• [ ] Create the tool venv and write Appendices A–C into $RB/tools/ (copy each block verbatim).
source "$RB/env.sh"
python3 -m venv "$RB/venv" && "$RB/venv/bin/pip" install -q 'ga4gh.gkm==0.4.0' ijson duckdb orjson
"$RB/venv/bin/python" -c 'import ga4gh.gkm.bundles.schema_validation, ijson, duckdb; print("tools-ok", ijson.backend)'
# then: $RB/tools/toolkit-validate-bundle.py (Appendix A), $RB/tools/bundle-parquet-check.py (Appendix B),
