items.title: 0.13 Monthly mapping (ADR 0002)
items.text:
• [ ] Read ClinVar's monthly index.
curl -sf --max-time 60 https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pub/clinvar/xml/ | sed -E 's/<[^>]+>/ /g' | tr -s ' ' \
  | awk '$1 ~ /^ClinVarVCVRelease_[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}\.xml\.gz$/ {print substr($1,19,7), $3, $4}' | sort -u | tail -5

Expect: 2026-07 2026-07-02, 2026-08 2026-08-06, 2026-09 2026-09-03, 2026-10 2026-10-01, and no 2026-11. The newest GKM dataset strictly before each date is 06-27, 08-04, 08-29, 09-28. Stop if 2026-11 has appeared: add a fifth full (from the newest dataset before its date) to FULLS in republish-v1.sh.

items.title: 0.14 Version-string gate (ADR 0006)
items.text:
• [ ] cd "$WT" && grep -rln '1\.0\.2' schema/clinvar-gkm src | wc -l

Expect: 0.

items.title: 1. Deploy (BigQuery clinvar_ingest; user-confirmed)
items.text: Prerequisite: every src/ fix you want in this release (G2, optionally G1/G3) is merged into 1.0, and §0.1 is re-run so $WT is on that tip (G8).

items.title: 1.1 Section UDF first
items.text:
• [ ] source "$RB/env.sh"; cd "$WT" && bq query --use_legacy_sql=false < src/procedures/gkm-proposition-section-func.sql
  • [ ] Check: bq query --use_legacy_sql=false --format=csv "SELECT clinvar_ingest.gkm_proposition_section('VariantPathogenicityProposition'), clinvar_ingest.gkm_proposition_section('ClinvarUndefinedProposition')"

Expect: propositionPathogenicity,propositionClinvarCustom. Stop if the function is missing (every statement proc calls it).

items.title: 1.2 Changed procs
items.text:
The exact set, from git diff --stat 1.0.1 origin/1.0 -- src/procedures and confirmed against INFORMATION_SCHEMA.ROUTINES (each file re-creates its _build, _proc and _proc_incremental procedures): gkm-catvar-proc.sql, gkm-scv-condition-proc.sql, gkm-scv-statement-proc.sql, gkm-rcv-proc.sql, gkm-rcv-statement-proc.sql, gkm-vcv-proc.sql, gkm-vcv-statement-proc.sql, gkm-change-log-proc.sql, variation-identity-proc.sql. variation-identity-proc.sql (total-order fix e0fe8e9) does not affect this rebuild, which does not rebuild variation_identity; it is deployed so the next weekly uses it. Optional: gkm-scv-changed-proc.sql (comment-only drift).

  • [ ] Deploy in dependency order.
source "$RB/env.sh"; cd "$WT"
for f in gkm-catvar-proc gkm-scv-condition-proc gkm-scv-statement-proc gkm-rcv-proc gkm-rcv-statement-proc gkm-vcv-proc gkm-vcv-statement-proc gkm-change-log-proc variation-identity-proc; do
  echo "== $f"; bq query --use_legacy_sql=false --quiet < "src/procedures/$f.sql" || { echo "STOP: $f failed"; break; }
done
  • [ ] Verify every deployed body now equals origin/1.0.
source "$RB/env.sh"; cd "$WT"
bq query --use_legacy_sql=false --format=json --max_rows=500 "SELECT routine_name, routine_definition FROM \`clingen-dev.clinvar_ingest.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.ROUTINES\`" > "$RB/logs/routines.json"
python3 - "$RB/logs/routines.json" <<'PY'
import glob, json, re, sys
norm = lambda s: re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s or "").strip()
files = {f: norm(open(f).read()) for f in glob.glob("src/procedures/*.sql")}
bad = []
for r in json.load(open(sys.argv[1])):
    n = r["routine_name"]
    hit = [f for f, t in files.items() if re.search(r"CREATE (OR REPLACE )?(TEMP )?(PROCEDURE|FUNCTION|TABLE FUNCTION) `?clinvar_ingest\." + re.escape(n) + r"`?\s*\(", t)]
    if hit and not any(norm(r["routine_definition"]) in files[f] for f in hit):
        bad.append(n)
print("differ from origin/1.0:", bad or "none")
PY

Expect: differ from origin/1.0: ['gkm_scv_changed'] (comment only) or none. Stop if any other routine is listed.

items.title: 2. Snapshots (16 existing datasets; user-confirmed)
items.text:
A CREATE SNAPSHOT TABLE … CLONE is metadata-only and free to create; it then bills the bytes the rebuild replaces (~3.4–3.6 GiB physical / ~35–80 GiB logical per dataset; about $1–12 a month for all 16, depending on the dataset billing model). They expire on their own at SNAP_EXPIRES (D5). 10-18 has nothing to snapshot.

Exact table list, the same for each of the 16 datasets (45 tables): the 21 dicts that the expected-diff gate compares, plus gkm_pipeline_version (provenance, re-stamped in Step 3), gkm_change_log and the 22 delta_gkm_* tables (so a rollback restores the published deltas too).

  • gkm_dict_sequence_reference, gkm_dict_location, gkm_dict_allele, gkm_dict_copy_number_count, gkm_dict_copy_number_change, gkm_dict_gene, gkm_dict_submitter, gkm_dict_therapy, gkm_dict_therapygroup, gkm_dict_proposition, gkm_dict_vcv_proposition, gkm_dict_rcv_proposition, gkm_dict_variation, gkm_dict_condition, gkm_dict_condition_set, gkm_dict_evidence_line, gkm_dict_vcv_evidence_line, gkm_dict_rcv_evidence_line, gkm_dict_scv, gkm_dict_vcv, gkm_dict_rcv
  • gkm_pipeline_version, gkm_change_log

  • delta_ + each of the 21 dict names above, and delta_gkm_scv_condition_sets

  • [ ] Create the snapshots, one dataset per statement batch.

source "$RB/env.sh"
DICTS="gkm_dict_sequence_reference gkm_dict_location gkm_dict_allele gkm_dict_copy_number_count gkm_dict_copy_number_change gkm_dict_gene gkm_dict_submitter gkm_dict_therapy gkm_dict_therapygroup gkm_dict_proposition gkm_dict_vcv_proposition gkm_dict_rcv_proposition gkm_dict_variation gkm_dict_condition gkm_dict_condition_set gkm_dict_evidence_line gkm_dict_vcv_evidence_line gkm_dict_rcv_evidence_line gkm_dict_scv gkm_dict_vcv gkm_dict_rcv"
SNAP_TABLES="$DICTS gkm_pipeline_version gkm_change_log $(for t in $DICTS gkm_scv_condition_sets; do printf 'delta_%s ' "$t"; done)"
for s in $EXISTING; do
  D=$(ds "$s"); q=""
  for t in $SNAP_TABLES; do
    q="${q}CREATE SNAPSHOT TABLE \`${D}.${t}__pre110\` CLONE \`${D}.${t}\` OPTIONS (expiration_timestamp = TIMESTAMP '${SNAP_EXPIRES}');
"
  done
  bq query --use_legacy_sql=false --quiet "$q" >/dev/null && echo "$D: snapshots created" || { echo "STOP: $D"; break; }
done
  • [ ] Verify: 45 snapshots in each of the 16.
source "$RB/env.sh"
q=""; for s in $EXISTING; do D=$(ds $s); q="$q${q:+ UNION ALL }SELECT '$D' ds, COUNTIF(table_type='SNAPSHOT' AND ENDS_WITH(table_name,'__pre110')) snaps FROM \`$D.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES\`"; done
bq query --use_legacy_sql=false --format=csv --max_rows=100 "$q ORDER BY ds"

Expect: 16 rows, snaps=45. Stop if any row is short; do not start Step 3 without snapshots.

Rollback (any dataset, if needed): CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE \.` CLONE `.__pre110`` for each of the 45 tables. Nothing in R2 changes before Step 5, so a BigQuery rollback is complete on its own.

items.title: 3. Rebuild (BigQuery; date order; user-confirmed): 17 full builds
items.text:
Decision (2026-10-21, option A): every dataset is rebuilt FULL. The incremental path is not used for 1.1.0: the job history shows it falling back to full without saying so (G18), and ADR 0007 workstream 3 will decide whether to retire it.

Each gkm_change_log still diffs against the previous dataset, which by then is the rebuilt one. So the order is strict: 06-27 first, 10-18 last. A full build has no other dependency on its neighbours.

Measured per dataset (region-us.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS_BY_PROJECT: the 10-11 full rebuild of 2026-10-13 and the 2026-10-11 full chain):

  • ~13–15 min of procs, ~0.20 TiB billed (~$1.25), ~13.5–16.5 slot-h;
  • the first dataset, 06-27, is lighter: ~0.13 TiB, its change log has no GKM predecessor.

No dataset_diff_on for 07-15. 07-15 has no diff_* tables, but the full path does not need them:

  • they are read only by the incremental guards and by gkm_scv_changed / gkm_rcvvcv_changed;
  • those two take an "everything changed" fallback when drivers are missing, and their changed sets only filter incremental builds;
  • gkm_change_log and gkm_delta_build never read diff_*;
  • 07-15 built FULL successfully without them in the 2026-10-11 full chain.

items.title: 3.0 Stamp values
items.text:
• [ ] Compute the stamp once, from the clean $WT, and write the stamping helper.
source "$RB/env.sh"; cd "$WT"
git fetch origin -q; test "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = "$(git rev-parse origin/1.0)" || echo "STOP: WT is not origin/1.0"
AUDIT=$(git describe --tags --always --dirty); GATE=$(git log -1 --format=%H -- src/procedures src/scripts src/vrsify)
case "$AUDIT" in *dirty*|*\'*) echo "STOP: bad audit stamp $AUDIT";; esac
printf 'export AUDIT=%s GATE=%s\n' "$AUDIT" "$GATE" | tee -a "$RB/env.sh"
cat > "$RB/tools/step3.sh" <<'EOF'
# sourced: stamp a dataset (as run-release.sh does before stage 4), then build it FULL
stamp() { bq query --use_legacy_sql=false --quiet "CALL \`clinvar_ingest.gkm_pipeline_version\`(DATE '$1', '$AUDIT', '$GATE')" >/dev/null; }
rebuild() {   # <date> [vrs-to-bq start step, default 3]
  local d="$1"
  stamp "$d" || { echo "STOP: stamp $d"; return 1; }
  ( set -o pipefail; GKS_FULL=true "$WT/src/scripts/vrs-to-bq-table.sh" "$d" "${2:-3}" 2>&1 | tee "$RB/logs/rebuild-$d.log" ) \
    || { echo "STOP: build $d"; return 1; }
  grep -q 'All steps completed successfully' "$RB/logs/rebuild-$d.log" || { echo "STOP: $d log incomplete"; return 1; }
}
EOF

Expect: AUDIT=1.0.1-… (or 1.1.0-rc1 with D2's tag, or a later tip); GATE= a 40-hex commit.

items.title: 3.1 The 16 existing datasets, 06-27 … 10-11
items.text:
rebuild runs vrs-to-bq-table.sh <date> 3 with GKS_FULL=true, which calls, in order:

  1. gkm_catvar_proc;
  2. gkm_scv_changed;
  3. gkm_scv_condition_proc;
  4. gkm_scv_statement_proc;
  5. gkm_rcvvcv_changed;
  6. gkm_rcv_proc;
  7. gkm_rcv_statement_proc;
  8. gkm_vcv_proc;
  9. gkm_vcv_statement_proc;
  10. gkm_change_log;

  11. gkm_delta_build.

  12. [ ] Canary: 2026-06-27 alone, then inspect its log.

  13. [ ] The other 15, in order (run the loop, or one date at a time).
source "$RB/env.sh" "$RB/tools/step3.sh"
rebuild 2026-06-27                     # canary
for s in ${EXISTING#2026-06-27:v2_5_0 }; do rebuild "${s%%:*}" || break; done

Expect (each): the log shows the (FULL, --full requested) wrappers for catvar, scv-condition, scv-statement, rcv, rcv-statement, vcv and vcv-statement, and ends with ✅ All steps completed successfully for <date>. Stop if any proc fails: fix it, then re-run that date. Each proc is CREATE OR REPLACE, so re-running a date is safe. Continue from that date and never skip one: the next date's change log diffs against it.

items.title: 3.2 2026-10-18 (new dataset, full chain)
items.text:
Stages 0–3 (diff, variation_identity, export, vrsify) are done. This replays run-release.sh stage 4 without stage 5 (G1). The Cloud Run transform comes first, with a check before the load.

  • [ ] Stamp, then run the Cloud Run transform.
source "$RB/env.sh" "$RB/tools/step3.sh"
stamp 2026-10-18
gcloud run jobs execute vrs-to-vi-location-transformer --project clingen-dev --region us-east1 --wait \
  --args gs://clinvar-gkm/2026-10-18/dev/vi-normalized-no-liftover.jsonl.gz \
  --args gs://clinvar-gkm/2026-10-18/dev/vi-final.jsonl.gz
gsutil cat gs://clinvar-gkm/2026-10-18/dev/vi-final.jsonl.gz | gunzip -c | wc -l

Expect: the execution succeeds (~1 min); 43868. Stop if the count is not 43,868 (the gkm_vrs load is incremental: staging must equal the changed set).

  • [ ] Load gkm_vrs and build the procs FULL (vrs-to-bq-table.sh from step 2; GKS_FULL affects only the procs).
source "$RB/env.sh" "$RB/tools/step3.sh"
rebuild 2026-10-18 2
bq query --use_legacy_sql=false --format=csv "SELECT COUNT(*) gkm_vrs_1018 FROM clinvar_2026_10_18_v2_6_0.gkm_vrs"

Expect:

  • the log says Incremental: carry forward clinvar_2026_10_11_v2_6_0.gkm_vrs + merge 43868 changed rows (the gkm_vrs load), then the (FULL, --full requested) proc wrappers;
  • it ends with ✅ All steps completed successfully for 2026-10-18.;
  • gkm_vrs_1018 ≈ 4,691,8xx (4,687,256 + 4,576 new − ≤5 removed).

Stop if the log says Full replace, or the count is far below 4.6 M: gkm_vrs would hold only the changed subset. Re-run from step 2 after fixing the mismatch.

Step 3 total: 17 builds, ~3.7–4.3 h, ~3.3–3.6 TiB (0.13 + 16 × ~0.20–0.21).

items.title: 4. Gates (all must pass before any R2 write)
items.text: BigQuery cost for §4.1, 4.2 and 4.4: ~2.6 TiB (~$16). Run the BigQuery gates on all 17 datasets before staging anything.

items.title: 4.1 Reference integrity and bare references (every dataset)
items.text:
• [ ] validate-proposition-conformance.sh on all 17 (structure, section reference integrity, coverage, and the hard bare-reference check; exits non-zero on any *_BAD or bare id).
source "$RB/env.sh"
for s in $ALL; do d="${s%%:*}"; v="${s##*:}"
  "$WT/src/scripts/validate-proposition-conformance.sh" "$d" "$v" > "$RB/logs/conformance-$d.log" 2>&1 \
    && echo "$d PASS" || { echo "$d FAIL (see $RB/logs/conformance-$d.log)"; }
done

Expect: 17 × PASS: every *_BAD column 0 (leftover_old_ref_BAD, unparsed_ref_BAD, dangling_ref_BAD, misrouted_ref_BAD, structure, conceptType) and bare_BAD 0. Stop if any dataset fails.

items.title: 4.2 Expected-diff against the snapshots (16 datasets)
items.text:
$RB/tools/expected_diff.sh (Appendix C) joins <t>__pre110 to <t> on the primary key for all 21 dicts and classifies every row that differs. pointer-section-only means the rows are equal once proposition pointers are normalized (#/var*-proposition/… and #/proposition*/… → #/P/…); (order-only) means the changed columns are equal after canonical (order-insensitive) comparison; otherwise it lists the changed top-level columns (dicts with key/value compare inside value). Cost: ~79 GB scanned per dataset (~1.2 TiB, ~$7, for 16).

  • [ ] Run it.
source "$RB/env.sh"
for s in $EXISTING; do D=$(ds $s); "$RB/tools/expected_diff.sh" "$D" > "$RB/logs/expected-diff-$D.csv" || echo "STOP: $D"; done
cat "$RB/logs"/expected-diff-*.csv | awk -F, '{print $1","$2}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -k2   # signature x dataset count

Expected-change classes (any other signature, or ADDED/REMOVED outside the rows below, is a stop):

Table Allowed signatures Cause gkm_dict_scv pointer-section-only; reportedIn (citations); (order-only) reorg; fix/scv-citations; total order gkm_dict_vcv, gkm_dict_rcv pointer-section-only; (order-only) reorg gkm_dict_evidence_line pointer-section-only (targetProposition) reorg gkm_dict_vcv_evidence_line, gkm_dict_rcv_evidence_line none, or (order-only) (they point at statements, not propositions) gkm_dict_proposition geneContextQualifier (geneContextSource, placeholder name, trimmed/ordered submittedGeneSymbols); (order-only) #159 / #179 / #178 (3.A) gkm_dict_vcv_proposition object (bare CURIE → #/condition/… / #/conditionSet/…; ~7.47 M on 10-11); (order-only) 3.D (#160) gkm_dict_rcv_proposition none, or (order-only); the 4 object-less RCV000001117 propositions (from 10-04) if fixed 3.D note gkm_dict_condition_set concepts on vcv- sets (bare ids → #/condition/…; all ~95 K vcv- sets); (order-only); no ADDED/REMOVED (vcv- ids are unchanged) 3.D gkm_dict_condition name / primaryCoding / aliases / mappings (condition names); (order-only) condition-name fix; total order gkm_dict_variation extensions on the 14 A1 hgvs.? ids (where present in that dataset); (order-only) A1 (#145); total order gkm_dict_allele the duplicate key only (09-23 onward): one REMOVED / changed row per duplicate allele de-duplication gkm_dict_location, gkm_dict_gene, gkm_dict_submitter, gkm_dict_sequence_reference, gkm_dict_copy_number_*, gkm_dict_therapy* none, or (order-only); location only if C3 (#150) changed stored values C3; total order

(order-only) rows are the determinism fix (e0fe8e9). For reference, the same query between the published 10-04 and 10-11 (no rebuild) already shows 1,101 (order-only) rows in gkm_dict_condition. Record the per-table counts in the PR/Release notes.

items.title: 4.3 Full-vs-incremental oracles: not run for 1.1.0
items.text: Every dataset is built FULL (Step 3, option A), so there is no incremental build to compare. Correctness of the published chain is gated by §4.4: every delta reconstructs the next full, on all 16 pairs.

items.title: 4.4 Delta-reconstruction oracle (all 16 pairs)
items.text:
baseline minus deletes minus delta keys, plus the delta, must equal the compare full on all 21 tables.

  • [ ] Run the 15 same-version pairs, and the cross-version pair with the CVER shim (G3).
source "$RB/env.sh"; cd "$WT"
set -- $ALL; prev="$1"; shift
for cur in "$@"; do
  b="${prev%%:*}"; bv="${prev##*:}"; c="${cur%%:*}"; cv="${cur##*:}"
  if [ "$bv" = "$cv" ]; then
    ./src/scripts/oracle-delta-reconstruction.sh "$b" "$c" "$bv" > "$RB/logs/recon-$c.log" 2>&1
  else   # 2026-08-22 (v2_5_0) -> 2026-08-29 (v2_6_0)
    CVER="$cv" bash <(sed -e 's|^CDS="clinvar_${COMP//-/_}_${VER}"$|CDS="clinvar_${COMP//-/_}_${CVER:-$VER}"|' \
                          -e 's|^RECON="clinvar_${COMP//-/_}_${VER}_recon"$|RECON="${CDS}_recon"|' \
                          src/scripts/oracle-delta-reconstruction.sh) "$b" "$c" "$bv" > "$RB/logs/recon-$c.log" 2>&1
  fi
  printf '%s -> %s: %s\n' "$b" "$c" "$(tail -1 "$RB/logs/recon-$c.log")"
  prev="$cur"
done

Expect: 16 × PASSED delta reconstruction oracle: all sections 0,0,0. Stop if any pair fails, unless the user explicitly re-accepts it (D3); record any accepted residue (table, counts) in the Release notes.

items.title: 4.5 Disk check before staging
items.text:
• [ ] df -h "$HOME" | tail -1 and du -sh "$STAGE_DIR"

Expect: ≥ 40 GB available (D8). Stop if not: free space first, or move §4.6–4.8 to a VM.

items.title: 4.6 Stage the 16 deltas and the 4 fulls (no upload)
items.text:
release-gkm*.sh --no-upload export to GCS (gkm-dicts/, gkm-deltas/), assemble into $STAGE_DIR, and keep the artifacts. They share the GCS prefixes, so run them one at a time. Each full is validated (§4.8), its sha256 recorded, and parked in $GCS_STAGE before the next is staged (G7). Per item (plan §6.6): a full ~1.5–2.5 h, a delta ~15–30 min; ~0.8 TiB billed in total.

  • [ ] Deltas (16; ~0.6 GB in total, kept locally until Step 5).

republish-v1.sh stage all would stage the four fulls first, and they do not fit on disk together (G7), so stage the deltas with their own script:

source "$RB/env.sh"; cd "$WT"
for s in ${ALL#2026-06-27:v2_5_0 }; do d="${s%%:*}"; v="${s##*:}"
  ( set -o pipefail; ./src/scripts/release-gkm-delta.sh "$d" "$v" --no-upload 2>&1 | tee "$RB/logs/stage-delta-$d.log" ) || { echo "STOP: $d"; break; }
done
ls -l "$STAGE_DIR"/clinvar-gkm-delta-*.json.gz | wc -l; ls -l "$STAGE_DIR"/clinvar-gkm-delta-*-manifest.json | wc -l

Expect: 16 and 16. (With G2 merged, ./src/scripts/republish-v1.sh stage 2026-10-18 works too.)

  • [ ] Fulls, one at a time: stage → §4.8 validation → sha256 → park in GCS → delete locally.
source "$RB/env.sh"; cd "$WT"
for spec in "2026-07 2026-06-27" "2026-08 2026-08-04" "2026-09 2026-08-29" "2026-10 2026-09-28"; do
  set -- $spec; label=$1; d=$2; f="$STAGE_DIR/clinvar-gkm-$d.json.gz"
  ( set -o pipefail; ./src/scripts/republish-v1.sh stage "$label" 2>&1 | tee "$RB/logs/stage-full-$label.log" ) || { echo "STOP: $label"; break; }
  if [ "${VALIDATE_LOCAL:-0}" = 1 ]; then   # D1 option B: §4.8 on this laptop (~7 h) before parking
    "$RB/venv/bin/python" -I "$RB/tools/toolkit-validate-bundle.py" "$f" "$WT" > "$f.toolkit.log" 2>&1 \
      || { tail -25 "$f.toolkit.log"; echo "STOP: toolkit $label"; break; }
    mv "$f.toolkit.log" "$RB/logs/"
  fi
  (cd "$STAGE_DIR" && shasum -a 256 "$(basename "$f")" > "$(basename "$f").sha256")
  gsutil -q cp "$f" "$f.sha256" "$GCS_STAGE/" && rm -f "$f"
done
gsutil ls -l "$GCS_STAGE/"

Expect: four bundles (~4.6–4.9 GB each) and four .sha256 in $GCS_STAGE. Stop if an assemble step fails or a bundle is under 4 GB.

  • [ ] Weekly fulls (new layout). October is the current month, so weekly/ gets the weekly fulls of 10-04, 10-11 and 10-18. Stage 10-04 and 10-11 here, the same way as the monthlies (one at a time → §4.8 → sha256 → park); 10-18 is staged in §4.7, where it is also the bundle ↔ Parquet reference, and it is now published. Each: ~1.5–2.5 h export + assemble, ~0.2 TiB billed (~$1.25), 4.8–4.9 GB local until parked. republish-v1.sh stage <date> would also re-stage that date's delta, so call release-gkm.sh directly:
source "$RB/env.sh"; cd "$WT"
for d in 2026-10-04 2026-10-11; do f="$STAGE_DIR/clinvar-gkm-$d.json.gz"
  ( set -o pipefail; ./src/scripts/release-gkm.sh "$d" v2_6_0 --weekly --no-upload 2>&1 | tee "$RB/logs/stage-weekly-$d.log" ) || { echo "STOP: $d"; break; }
  (cd "$STAGE_DIR" && shasum -a 256 "$(basename "$f")" > "$(basename "$f").sha256")
  gsutil -q cp "$f" "$f.sha256" "$GCS_STAGE/" && rm -f "$f"
done

Expect: clinvar-gkm-2026-10-04.json.gz and clinvar-gkm-2026-10-11.json.gz (+ .sha256), ~4.8–4.9 GB each, in $GCS_STAGE. The weekly and monthly staged names are the same pattern (clinvar-gkm-<source date>.json.gz); no weekly date is also a monthly source, so they never collide.

items.title: 4.7 Stage the Parquet set (from 10-18) and the 10-18 weekly full
items.text:
Peak local disk ≈ 26 GB (Parquet shards + merged) + 4.9 GB (10-18 weekly full).

  • [ ] Latest Parquet: source "$RB/env.sh"; cd "$WT"; ( set -o pipefail; ./src/scripts/republish-v1.sh stage parquet 2>&1 | tee "$RB/logs/stage-parquet.log" )
  • [ ] The 10-18 weekly full (published in weekly/, and the reference for the bundle ↔ Parquet gate in §4.9): ( set -o pipefail; ./src/scripts/release-gkm.sh 2026-10-18 v2_6_0 --weekly --no-upload 2>&1 | tee "$RB/logs/stage-weekly-2026-10-18.log" )

Expect: $STAGE_DIR/clinvar-gkm-parquet-latest-2026-10-18/ with 22 files: the four proposition*.parquet (propositionPathogenicity, propositionOncogenicity, propositionSomaticClinicalImpact, propositionClinvarCustom) and no *-proposition.parquet; $STAGE_DIR/clinvar-gkm-2026-10-18.json.gz (~4.9 GB).

items.title: 4.8 gkm-toolkit, strict, on every staged bundle
items.text:
Repo root needs its submodules. The <repo_root> argument must be a checkout with git submodule update --init --recursive done; otherwise every gkm-core reference is unresolvable and every record fails. The release worktree $WT was created without them.

Appendix A validates every record of a real staged bundle, verbatim, with validate_bundle_schema and the registry from load_registry over the whole schema/ tree (strict).

  • [ ] All 16 deltas (laptop; minutes each, the 09-23 and 10-04 deltas are the largest).
source "$RB/env.sh"
for f in "$STAGE_DIR"/clinvar-gkm-delta-2026-*.json.gz; do
  "$RB/venv/bin/python" -I "$RB/tools/toolkit-validate-bundle.py" "$f" "$WT" > "$f.toolkit.log" 2>&1
  printf '%s %s\n' "$(basename "$f")" "$(tail -1 "$f.toolkit.log")"
done

Expect: 16 × PASS (schema_version 1.1.0, failing: 0). The 2026-1004 delta carries the 4 RCV000001117 propositions that had no object in 1.0.1 (plan §3.D); va-spec requires object, so they fail here unless the RCV cause was fixed. Stop if any delta fails.

  • [ ] The four fulls (D1). Laptop (B): run it on each full in §4.6 before parking it; ~7 h each: "$RB/venv/bin/python" -I "$RB/tools/toolkit-validate-bundle.py" "$f" "$WT" | tee "$f.toolkit.log". VM (A):
gcloud compute instances create gkm-validate-110 --project clingen-dev --zone us-east1-b \
  --machine-type n2-highcpu-64 --boot-disk-size 100GB --image-family debian-12 --image-project debian-cloud \
  --scopes storage-ro
gcloud compute scp "$RB/tools/toolkit-validate-bundle.py" gkm-validate-110:~ --zone us-east1-b --project clingen-dev
gcloud compute ssh gkm-validate-110 --zone us-east1-b --project clingen-dev -- bash -s <<'EOF'
set -e
sudo apt-get -qq update && sudo apt-get -qq install -y git python3-venv
git clone -q https://github.com/clingen-data-model/clinvar-gkm.git repo && cd repo && git checkout -q origin/1.0 \
  && git submodule update -q --init submodules/va-spec && cd ..
python3 -m venv v && v/bin/pip install -q 'ga4gh.gkm==0.4.0' ijson orjson
for d in 2026-06-27 2026-08-04 2026-08-29 2026-09-28 2026-10-04 2026-10-11 2026-10-18; do
  gsutil -q cp gs://clinvar-gkm/staging/1.1.0/clinvar-gkm-$d.json.gz .
  v/bin/python -I toolkit-validate-bundle.py clinvar-gkm-$d.json.gz repo --workers 63 | tee $d.toolkit.log | tail -3
  rm -f clinvar-gkm-$d.json.gz
done
EOF
gcloud compute instances delete gkm-validate-110 --zone us-east1-b --project clingen-dev --quiet

Expect: 7 × PASS (4 monthlies + 3 weekly fulls), failing: 0, record counts ~90 M per full. Park the 10-18 weekly full in $GCS_STAGE (§4.9) before the VM loop reaches it. Stop if any record fails. Check out the same commit as $WT on the VM (git checkout <sha> if 1.0 moved). If gsutil cp is denied, the VM's service account lacks read on gs://clinvar-gkm: grant it Storage Object Viewer, or create the VM with --scopes cloud-platform.

items.title: 4.9 Bundle ↔ Parquet (latest set)
items.text:
• [ ] Compare the staged Parquet with the 10-18 weekly full (Appendix B), then park that full in $GCS_STAGE.
source "$RB/env.sh"
"$RB/venv/bin/python" -I "$RB/tools/bundle-parquet-check.py" "$STAGE_DIR/clinvar-gkm-2026-10-18.json.gz" \
  "$STAGE_DIR/clinvar-gkm-parquet-latest-2026-10-18" --mod 500 | tee "$RB/logs/bundle-parquet.log"
f="$STAGE_DIR/clinvar-gkm-2026-10-18.json.gz"
(cd "$STAGE_DIR" && shasum -a 256 "$(basename "$f")" > "$(basename "$f").sha256")
gsutil -q cp "$f" "$f.sha256" "$GCS_STAGE/" && rm -f "$f"

Expect: every section row shows bundle count = Parquet count and 0 0 for b-not-p / p-not-b; evidenceLine = evidenceLine + vcv_evidenceLine + rcv_evidenceLine; the four proposition* tables sum to the three proposition dicts; conditionSet excludes single-member sets in both; data spot-check … 0 differ; PASS. Stop if any count, id or data differs.

items.title: 4.10 Examples re-extraction (commit to 1.0 before the tag)
items.text:
• [ ] Re-extract all 42 from the rebuilt 2026-10-04 (D6) and validate them.
source "$RB/env.sh"; cd "$WT"
git switch -c docs/examples-1.1.0 origin/1.0
for f in examples/cat-vrs/*.jsonc examples/scv/*.json* examples/vcv/*.jsonc examples/rcv/*.jsonc; do
  sec=$(basename "$(dirname "$f")"); [ "$sec" = cat-vrs ] && sec=variation
  id=$(python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))["id"])' "$f")
  python3 src/scripts/extract-example.py "$sec" "$id" --dataset clinvar_2026_10_04_v2_6_0 > "$f.new" && mv "$f.new" "$f" || echo "STOP: $f"
done
for f in examples/cat-vrs/*.jsonc; do python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.dumps(json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))))' "$f"; done | "$RB/venv/bin/python" src/scripts/validate-schema-conformance.py --as CategoricalVariant
for f in examples/scv/*.json*; do python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.dumps(json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))))' "$f"; done | "$RB/venv/bin/python" src/scripts/validate-schema-conformance.py --as ClinvarScvStatement
for f in examples/vcv/*.jsonc examples/rcv/*.jsonc; do python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.dumps(json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))))' "$f"; done | "$RB/venv/bin/python" src/scripts/validate-schema-conformance.py --as ClinvarAggregateStatement
git diff --stat

Expect: 42 files rewritten; the diff shows the 1.1.0 shapes (geneContextSource, placeholder gene name, ordered submittedGeneSymbols, citations, 3.D #/condition/… objects) and nothing else structural; the three validator runs report 0 failures (2 / 8 / 32 records; strict by default, --relax only to debug). Stop if an id is not found or validation fails. Then: commit, push, PR to 1.0, merge. examples/ is outside src/, so the gate_key does not move.

items.title: 5. Publish (live R2 and Cloudflare; each step user-confirmed)
items.text:
The layout and its rules are in PR #182 (src/scripts/r2_layout.py, docstring), and the driver is republish-v1.sh. Nothing that exists today is overwritten before §5.11. Every new object goes under v1/1.1/ (current) or v1/1.0/ (frozen 1.0.1). A failure before §5.11 therefore leaves the old /v1/ paths serving.

Order:

  1. plan;
  2. archive check;
  3. the 1.0.1 move;
  4. monthlies before deltas: a delta's checkpoint_full is resolved from the monthlies' source_release in v1/1.1/index.json;
  5. weekly fulls;
  6. deltas, in date order: each one's baseline is checked against the previous one;
  7. Parquet;
  8. index;
  9. verify;
  10. Cloudflare rules;
  11. the docs gate;
  12. cleanup;
  13. purge.

Run every step with --dry-run first, read the output, then run it for real.

Dry-run results against the live bucket (2026-10-21). All numbers come from the read-only live listing.

Step Objects Size Bucket now 545 113.42 GB Move into v1/1.0/ 35 server-side copies (+ 24 new small files) 24.29 GB Uploads into v1/1.1/ ~87 ~47 GB Server-side copies in v1/1.1/ (00-latest, 00-latest_weekly) 2 ~9.7 GB Cleanup (deleted) 544 113.42 GB Final v1/1.0/ ≈ 60 objects, v1/1.1/ ≈ 95 objects, plus the root index.json ≈ 24.3 GB + ≈ 57 GB ≈ 81 GB

The uploads into v1/1.1/ are:

  • 4 monthlies, 18.9 GB;
  • 3 weekly fulls, ~14.5 GB;
  • 16 deltas, bundle + sidecar + manifest each, ~0.57 GB;

  • Parquet, 22 files + manifest, ~13 GB.

  • [ ] 5.0 Plan (read-only): source "$RB/env.sh"; cd "$WT"; ./src/scripts/republish-v1.sh plan | tee "$RB/logs/plan.txt". Expect the numbers above. Anything new since then (a 10-25 dataset, a _backup/) shows up in the cleanup list. Stop if the cleanup list holds a key under v1/1.0/ or v1/1.1/; it cannot, by construction.

  • [ ] 5.1 Verify the 1.0.1 archive: ./src/scripts/republish-v1.sh verify-archive. Expect: PASS: archive/1.0.1/ holds every live v1/ bundle file at its live size. (40 files; dry-run PASS on 2026-10-21). Stop if FAIL.
  • [ ] 5.2 Move 1.0.1 to the frozen line v1/1.0/: ./src/scripts/republish-v1.sh move-1.0 --dry-run, then without --dry-run.
  • Expect:
    • 35 server-side copies (24.29 GB; the five ≥2 GB bundles go multipart);
    • 21 .sha256 sidecars written from the archive MANIFEST, so nothing is downloaded;
    • v1/1.0/MANIFEST.json, README.txt, index.json and feed.xml;
    • the index summary reads 4 monthly, 00-latest=2026-10, 0 weekly, 15 deltas.
  • Not carried over:
    • the 1.0.1 deltas/00-latest/ copy;
    • the 1.0.1 index and feed snapshots.
  • Every delta lands in v1/1.0/deltas/YYYY-MM/ (October too, because the line is frozen).
  • The step is idempotent: a copy already in place is skipped.
  • Stop if a copy's size check fails.
  • [ ] 5.3 Monthlies, in month order, one at a time from $GCS_STAGE:
source "$RB/env.sh"; cd "$WT"
for spec in "2026-07 2026-06-27" "2026-08 2026-08-04" "2026-09 2026-08-29" "2026-10 2026-09-28"; do
  set -- $spec; label=$1; d=$2; f="clinvar-gkm-$d.json.gz"
  gsutil -q cp "$GCS_STAGE/$f" "$GCS_STAGE/$f.sha256" "$STAGE_DIR/"
  (cd "$STAGE_DIR" && shasum -a 256 -c "$f.sha256") || { echo "STOP: checksum $f"; break; }
  ./src/scripts/republish-v1.sh upload "$label" --dry-run | tail -5
  read -r -p "upload monthly $label for real? [y/N] " ok; [ "$ok" = y ] || break
  ./src/scripts/republish-v1.sh upload "$label" 2>&1 | tee "$RB/logs/upload-monthly-$label.log" && rm -f "$STAGE_DIR/$f" "$STAGE_DIR/$f.sha256"
done

Expect: each upload writes v1/1.1/clinvar-gkm_<label>.json.gz and its .sha256, and refreshes v1/1.1/clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz (a server-side copy, ending on 2026-10). Each index regeneration prints source_release for every monthly, with no WARNING source_release unknown.

  • [ ] 5.4 Weekly fulls, in date order (10-04, 10-11, 10-18), one at a time from $GCS_STAGE:
source "$RB/env.sh"; cd "$WT"
for d in 2026-10-04 2026-10-11 2026-10-18; do f="clinvar-gkm-$d.json.gz"
  gsutil -q cp "$GCS_STAGE/$f" "$GCS_STAGE/$f.sha256" "$STAGE_DIR/"
  (cd "$STAGE_DIR" && shasum -a 256 -c "$f.sha256") || { echo "STOP: checksum $f"; break; }
  ./src/scripts/upload-gkm-to-r2.sh "$d" v2_6_0 "$STAGE_DIR/$f" --weekly --dry-run | tail -4
  read -r -p "upload weekly full $d for real? [y/N] " ok; [ "$ok" = y ] || break
  ./src/scripts/upload-gkm-to-r2.sh "$d" v2_6_0 "$STAGE_DIR/$f" --weekly 2>&1 | tee "$RB/logs/upload-weekly-$d.log" && rm -f "$STAGE_DIR/$f" "$STAGE_DIR/$f.sha256"
done

(republish-v1.sh upload <date> would also upload that date's delta.) Expect: v1/1.1/weekly/clinvar-gkm_2026-10{04,11,18}.json.gz and their .sha256, and weekly/clinvar-gkm_00-latest_weekly.json.gz (a server-side copy) ending on 10-18. - [ ] 5.5 Deltas, in date order: ./src/scripts/republish-v1.sh upload deltas --dry-run, then for real. - Expect the folder rule: - Folder: v1/1.1/deltas/ for 10-04, 10-11 and 10-18 (October is the current month); - deltas/2026-07/ ×4, deltas/2026-08/ ×5, deltas/2026-09/ ×4 (dry-run 2026-10-21). - Each delta writes clinvar-gkm-delta_YYYY-MMDD.json.gz, .json.gz.sha256 and .manifest.json. - Before each upload the uploader checks: - the manifest's baseline_release equals the release of the previous delta in the line; - otherwise it stops with the chain would have a gap. - It also prints the completed manifest: checkpoint_full, sha256 and schema_version. - Expected checkpoint_full, i.e. the newest monthly whose source_release ≤ baseline_release. checkpoint_full.release is that monthly's source release, and path is v1/1.1/clinvar-gkm_<month>.json.gz:

Deltas baseline_release range checkpoint_full (month ← release) 07-06, 07-15, 07-20, 07-27, 08-04 06-27 … 07-27 2026-07 ← 2026-06-27 08-08, 08-16, 08-22, 08-29 08-04 … 08-22 2026-08 ← 2026-08-04 09-05, 09-13, 09-23, 09-28 08-29 … 09-23 2026-09 ← 2026-08-29 10-04, 10-11, 10-18 09-28 … 10-11 2026-10 ← 2026-09-28

This table was reproduced offline on 2026-10-21 by running 16 synthetic manifests through r2_layout.py patch-manifest. Stop if any upload reports a gap or a different checkpoint. - [ ] 5.6 Parquet: ./src/scripts/republish-v1.sh upload parquet --dry-run, then for real. Expect: - 22 <section>.parquet in v1/1.1/parquet/; - parquet/manifest.json with source_release 2026-10-18, dataset clinvar_2026_10_18_v2_6_0, builder BigQuery export, schema_version 1.1.0, and 22 files with size and sha256; - no *-proposition.parquet. - [ ] 5.7 Index: ./src/scripts/republish-v1.sh index --dry-run, then for real. It writes v1/1.1/index.json + feed.xml, v1/1.0/index.json + feed.xml, and the root index.json. The root has manifest_version 2 and versions 1.1 (status current, schema 1.1.0, index v1/1.1/index.json) and 1.0 (frozen, schema 1.0.1, superseded_by v1/1.1). The dry-run copies go to $INDEX_OUT_DIR (default /tmp/clinvar-gkm-index-dry-run/). - [ ] 5.8 Verify (read-only): ./src/scripts/republish-v1.sh verify. It checks: - every planned key in both lines, with sizes; - that 00-latest equals 2026-10 (size and sha256); - that 00-latest_weekly equals 10-18; - the Parquet files against parquet/manifest.json; - each monthly's source_release in the index; - for each of the 16 manifests: - release and compare_release; - baseline_release, which must equal the previous delta's release (the first is 2026-06-27); - checkpoint_full (the table above); - sha256, which must equal the bundle's sidecar; - schema_version 1.1.0; - every v1/1.0/ file against its MANIFEST.json (size and sha256 sidecar); - the root index.

Expect: 16 delta rows ending OK, then PASS: both lines match the plan. Stop if FAIL; cleanup refuses to run anyway. - [ ] 5.9 Cloudflare rules (zone clinvar-gkm.org; the tokens are read from ~/.config/clinvar-gkm/cloudflare.env and never printed). ./src/scripts/cf-rules.sh show (read-only) prints each live expression next to the proposed one; then ./src/scripts/cf-rules.sh apply --dry-run, then apply.

Rule (phase) Token Live (2026-10-21) Proposed 1 "R2 immutable artifacts" (cache) CF_CACHE_TOKEN host only: edge 1 month, browser 1 day unchanged. Covers dated monthlies, deltas (incl. deltas/YYYY-MM/), archive/YYYY/ and all of v1/1.0/ 2 "R2 mutable pointers" (cache, bypass) CF_CACHE_TOKEN contains "00-latest" or contains "index.json" or contains "feed.xml" contains "00-latest" (incl. 00-latest_weekly) or ends_with "/index.json" or ends_with "/feed.xml" or ends_with "/README.txt" or contains "/weekly/" (weekly fulls are deleted at month end) 3 "Latest Parquet: cache 1 day" (cache) CF_CACHE_TOKEN starts_with "/v1/datasets/parquet/00-latest/" starts_with "/v1/" and contains "/parquet/" (overwritten every release; edge 1 day; run-release.sh purges parquet/ on each rebuild) PATH ALLOWLIST (WAF custom) CF_WAF_TOKEN allows /v1/, /archive/, /.well-known/, /, /index.json unchanged: /v1/ covers both lines. /archive/ is empty after §5.11; apply --drop-archive removes it (optional, after cleanup)

The last matching cache rule wins, so the order stays 1, 2, 3. Rollover moves deltas and archives monthlies to new keys and purges the old ones (r2-rollover.sh), so the 1-month immutable TTL stays safe. Expect: show marks rules 2 and 3 CHANGE, apply prints PATCH … OK twice. Stop if a rule is not found by its description (fix by hand in the dashboard). - [ ] 5.10 Docs gate: PRs #146 and #168 are merged and the site is deployed. They read the new paths: the R2 browser, the DuckDB console and the replay recipe. Cleanup removes every path the old docs read (G16). - [ ] 5.11 Cleanup: ./src/scripts/republish-v1.sh cleanup --dry-run prints the delete list grouped by folder, plus guard (verify): PASS. Then run it without --dry-run. Expect: 544 objects, 113.42 GB: - v1/datasets/ (incl. parquet/ 00-latest and 4 dated sets); - v1/deltas/ (incl. 00-latest/ and every parquet/); - v1/index.json, v1/feed.xml, v1/README.txt; - archive/1.0.1/; - any _backup/.

The root index.json is kept (rewritten in §5.7). Stop if the guard fails, or the list holds anything under v1/1.0/ or v1/1.1/. - [ ] 5.12 CDN purge (everything on the zone): ./src/scripts/republish-v1.sh purge --dry-run (token status active), then ./src/scripts/republish-v1.sh purge. Expect: purge: OK.

items.title: 6. Verify through the CDN
items.text:
• [ ] Root and line index, every listed bundle (HEAD, size, sidecar sha256), and the delta chain and checkpoints, read through the public host. The requests are throttled under the CDN rate limit.
source "$RB/env.sh"
python3 - <<'PY'
import json, time, urllib.request
B = "https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/"
get = lambda p: urllib.request.urlopen(B + p, timeout=120).read()
root = json.loads(get("index.json"))
cur = [v for v in root["versions"].values() if v["status"] == "current"]
assert len(cur) == 1 and cur[0]["index"] == "v1/1.1/index.json" and cur[0]["schema"] == "1.1.0", root
assert root["versions"]["1.0"]["status"] == "frozen" and root["versions"]["1.0"]["superseded_by"] == "v1/1.1", root
idx = json.loads(get("v1/1.1/index.json")); old = json.loads(get("v1/1.0/index.json"))
assert idx["schema_version"] == "1.1.0", idx["schema_version"]
mon = {m["release"]: m for m in idx["datasets"]["monthly"] if not m["latest"]}
src = {"2026-07": "2026-06-27", "2026-08": "2026-08-04", "2026-09": "2026-08-29", "2026-10": "2026-09-28"}
assert {k: m["source_release"] for k, m in mon.items()} == src, mon
lat = [m for m in idx["datasets"]["monthly"] if m["latest"]][0]; assert lat["sha256"] == mon["2026-10"]["sha256"]
wk = [w["release"] for w in idx["datasets"]["weekly"] if not w["latest"]]
assert wk == ["2026-10-04", "2026-10-11", "2026-10-18"], wk
assert len(idx["deltas"]) == 16 and idx["parquet"]["source_release"] == "2026-10-18", idx["parquet"]
assert len([m for m in old["datasets"]["monthly"] if not m["latest"]]) == 4 and len(old["deltas"]) == 15
objs = [(m["path"], m["size"], m["sha256"]) for m in idx["datasets"]["monthly"] + idx["datasets"]["weekly"]]
objs += [(d["bundle"]["path"], d["bundle"]["size"], d["bundle"]["sha256"]) for d in idx["deltas"]]
bad = 0
for path, size, sha in objs:
    r = urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(B + path, method="HEAD"), timeout=60)
    side = get(path + ".sha256").decode().split()[0]
    ok = r.status == 200 and int(r.headers["Content-Length"]) == size and side == sha
    bad += not ok; print("OK " if ok else "BAD", path); time.sleep(0.3)
prev = "2026-06-27"
for d in idx["deltas"]:                       # chain + checkpoint_full + sha256, from the manifests themselves
    m = json.loads(get(d["manifest"])); cp = m["checkpoint_full"]
    want = max((s, k) for k, s in src.items() if s <= m["baseline_release"])
    ok = (m["release"] == d["release"] and m["baseline_release"] == prev and cp["release"] == want[0]
          and cp["path"] == f"v1/1.1/clinvar-gkm_{want[1]}.json.gz" and m["sha256"] == d["bundle"]["sha256"])
    bad += not ok; print("OK " if ok else "BAD", d["release"], m["baseline_release"], cp["path"], cp["release"])
    prev = d["release"]; time.sleep(0.3)
print("objects:", len(objs), "deltas:", len(idx["deltas"]), "bad:", bad)
PY
curl -s https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.1/parquet/manifest.json | python3 -c 'import json,sys; m=json.load(sys.stdin); print(m["source_release"], m["builder"], len(m["files"]))'
for p in v1/datasets/clinvar-gkm_00-latest.json.gz v1/index.json archive/1.0.1/README.txt; do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} $p\n" "https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/$p"; done

Expect:

  • no assertion error;
  • bad: 0;
  • 2026-10-18 BigQuery export 22;

  • the three old paths return 404: they were deleted and purged. They return 403 if /archive/ was dropped from the allowlist.

  • [ ] Downloaded copies equal the validated ones:

  • download the largest delta (2026-0923, now v1/1.1/deltas/2026-09/) and check it with Appendix A;
  • curl -s …/v1/1.1/clinvar-gkm_2026-10.json.gz.sha256 must equal the sha256 recorded in §4.6;
  • …/v1/1.1/weekly/clinvar-gkm_2026-1018.json.gz.sha256 must equal the one recorded in §4.9.
  • [ ] Cache behaviour (GET, run twice):
  • a delta manifest → MISS then HIT;
  • v1/1.1/index.json and weekly/…sha256 → DYNAMIC/BYPASS;
  • parquet/manifest.json → HIT on the second request.
  • [ ] Console example queries (DuckDB over the CDN):
duckdb -c "INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM read_parquet('https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.1/parquet/proposition*.parquet');
SELECT s.proposition_section, COUNT(*) n FROM read_parquet('https://data.clinvar-gkm.org/v1/1.1/parquet/scv.parquet') s GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;"

Expect: the union reads with no schema error (shared column schema); proposition_section shows only the four new names. Then run the examples on the Query the Data page (PR #146).

items.title: 7. Wrap-up
items.text:
• [ ] Tag 1.1.0 on the 1.0 tip (after the examples PR): git -C "$REPO" fetch origin && git -C "$REPO" tag -a 1.1.0 origin/1.0 -m "ClinVar-GKM 1.1.0" && git -C "$REPO" push origin 1.1.0.
  • [ ] GitHub Release: gh release create 1.1.0 --repo clingen-data-model/clinvar-gkm --title "1.1.0" --notes-file <completion notice + changelog entry> --latest (text: 2026-10-18-1.1.0-announcements.md §2, updated for 16 deltas, latest-only Parquet and no advance notice).
  • [ ] w3id $ids resolve:
for p in 1.1.0/json/ClinvarCategoricalVariant 1.1.0/json/ClinvarScvStatement 1.1.0/json/ClinvarAggregateStatement 1.0.1/json/ClinvarCategoricalVariant 1.0.0/json/ClinvarCategoricalVariant; do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} $p\n" -L "https://w3id.org/clingen/schema/clinvar-gkm/$p"; done

Expect: 200 for each (the bundle $id itself is 404, G11). - [ ] Forward-merge 1.0 → main (no conflicts in today's trial) and move the dev tag (memory "Release branch/dev sync policy": main must never describe as a release tag):

cd "$REPO" && git fetch origin && git switch -c chore/merge-1.1.0-into-main origin/main
git merge --no-ff origin/1.0 -m "Merge 1.0 (1.1.0) into main"
git push -u origin chore/merge-1.1.0-into-main && gh pr create --base main --title "Merge 1.0 (1.1.0) into main" --body "Forward-merge of the 1.1.0 release."
# after the PR merges (merge commit, not squash):
git fetch origin && git tag -f dev origin/main && git push -f origin dev && git describe --tags origin/main

Expect: git describe prints dev (no dev tag exists today; this creates it). - [ ] Merge the held docs PR #146 (docs/release-1.0.2-data-changes → main; it carries ADR 0006 and the 1.1.0 changelog), after checking zensical build --strict. - [ ] Close issues #130 and #132 with a comment linking the Release. - [ ] Completion notice: GitHub Discussions Announcements, the Release notes, the Changelog (#146); the clinvar-gkm@broadinstitute.org list if wanted. No advance notice was posted. - [ ] Re-stamp 10-18 only if anything under src/ changed on 1.0 after §3.0 (G8):

source "$RB/env.sh"; cd "$WT" && git fetch origin -q && git checkout -q --detach origin/1.0
GATE2=$(git log -1 --format=%H -- src/procedures src/scripts src/vrsify); echo "$GATE vs $GATE2"
[ "$GATE" = "$GATE2" ] || bq query --use_legacy_sql=false "CALL \`clinvar_ingest.gkm_pipeline_version\`(DATE '2026-10-18', '$(git describe --tags --always)', '$GATE2')"
  • [ ] Resume weekly runs with the gkm procs FULL from the 1.0 checkout: run-release.sh <date> --full-procs (#182), starting with the first weekly, 2026-10-25. This holds until ADR 0007 workstream 3 decides whether to retire the incremental gkm machinery.
  • --full-procs sends GKS_FULL=true to stage 4 only: every catvar/scv/rcv/vcv proc runs its full wrapper.
  • variation_identity (stage 1), the export (2), vrsify (3) and the gkm_vrs load stay incremental, so only the ~changed variations (~44 K a week) are re-normalized.
  • --full is still "everything": it also re-vrsifies all ~4.6 M variations. Use it only after a version-invalidating change.
  • A stubbed trace confirms it: --full-procs gives stage 1 variation_identity_incremental, an export without --full, and stage 4 GKS_FULL=true.

Why: the incremental gkm path is unproven. INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS_BY_PROJECT shows it silently fell back to full builds: - in the 2026-10-01 rebuild chain: 07-15, 07-27, 08-29 and 09-13 (07-15 has no diff_* drivers); - in the normal 10-04 weekly (2026-10-07): gkm_catvar_proc_incremental ran its guard, then the full path.

The vrs-to-bq-table.sh log prints …_incremental in both cases. check_incr.sh (Appendix D) tells them apart from the job history: an incremental build reads the baseline's data tables, a fallback does not. Keep it as the reference check if the incremental path is ever used again. Full procs cost about what an "incremental" run did: ~0.20 vs ~0.22 TiB, 13–15 vs 18–19 min of procs (Step 3).

Stage 5 now runs: 1. r2-rollover.sh; 2. the weekly full (release-gkm.sh --weekly, +1.5–2.5 h and ~0.2 TiB ≈ $1.25 per week, 4.9 GB local); 3. any due official monthly (a server-side copy of its source release's weekly full); 4. r2-rollover.sh again; 5. the delta; 6. Parquet.

What to expect from the next runs: - The 10-25 run adds weekly/clinvar-gkm_2026-1025.json.gz and deltas/clinvar-gkm-delta_2026-1025.*. - The first November run moves October's deltas into deltas/2026-10/ and deletes the 10-04/10-11/10-18 weekly fulls. It keeps 10-25 (note: keep … until the 2026-11 monthly is posted). - When ClinVar posts ClinVarVCVRelease_2026-11 (~11-04), the next run copies the 10-25 weekly full to clinvar-gkm_2026-11.json.gz (source 2026-10-25, if 10-25 is the newest build before it), then deletes it. - Check each run's log for the rollover plan before the next week. - [ ] Snapshots: they expire at SNAP_EXPIRES (2026-11-20). To delete earlier: for s in $EXISTING; do D=$(ds $s); for t in $(bq ls -n 1000 "$D" | awk '$1 ~ /__pre110$/ {print $1}'); do bq rm -f -t "$D.$t"; done; done - [ ] Clean up: gsutil -m rm -r "$GCS_STAGE"; rm -rf "$STAGE_DIR"; git -C "$REPO" worktree remove "$WT".

items.title: Time and cost
items.text:
Phase Wall clock BigQuery billed Pre-flight, deploy, snapshots < 1 h ~0 Rebuild: 17 full builds (13–15 min of procs each; 06-27 lighter) ~3.7–4.3 h ~3.3–3.6 TiB (0.13 + 16 × 0.20–0.21) BigQuery gates (§4.1, 4.2, 4.4; no full-vs-incremental oracles, §4.3) 3.5–5 h ~2.6 TiB (conformance + delta reconstruction ~1.4 TiB, expected-diff ~1.2 TiB) Staging: 16 deltas, 4 monthlies, 3 weekly fulls (10-04, 10-11 new; 10-18 was already the reference full), Parquet 15–23 h (+3–5 h for the two new weekly fulls) ~1.4 TiB (+0.4 TiB ≈ $2.50 for the two) gkm-toolkit: 16 deltas + 7 fulls (4 monthlies + 3 weekly) VM: ~8–10 h (~$18–25 compute); laptop: ~50 h — Bundle ↔ Parquet, examples 1–2 h small Publish (move 24 GB server-side, upload ~47 GB, cleanup 113 GB), rules, purge, verify 4–6 h — Total ~3–3.5 working days elapsed (VM for fulls) ~7.5 TiB ≈ $47 on-demand ($6.25/TiB)

The rebuild is 17 full builds (option A). Measured, a full build bills ~0.20 TiB in 13–15 min of procs. An incremental one bills ~0.22 TiB in 18–19 min, because the change log and delta build are half the bytes in both modes. So the full rebuild is the cheaper choice as well as the proven one. The full-vs-incremental oracles were dropped (§4.3); §4.4 delta reconstruction gates the chain.

Other costs:

  • snapshots ~$1–12 a month until they expire;
  • GCS staging ~35 GB for a few days (cents);
  • R2 goes from 113.4 GB (all objects) to ~81 GB: v1/1.0/ ≈ 24.3 GB and v1/1.1/ ≈ 57 GB.

Steady state afterwards:

  • a weekly full every week: +0.2 TiB BigQuery ≈ $1.25/week, +1.5–2.5 h;
  • a monthly copied from a weekly full replaces the old monthly re-export: −0.2 TiB/month;
  • net ≈ +$4/month and ~6–10 h of pipeline time a month;
  • weekly/ holds ≤ 6 × 4.9 GB ≈ 29 GB, about $0.45/month of R2 storage.

items.title: Appendix A — toolkit-validate-bundle.py
items.text:
Fixed 2026-10-21: the first version computed nesting depth by counting dots in the ijson prefix, so every section whose record keys contain a dot (sequenceReference, location, allele, condition, conditionSet, submitter, evidenceLine, scv, vcv, rcv) was silently skipped. The reader below tracks depth from the start/end events. Check the per-section counts in the output: every bundle section must appear.

Write to $RB/tools/toolkit-validate-bundle.py. Tested on the live 2026-1011 delta (streams, bounded memory, reports per-record failures).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Validate EVERY record of a real published/staged bundle (.json.gz) with the GA4GH gkm-toolkit.

The bundle is streamed (ijson) so a 4.8 GB full never has to fit in memory. Records are passed to
ga4gh.gkm validate_bundle_schema VERBATIM (no cleanup, no re-collapse: unlike sub-bundle.py this cannot
mask an export/assembler bug), in chunks of --chunk records per section, each chunk wrapped as
{"schema_version": <bundle's own value>, <section>: {key: record, ...}}. The registry is built by
validate-schema-conformance.py's load_registry over the whole schema/ tree (strict, as published).

Also checks: the bundle's schema_version equals the schema const; every section is non-empty
(minProperties 1). Exit 0 only when every record passes.

Usage: python toolkit-validate-bundle.py <bundle.json.gz> <repo_root> [--workers N] [--chunk N] [--sections a,b]
"""
import argparse
import collections
import gzip
import importlib.util
import json
import multiprocessing as mp
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import ijson

G = {}


def _init(repo_root):
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
        "vsc", Path(repo_root) / "src/scripts/validate-schema-conformance.py")
    vsc = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(vsc)
    from jsonschema import Draft202012Validator
    from ga4gh.gkm.bundles.schema_validation import validate_bundle_schema
    registry, _ = vsc.load_registry(Path(repo_root) / "schema", relax=False)
    schema = json.loads((Path(repo_root) / "schema/clinvar-gkm/clinvar-gkm-bundle.schema.json").read_text())
    G.update(schema=schema, validate=validate_bundle_schema,
             validator=Draft202012Validator(schema, registry=registry))


def _check(task):
    sv, section, items = task
    try:
        G["validate"]({"schema_version": sv, section: dict(items)}, G["schema"], validator=G["validator"])
        return section, len(items), []
    except Exception:  # find the failing records in this chunk
        bad = []
        for k, rec in items:
            try:
                G["validate"]({"schema_version": sv, section: {k: rec}}, G["schema"], validator=G["validator"])
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
                bad.append(f"{section}/{k}: {str(e)[:300]}")
        if not bad:
            bad.append(f"{section}: chunk-level failure not reproducible per record")
        return section, len(items), bad


def records(path):
    """Yield ('schema_version', None, value) once, then (section, key, record) for every entry.

    Depth is tracked from the start/end events, NOT from dots in the ijson prefix: record keys such as
    'ga4gh:SL.x', 'clinvar.trait:1' or 'clinvar.submission:SCV1.2' contain dots (a dot-count depth
    silently dropped every such section)."""
    with gzip.open(path, "rb") as fh:
        lvl = 0; section = key = builder = None; bdepth = 0
        for prefix, event, value in ijson.parse(fh, use_float=True):
            if builder is not None:
                builder.event(event, value)
                if event in ("start_map", "start_array"):
                    bdepth += 1
                elif event in ("end_map", "end_array"):
                    bdepth -= 1
                    if bdepth == 0:
                        yield section, key, builder.value
                        builder = None
                continue
            if event in ("start_map", "start_array"):
                if lvl == 2:                       # a record value
                    builder = ijson.ObjectBuilder(); builder.event(event, value); bdepth = 1
                else:
                    lvl += 1
            elif event in ("end_map", "end_array"):
                lvl -= 1
            elif event == "map_key":
                if lvl == 1:
                    section = value
                elif lvl == 2:
                    key = value
            elif lvl == 1 and section == "schema_version":
                yield "schema_version", None, value
            elif lvl == 2:                         # scalar record value
                yield section, key, value


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("bundle")
    ap.add_argument("repo_root")
    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=max(1, mp.cpu_count() - 1))
    ap.add_argument("--chunk", type=int, default=2000)
    ap.add_argument("--max-print", type=int, default=20)
    ap.add_argument("--sections", default="", help="comma list: validate only these sections (others are counted only)")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    _init(a.repo_root)
    const = G["schema"]["properties"]["schema_version"].get("const")
    t0 = time.time()
    counts, failures, sv = {}, [], None
    only, skipped = set(filter(None, a.sections.split(","))), {}

    def tasks():
        nonlocal sv
        buf, cur = [], None
        for section, key, rec in records(a.bundle):
            if section == "schema_version":
                sv = rec
                continue
            if only and section not in only:
                skipped[section] = skipped.get(section, 0) + 1
                continue
            if cur is not None and section != cur and buf:
                yield sv, cur, buf
                buf = []
            cur = section
            buf.append((key, rec))
            if len(buf) >= a.chunk:
                yield sv, cur, buf
                buf = []
        if buf:
            yield sv, cur, buf

    nfail = 0
    with mp.Pool(a.workers, initializer=_init, initargs=(a.repo_root,)) as pool:
        pending = collections.deque()

        def drain(limit):
            nonlocal nfail
            while len(pending) > limit:  # bounded in-flight work: the bundle is never buffered in memory
                section, n, bad = pending.popleft().get()
                counts[section] = counts.get(section, 0) + n
                nfail += len(bad)
                failures.extend(bad[: max(0, 1000 - len(failures))])

        for task in tasks():
            pending.append(pool.apply_async(_check, (task,)))
            drain(a.workers * 3)
        drain(0)

    total = sum(counts.values())
    for s_, n_ in skipped.items():
        print(f"  (not validated: {s_} {n_:,d})")
    print(f"bundle: {a.bundle}")
    print(f"schema_version: bundle={sv!r} schema const={const!r} -> {'OK' if sv == const else 'MISMATCH'}")
    for s, n in counts.items():
        print(f"  {s:28s} {n:>10,d}")
    print(f"records: {total:,d}  failing: {nfail:,d}  ({time.time() - t0:,.0f} s, {a.workers} workers)")
    for f in failures[: a.max_print]:
        print("  FAIL", f)
    ok = sv == const and nfail == 0 and total > 0 and all(n > 0 for n in counts.values()) and not skipped
    print("PASS" if ok else "FAIL")
    sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

items.title: Appendix B — bundle-parquet-check.py
items.text:
Fixed 2026-10-21: same dot-counting depth bug as Appendix A; the reader below tracks depth from events.

Write to $RB/tools/bundle-parquet-check.py. Tested against the live CDN Parquet (--subset mode with a delta).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Bundle <-> Parquet gate: the Parquet set must be recomputable from the bundle (ADR 0008).

For every Parquet table (one file per section; evidenceLine + vcv_evidenceLine + rcv_evidenceLine all map to
the bundle's evidenceLine section; therapy/therapyGroup use key/value, the rest id/data):
  1. per-section record count  == the bundle section's entry count
  2. id set                     == the bundle section's key set (both directions)
  3. `data` == the bundle record (canonical JSON compare) for a deterministic sample (crc32(key) % --mod == 0)
The bundle is streamed (ijson); only keys and the sampled records are held.

Usage: bundle-parquet-check.py <bundle.json.gz> <parquet_dir_or_url_prefix> [--mod 500] [--tables a,b,...]
       [--subset]   bundle is a delta: only check bundle -> Parquet (ids present, sampled data equal)
Exit 0 only when every check passes.
"""
import argparse
import gzip
import json
import os
import sys
import tempfile
import zlib

import duckdb
import ijson

EVIDENCE = {"evidenceLine", "vcv_evidenceLine", "rcv_evidenceLine"}


def canon(v):
    return json.dumps(v, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)


def stream(path):
    """Yield ('schema_version', None, value) once, then (section, key, record) for every entry.

    Depth is tracked from the start/end events, NOT from dots in the ijson prefix: record keys such as
    'ga4gh:SL.x', 'clinvar.trait:1' or 'clinvar.submission:SCV1.2' contain dots (a dot-count depth
    silently dropped every such section)."""
    with gzip.open(path, "rb") as fh:
        lvl = 0; section = key = builder = None; bdepth = 0
        for prefix, event, value in ijson.parse(fh, use_float=True):
            if builder is not None:
                builder.event(event, value)
                if event in ("start_map", "start_array"):
                    bdepth += 1
                elif event in ("end_map", "end_array"):
                    bdepth -= 1
                    if bdepth == 0:
                        yield section, key, builder.value
                        builder = None
                continue
            if event in ("start_map", "start_array"):
                if lvl == 2:                       # a record value
                    builder = ijson.ObjectBuilder(); builder.event(event, value); bdepth = 1
                else:
                    lvl += 1
            elif event in ("end_map", "end_array"):
                lvl -= 1
            elif event == "map_key":
                if lvl == 1:
                    section = value
                elif lvl == 2:
                    key = value
            elif lvl == 2:                         # scalar record value
                yield section, key, value


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("bundle")
    ap.add_argument("parquet")
    ap.add_argument("--mod", type=int, default=500)
    ap.add_argument("--tables", default="")
    ap.add_argument("--subset", action="store_true")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    remote = a.parquet.startswith("http")
    tables = [t for t in a.tables.split(",") if t] or sorted(
        f[:-8] for f in os.listdir(a.parquet) if f.endswith(".parquet"))
    sec_of = {t: ("evidenceLine" if t in EVIDENCE else t) for t in tables}
    wanted = set(sec_of.values())

    tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="bpq-")
    ids_path = os.path.join(tmp, "bundle_ids.tsv")
    sample, counts = {}, {}
    with open(ids_path, "w") as ids:
        for section, key, rec in stream(a.bundle):
            if section == "schema_version" or section not in wanted:
                continue
            counts[section] = counts.get(section, 0) + 1
            ids.write(f"{section}\t{key}\n")
            if zlib.crc32(key.encode()) % a.mod == 0:
                sample[(section, key)] = canon(rec)

    con = duckdb.connect()
    if remote:
        con.execute("INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;")
    con.execute(f"CREATE TABLE b AS SELECT * FROM read_csv('{ids_path}', delim='\t', header=false, "
                "columns={'section':'VARCHAR','k':'VARCHAR'}, quote='', escape='')")
    srcs = []
    for t in tables:
        url = f"{a.parquet.rstrip('/')}/{t}.parquet"
        cols = [r[0] for r in con.execute(f"DESCRIBE SELECT * FROM read_parquet('{url}')").fetchall()]
        idc, dc = ("id", "data") if "id" in cols else ("key", "value")
        srcs.append(f"SELECT '{sec_of[t]}' AS section, '{t}' AS tbl, {idc}::VARCHAR AS k, {dc}::VARCHAR AS d "
                    f"FROM read_parquet('{url}')")
    con.execute("CREATE TABLE p AS " + " UNION ALL ".join(srcs))

    fail = False
    print(f"{'section':30s} {'bundle':>11s} {'parquet':>11s} {'b-not-p':>9s} {'p-not-b':>9s}")
    for (section,) in con.execute("SELECT DISTINCT section FROM p ORDER BY 1").fetchall():
        pn = con.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM p WHERE section=?", [section]).fetchone()[0]
        bn = counts.get(section, 0)
        b_not_p = con.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM b WHERE section=? AND k NOT IN "
                              "(SELECT k FROM p WHERE section=?)", [section, section]).fetchone()[0]
        p_not_b = 0 if a.subset else con.execute(
            "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM p WHERE section=? AND k NOT IN (SELECT k FROM b WHERE section=?)",
            [section, section]).fetchone()[0]
        dup = con.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) - COUNT(DISTINCT k) FROM p WHERE section=?", [section]).fetchone()[0]
        bad = b_not_p or p_not_b or dup or (not a.subset and pn != bn)
        fail |= bool(bad)
        print(f"{section:30s} {bn:>11,d} {pn:>11,d} {b_not_p:>9,d} {p_not_b:>9,d}"
              f"{'  dup-ids=' + str(dup) if dup else ''}{'  <-- FAIL' if bad else ''}")

    con.execute("CREATE TABLE s (section VARCHAR, k VARCHAR)")
    con.executemany("INSERT INTO s VALUES (?, ?)", list(sample.keys()))
    got = {(s, k): d for s, k, d in con.execute(
        "SELECT p.section, p.k, p.d FROM p JOIN s USING (section, k)").fetchall()}
    mism = [sk for sk, j in sample.items() if sk not in got or canon(json.loads(got[sk])) != j]
    print(f"data spot-check: {len(sample):,d} sampled records (crc32 % {a.mod} == 0), {len(mism):,d} differ")
    for s, k in mism[:10]:
        print(f"  DIFF {s}/{k}")
    fail |= bool(mism) or not sample
    print("FAIL" if fail else "PASS")
    sys.exit(1 if fail else 0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

items.title: Appendix C — expected_diff.sh
items.text:
Write to $RB/tools/expected_diff.sh and chmod +x it. Usage: expected_diff.sh <dataset> (compares <t>__pre110 → <t>); TABLES= limits the tables; OLD_DS=… expected_diff.sh <ds> "" "" compares two datasets. Dry-run (expected_diff.sh <ds> --dry-run) passes on all 21 tables (10-04 → 10-11: ~79 GB).

#!/bin/bash
# expected-diff gate: classify every row that differs between <ds>.<t>__pre110 and <ds>.<t>.
# Usage: expected_diff.sh <dataset> [--dry-run] [OLD_SUFFIX]   (OLD_SUFFIX default __pre110)
set -euo pipefail
DS="$1"; DRY="${2:-}"; SUF="${3-__pre110}"
OLD_DS="${OLD_DS:-$DS}"
PTR="r'\"#/(?:var[a-z]+-proposition|proposition[A-Z][A-Za-z]*)/'"
ALL="gkm_dict_sequence_reference gkm_dict_location gkm_dict_allele gkm_dict_copy_number_count \
         gkm_dict_copy_number_change gkm_dict_gene gkm_dict_submitter gkm_dict_therapy gkm_dict_therapygroup \
         gkm_dict_proposition gkm_dict_vcv_proposition gkm_dict_rcv_proposition \
         gkm_dict_variation gkm_dict_condition gkm_dict_condition_set \
         gkm_dict_evidence_line gkm_dict_vcv_evidence_line gkm_dict_rcv_evidence_line \
         gkm_dict_scv gkm_dict_vcv gkm_dict_rcv"
for T in ${TABLES:-$ALL}; do
  case "$T" in
    gkm_dict_variation|gkm_dict_condition|gkm_dict_condition_set|*evidence_line|gkm_dict_scv|gkm_dict_vcv|gkm_dict_rcv)
      K=id; J=t ;;
    *) K=key; J=t.value ;;
  esac
  bq query --quiet --use_legacy_sql=false --format=csv --max_rows=1000 ${DRY:+--dry_run} "
    WITH o AS (SELECT CAST(t.${K} AS STRING) pk, TO_JSON_STRING(${J}) j FROM \`${OLD_DS}.${T}${SUF}\` t),
         n AS (SELECT CAST(t.${K} AS STRING) pk, TO_JSON_STRING(${J}) j FROM \`${DS}.${T}\` t),
         d AS (SELECT pk, o.j oj, n.j nj FROM o FULL JOIN n USING (pk) WHERE o.j IS DISTINCT FROM n.j),
         c AS (SELECT pk, oj, nj,
                 REGEXP_REPLACE(oj, ${PTR}, '\"#/P/') ojn, REGEXP_REPLACE(nj, ${PTR}, '\"#/P/') njn FROM d)
    SELECT '${T}' AS table_name,
      CASE WHEN oj IS NULL THEN 'ADDED' WHEN nj IS NULL THEN 'REMOVED'
           WHEN ojn = njn THEN 'pointer-section-only'
           ELSE IFNULL(NULLIF(\`clinvar_ingest.json_changed_keys\`(ojn, njn), ''), '(order-only)') END AS change,
      COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(pk) AS example_pk
    FROM c GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY n DESC" | { [[ -n "$DRY" ]] && sed "s|^|${T}: |" || tail -n +2; }
done

items.title: Appendix D — check_incr.sh
items.text:
Reference tool: not used by the 1.1.0 rebuild (all FULL, option A). Use it if a weekly run is ever made incremental again (Step 7 uses --full-procs), to prove the build did not silently fall back to full. Write to $RB/tools/check_incr.sh and chmod +x. Read-only (region-us.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS_BY_PROJECT). Validated on the job history: check_incr.sh 2026-07-06 clinvar_2026_06_27_v2_5_0 "2026-10-01 07:40:00" gives INCREMENTAL … 7/7, and the same for 07-15 (no diff drivers) gives NOT INCREMENTAL … 0/7.

#!/bin/bash
# check_incr.sh <date> <baseline_dataset> [since_timestamp]
# Proves that the newest CALL of each of the 7 *_proc_incremental procs for <date> took the INCREMENTAL path:
# in incremental mode each proc reads the baseline dataset's data tables (carry-forward), while a silent fallback
# to full reads only the baseline's INFORMATION_SCHEMA and gkm_pipeline_version (the guard). Exit 1 unless all 7
# show base_reads > 0. Read-only (INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS_BY_PROJECT, region-us).
set -euo pipefail
d="$1"; base="$2"; since="${3:-}"
since_sql="TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 12 HOUR)"; [ -n "$since" ] && since_sql="TIMESTAMP '$since'"
out="$(bq query --use_legacy_sql=false --format=csv --quiet --max_rows=50 "
WITH p AS (
  SELECT job_id, creation_time, REGEXP_EXTRACT(query, r'clinvar_ingest\.([a-z_]+_incremental)') proc
  FROM \`region-us\`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS_BY_PROJECT
  WHERE creation_time > ${since_sql} AND parent_job_id IS NULL AND error_result IS NULL
    AND REGEXP_CONTAINS(query, r\"_proc_incremental\`\\('${d}'\")),
last AS (SELECT * FROM p QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY proc ORDER BY creation_time DESC) = 1)
SELECT l.proc, COUNTIF(STRPOS(c.query, '${base}') > 0 AND NOT REGEXP_CONTAINS(c.query, r'INFORMATION_SCHEMA|gkm_pipeline_version')) AS base_reads
FROM last l JOIN \`region-us\`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS_BY_PROJECT c ON c.parent_job_id = l.job_id
WHERE c.creation_time > ${since_sql}
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1")"
echo "$out" | sed 1d | sed "s/^/  $d /"
n_ok="$(echo "$out" | sed 1d | awk -F, '$2 > 0' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
n_all="$(echo "$out" | sed 1d | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
if [ "$n_all" = 7 ] && [ "$n_ok" = 7 ]; then echo "INCREMENTAL $d: 7/7 procs read baseline $base"
else echo "NOT INCREMENTAL $d: $n_ok/$n_all procs read baseline $base (fell back to full, or a proc did not run)"; exit 1; fi

items.title: Goal
items.text: Refactor VCV and RCV aggregate propositions to mirror the underlying SCV proposition types instead of using generic aggregate-specific types. Move classification from proposition to statement, move submission level to statement strength, and add objectCondition to VCV propositions.

items.title: Current State
items.text:
Aggregate (VCV/RCV) statements currently use:

  • Proposition type: VariantAggregateClassificationProposition (VCV) / VariantAggregateConditionClassificationProposition (RCV)
  • Predicate: hasAggregateClassification (VCV) / hasAggregateConditionClassification (RCV)
  • Proposition attributes:
  • objectClassification (VCV) — MappableConcept with the aggregate classification label
  • objectConditionClassification (RCV) — ConceptSet with condition + classification
  • aggregateQualifiers — array of AssertionGroup, PropositionType, SubmissionLevel, and optionally ClassificationTier
  • subjectVariant — clinvar variation reference
  • Statement-level:
  • classification — already present as a Classification MappableConcept
  • strength — hardcoded to "definitive"

items.title: Proposition Changes (VCV + RCV)
items.text:
The proposition mirrors the underlying SCV proposition type:

  • type — matches the SCV proposition type (e.g., VariantPathogenicityProposition, ClinVarAssociationProposition)
  • predicate — matches the SCV predicate (e.g., isCausalFor, isOncogenicFor)
  • subjectVariant — unchanged (e.g., clinvar:12582)
  • objectClassification — REMOVED from proposition (classification lives on the statement only)
  • objectConditionClassification — REMOVED from RCV proposition
  • aggregateQualifiers — REMOVED entirely

items.title: VCV objectCondition (New)
items.text:
VCV propositions gain a new objectCondition attribute collecting unique conditions from contributing SCVs:

  • Single unique condition → the condition as a MappableConcept (a Condition)
  • Multiple unique conditions → ConceptSet with "OR" membershipOperator containing all unique conditions

This applies at all VCV aggregation layers. Each layer carries forward the objectCondition from its contributing child.

items.title: RCV objectCondition
items.text: No change. RCV is already scoped to a single condition per accession. The existing condition handling in temp_rcv_condition_data remains as-is, but moves to the proposition's objectCondition attribute instead of objectConditionClassification.

items.title: Statement-Level Changes
items.text:
• classification — unchanged (already present as a Classification MappableConcept with optional conflictingExplanation extension)
  • direction — derived from the aggregate classification label:
  • strength — derived from the aggregate classification label:
  • confidence — NEW attribute. Reflects the submission level label at each aggregate layer:
  • Base Grouping: submission level label from submission_level.label (e.g., "criteria provided", "practice guideline")
  • Tier Grouping: carried from contributing Base Grouping record
  • Aggregate Contribution: winning submission level's label — requires a new join to submission_level on agg.contributing_submission_level = sl.code (not currently present in Aggregate Contribution statement queries)
  • Non-contributing evidence lines carry confidence from their own layer — each layer sets its own confidence at the BASE step, and the PRE inlining carries it forward automatically

items.title: Single-SCV Passthrough Rule
items.text: When a Base Grouping contains exactly one contributing SCV, the aggregate statement inherits the SCV's direction, strength, and full proposition structure identically. The confidence is still set to the submission level label. The direction/strength mapping table below only applies when multiple SCVs are aggregated.

items.title: Direction and Strength Mapping (Multiple SCVs)
items.text:
When multiple SCVs are aggregated, the direction and strength values are derived from the aggregate classification label (the agg_label / actual_agg_classif_label value). This mapping is applied at every aggregate layer.

Classification Label direction strength Pathogenic supports definitive Likely pathogenic supports likely Uncertain significance neutral (null) Likely benign disputes likely Benign disputes definitive Pathogenic/Likely pathogenic supports (null) Benign/Likely benign disputes (null) Conflicting classifications of... neutral (null) All others supports definitive

Null strength values are omitted from JSON output by JSON_STRIP_NULLS.

items.title: SCV Statement Changes
items.text:
SCV statements also gain the confidence attribute. The submission level value currently stored in the clinvarReviewStatus extension moves to confidence on the SCV statement. This ensures a consistent confidence attribute across SCV and aggregate statements.

Note: This is a change to gks_scv_statement_proc, not the aggregate procedures. The SCV direction and strength values remain unchanged (they are already derived from the classification at the SCV level).

items.title: Proposition Type and Predicate Mapping
items.text:
The clinvar_proposition_types lookup table needs two new columns: gks_type and gks_predicate.

prop_type code gks_type gks_predicate path VariantPathogenicityProposition isCausalFor onco VariantOncogenicityProposition isOncogenicFor sci VariantClinicalSignificanceProposition isClinicallySignificantFor drug-resp ClinVarDrugResponseProposition isClinvarDrugResponseFor risk ClinVarRiskFactorProposition isClinvarRiskFactorFor protective ClinVarProtectiveProposition isClinvarProtectiveFor affects ClinVarAffectsProposition isClinvarAffectsFor assoc ClinVarAssociationProposition isClinvarAssociationFor confers-sens ClinVarConfersSensitivityProposition isClinvarConfersSensitivityFor other ClinVarOtherProposition isClinvarOtherFor np ClinVarNotProvidedProposition isClinvarNotProvidedFor

Each prop_type maps 1:1 to a single GKS proposition type. These are derived from the existing clinvar_clinsig_types.final_proposition_type / final_predicate values — all classification codes within a given prop_type share the same proposition type.

items.title: VCV Condition Data Flow
items.text: Currently condition data is only collected in VCV for somatic sci propositions (via gks_scv_condition_mapping for trait names). The new design requires condition concept collection for ALL proposition types.

items.title: Aggregation Proc Changes
items.text:
The VCV aggregation proc (gks_vcv_proc) needs to:

  1. Join gks_scv_condition_sets by scv_id in the base data or at the Base Grouping step
  2. Collect unique condition concepts per aggregation group (keyed by condition id to deduplicate)
  3. Store the collected conditions array on gks_vcv_grouping_base_agg

Handling compound conditionSets: Individual SCVs may have either a single condition or a conditionSet (multiple conditions). When collecting unique conditions across SCVs in a group, individual conditions within a conditionSet should be flattened and merged into the unique set — each condition is treated independently, not as an atomic group.

Pipeline ordering dependency: gks_scv_condition_proc must run before gks_vcv_proc (this is already the case in the pipeline, but the dependency is now explicit for VCV).

items.title: Statement Proc Changes
items.text:
The VCV statement proc (gks_vcv_statement_proc) builds the objectCondition:

  • Single condition in array → output as the MappableConcept directly
  • Multiple conditions in array → wrap in ConceptSet with "OR" membershipOperator
  • No conditions found → objectCondition is NULL, omitted from output by JSON_STRIP_NULLS

At each layer, the objectCondition is carried forward from the contributing child (same as classification is today).

items.title: RCV Condition Data Flow
items.text: The existing temp_rcv_condition_data resolution remains, but the output moves from objectConditionClassification (a ConceptSet of condition + classification) to objectCondition (just the condition, without the classification). When no condition data exists for an RCV (the LEFT JOIN yields NULL), objectCondition will be NULL and omitted from output by JSON_STRIP_NULLS.

items.title: What Gets Removed
items.text:
• VariantAggregateClassificationProposition type
  • VariantAggregateConditionClassificationProposition type
  • hasAggregateClassification predicate
  • hasAggregateConditionClassification predicate
  • objectClassification from VCV propositions
  • objectConditionClassification from RCV propositions
  • aggregateQualifiers from all propositions
  • Hardcoded "definitive" strength and "supports" direction — replaced with classification-derived values
  • Added: confidence attribute on all aggregate statements (carrying submission level label)
